docs.title: Excel link
docs.text:
The number of one legend row sits in one workbook cell and updates by itself when the measurements change. Here: how to link, what happens with an open and a closed workbook, the four states, Auto Link for the whole DFL, resetting all links and what to do before handing the workbook to the client. A regular one-time paste is described on the Measurements page.

One way only, from OurPDF to Excel

Editing a cell does not change the measurement. The app never saves an open workbook: you save it, as after a regular paste. Until you press "Link to Excel", OurPDF does not touch Excel.

The Corridor row is selected. The Auto Link and "Link to Excel" buttons sit next to the Excel button, linked legend rows have a chain icon. The workbooks here are made up.

docs.title: How to link
docs.text:
1. In OurPDF, select one legend row: click the row or its measurement on the sheet.
  2. In Excel, open a saved workbook and click the cell you need.
  3. In OurPDF, press Link to Excel. The number appears in the cell right away.

Good to know:

  • The button is in the "Scale" block; with the lock open it comes in the style block together with the selection.
  • The same command: right-click a legend row, the Export PDF menu on the right strip. There is no default key, but you can assign one.
  • The number is the same as with the "values only" export: same units, decimals and J2.
  • If the cell already has something in it, the app asks first.

docs.title: How it updates
docs.text: What happened What happens the workbook is open the cell updates right away, after a short pause. The worksheet and the selection in Excel stay where they are. The write clears Excel's own undo (Ctrl+Z) the workbook is closed the link waits in the "Pending" state. The number is written on Ctrl+S or on the "Update Links" command: in a hidden Excel with macros off, with a backup of the workbook in the app folder, %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPDF\excel-link-backups. Nothing appears next to the workbook rows were inserted in Excel the link holds on to a hidden name in the workbook, which follows the cell. The app does not guess the address the legend row was renamed or recolored the link follows it measurements hidden in the legend they are included in the number, as in the legend total: hiding only removes them from the screen the file was closed and reopened the links are in place. They are stored in the profile, not in the PDF, they are not a Ctrl+Z step and not an unsaved change. Answering "No" when closing the file does not drop them

docs.title: States
docs.text: The icon color shows the worst state of the row's links. The icon tooltip: workbook, worksheet, cell, last number, reason. State Icon What it means What to do Linked text color the cell holds this row's number nothing Pending yellow the new number is not written yet: the workbook is closed, Excel is busy or a cell is being edited, the file is busy, read-only or missing, the row has no scale closed workbook: Ctrl+S or "Update Links". Busy Excel: the app retries by itself. Missing file: "Point to New Path...". The reason is written in the link list Conflict orange the cell was changed by hand, the app leaves it alone "Overwrite the Cell" or "Keep the Cell and Unlink" Broken red the legend row was deleted, the cell was deleted (#REF!) or the joists now have a different number of lengths. Nothing is written, the cell stays as it is Ctrl+Z brings back a deleted row. Otherwise unlink and link again

docs.title: Joists: two numbers
docs.text: A joists row has two numbers for each length: count and length. "Link to Excel" asks which one goes into this cell; if there are several lengths, the list also has the totals. For the second number, click another cell and press the button again.

docs.title: All links of the file
docs.text:
"All Excel Links...": where each link is and what state it is in. The two conflict buttons show when such a row is selected. Button What it does Go to Cell shows the cell in Excel, opens a closed workbook first Unlink the link is gone, the number stays in the cell. If the workbook is closed, its hidden name goes away when it is opened while this file is open Update Links writes everything that is waiting, including into closed workbooks Point to New Path... the workbook was moved or renamed Remove All Links from This Workbook... see below Reset All Links... removes all links of this file: see below

Before handing the workbook to the client

"All Excel Links...", the row of this workbook, "Remove All Links from This Workbook...". The numbers stay in the cells, the hidden names go away, including those made by other files and by OurPlanCore.

docs.title: Auto Link: the whole DFL in one click
docs.text:
What for: the numbers are already exported to the J:L list, and linking each legend row by hand takes long. Needed: OurPDF 0.9.27 or newer, a saved DFL workbook active in Excel. OurPlanCore has the same since version 3.0.29: Auto Link in OurPlanCore.

Look at the result window right after pressing

There is no question before linking, the result window is the check. A probable link can land on someone else's row with the same number, and the next measurement edit will write the new number there. Once you close the window, "Undo This Auto Link" is gone.

  1. In the legend, pick the scope: "Current sheet" or "Entire PDF". Auto Link takes only the rows of this scope. A PDF of several buildings and a workbook for one: do not pick "Entire PDF".
  2. Press Auto Link next to "Link to Excel". The same command: right-click a legend row, the Export PDF menu on the right strip. There is no default key.
  3. Links appear right away, the window shows the result for each row.
  4. Check every Probable row: the label in column J must be about this legend row.
  5. Save the workbook in Excel yourself. Auto Link does not change cell values and does not save the workbook, it only adds hidden names. Close the workbook without saving: the names disappear, the links show "Broken".

Result: the "Sure" and "Probable" rows are linked, the rest are described in the window with a reason.

The result window, the workbook is made up. Corridor is linked as Sure. Units is linked as Probable: the label Hand line says nothing about it, and that is exactly the row to check by eye.

DFL only: a .xlsm, .xlsb or .xls workbook with a Detailed Frame List worksheet whose column A has the word Description in the first 150 rows. Another workbook: the status bar says so, and nothing else happens. "Link to Excel" works on any workbook.

What gets linked. There is only one target: constant numbers in column K of this worksheet, from row 2, with the label taken from column J. Formulas never count. Columns A:H, block O and other macro blocks, other worksheets are never targets, even if the number matches.

Group When What happens Sure the label in J equals the legend row name (case and spaces do not matter), the number matches, there is only one such row linked right away Probable the label does not equal the name, but the number is one to one: it is in exactly one K cell and no other participating legend row has it (openings, joists and already linked rows do not count). That row's label is not the name of another legend row linked right away, check by eye Ambiguous this number is in several cells or on several rows, the name does not decide it not linked: select the row in the window, pick a cell in the "Cell" column, press "Link This Row" Skipped see the list below, the reason is written on the window row not linked

The number is compared at the Excel export precision (2 decimals by default) and no wider. A cell 162.504 matches the row 162.50 and keeps its value until the row number changes. You changed a measurement after the export: the number is not in the list, the row will be skipped.

What is skipped:

  • windows, doors and other openings, by the row name and by the label in J: window, windows, wind, wnd, door, doors, opening, openings, storefront, gd, lv, louver, words starting with окн, двер, проём (Russian for window, door, opening), an opening size with a dot like 3.0x6.7 d. A manual "Link to Excel" works on them;
  • joists: the row has several numbers, link them by hand;
  • Count without its own name in J: Count links only by name, whatever the number;
  • a small whole number without a name: a line or area with a whole number below 10 (threshold in settings). With a name it links;
  • zero and a row with no number (no scale);
  • an already linked row, a cell with someone else's link, a formula in the cell, a list row with the name of another legend row, the number is not in the list.

A legend row without a name has nothing to compare: at best Probable, and Count without a name never links.

When Probable is wrong:

  • a row with a different name and the same number was typed into J by hand, and the item itself has not been exported to the list yet;
  • a total row (two items as one number) happens to equal a third one;
  • the legend scope is wider than the workbook: "Entire PDF" of several buildings;
  • the legend row has no name, only a number.

What to do. "Undo This Auto Link" removes all links from this window, including those linked in it by hand. One row is removed with "Unlink" in the legend row menu. The numbers in the cells stay, including those written after linking. A closed workbook loses the names the next time it is opened.

docs.title: Reset all links
docs.text:
"Reset All Links..." removes all links of this file. The button is in the "All Excel Links..." window, on the right-click menu of a legend row, and in the Export PDF menu. First a question with the number of links. It cannot be undone. The values in the cells stay.

  • Open workbooks lose this file's hidden names right away. The workbook is not saved, you save it.
  • Closed workbooks lose the names when the workbook is opened while this file is open. Without saving.
  • A second button, "Remove Them and Clean the Closed Workbooks Now", shows if some workbook is closed. It cleans closed workbooks right away, with a hidden Excel and a backup, and removes all names from them, including those of other files and OurPlanCore.
Reset All Links Remove All Links from This Workbook Scope this file, all its workbooks one workbook Which names only this file's, except with the second button all, including other files' and OurPlanCore's Closed workbook at the next opening or with the second button right away, with a hidden Excel and a backup When to link the file again before handing the workbook to the client

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings, section "Link to Excel behaviour":

Setting Default Update an open workbook at once on Update a closed workbook on Ctrl+S on Backups kept per workbook 5, from 1 to 50 Delay before an open workbook is updated 800 ms, from 100 to 10000 Time limit for a closed workbook 180 s, from 15 to 1800 Auto Link: lines and areas, a whole number below this needs its name; Count always does 10, from 0 to 1000

docs.title: How to measure step by step
docs.text:
Ready-made scenarios: what to press, where to click and what to check. Details on each tool are on the Measurements page, all keys on the Keyboard shortcuts page.

Three rules

  1. Scale first, then measurements. Without a scale, OurPDF writes inches on paper.
  2. The cursor snaps to drawing lines: place points on the line, not next to it.
  3. Esc cancels what is being drawn, Ctrl+Z undoes what is finished.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the sheet
docs.text:
1. Open the PDF (Ctrl+O or drag the file into the window) and go to the sheet you need.
  2. Turn measuring on: the ruler button. The buttons sit in blocks on the top toolbar (Top toolbar).
  3. In the "Scale" block, pick the scale from the title block or the caption under the view (1/8" = 1'-0") and press Enter.
  4. Check the scale: R and two clicks on the ends of a known dimension (a dimension string, a long wall). The value must match the dimension on the drawing.
  5. It doesn't match: the calibrate button next to the scale box, mark a known segment and enter its length (25'-6").
  6. Save the scale in the sheet: the pin button next to the box (or Ctrl+S). The file will then open with it already set, here and in Acrobat.

A detail at a different scale

There is one scale for the whole sheet, and changing it recalculates all OurPDF measurements on that sheet. To get a dimension of a detail at its own scale: set the detail scale, take the dimension (R), write it down and set the sheet scale back. Do permanent measurements of such a detail in OurPlanCore.

docs.title: 2. Walls in LF
docs.text:
1. Press L (line).
  2. Click the wall corners along one face (or the centerline); each point snaps to a drawing line.
  3. Perfectly horizontal or vertical: hold Shift or turn on Ortho (F8).
  4. Finish: C, Enter or double-click.
  5. Name it: double-click the line (the "Select" tool, V) and type a label, for example 1st Ext 2x6.

Faster along the drawing: before the first point, hover over the wall line and press Tab. The edge (this line) highlights, a second Tab highlights the whole contour, a click takes it all (Tab along a line).

The line's length shows in a box by the cursor on hover; all lines with their values are in the "Comments" list on the right.

docs.title: 3. Floor or room area in SF
docs.text:
Tab on a room wall: the first press takes the edge, the second the closed contour. A click turns the contour into an area.

Three ways, from fast to manual:

Way When How Tab along the contour the room or floor is outlined with a solid line A, cursor on the wall, Tab Tab, click Box (F9) a rectangle A, F9, click one corner, click the opposite one; width x height shows under the value By corners a complex shape A, click the corners, click the first point, double-click or Enter

What to subtract (stair, shaft, atrium): X, a box or polygon over the area. Inside the area you get a hole, across the edge it bites off a piece, across the whole area it splits it in two (Cut).

docs.title: 4. Elevation: sheathing and siding
docs.text:
1. Set the elevation scale (step 1).
  2. A and trace the elevation wall along its outline: by corners, or Box (F9) if the wall is rectangular.
  3. Subtract windows and doors: X, drag a box over each opening. If the area was selected, only it is cut.
  4. The area value is already net of openings (net SF); check it in the box on hover.
  5. For finishes by height (for example, siding only up to a band), split the area with a cut across it.

If the elevation hatch sits on its own PDF layer, the areas can be taken with one button: the "Layers" tab, pick the layer, "Trace layer as areas" (Trace a layer).

docs.title: 5. Joists and rafters
docs.text:
Joists area: the joists are laid out at spacing, the label "2x10 1152 FT (24 pcs)" is calculated by OurPlanCore code.
  1. The gear in the "Measure" block: type (2x10), spacing (16"), pitch (empty for joists, 6:12 for rafters), rounding.
  2. J, trace the area like an area (or F9 and two corners, or Tab along the contour).
  3. Two points along the joist direction (Enter takes the long side).
  4. Extra joists (doubled under walls, at openings): select the area, D, click inside; Shift and click removes one, D or Esc exits.
  5. Right-click the area: "Copy joists note" gives the label and a list of lengths with counts for Excel.

docs.title: 6. Check a dimension on the drawing
docs.text:
R and two clicks: you get a dimension line with ticks at the ends, and the dimension is always labeled on the sheet. Handy for checking the scale, a span or an opening width. Delete it afterwards if not needed: select it and Del.

Both room dimensions at once: R, F9, two opposite corners. You get two separate distances from the first corner, horizontal and vertical (Box).

docs.title: 7. Fix a measurement
docs.text: A click on a point of the selected area selected it (orange): Del removes only this point. What you need How move a point V, select the measurement, drag the point (it snaps to the drawing) move an edge drag an edge of the selected measurement; Shift keeps it straight delete a point click the point, Del delete an edge click the edge (both its points get selected), Del move the whole measurement drag from inside the area or with Alt select many E and a frame: left to right takes what is wholly inside, right to left everything touched undo Ctrl+Z

docs.title: 8. Mark a question on the sheet
docs.text: Callout (the button next to "Text" on the toolbar): click where the arrow points, a second click where the text goes, then the text. Handy for questions to the client and notes to yourself; it goes into the PDF together with the measurements.

docs.title: 9. Save and export
docs.text:
1. Measurements are saved automatically in the app profile while the PDF is open.
  2. Ctrl+S writes them into the PDF itself (a copy of the previous file goes into backups); they are visible in Acrobat and Bluebeam.
  3. Totals by type: the "Legend" tab on the right strip. A list of all measurements: the "Comments" tab.
  4. Into an open Excel workbook: select a cell, go back to OurPDF, the Excel button in the "Scale" block, Ctrl+E or Ctrl+T (Excel). To make the cell update by itself: Excel link.
  5. As a separate .xlsx file: the "Measurements to Excel" button in the "Comments" list.

docs.title: 10. Compare two sheets
docs.text:
1. Open the new sheet, the "Overlay" icon on the left strip.
  2. Add..., pick the old sheet of this PDF or a page of another file.
  3. Auto Fit. It doesn't match: Edit by Points, or drag the orange frame.
  4. Colored lines with no black under them are the differences.

Details: Sheet overlay. The overlay is not written on Ctrl+S and is not printed.

docs.title: 11. Gather details on one sheet
docs.text:
1. The "Crop" icon on the left strip, "Target sheet": a new blank sheet, Start Cropping.
  2. On the sheets you need, drag frames around the details: they land on the new sheet at 100 %.
  3. Esc, open the new sheet, arrange the crops with the mouse.
  4. Measure over the crop as usual, Ctrl+S.

Details: Crop to sheet.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Mistake How to avoid it dimensions in inches on paper the sheet scale is not set: step 1 the value does not match the dimension on the drawing wrong scale or the sheet is not to scale: calibrate on a known dimension a detail measured at the sheet scale one scale per sheet: measure a detail at its own scale in OurPlanCore, or take the dimension and set the sheet scale back a point landed on hatching or text zoom in; turn off the extra snap in the "Snap" block or hide the hatch layer (the "Layers" tab) an area counted twice look at the "Comments" list: identical values next to each other Excel shows less than the sheet measurements hidden in the legend are not included in an area export; the status bar says how many measurements are not on paper printing draws the file as it is saved: Ctrl+S first openings not subtracted from the elevation a cut X with a box over each opening

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
The main part of OurPDF. Measurements as in Acrobat (distance, perimeter, area) plus what you are used to in OurPlanCore: the keys R, L, A, J, X, C, B, O, Ortho and Box modes, Tab along a drawing line, cutouts, joists and extra joists, Beam and Openings, Merge, Split and Combine, snapping on F3 and Ctrl+F3, moving edges, frame selection, lengths in LF on hover. The line end style (arrows, ticks) is changed in Settings. Here, step by step: scale, toolbar blocks, each measurement type, editing, deleting points, legend, list and Excel. Linking a legend row to a workbook cell has its own page: Excel link.

Area measuring is on. Room UNIT 102 is already measured: its width and height are under the value in sf. UNIT 104 is being traced now, guide lines run through the cursor, measurement info at the bottom.

docs.title: In short
docs.text: Task Key How Result turn measuring on none the ruler button on the toolbar or on the right strip; press again to turn it off. You can assign a key in Settings: Ctrl+Shift+M is now Split, as in OurPlanCore top toolbar blocks (lock) dimension between two points R two clicks length 12'-6" (12.50 ft) wall length, polyline L click the points, C, Enter or double-click polyline length in LF room area A click the corners, close SF at the center of the area joists / rafters J trace the area, two points along the joists count and lengths by OurPlanCore's calculation cutout from an area X a box or polygon over the area hole, bite or split rectangle by two corners F9 Box mode for area, line, joists, cut measurement by two corners both sides of a room R and F9 two corners two distances at once pieces P a click on each Count, a row in ea strictly horizontal or vertical F8 Ortho mode; Shift for a moment a straight line take a whole drawing line Tab hover the line before the first point edge, then contour beam with order length B two clicks along the beam a dimension and Count Beam 12 (Beam) opening O two corners of the opening width, height and Count 3.0x6.8 move measurements into another or a new takeoff Ctrl+M, Ctrl+Shift+M select the measurements Merge and Split (details) snap to measurements, to PDF lines F3, Ctrl+F3 press, press again to turn off as in OurPlanCore (Snapping) arrows at line ends none Settings, "Line ends" Line ends

docs.title: Scale and calibration
docs.text: Without a scale, values are written in inches on paper. The scale is stored for each sheet separately and affects only OurPDF measurements: it does not change OurPlanCore takeoffs.

docs.title: Pick or type a scale
docs.text:
1. Turn measuring on: the ruler button.
  2. In the "Scale" block on the second toolbar row, pick a value from the list:
    • architectural 1/32" = 1'-0" to 3" = 1'-0";
    • engineering 1" = 10' to 1" = 200';
    • metric 1:1 to 1:1000.
  3. Or type your own: 1/8" = 1'-0", 1" = 20', 1:100, 1 in = 8 ft and press Enter.
  4. Where the scale came from ("set by hand", "by calibration", "from the PDF", "from OurPlanCore") shows in the measurement info on the bottom bar.

Take the scale from the title block or the caption under the view (SCALE: 1/8" = 1'-0"), then check it with one measurement along a dimension string.

docs.title: Calibrate on a known dimension
docs.text:
Needed when the sheet has no scale or was printed not to scale.

  1. Click the calibrate button to the right of the scale box.
  2. Click the start and end of a segment of known length, for example a dimension line.
  3. In the "Calibrate scale" window, enter the real length: 12'-6", 25', 3.5 m.
  4. The status bar shows "Sheet scale by calibration: ...".

docs.title: Save the scale in the sheet
docs.text: The pin button next to the scale box (or right-click with the ruler on, "Save the scale into the PDF sheet") writes the scale into the PDF itself, as Acrobat does: a viewport with the scale is added to the sheet. It is the same write as Ctrl+S, with a backup of the previous file. After that the file opens with this scale in OurPDF, Acrobat and Bluebeam, on any computer. Ctrl+S also writes the sheet scale by itself, together with the measurements.

docs.title: Scale and precision for all sheets
docs.text:
The ... button next to the box opens the "Scale and precision" window (also in the right-click menu with the ruler on: "Change scale and precision").

Field Options Sheet scale a list or your own text; OurPlanCore snapshots have the item "As in OurPlanCore" Units feet-inches (12'-6"), feet (12.50 ft), inches, meters, centimeters, millimeters Precision inch denominator for ft-in, or decimal places Apply to this sheet or to all sheets of the document

A measurement taken in from another app's PDF keeps its own scale, as in Acrobat. For OurPlanCore project snapshots, the scale comes from OurPlanCore by default.

docs.title: Top toolbar blocks
docs.text:
The "Measure" card is gone: the buttons sit in blocks on two rows under the menu. How they work, how to move them and what the lock does: Top toolbar.

Block Buttons Measure distance (R), Pitch, perimeter or line (L), area (A), joists (J), Beam (B), Openings (O), cut (X); Ortho (F8) and Box (F9) modes; joists gear: type, spacing and pitch of new joists; Count (P), P Line, Break, Ends Snap to paths (any point of a line), to endpoints, to midpoints, to intersections, to OurPDF objects and measurements; "All off" and "All on"; F3 to measurements, Ctrl+F3 to PDF lines Measurement style colors, palette, line width, font, opacity; Rot, Scale, Mirror Scale combo box, calibration, ... (scale and precision), pin; Auto Link, "Link to Excel" and Excel buttons, J2, format circle

At the bottom, in the status bar, "Measurement info": tool, scale and where it came from, value, ΔX, ΔY, angle, snap type.

docs.title: Snapping
docs.text:
• The cursor snaps to drawing lines. While a point is snapped, the line highlights purple and the icon by the cursor shows the snap type.
  • Types are turned on and off with the buttons of the "Snap" block. All at once: the "All off" button (and "All on"). All snapping in one go: right-click, "Snap to page content".
  • F3 turns snapping to existing measurements (their corners, midpoints and lines) on and off, Ctrl+F3 snapping to the PDF's own lines, as in OurPlanCore. They are independent: without PDF snapping a point still lands on measurement corners, without measurement snapping on drawing lines. What turned on or off is written in the status bar. The same two checkboxes are in the right-click menu and in Settings.
  • Tab along a drawing line works while snapping to PDF lines is on.
  • Snapping does not catch the content of an overlay.
  • The snap radius is set in Settings: "Snap radius, px", 10 by default (from 2 to 40).
  • Snapping does not catch lines on hidden PDF layers (Layers).
  • While measuring, thin horizontal and vertical guide lines run through the cursor, as in OurPlanCore. Turned off in Settings: "Guide lines through the pointer while measuring".

docs.title: Distance: dimension between two points
docs.text:
What for: check the scale, take a dimension that is not labeled on the drawing.

  1. Press R (or the "Distance" button on the toolbar).
  2. Click the start and the end.
  3. The measurement is done right after the second click. The length is written as 12'-6" with feet in parentheses.

A distance is drawn as a dimension line, like the Ruler in OurPlanCore: ticks across the ends, and the dimension is always labeled on the sheet (for a perimeter the length shows on hover).

docs.title: Pitch: slope from two points
docs.text: The Pitch button in the "Measure" block. Two clicks along the slope on an elevation or section. No scale needed; for a sloped line, turn Ortho off (F8). Label: slope and angle, for example 6:12 (26.57°). Moving the ends recalculates the label.

docs.title: Line and perimeter: length by points
docs.text:
What for: wall length, polyline, room perimeter in LF.

  1. Press L (the "Perimeter" button).
  2. Click points along the wall centerline, corner by corner.
  3. Finish: C (as in OurPlanCore), Enter or double-click.
  4. Backspace removes the last point, Esc cancels the whole measurement.

For a rectangular perimeter, turn on Box (F9): a line in Box mode is drawn by two corners and becomes a closed rectangle around the perimeter.

docs.title: Area: room, floor, balcony
docs.text:
What for: SF of a room, floor, balcony.

  1. Press A (the "Area" button).
  2. Click the corners of the outline.
  3. Close it: click the first point, double-click, Enter or C.
  4. The value in sf appears at the center of the area, net of cutouts. For a rectangle, width x height shows under the value.
  5. To label a room, double-click the measurement and type a label (UNIT 102): it is written before the value.

Faster: a rectangle with Box (F9, two corners) or the closed room contour with Tab (Tab).

docs.title: Box: rectangle by two corners (F9)
docs.text:
As in OurPlanCore. The mode applies to distance, area, line, joists and cut.

  1. Press F9 or the Box button on the toolbar.
  2. Pick the type (R, A, L, J or X).
  3. Click the first corner: the rectangle follows the cursor.
  4. Click the opposite corner.
  5. F9 again goes back to drawing by points.

Left, distance in Box mode: UNIT 107, two sides with labels. Right, area in Box mode: width x height under the value.
  • Distance in Box mode measures both sides: two corners give two separate distances from the first corner, horizontal and vertical, and one Ctrl+Z step. A flat frame gives only the side it has.
  • A line in Box mode is a closed rectangle around the perimeter.
  • Box can be on by default in Settings: "Box: area, line, cut and size by two corners (F9)".

docs.title: Width x height on rectangles
docs.text: A rectangular area, joists and a closed rectangular line show width x height under the value: on the sheet, in the hover box and in the info at the bottom. Any rectangle counts, whether drawn by points or brought in from another app (tolerance 1 % and about half a degree). Turned off in Settings: "Rectangular measurements: show both sides". Only the value itself is written into the PDF comment.

docs.title: Ortho: strictly horizontal or vertical (F8)
docs.text:
• F8 or the Ortho button on the toolbar keeps the line strictly horizontal or vertical.
  • Shift does the same while held. With Ortho on, Shift frees the line instead.
  • Ortho can be on by default in Settings: "Ortho by default (Shift inverts)".

docs.title: Tab: take a whole drawing line
docs.text:
Like edge snap in OurPlanCore: instead of clicking corners, you take a line or contour already drawn in the PDF.

Left: one Tab, the edge is highlighted (pdf edge). Right: a second Tab, the closed contour of room UNIT 106 (pdf contour). A click gives the room area right away.
  1. Pick the measurement type and do not place any points.
  2. Hover over a drawing line and press Tab: the edge (this line) highlights.
  3. Tab again: the contour, the whole chain of lines; if it closes, the closed contour of the room.
  4. Further Tab presses cycle through polylines and adjacent edges and return to regular points.
  5. A click takes what is highlighted. Esc cancels.

What you get by type:

Type Edge Chain area, cut, joists a closed contour becomes an area right away (or a cut, or a joists area); an open chain places its points, then keep clicking as usual perimeter edge the whole chain, closed back to the first point distance distance along the edge perimeter along the chain

Hovering another line starts again from points, as in OurPlanCore. The contour jumps over doors and small gaps in walls.

docs.title: Continue takeoff (Space)
docs.text: As in OurPlanCore: select a measurement, press Space and keep drawing in it. New measurements get the same type, color, name, line width, opacity and font, for joists the joist type and spacing, and add up with it in one legend row. The takeoff row in the legend is bold. Space again stops recording (an unfinished measurement is dropped), and Space with nothing selected goes back to the last takeoff of this file.

docs.title: Count, P Line, Break, Ends
docs.text:
The buttons in the "Measure" block. The corridor line is selected, with two Posts count points at its ends (the Ends button). In the corner of the sheet, the pinned legend, the Corridor row selected together with the line. Tool How Result Count (P) a click on each point, Esc finishes count points, no scale needed P Line select lines, press P Line, set the name and spacing in inches points at spacing from the start of each line; a physical spacing needs a scale Break (Ctrl+Shift+B) select a polyline independent segments, the total length is kept Ends select lines Count at starts and ends; coinciding ends can be merged

P Line and Ends keep the source lines. Ctrl+Z undoes the creation of the whole group in one operation.

docs.title: Beam and Openings
docs.text:
Like B and O in OurPlanCore. The buttons sit in the "Measure" block.

Tool Key How Result Beam B two clicks along the beam a beam dimension and a Count takeoff with the order length in the name: Beam 12 Openings O two opposite corners of the opening width as a dimension on top, height on the left, Count takeoff 3.0x6.8 with a mark in the middle
  • The order length in the Beam name is calculated as in OurPlanCore: up to 8 ft round up to whole feet, longer round up to even feet (10'-3" gives Beam 12). You can pick in Settings: whole feet or as measured.
  • After two Beam clicks a window opens: name (the beginning selected), color and the "Keep a line along the beam" checkbox. If that name already exists, its color is used, and beams of one size go on one legend row. "Cancel" keeps only the dimension.
  • Then the tool switches to Count of this takeoff by itself: click the other identical beams or openings, Esc finishes. In Settings you can make it measure the next beam or opening right away instead.
  • Openings works by two corners even with Box off.
  • Beam and Openings dimensions are for reference: they show on the sheet with their length, but do not go into the legend, totals, Excel or Excel links. The Count takeoffs are what counts.
  • One Ctrl+Z removes the whole beam or the whole opening.

docs.title: Merge, Split, Combine
docs.text:
A takeoff here is a legend row: type, color and name.

Command Key What it does Merge Ctrl+M the selected measurements move into another takeoff of the same type (if several fit, a list appears) and take its color, name, line width, opacity and font. Collinear straight lines that touch become one segment, touching areas become one area Split Ctrl+Shift+M the selected measurements go into a new takeoff with its own name and color Combine Union none the selected areas become one Combine Subtract none the first selected area minus the rest Combine Intersect none only the common part of the areas remains Combine Remove Overlap none removes double counting, the common part stays with the first selected Combine Divide none each area keeps its own part, the common part becomes a new area
  • The Merge, Split and Combine buttons are in the legend header. The same commands are in the Edit menu, in the right-click menu on the sheet and on a legend row (then the whole takeoff is taken).
  • For Combine, select two or more areas. The first selected is the main one.
  • Each command is undone with one Ctrl+Z.
  • Merging of lines and areas, the merge tolerance (0.75 pt) and the new color on Split can be changed in Settings, section "Line ends, Beam, Openings, Merge".

docs.title: Joists and rafters
docs.text:
2x10 joists at 16" in UNIT 103: count, lengths and label are calculated by OurPlanCore code. Label UNIT 103 floor: 2x10 1152 FT (24 pcs).

What for: count and lengths of joists or rafters over an area, with the same calculation as in OurPlanCore (J Area).

docs.title: Set up new joists
docs.text:
1. In the "Measure" block, click the gear next to the types.
  2. Fill in the "Joists / rafters: new areas" window:
Field What to enter Type (label) 2x10, 11 7/8 TJI Spacing, inches (o.c.) 16, 19.2, 24 Pitch (rafters) empty - flat joists; for rafters 6:12, 6/12 or 4 (= 4:12), lengths are calculated along the slope Length rounding no rounding, up to the foot, up to the even foot, up to 2 feet End joist at the far edge checkbox Detailed label lengths by group: order, flat, along the slope Length at each joist checkbox

docs.title: Draw the area
docs.text:
1. Press J.
  2. Trace the area by its corners and close it (or F9 and two corners, or Tab along the contour).
  3. Place two points along the joists. Enter (or right-click, "Direction along the longest side") lays the joists along the long side.
  4. The joists and a label like 2x10 64 FT (8 pcs) appear on the sheet: type, total length, count.

Double-clicking a finished area opens the same settings for it ("Joists / rafters: this area"): a label before the total and the checkbox "Set the direction again (two points along the joists)".

docs.title: Extra joists (D)
docs.text:
1. Select the joists area (V and click).
  2. Press D.
  3. Click inside the area: each extra joist lands along the joist direction and highlights.
  4. Shift and click removes the nearest extra.
  5. D or Esc: exit.

Extras go into the total and into a separate "Extra" block in the note.

docs.title: Right-click menu of a joists area
docs.text:
Item What it does Add extra joists (by clicks) same as D Remove all extra joists deletes all extras of this area Copy joists note the label and the list of lengths with counts as text, for Excel or an email Joists settings the settings window of this area

Rules on what to count as joists: Joist. The same tool in OurPlanCore: J Area.

docs.title: Cutout from an area
docs.text:
The stair is cut out of the STAIR BAY area (a hole), UNIT 110 has a corner bitten off for a closet. The values in sf are already net of the cutouts.

What for: a shaft, stair, open to below inside an area; a corner that is not part of the room.

  1. Turn the cut on: the cut button in the "Measure" block, X or right-click an area, "Cut from area".
  2. Drag a box or click the corners (close: first point, double-click, Enter).
  3. The result depends on where the cut goes:
    • inside the area you get a hole;
    • across the edge a piece is bitten off;
    • across the whole area it is split in two.
  4. If areas were selected before the cut, only they are cut. Otherwise all areas and joists the cut touched are cut.
  5. The mode stays on for the next cut. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole cut.

Points and edges of cutouts are dragged the same way as those of the area itself. If you delete all points of a cutout, the cutout itself disappears.

Cut from lines: the same for lines. The part of a line inside the cut is deleted, the rest becomes separate lines with the same style, name and scale.

docs.title: Values: labels and hover
docs.text:
For lines, the length appears in a box by the cursor on hover ("Corridor 188,44 LF"). Over an area the box shows SF and the perimeter in LF.
  • An area is labeled at the center of the sheet area. The measurement label (for example UNIT 102) is written before the value: double-click the measurement or right-click, "Change markup label".
  • A distance is a dimension line: ticks at the ends, the dimension always on the sheet.
  • Lines (perimeter, and in a snapshot's live layer also OurPlanCore lines) show the length in LF only on hover, in a box by the cursor on top of everything.
  • Over an area, the hover box shows SF and the perimeter in LF.
  • To always label lines on the sheet: Settings, "Line lengths (LF) on the sheet" = "always labelled", or right-click with the ruler on and uncheck "Line lengths only on hover (LF)".
  • Hide all value labels: right-click, "Hide measurement labels". The values stay in the list and in the info window.
  • The hover box can be turned off in Settings: "Measurement value in a box by the pointer on hover".

docs.title: Measurement style: color, line width, font
docs.text:
The style block on the top toolbar: seven quick colors (red, blue, green, orange, black, yellow, purple), the palette square, line width and font in points with sliders, opacity. One slider movement equals one Ctrl+Z step.

  • While nothing is selected, the block sets the style of new measurements ("Measure: style of new measurements").
  • If a measurement is selected, it changes.
  • Defaults: line width 4, font 14, opacity 70 %.
  • Color: each new takeoff gets a random color not yet on this sheet, as in OurPlanCore (not gray, black or white). The color shows in the preview and in the style block before the click; a color picked in the block goes to the next measurement. Space, Beam and Openings take the color of their takeoff. To turn it off: Settings, "A new measurement gets a random color", then all new measurements are orange #D9480F (or the measurement color from Settings).
  • The palette square opens any color: a grid, "OurPDF colours", a #RRGGBB box and the "More colours" button (the Windows color picker). Every color in Settings has the same square.
  • The Set default button: select a finished measurement and press it, new measurements will have the same color, line width, font and opacity. The circular-arrow button next to it restores the factory style of new objects.

The palette square: a color grid, OurPDF colors, a #RRGGBB box and the Windows color picker.

Measurements are drawn as in Acrobat: circles at the ends and bends of lines, ticks on a dimension. Arrows and other ends: Line ends.

docs.title: Line ends: arrows, ticks, dots
docs.text: The ends of lines and dimensions can be changed: for example, arrows, as in Acrobat. It is one setting for the whole app, in the Settings window.

docs.title: Where to change it
docs.text:
1. Open Settings: Ctrl+, or the Edit menu, Settings….
  2. Scroll to the "Line ends, Beam, Openings, Merge" section. It comes right after the "Measure and comments" section.
  3. Pick a style in the row you need:
Row in Settings What it changes Default Line ends (L, perimeter) both ends of lines and perimeters (L) dot Line: dots at the bends dots at every bend of a line, not only at the ends on Dimension ends (R) both ends of a dimension (R), and also Beam and Openings dimensions tick End size, % (25-400) size of the end symbols, 100 = normal size 100

End styles: dot, arrow, as in Acrobat, closed arrow, tick, square, diamond, no ends.

  1. Click Save. All measurements on the sheet, old and new, are redrawn with the new ends right away.

The "Line ends, Beam, Openings, Merge" section in Settings. Here "arrow, as in Acrobat" is picked for lines and dimensions. The reset button is at the bottom of the section.

To restore: in the same section, the Reset line ends, Beam, Openings, Merge button, then Save. The button restores the factory values of the whole section, including the Beam, Openings and Merge settings.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Where it is viewed What shows OurPDF on this computer the chosen ends on all lines and dimensions The PDF after Ctrl+S or "Save As", opened in Acrobat or Bluebeam ends as before: circles on lines, ticks on dimensions OurPDF on another computer the ends chosen in that computer's Settings As before and as set by default: ticks on the dimension (blue), dots at the ends of the corridor line (orange). The same sheet after picking "arrow, as in Acrobat" for the line and the dimension. The values did not change, only the look of the ends did.
  • The setting changes only the look on the OurPDF screen; the PDF gets the old look. This is on purpose: a file sent to the client looks the same as before.
  • Measurement values, the legend and Excel do not depend on the end style.
  • The setting is stored in %APPDATA%\OurPDF\settings.json (section measure_tools, key line_ends). You do not need to edit this file by hand, everything is changed in the Settings window.

docs.title: Editing finished measurements
docs.text:
A selected area: the white squares are its points; the edge under the cursor is highlighted orange and can be dragged. Next to it, the hover box: SF and perimeter.
  1. Turn on Select (V, the normal mode the app opens in).
  2. Click a measurement: it is selected, the line gets thicker, its points show as white squares, with an orange frame with handles around it (Rotate and resize). Ctrl and click adds to the selection. A click on empty space moves the sheet.
  3. What a click will take highlights under the cursor: the whole measurement, or for a selected one its edge (orange) or a point.
  4. Edit:
What to drag What happens a point the value recalculates, the point snaps to drawing lines an edge both points of the edge follow the mouse, the adjacent edges stretch; Shift - strictly horizontal or vertical the whole measurement drag from inside the area or with Alt

Also:

  • Del with no points selected deletes the whole measurement.
  • Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy and paste measurements and comments; on another sheet they are pasted in the same spot.
  • Arrow keys move the selection.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes. The Edit menu shows which action will be undone.

Area UNIT 102 and the corridor line are selected: thicker lines, white squares on the points, a blue dashed frame around each, an orange frame with handles outside.

docs.title: Rotate, scale and Mirror
docs.text:
The bottom row of the style block and the orange frame around the selection.

Select one or several measurements. Works only with measurements: line, area, joists, Count. A group rotates and mirrors around a common center.

What How Rot from -180° to 180°, with the slider or by typing the angle; Shift while moving the slider: 15° steps Scale from 0.25x to 3x; you can type 1.25x or 125% and Enter. The sheet scale does not change, lengths and areas are recalculated Mirror horizontal and vertical. Cutouts, joist direction and extra joists follow the measurement reset button Rot 0 and Scale 1 for the next change, the resulting shape is kept the orange frame on the sheet corners: proportional resize; sides: width or height (Shift keeps proportions); round handle: rotate (Shift 15°); drag the border: move

Until you release the mouse you see a preview, Esc cancels it; after release Ctrl+Z reverts it in one step. The frame is turned off in Settings: "Measurement rotation and resize handles".

docs.title: Delete a point or an edge
docs.text:
Area UNIT 108 is selected, a click on the inside corner selected that point (orange). Del removes only it, the adjacent edges join directly.
  1. Select the measurement (V, click).
  2. Click one of its points: it turns orange. A click on an edge selects both its points.
  3. Ctrl and click adds more points or edges.
  4. Press Del: the selected points are deleted, not the whole measurement. The neighboring points join directly.
  5. Esc clears the point selection, Ctrl+Z brings back what was deleted.

The same via right-click on a point or edge: "Delete point", "Delete edge (its two points)", "Delete selected points (N)".

Limits: an area keeps at least 3 points, a line 2. Cutout points can be deleted too; deleting all points of a cutout removes the cutout itself.

docs.title: Frame selection (E)
docs.text:
The E key: a frame over empty space. Left to right selects what is wholly inside; right to left everything the frame touches (as in OurPlanCore).
  1. Press E: frame selection turns on.
  2. Drag a frame over empty space:
    • left to right selects what is wholly inside;
    • right to left selects everything the frame touches.
  3. Ctrl with a frame adds to the selection. A click on empty space clears the selection.
  4. Then Del deletes, dragging moves, Ctrl+C copies.
  5. V returns to regular selection, where empty space moves the sheet.

The middle and right mouse buttons always move the sheet, in any mode.

docs.title: Legend
docs.text:
Its own tab in the right panel: the icon with green rows, the top one on the right strip. The panel shows either the legend or the takeoffs. F5 collapses the panel.

A click on the Corridor row selected the line on the sheet; the Stair bay row is hidden, the stair area left the sheet, the value stayed and dimmed.

Type icon in the takeoff color, name, total.

What each action does to a row.

docs.title: What is in a row
docs.text:
• One row is one takeoff type, color and name. The scope is picked at the top: Current sheet or Entire PDF.
  • Type icon, as in OurPlanCore: a thick line with dots for distance and line, a rounded square for area, the same with joists for joists, a dot for Count.
  • Numbers, as in the OurPlanCore sheet legend: ft for lines, sf for areas and joists, ea for pieces and regular comments. Without a scale the row shows the number of segments or points. In Settings, "Numbers in the legend", you can turn on measurement units (ft-in and others).
  • Each measurement is counted at its own scale if it has one, otherwise at the sheet scale. Measurements without a scale are not added to physical lengths and areas, they are listed separately.
  • The drawing's own content, OurPlanCore snapshot takeoffs and crops are not part of the legend.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
Action What happens click a row selects its measurements on the sheet, a second click clears them. A measurement selected on the sheet also highlights its row Ctrl and click adds to or removes from the selection click the icon hides or shows the takeoff in the legend scope; the icon dims, for a partly hidden takeoff it is half light the dot at the top right hides or shows everything in the legend scope; filled while everything is shown double-click rename: type the name, Enter. A click outside the box also saves, Esc cancels, an empty name restores the default. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+S writes the name into the PDF right-click Rename, Hide or Show, Only this row, Show all

If the measurements are on another sheet (the "Entire PDF" scope), a click goes to it; if they are off screen, the view moves, the zoom does not change.

docs.title: What "hidden" means
docs.text:
Hidden means removed from the screen, nothing more. It is not a Ctrl+Z step and not an unsaved change, the markup itself in the PDF is not rewritten.

Where What happens to a hidden measurement on the sheet not visible, not selectable, snapping does not catch it and cuts do not cut it. Right-click on the sheet: "Show hidden measurements" in the legend the row stays, the value is dimmed and is included in the total Excel button, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+T not included in a legend-scope export; the status bar says how many were left out Excel link included in the number: hiding writes nothing to the cell "Save As", burned into the sheet not burned in Ctrl+S, "Save As" with editable markups stays in the file; visibility is remembered in the profile and carries over to the new version of the file printing not printed, same as on screen

If you answer "No" when closing the file, the visibility set after the last save is restored together with the draft.

docs.title: Keep on sheet
docs.text:
The checkbox is on, the right panel is closed: the legend sits in the corner of the sheet.

The "Keep on sheet" checkbox at the bottom of the "Legend" tab. The legend stays in the corner of the sheet as a white semi-transparent panel with black text, as in OurPlanCore, in any tool. The corner is picked from a list above the checkbox, bottom left by default. Icons, the dot, clicks and the menu work there the same way as in the tab. It is an on-screen panel: it is not added to the sheet on save or print.

docs.title: Excel: paste into an open workbook
docs.text:
Lock open, an area selected: the style block came in with the Auto Link, "Link to Excel" and Excel buttons, the J2 toggle and the format circle. With the lock closed, the button sits in the "Scale" block.
  1. Open the Excel workbook and select the cell where the paste should start.
  2. Go back to OurPDF and select the measurements you need. With no selection, the legend scope is exported: the current sheet or the entire PDF, without hidden items.
  3. Press the Excel button, Ctrl+E or Ctrl+T. Save the workbook in Excel: OurPDF does not save or close it.
Command What is written Ctrl+E one column: the number Ctrl+T three columns: name or color, number, unit Excel button the format is set by the circle on the right: off - numbers, on - three columns joists, in any mode exactly two columns: count and length, identical lengths are merged

J2 (blue means on): a length up to 8 feet inclusive rounds up to the whole foot, longer than 8 feet up to the even foot. Only on export, the geometry does not change. Off by default.

The export overwrites the values in the target cells: check the cell and the free space. No open workbook, protected or merged cells, a read-only workbook: the paste fails, and the status bar says why.

To keep a legend row number in a cell and have it update by itself: Excel link. The whole DFL in one click: Auto Link.

docs.title: Measurement list and a separate Excel file
docs.text:
The "Comments" tab: all measurements and markups with their values. At the top, a summary: how many measurements, how many from the PDF and what is not yet written to the file. At the bottom, the Delete, Measurements to Excel..., Save as PDF... buttons.
  1. Open the "Comments" tab on the right strip.
  2. At the top, a summary: "N in all, N of them measurements, N from the PDF; not in the file: new, edited, deleted. Ctrl+S writes into this PDF".
  3. Each row: page, type, author, time, label and value. A click on a row shows the measurement on the sheet.
  4. "Measurements to Excel..." saves the workbook <PDF name> - measurements.xlsx, worksheet "Measurements", one row per measurement.

Excel columns: Sheet, Page, Type, Value, Unit, Label, Caption, Scale, Scale source, Points, Author, Created.

The same from the menu: File > Export measurement markup to Excel, right-click with the ruler on, or Export PDF > Measurements to Excel on the right strip. If there are no measurements, the status bar suggests enabling measurement markup and measuring something.

docs.title: Right-click menu
docs.text:
With the ruler on (the Measure tool):

Item What it does Complete measurement, Cancel measurement while a measurement is being drawn Direction along the longest side, Cancel joists at the joist direction step Change scale and precision the "Scale and precision" window Change markup label the label of the selected measurement Show hidden measurements (N) when there are items hidden in the legend Enable / Disable measurement markup off: only the last measurement stays on the sheet and it is not saved Enable / Disable ortho like F8 Box: by two corners of a rectangle like F9 Hide / Show measurement labels on the sheet values on the sheet Line lengths only on hover (LF) or always on the sheet Cut from area like X Hide / Show rulers rulers along the sheet edges Snap to page content snapping on and off as a whole Snap to OurPDF objects and measurements (F3) snapping to measurements, like F3 Snap to PDF lines (Ctrl+F3) snapping to drawing lines, like Ctrl+F3 Export measurement markup to Excel like the "Measurements to Excel" button Preferences the Settings window Hide measurement info window, Hide the "Measure" toolbar the info on the bottom bar and the second toolbar row (same as the lock)

On a selected measurement (the Select tool): delete the point or edge under the cursor, cut from area, edit text, delete, undo, hide measurement labels, write markups into this PDF.

At the bottom of any right-click menu: zoom 25 % - 400 %, "Actual size" (100 % = sheet size, as in Acrobat), fit page, fit width, fit content.

docs.title: Measurements from Acrobat, Bluebeam and other apps
docs.text:
• Markups already in the PDF become OurPDF markups on open: Acrobat, Bluebeam, Nitro measurements at their scale, pencil, text and callouts, shapes, clouds, polylines. You can select, move, edit and delete them; the values are recalculated and match what that app showed.
  • A measurement made at a different scale on the same sheet keeps its scale.
  • Strikeouts, stamps, links, replies and hidden annotations stay as the PDF draws them. Exception: the OurPDF crop stamp (Crop).
  • To turn off importing: Settings, "Accept markups from the PDF on open".
  • After Ctrl+S, Acrobat redraws measurements from their properties by itself, so OurPDF writes them so that our look shows there too: color, line width, opacity, dots at the ends, area without a solid fill. Measurements written earlier the old way (the area in Acrobat was filled solid) are rewritten in the new form on the next Ctrl+S of that file.
  • Area cutouts are saved in the file and come back into OurPDF; in Acrobat the area shows as an outline.

docs.title: If something is wrong
docs.text: What you see Why and what to do values in inches "on paper" the sheet has no scale: set it (Scale) the dimension does not match the dimension string wrong scale or the sheet was printed not to scale: calibrate on a known dimension the cursor does not snap to a line a snap type or all snapping is off ("Snap to page content"), or the line is on a hidden layer Tab takes nothing a point is already placed: Tab works before the first point; or the cursor is not on a drawing line (scans have no lines) a line shows no length line lengths show on hover; you can always label them in Settings the cut cut the wrong area with no selection, all areas under the cut are cut: select the ones you need first, Ctrl+Z undoes the whole cut Del deleted the whole measurement no points were selected: click a point or edge first measurements are not visible in Acrobat or in print they are still in the OurPDF profile: press Ctrl+S (Saving) not all measurements in Excel with no selection, the legend scope goes out without hidden items: check the scope and the icons the blocks are not visible the lock is open: press the ruler or close the lock (Lock)

docs.title: Sheet overlay
docs.text:
Another sheet lies over the current one as a colored semi-transparent layer: the paper disappears, the lines become colored. This is how you compare revisions, floors, or a plan against an elevation. One sheet can have several layers. Here, step by step: add a layer, align it with the sheet, what is saved and what is not.

The "Overlay" icon on the left strip. Sheet 1 lies over sheet 2, shifted on purpose: red lines and the orange frame of the active layer.

The usual order of working with a layer.

What an overlay does not do

Ctrl+S does not write the overlay into the PDF, and it does not print. Layers live in the app profile on this computer. They get into a file only through "Save As", the burn-into-sheet option (below).

docs.title: Add a layer
docs.text:
1. Open the sheet you want to put another one over.
  2. Click the "Overlay" icon on the left strip.
  3. Add..., then one of two:
    • Page of this PDF: pick the sheet in the window;
    • Page of another PDF: pick the file, then the page. The file opens read-only.
  4. The layer lands on the sheet in red, at its original position and scale. Next you need to align it.

The same, faster: right-click a sheet in the "Sheets" list or a thumbnail.

Menu item What it does Use as Overlay changes the source of the active layer to this sheet Add as Overlay puts a new layer on the open sheet Overlay Properties... opens the panel with the sheet's layers Clear Current Sheet Overlay removes the active layer Batch Overlay... batch window

A sheet cannot lie on itself: the app tells you to pick another one. While a layer uses a file of another PDF, another app cannot overwrite that file, as with any PDF open in OurPDF.

docs.title: What is in the panel
docs.text:
Sheet layers, buttons, alignment, color and opacity. What How it works Layers of this sheet the top one in the list is drawn over the rest. The checkbox shows and hides a layer, on the right the scale and opacity or "hidden". The selected row is the active layer; a click on the sheet does not select a layer Choose or Replace... another source for the selected layer, the position is kept Open Source goes to the source sheet or opens the other file Remove, up and down arrows removes the layer, changes the order. Same via right-click on the layer row Reciprocal layer below, off by default X, Y, Scale, Rotation the slider shows the change at once, the box takes a value on Enter. X and Y in sheet points, scale keeps the layer center Color six quick colors and the palette square. The first layer on a sheet is red, the next ones take a free color Opacity from 5 to 100 %, 100 % by default

Esc restores the saved position. Reset sets X and Y to 0, scale 1, rotation 0.

docs.title: Align the layer with the sheet
docs.text: Left, the layer is shifted; right, after Auto Fit: the walls line up, only the unit numbers differ.

docs.title: Auto Fit
docs.text:
1. Select the layer in the list.
  2. Press Auto Fit (or right-click the sheet, "Auto Fit Overlay").
  3. The app finds the position from the lines of both sheets, for scans from the image. The result and the confidence go to the status bar.
  4. On a sheet with few lines, the status bar says there are too few lines. Then align by points.

docs.title: Next Match
docs.text: Cycles through other pages of the source document (up to 160) by similarity and aligns right away; on a tie, nearer pages come first. The first press takes longer, after that the order is known. Use it when it is unclear which sheet would fit best.

docs.title: Edit by Points
docs.text:
1. Edit by Points (or right-click the sheet, "Fit by 2 Points").
  2. Click a point on the overlay, for example a building corner.
  3. Click where that point should land on the sheet: the layer moves.
  4. A second pair of points, farther from the first, sets the scale and rotation.
  5. Esc after the first pair finishes, the layer stays moved.

Points snap to the lines of both sheets.

docs.title: With the mouse: the frame
docs.text:
While the "Overlay" panel is open, the active layer has an orange frame on the sheet.

What to drag What happens inside the frame moves the layer a square corner scales around the center the round handle above the top edge rotates around the center

The panel shows the values as you go, releasing saves, Esc during the move reverts.

  • The frame takes presses only in the Select and Hand tools. With the ruler or a comment tool, clicks stay with the tool and the frame is drawn without handles, so you can measure over the layer.
  • Pressing a measurement or comment over the layer selects it rather than moving the layer. Handles of a selected markup win over the frame.
  • While the panel is open, a left click on empty space inside the frame moves the layer, not the sheet. The wheel and the middle and right buttons move the sheet as usual.
  • Panel closed: no frame.

docs.title: Without the panel: Ctrl+Alt
docs.text:
Action How With Shift move with the mouse Ctrl+Alt and drag inside the layer 4 times finer nudge Ctrl+Alt and arrows, 6 pt 1 pt scale Ctrl+Alt++ or Ctrl+Alt+-, x1.05 x1.01 rotate Ctrl+Alt and [ or ], 1 degree 0.25 degree reset position Ctrl+Alt+0

The keys can be reassigned in Settings, like any others (Keyboard shortcuts).

docs.title: Undo
docs.text:
Ctrl+Z undoes the layer position interleaved with measurements: one move, a slider release, a key press, Reset, Auto Fit or a point-fit step equals one step. Ctrl+Y redoes.

  • Source, color, opacity and layer order have no undo.
  • The history works like that of measurements: Ctrl+S and page edits start a new one.
  • An overlay does not count as an unsaved change: it adds no asterisk to the tab and no question on close.

docs.title: Reciprocal layer
docs.text:
The checkbox "Reciprocal layer on the source sheet" in the panel and in Settings, off by default (the same in OurPlanCore now).

  • On: a layer of sheet B on sheet A gives sheet B a layer of sheet A with the reverse position, same color, opacity and visibility.
  • An edit on one sheet goes to the other. Remove removes both.
  • Works only between pages of the same PDF.
  • A sheet that already has other layers is not touched; the status bar says so.

docs.title: Batch Overlay
docs.text:
All sheets on the left, "target sheet" and "overlay sheet" pairs on the right.

Many sheets at once, for example a whole revision over the old plan set.

  1. The Batch... button in the panel, Edit > Batch Overlay... or right-click a sheet.
  2. Select sheets on the left, Add as targets: one row per sheet.
  3. Select one sheet on the left, select rows on the right, Use as overlay. Each row also has its own lists.
  4. Add PDF... adds pages of another file; they can only be overlays, targets always come from the open PDF.
  5. Color and opacity are shared for the batch.
  6. Apply overlays. Before the first write, all pairs are checked: a sheet on itself or an empty row stops the whole batch. Repeated and already existing pairs are skipped and counted.
  7. The layers land at their original position and scale, then align them as usual.

Undo last batch restores the layers exactly as they were; if the layers changed after the batch, it refuses. A new file version (Ctrl+S) or closing the file ends this undo.

docs.title: How it shows on thumbnails
docs.text: Thumbnails have small colored squares: one per layer, pale means hidden.

docs.title: What is saved and what is not
docs.text:
Where What happens to the layers app profile position, color and order are in %APPDATA%\OurPDF\overlays, separately for each file. On another computer there will be no layers Ctrl+S not written to the PDF "Save As", editable comments not included in the copy "Save As", burned into the sheet visible layers are burned in under the markups; such a copy opens without layers, so they are not drawn twice printing not printed. Need them on paper: do "Save As" with burn-in and print that file page edits layers rotate with their page and follow the source page. If the source is deleted, the row says "(source removed)": replace the source or remove the layer

Layers are drawn over the drawing and under crops, measurements and comments. Measurement snapping does not catch them. Works in continuous scroll and in separate view windows.

docs.title: If something is wrong
docs.text: What you see Why and what to do no frame the "Overlay" panel is closed, the layer is hidden or has no source a frame without handles a measure or comment tool is on: press V or H a click on the sheet does not select another layer that is by design: the active layer is picked in the panel list Auto Fit says there are too few lines align by points the layer did not print overlays do not print: "Save As" with burn-in "(source removed)" the source page was deleted by a page edit: Choose or Replace... or Remove

docs.title: Pages, PDF editing, layers, search
docs.text:
Here: how to reorder, rotate, delete and extract pages, edit sheet content, turn PDF layers on and off, search text and open OurPlanCore projects and snapshots. Everything that changes the PDF itself goes into a modified copy: the source file is not touched until you save. Another sheet over this one: Sheet overlay. A detail onto another sheet and new sheets: Crop to sheet.

The "Pages" tab: thumbnails and buttons to rotate, delete, insert, extract, duplicate, crop and move. The hint above the thumbnails: Ctrl or Shift selects several pages, dragging changes the order.

docs.title: Modified copy: the general rule
docs.text:
• Editing pages and content goes into a modified copy: the source PDF does not change until you save, and the tab gets a *.
  • Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y - steps back and forward.
  • Comments, measurements, crops and overlays move together with their pages. Markups accepted from the PDF too; deleted ones stay deleted.
  • Ctrl+S writes the modified copy into the source file under the same name: it checks the result and that the original has not changed, and puts a copy of the previous file into backups. The setting "Ctrl+S after editing pages or content" switches it to a new file. "Save As" writes a new file. When you close such a tab, the app asks whether to save it.
  • Bookmarks and page labels are not carried into the modified copy; layers are not kept after page edits (rotate, delete and so on).
  • An OurPlanCore project snapshot becomes a regular PDF after page edits (the app warns you), the original snapshot stays as it was.

docs.title: The "Pages" tab on the left
docs.text:
Narrow thumbnails and buttons above them:

Button What it does rotate counterclockwise and clockwise rotates the selected pages (changes the pages, not the view) delete deletes the selected pages (Del) insert inserts pages from a file after the selected one extract the selected pages to a new PDF, with comments duplicate copies the selected pages crop drag a frame over the sheet up, down moves the selected pages
  • Ctrl and Shift select several pages, dragging changes the order.
  • Pages can be dragged out with the mouse into a folder, and PDFs from a folder can be dropped into the list, as in the "Organize Pages" grid.
  • Pages can also be cropped from the menu: Edit > Crop pages.

docs.title: Organize Pages
docs.text:
Like "Organize Pages" in Acrobat: a grid of pages instead of the sheet.

  1. Open the pink "Organize Pages" icon on the right strip or Edit > Organize Pages.
  2. It has its own toolbar at the top: left, right, delete, insert, extract, duplicate, undo, redo, a size slider (or Ctrl and the wheel).
  3. Select pages: click, Ctrl, Shift, a mouse frame, Ctrl+A. On hover a page shows rotate and delete buttons.
  4. Drag pages to change the order: a blue bar shows where they will go.
  5. Double-click or Enter opens a page, Esc or "Close" returns to the sheet.

Exchanging pages with folders:

  • Drag the selected pages to the desktop or a folder: a Name (pp. 3-5).pdf appears there with these pages and their comments.
  • A PDF from a folder dropped into the grid is inserted where you dropped it.
  • The same works between two OurPDF windows.

docs.title: Edit PDF: sheet content
docs.text: Edits the drawing itself: text, lines, images. Turned on with the orange "Edit PDF" icon on the right strip or Edit > Edit PDF content. A strip appears above the sheet: Select, Text, Image, Delete in frame, White-out, Select all, Delete, Close. Its right side says what is selected.

docs.title: Select and move
docs.text:
1. Select mode: a click takes one object (text, line, image, block).
  2. A frame left to right takes everything wholly inside (blue); right to left everything it touches (green dashed, as in AutoCAD).
  3. Ctrl or Shift add to the selection, Ctrl and click removes, Ctrl+A - the whole sheet, Esc - clear the selection. The selection is outlined in pink.
  4. Move by dragging or with the arrow keys: 1 pt steps, with Shift 10 pt. Consecutive arrow presses are one edit (one Ctrl+Z).
  5. Del deletes the selection.

docs.title: Fix text on the sheet
docs.text:
1. Double-click the text (or Enter if one text item is selected).
  2. A box appears over it with the same font, size and slant.
  3. Enter writes, Esc cancels, empty text deletes the item.

If the embedded font lacks a typed character, the text is set in an installed font of the same family (Arial, Trebuchet MS, Calibri), and if there is none, in the fallback font from Settings.

docs.title: Add and remove
docs.text:
Mode How Text click on the sheet and type: new text in the sheet itself Image pick a file, drag a frame (proportions kept) or click: width from Settings Delete in frame everything wholly inside the frame is deleted White-out the frame is covered with a solid fill, white by default

Added text, an image and a fill become one small block over the sheet: it can be moved or deleted as a whole. Fixed text that could not be rewritten in place also becomes such a block. Blocks (forms) move and delete as a whole; objects inside a shared form cannot be edited one by one.

docs.title: How edits are saved
docs.text:
• An edit changes only its own operators in the sheet, everything else stays byte for byte.
  • After each edit the sheet is re-read and checked. If anything changed beyond what was intended, the edit is undone, the document stays as it was, and the reason goes to the status bar.
  • The app redraws a whole sheet only when there is no other way, with the same check. On CAD drawings this can be lossy, and then the edit is not made.
  • Same as with pages: the source PDF does not change until you save, edits go into the modified copy, Ctrl+S writes into the source file.

Settings, section "Edit PDF": arrow steps and the pause between presses, fonts, colors of new text and fill, right-to-left frame, image size (Settings).

docs.title: PDF layers
docs.text:
Like "Layers" in Acrobat. The stack-of-sheets icon on the left strip or the "PDF layers" command.

  • The list mirrors the PDF's own layer tree; in merged plan sets the layers are grouped by source file.
  • The eye on a row shows and hides the layer, the eye on a group all its layers. Layers locked in the PDF (padlock) cannot be toggled; in a radio group, turning a layer on turns its neighbors off.
  • Buttons at the top: show all, hide all (what is in the list right now: the name filter and "Only layers of this page" narrow it), restore as in the file.
  • The layer selected in the list is highlighted on the sheet in crimson (a group, all its layers) and stays highlighted when you go to another page. Esc clears the selection and the highlight.
  • Row menu: show only this layer, hide or show all layers with the same name on all sheets, highlight the layer on the sheet.

docs.title: Which layer
docs.text:
1. Press the crosshair button "Which layer".
  2. Click a line or text on the sheet.
  3. The panel selects the layer, and everything it draws is highlighted on the sheet. Esc - exit.

What matters:

  • Visibility is remembered for this file in the OurPDF profile and comes back at the next opening; the PDF itself does not change.
  • Hidden layers are not printed, do not show in thumbnails, and measurement snapping does not catch them.
  • "Save As" without editing (flatten) turns hidden layers off in the new PDF; with editable comments it keeps the visibility set in the file.
  • In an encrypted PDF, layers are only shown and cannot be toggled.

docs.title: Trace a layer as an area or a line
docs.text:
A fast way to take the area of a hatch (stone base, siding, roofing) or its outline, if the hatch sits on its own PDF layer.

  1. The "Layers" tab on the left, pick the layer in the list: it highlights on the sheet.
  2. The "Trace layer as areas" button: each separate zone of the layer on this sheet (for example, each hatched elevation wall) becomes its own area, windows inside are subtracted as cutouts.
  3. Or the "Trace layer as lines" button: the outline of each zone becomes a line in LF.
  4. Check the result on the sheet and in the "Comments" list; one Ctrl+Z removes the whole trace.

The hatch merges into a solid zone if its lines are closer than the gap from Settings ("Trace layer: merge hatch lines with gaps up to", 6 pt by default). If the layer broke into many small zones, increase the gap; if neighboring walls stuck together into one, decrease it.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
1. Ctrl+F or the magnifier button: the "Search" tab opens on the left.
  2. Type the text. PDF text and the names of sheets, takeoffs and measurements are searched.
  3. Enter - next, Shift+F3 (in the box Shift+Enter) - previous. Since version 1.0, F3 turns snapping to measurements on and off, as in OurPlanCore.
  4. Checkboxes: match case, whole word.

The app does not OCR scans without a text layer; their number is written in the search results.

docs.title: Sheets, bookmarks, attachments, properties
docs.text:
• Sheets (left): page tree with sheet names and a name filter.
  • Bookmarks (left): the PDF table of contents.
  • Attachments (left, or the icon on the right strip): files inside the PDF, a button to save the selected one to a file. Attachments are never launched.
  • Properties (right): document and sheet information.

docs.title: OurPlanCore projects and snapshots
docs.text: OurPDF shows OurPlanCore data view only: the project itself does not change, takeoffs are edited only in OurPlanCore.

docs.title: Open an .ourplan project
docs.text:
• Open, drag the file into the window, or "Open with" OurPDF.
  • The project opens in a Name.ourplan tab, view only: sheets, takeoffs, measurements with quantities, joists, annotations, sheet overlays.
  • The first opening builds the view (a large project takes up to a minute), the next one is instant until the project is saved again.

docs.title: Make a project snapshot
docs.text:
A snapshot (formerly called a "shadow") is a light PDF with the data of a saved project.

  1. Press "Project snapshot from .ourplan" on the right of the toolbar (also in the File menu and on the right strip).
  2. Pick a saved project.
  3. Pick where to save it. By default Documents\OurPDF\Снимки (the folder name is Russian), outside the jobs folder.
  4. The project does not change.

docs.title: Work with a snapshot
docs.text:
• On the right, the takeoff tree with quantities, a name filter and the "This sheet only" checkbox.
  • A click on a takeoff highlights its measurements on the sheet and its row in the legend.
  • The "Select" tool picks a measurement with a click on the sheet or on a legend row. A click on a measurement on the sheet opens the takeoff tree on the right, expands its folders and shows the takeoff. Folders you expanded stay expanded when you pick another takeoff.
  • Live measurements (the button on the right of the toolbar):
    • on: OurPDF draws the measurements from the data itself, only on sheets with a verified binding; OurPlanCore lines in the live layer also show LF on hover;
    • off: the view saved in the PDF is shown.
  • Whether live measurements are on by default: Settings, "OurPlanCore project snapshots: live measurements by default".
  • Any other app (Acrobat and so on) shows a snapshot as a regular PDF with an "OurPlanCore Measurements" layer.
  • You can put your own OurPDF markups over a snapshot, but Ctrl+S does not write into a snapshot: save with "Save As".

docs.text:
Here: all OurPDF 1.0.0 keys with their default assignments, by group; mouse and modifiers; how the keys differ from OurPlanCore; how to reassign them. "None" in the key column means the command has no default key; you can assign one in Settings.

A key does not work while the focus is in a text box: the letter is typed there. Click the sheet and the keys work again.

In the app itself, F1 opens a panel with all active keys, a second F1 or Esc closes it.
