docs.text: What Action middle or right button, drag move the sheet in any tool wheel scroll; in single-page view turns pages Ctrl and wheel zoom right button (click) menu: with the ruler on, the measure menu; on a measurement, its actions; at the bottom, zoom levels double-click finish a line or area; on a finished measurement - label; on a joists area - its settings; on text - edit Ctrl and click add a measurement, comment, point or edge to the selection Ctrl and a frame (E) add to the selection Shift while drawing Ortho for a moment (with Ortho on, frees the line instead) Shift while dragging an edge strictly horizontal or vertical Alt and drag move the whole measurement Shift and click in extra joists mode remove the nearest extra click the icon of a legend row hide or show the takeoff toolbar block handle, drag move the block; right-click the handle: reset toolbar Shift while drawing a shape straight: square, circle, 45 degrees Ctrl+Enter finish text on the sheet

docs.title: Differences from OurPlanCore
docs.text:
The measurement keys are the same: R, L, A, J, X, C, B, O, Ctrl+M, Ctrl+Shift+M, F3, Ctrl+F3, F8, F9, D, P, Space, Ctrl+Shift+B, Tab, Backspace, Esc, F1, the overlay keys with Ctrl+Alt. The rest differ:

Key OurPDF OurPlanCore V Select Pan E Frame selection Select H Hand hide the takeoff of the selection Ctrl+Y Redo no Redo F4, F5 left and right panels Set Scale, Name / Scale Setup F none (fit page on Ctrl+0) Fit: whole sheet

The full OurPlanCore table: OurPlanCore keyboard shortcuts.

docs.title: Assign or change a key
docs.text:
1. Open Settings: Ctrl+, or Help > Keyboard shortcuts and settings.
  2. Scroll down to the section "Keyboard shortcuts (empty = default, None = off)". Each row has the command, its default key and a box.
  3. Type the combination in the box as text: Ctrl+Shift+F, F3, PageDown. Several combinations separated by commas: V, E.
  4. An empty box keeps the default key, None turns the command off.
  5. If two actions got the same combination, "Shortcut conflict" appears under the table with their list.
  6. Click "Save". The app does not accept a combination it cannot read and shows an example.

Key names are in English, as in the default column: the digit 6 is D6 (Ctrl+D6), plus and minus are OemPlus and OemMinus, comma is Oemcomma, Backspace is Back, Esc is Escape. "Reset to defaults" at the bottom of the window restores all keys (and the other settings) to defaults.

docs.title: View and settings
docs.text:
Here: how to view a sheet (scroll modes, zoom, rotation, full screen) and what is in the Settings window, section by section.

The Settings window, measurement section: line lengths, Excel, numbers in the legend, legend on the sheet, rotation and resize handles, value box, guide lines, both sides of rectangles, AI agent bridge. At the bottom, "Reset to defaults", "Save", "Cancel".

docs.title: View modes
docs.text:
The view button with an arrow on the toolbar (as in Acrobat):

Mode Key What the wheel does Continuous scrolling, fit width Ctrl+3 all sheets as a strip; the wheel scrolls, Ctrl and wheel zooms Single page Ctrl+1 one sheet at a time, as in Acrobat: the wheel turns pages (a zoomed-in sheet scrolls to its edge first), Ctrl and wheel zooms Reading mode Ctrl+H hides the panels Full screen mode Ctrl+L exit with Esc

The old "wheel zooms" behavior in single-page view is turned on in Settings: "Mouse wheel in single-page view" = "zoom".

docs.title: Zoom and rotation
docs.text:
• Fit page Ctrl+0, fit width Ctrl+2.
  • Zoom in and out: Ctrl++, Ctrl+-, the buttons and the percent zoom box on the toolbar.
  • Right-click the sheet: zoom 25 % - 400 %, "Actual size" (100 % = the real sheet size, as in Acrobat), fit page, fit width, fit content.
  • The wheel step is set in Settings: "Wheel zoom factor per notch", from 1.05 to 4, as in OurPlanCore 2.
  • Rotate the view: Ctrl+R clockwise, Ctrl+Shift+R counterclockwise. The PDF itself does not rotate; pages in the file can be rotated in the "Pages" tab (Pages).

docs.title: Move the sheet and turn pages
docs.text:
• Move the sheet: the "Hand" tool (H), the middle or right mouse button (in any tool), empty space in "Select" mode (V).
  • Turn pages: Page Up, Page Down; first and last page Home, End.
  • Go to a page: Ctrl+G or the page number box on the toolbar; you can type a page number or label.
  • Rulers along the sheet edges: Ctrl+Alt+R or View > Show rulers.
  • A separate view window of the same document: Ctrl+Shift+N.
  • Left and right panels: F4, F5 or the arrows on the sheet edges.

docs.title: Settings window
docs.text:
Open it: Ctrl+,, the gear button on the right of the toolbar or Edit > Settings. Sections from top to bottom:

Section What is set Язык интерфейса / Interface language Русский (Russian) or English; the new language takes effect after a restart, OurPDF offers to restart right away and reopens the same files Appearance as in Windows, light or dark; applied after a restart Memory and rendering rendered page cache (MB), thumbnail cache, thumbnail width, page overview (long side in px), detailed render of the visible area (MP), neighboring pages in advance, open PDFium pages per document General wheel zoom step (as in OurPlanCore: 2), number of recent files, show PDF annotations (comments, stamps), live measurements of OurPlanCore snapshots by default, offer at start-up to make OurPDF the default app Measure and comments see the table below Markups in the PDF itself (Ctrl+S) accept markups from the PDF on open (Acrobat and Bluebeam measurements, pencil, text become editable), Ctrl+S after editing pages or content: save the original PDF under the same name, backups per file before Ctrl+S (1-50), the backup folder path and how much is there now, the "Open backup folder" button Link to Excel behaviour open workbook at once, closed one on Ctrl+S, backups, delay, time limit, small-number threshold for Auto Link (Excel link) Sheet overlay color of the first layer on a sheet, opacity of a new layer, memory for overlay images, reciprocal layer, dashed frame and crop badge (Overlay, Crop) Blank sheets width and height of a new sheet, list of paper sizes (New sheets) Edit PDF arrow and Shift plus arrow nudge (pt), the pause within which arrow presses count as one edit (ms), fallback font, font, size and color of new text, "White-out" color, width of an image placed with a click, maximum image size, right-to-left frame also takes touched objects (as in AutoCAD) Keyboard shortcuts all commands in a list: the default key and a box for your own (Keyboard shortcuts)

docs.title: The "Measure and comments" section
docs.text:
Field Default What it changes Measurement units ft-in ft-in, ft, in, m, cm, mm Precision for ft-in: inch denominator 16 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 Decimal places 2 from 0 to 6 Snap radius, px 10 from 2 to 40 Measurements stay on the sheet as markup on off: only the last measurement on the sheet, and it is not saved Ortho by default off Shift inverts Box: area, line, cut and size by two corners off same as F9 Measurement value labels on the sheet on values on the sheet Line lengths (LF) on the sheet on hover or "always labelled" Excel button: values only on or three columns; same as the circle by the button Joists: round up to whole feet through 8, even feet above 8 off J2, export only Excel: decimal places 2 from 0 to 10 Numbers in the legend as in OurPlanCore (ft, sf, ea) or in the measurement units Keep legend on the sheet off same as the checkbox in the legend Measurement rotation and resize handles on the orange frame around the selection Legend: entire PDF off or the current sheet Measurement value in a box by the pointer on hover on a box as in Acrobat Guide lines through the pointer while measuring on lines as in OurPlanCore Rectangular measurements: show both sides on width x height under the value Mouse wheel in single-page view turns pages "turns pages (Ctrl zooms)" or "zoom" AI agent bridge on Claude and Codex agents drive the open OurPDF; takes effect after a restart (AI agent control) Measurement color #D9480F palette square next to it Comment color #E5262B Highlight color, note color #FFD400 Comment line width, pt 2 from 0.25 to 20 Text font size, pt 12 from 4 to 96 Comment author empty empty = the Windows user name

Line width, font and opacity of new measurements (4, 14, 70 %) are set in the style block of the top toolbar while nothing is selected (Measurement style). The top toolbar block layout is remembered by itself; to restore it: Window > Reset toolbar (Top toolbar). The lock: the button at the end of the first row.

docs.title: Buttons at the bottom
docs.text:
• Reset to defaults restores everything as designed.
  • Save applies. If a value is out of range, the app brings it into range and tells you what it changed.
  • Cancel closes without changes.

docs.title: Default PDF app
docs.text:
1. Help > Make OurPDF the default PDF app.
  2. OurPDF registers for PDF (for your user only) and opens Windows Settings.
  3. Click "Set default" there: Windows lets only the user do that.

When OurPDF is already the default, the menu item shows "OurPDF opens PDFs by default".

docs.title: The app window
docs.text:
Here: what is where in the OurPDF window, from the menu to the status bar. Use it to find a button fast; how to use it is covered on the Measurements, Comments and saving and Pages, editing, layers pages.

At the top, the menu, the demo-plan.pdf file tab and two toolbar rows. On the left, a narrow tab strip and the "Sheets" panel, the sheet in the middle, the tab and tool strip on the right, the status bar at the bottom.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text: Menu What is there File open, recent, save as (a new PDF with comments, the source does not change), export measurement markups to Excel, project snapshot from .ourplan, print, close document, exit Edit undo and redo (with the action name, for example "Undo: Markup properties"), delete comment, legend on the sheet, rotate and mirror measurements, continue takeoff, Count, Break, P Line, Ends, edit PDF content, organize pages, crop pages, overlay a sheet, batch overlays, crop to sheet, new blank sheet, new sheet from the visible area and from a frame, select and copy text, find, find next, settings View fit page, fit width, zoom in, zoom out, rotate view clockwise and counterclockwise, first, previous, next, last page, go to page, show or hide rulers, full screen Window new view window of the same document, "Reset toolbar", show or hide the left and right panels, open a specific panel tab ("Right: Comments", "Panel: Layers" and so on) Help keyboard shortcuts (F1), "How everything works" (the guide as a PDF), "For AI agents", keyboard shortcuts and settings, logs folder, default PDF app, about

docs.title: First toolbar row
docs.text:
Left to right:

Group Buttons File Open (Ctrl+O), Save As (Ctrl+Shift+S, a new PDF with markups), Print (Ctrl+P), Find (Ctrl+F) Pages previous and next page (Page Up, Page Down), the page number box: type a page number or label and Enter (Ctrl+G), the total page count next to it Select Select (V), Hand (H), select text with a frame (then Ctrl+C copies the text) Zoom zoom out, zoom in, zoom box in percent, view button with an arrow: continuous scroll, single page, reading mode Rotate rotate view counterclockwise and clockwise (Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+R); the PDF itself does not change Measure the ruler button: a toggle, pressing it again returns to "Select" (Measurements) Comments note (Ctrl+6), text on the sheet, highlight, freehand drawing, a shape with a picker arrow: rectangle, oval, cloud, arrow, line, polyline (Comments) Right Live measurements (for OurPlanCore snapshots), Project snapshot from .ourplan, separate view window (Ctrl+Shift+N), Settings (Ctrl+,), the second-row lock

Every button has a hover tooltip: what it does and which key.

docs.title: Left tabs
docs.text:
A narrow strip of icons at the left edge. A click opens the panel, a second click on the same icon collapses it.

Tab What is there Details Sheets page tree with sheet names, filter by name; a click opens the sheet Pages thumbnails; rotate selected pages, delete, insert from file, extract to a new PDF, duplicate, crop, move up and down. Ctrl and Shift select several, dragging changes the order Pages Bookmarks the PDF table of contents Search PDF text and sheet and takeoff names; Enter next, Shift+F3 back, match case, whole word Search Attachments files inside the PDF, a button to save the selected one; attachments are never launched Layers PDF layers, as in Acrobat: the eye shows and hides a layer, buttons "show all", "hide all", "as in the file", "which layer", filter, only this page's layers PDF layers Overlay another sheet over this one as a colored semi-transparent layer: layers, alignment, color Sheet overlay Crop a detail from one sheet onto another, the sheet's crops, new sheets Crop to sheet

docs.title: Right strip
docs.text:
Icons at the right edge, as in Acrobat. The top four open a panel on the right, the bottom ones turn on tools.

Button What it does Legend measurement totals by type, color and name: select, hide, rename, keep on the sheet (Legend) Takeoffs the takeoff tree of an OurPlanCore project snapshot with quantities, search by name, a "This sheet only" checkbox. The panel shows either the legend or the takeoffs. F5 collapses the panel Comments a list of all markups and measurements in the document with their values; buttons Delete, Measurements to Excel..., Save as PDF... (Measurement list) Properties document and sheet information Measure, Comment turn on tools, same as the buttons on the top toolbar Edit PDF move and delete sheet objects, edit and add text and images (Editing the PDF) Organize Pages a grid of pages: order, rotate, delete, insert, extract, drag pages into a folder (Pages) Export PDF a menu: PDF with comments (Save As), selected pages to a new PDF, measurements to Excel, Excel link, project snapshot from .ourplan Project snapshot project snapshot from .ourplan (OurPlanCore snapshots) Print Ctrl+P Attachments opens the "Attachments" tab on the left More tools a menu with all tools at once: measure, edit PDF, pages, note, Excel, save as, snapshot, rulers, new view window, print, attachments, settings

docs.title: Top toolbar: two rows of blocks
docs.text:
The floating measurement card is gone. Everything that belonged to it now sits in two rows under the menu, as blocks you can rearrange.

The layout as designed, a window about 1900 pixels wide. The first row holds the regular buttons and the "Measure" block; the second row has "Snap" and measurement style on the left, and "Scale" with the "Link to Excel" and Excel buttons on the right. If the window is not wide enough, the "Measure" block moves to the second row, "Snap" to the row below, and they come back when there is room.

What sits where and what the lock does.

docs.title: Four blocks
docs.text:
Measure: distance (R), Pitch, perimeter or line (L), area (A), joists (J), cut (X), Ortho (F8), Box (F9), joists gear; then Count (P), P Line, Break, Ends. Snap: to paths, to endpoints, to midpoints, to intersections, and a fifth button: to OurPDF objects and measurements. "All off" turns off all types at once and becomes "All on". F3 turns snapping to measurements on and off, Ctrl+F3 to PDF lines, as in OurPlanCore. Measurement style: colors, line width and font with sliders, opacity. With nothing selected it sets the style of new measurements; with a selection it changes what is selected. The bottom row Rot, Scale, Mirror always stays in place, the toolbar does not jump. Scale and Excel: the sheet scale box, calibration, ..., the pin, then the Link to Excel button, the Excel button, J2 and the format circle.

If only a crop is selected, the style block goes empty: color and line width do not apply to a crop. With the lock closed its spot stays empty, the sheet does not shift.

docs.title: Move a block
docs.text:
1. Grab the block by its handle: the dots at its left edge.
  2. Drag it onto a toolbar row: a yellow vertical marker shows where it will go. Let go.
  3. A block released over the sheet floats above the window. You can keep dragging it by the same handle and dock it back to a row.
  4. The layout is remembered. Reset toolbar: Window > Reset toolbar or right-click the handle.
The "Snap" block being dragged along the second row: the yellow marker shows the spot. The "Snap" block released over the sheet, floating.

docs.title: Lock
docs.text:
The lock button at the end of the first row. Closed by default.

Lock What happens closed all blocks are always on screen, in any tool, the sheet does not jump open the second row is hidden, the sheet gets more room. The ruler button brings all blocks, pressing it again removes them and turns on "Select" open, a measurement selected the style block comes in with the "Link to Excel" and Excel buttons open, lines selected the "Measure" block with Break and P Line comes in too open, a comment tool the style block comes in

The same toggle: right-click with the ruler on, "Hide the "Measure" toolbar". In reading mode and full screen there are no blocks.

Lock open, the "Select" tool: only the first row.

Lock open, the ruler pressed: all blocks came in. In this window "Measure" sits in the second row because there is not enough room in the first.

docs.title: Panels and windows
docs.text:
• The arrows on the sheet edges and the keys F4 (left panel), F5 (right panel) collapse and expand the panels.
  • Each file opens in a tab above the sheet. The tab of a modified copy (after editing pages or content) is marked *.
  • A separate window of the same document: Ctrl+Shift+N or the button with a square and an arrow. Handy for keeping the plan on one monitor and the section on another.

docs.title: Status bar
docs.text:
At the bottom, left to right: file name, page number, a hint for the current action, zoom in percent, document type.

While the ruler is on, the document type is replaced by measurement info: tool, scale and where it came from, value, ΔX, ΔY, angle, snap. To remove it: right-click with the ruler on, "Hide measurement info window".

Measurement info while a line is being drawn.
  • The hint changes with the tool: while measuring "click the points, snapping to PDF lines, Shift or Ortho keeps it straight. Right-click for the menu. Esc resets", while selecting "click to pick, empty space pans. E selects with a frame".
  • The document type tells what Ctrl+S will do: for an ordinary PDF "Ctrl+S writes the markups into this file"; for a modified copy "saves into the original PDF"; for an OurPlanCore snapshot saving works differently (Saving).
  • After any command, the result or the reason it failed is written here. Read the status bar when something did not work.

docs.title: AI help in estimating work
docs.text: Here: where AI helps in the current workflow, what it does well, what stays with the estimator and how to check the result. AI speeds up reading the plan set and routine work in the workbook; the decision and the responsibility for quantities stay with the estimator.

docs.title: Where AI is used now
docs.text: Step What AI does What to check Job intake PDF breakdown: sheet numbers and types, scope, sheet summary, a "To check" list, draft header notes sheet numbers and scale; template notes against the scope Sheet names in OurPlanCore reads the title block on the Name command, suggests a number and a tag (reading the title block with an AI model is in the full version of OurPlanCore only) tag last (a101 1st, s101 f), f only on the foundation Detail crops AI Crop Notes: text and a note for a detail crop (full version of OurPlanCore) marks, sizes, layers against the source sheet Agent terminals in the app built-in terminals (full version of OurPlanCore only) and Agent Bridge: the agent sees the open job and can create and fix takeoffs, the tree, names every new takeoff by eye on the sheet; color and symbol of the new item Excel workbook inserting rows and notes by the rules, blocks copied from the reference, checking note length and rounding, a draft Changes.txt for a revision compare the processed .xlsx with the .xlsm; notes per the rules Note text Y_Improve_Note in Excel rewrites a note following the samples on the Standarts worksheet natural phrasing, per <sheet>, length up to 100 Checking a delivered job comparing the workbook with the drawings: misses, doubles, formulas pointing into another block open every comment on the sheet, do not fix blindly

docs.title: How to ask
docs.text:
1. Give the scope, sheet and scale: "S201, 3/16", second floor beams".
  2. Ask for a list with sources: mark, size, sheet and detail, what is unclear.
  3. Carry over only what you checked; write assumptions as assumed; verify notes.
  4. A similar delivered job is a hint for misses, not the content of the new one.

docs.title: What not to carry over blindly
docs.text: Data Why Beam, header, post codes (H5, B2, C5) per project: the legend is in this plan set's schedule Wall types, holdowns, hangers, anchor spacing, insulation, sheathing read them in the schedules and details of your own project Template values (Zip Tape, 29 oz adhesive, Tyvek) replaced per the spec, they do not stay as defaults Quantities from similar buildings only as an order-of-magnitude check (Benchmarks)

docs.title: Rules for AI in this knowledge base
docs.text:
• Cite the sheet or detail number, not the PDF page; no source - assumed; verify.
  • Do not pass off an open question as fixed; do not make up hardware models: a condition not in the tables gets TBD with a note.
  • Read the whole workbook row, including the working zones on the right (DFL).
  • A new correction from the owner becomes a rule here and in the rules canon, it does not stay in the chat.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• OurPlanCore: interface and tools, Getting started
  • DFL: how the workbook is built, Notes in DFL, QA checklist

docs.title: Tips and key rules
docs.text: Here: rules collected from corrections and comments on delivered jobs, grouped by topic. Many of them are not in general estimating guides: this is local memory. What the mistake looks like and how to catch it is on the Common mistakes page; here you get only the rule.

docs.title: Walls and studs
docs.text:
• Stud height = floor-to-floor minus subfloor, minus floor system depth, minus plates. Floor-to-floor and ceiling height are not the stud height; check against the section of each building. Example: 11'1" wall - 22" truss - 3/4" subfloor = 9'2" stud. On COM, the exact height to 1/8" goes in E of the stud row.
  • Wall type (ext, corr, dem, party) is set by the wall schedule segments, not by the group: a piece of demising inside the exterior line stays demising.
  • P.T. bottom plate only on concrete and masonry. Double bottom plate only where the detail shows it.
  • Stud factors: Stud spacing factors, 12 / 16 / 24 = 1.4667 / 1.1 / 0.625. Joists use a different table (12 / spacing). The numbers are not repeated here.
  • Corridor 2x4 staggered = two rows at 16" o.c., 2x6 plates. Bearing walls on lower floors may need double studs: count them as Extra per the floor's stud schedule.
  • Metal walls: even when metal is by others, the row or the note Metal studs are by others stays. Client list: Client rules, Metal Studs.
  • Shafts are always in the workbook, material per the drawings (a CMU elevator is not a wood shaftliner).
  • Interior drywall, interior insulation and sound batt are not counted in frame scope; insulation only exterior, outside the sheathing, even on CMU. Exterior gypsum (parking, mech) is counted.
Staggered stud wall: two rows of 2x4 studs on shared 2x6 plates. In the workbook, two rows of studs at 16" o.c. and 2x6 plates.

docs.title: FRT
docs.text:
FRT is driven by the construction type from the Code Compliance Summary, not by a generic note.

Construction type What is FRT Type III everything in the exterior wall plane: studs, plates, headers, blocking, sheathing; wood walls below the podium. LVL, PSL, LSL are not allowed in this plane, do not write LVL FRT Type V-A, V-B no general FRT; only where a detail explicitly requires it Any parapets and exterior blocking same as the exterior wall; subfloor: 2' or 4' strips along the perimeter of its own floor; demising shear wall sheathing is regular unless the schedule says FRT; stair and shaft walls are often FRT per detail

FRT and FRTW on a drawing are the same requirement. The note all wood materials at exterior to be FRT = all loose plywood on the exterior is FRT, with verify.

docs.title: Sheathing and WRB
docs.text:
• 19/32" = 5/8", not 1/2". Applies to plywood and OSB.
  • The structural sheet wins on thickness; Zip on the arch sheets overrides the structural note, but with a note. 7/16" Zip on S and Zip R-3 on A are one product, not a conflict.
  • The sheathing name comes from the project: LP FlameBlock 2-sided is not 7/16 OSB FRT; do not turn 5/8 EXT. SHEATHING into Ply without a reason; CDX only if the spec says so.
  • The exterior barrier is called WRB or Air Barrier, not Vapor Barrier; the product per spec (fluid-applied is not Tyvek).
  • Read spec tables to the end: WS-1 (walls) and WRS-1 (roof) are different tables.
  • Layers per the detail arrows: a double arrow to one hatch = two layers, each on its own row.
  • Panel job: one side of sheathing is in the panel; count only the required second side. The exterior side of an SW is already in ext walls, only the interior side is needed; label a double-sided SW "both sides", G = sum of the two faces without another x2. P in the mark = perforated, not two sides.
  • Subtract openings from sheathing, WRB, insulation, Z-girt and the foundation line on their own floor and only once. Windows under 4' are not subtracted.
  • H-clips are not needed with T&G or with decking thicker than the spec threshold; otherwise per support spacing, not "4 per sheet". H-clips.
  • The measured area must reach Excel and update after edits in the app.

docs.title: Wall panels
docs.text:
Full breakdown, scope table and exceptions under concrete and in reconstruction: Wall Panels.

  • In panelized scope, walls next to CMU can be panels. Being next to CMU or named furring wall does not by itself make a wall stick-framed and is not a reason for optional framing.
  • Not panels: walls under a concrete slab, inside existing frames, short walls and walls with an irregular slope. Exterior build-up walls can be an exception: check the construction and scope, do not exclude all build-ups automatically.
  • Furring under siding and insulation are separate items with their own scope: Furring.
  • Headers inside panels are not drawn; only flush headers separately; on export, headers go into the wall block of the floor below.

docs.title: Rim, ribbon, blocking
docs.text:
Mistake Correct 1-3/4 LVL Rim when LVL is not specified 11-7/8" Rim; LSL named - 11-7/8" LSL Rim Rim split into 16' pieces rim in LFT with factor 1.05 (EWP) or 1.1 Ribbon board with top chord bearing trusses blocking between trusses, often (2) 2x6
  • 1-3/4 LVL Rim only when a deck or corridor frame attaches to the rim. With I-joists, engineered rim only. Roof TJI also need rim.
  • Walls 10' and taller get two rows of blocking. Blocking, drywall blocking, ribbon, ledger are in LFT with 10% waste, once (Rim, ribbon, blocking).
  • Ledger and its fasteners on separate rows per detail (3 SDWS per truss end at 16"), entered on their own floor.
  • Piggyback trusses: 2x6 sleepers between the truss tops.
Ribbon per the truss manufacturer's standard on top chord: with top chord bearing, count blocking between trusses instead of ribbon.

docs.title: Hangers, ties, holdowns
docs.text:
• DHU / DGU only where joists hang over a firewall at stairs, elevators, shafts; a regular demising wall with gypsum under the floor framing gets ITS. DHU is much more expensive, flag those stacks separately for review.
  • Hangers on both ends of every joist, by assembly; Zmax on the exterior; ties to trusses under the sheathing without Zmax. Row format: Hangers, how to write them.
  • Roof-to-wall ties along all bearing lines, spacing = truss spacing, H3 on both sides of the truss and base ties at every stud, if the detail says so.
  • Holdowns: to concrete one, through wood floor framing two; over a beam, no transfer holdown is needed (client instruction); do not delete hardware the engineer explicitly shows. The block goes at the end of the floor's wall section: Blocks.
  • A35 / LTP4 on shear walls per the SW schedule and details: if the schedule names them, count by spacing.
  • Spread shear wall anchors by spacing, SW mark in E, type and size from the anchorage schedule in B; do not swap a wedge anchor for Titen HD without a reason; plate washers per the table, not generic 3x3.
Holdown detail at the foundation: threaded rod anchor, holdown on chord studs, plate washer on the SW anchor. To concrete, one row Holdowns (1) btm.

docs.title: Roof
docs.text:
• Pitch from the sheet, applied once; each building has its own. Do not add overframe automatically.
  • Eaves: all segments; canopy is not part of eave and rake. Frame for Eave per the section: an aluminum fascia is not counted.
  • Truss bracing over the whole area under the roof, including the garage.
  • Kickers only where they are on a detail; firewall and gable kickers per the detail spacing.
  • Soffit: count wood framing, not aluminum soffit; 5/8" exterior gypsum on canopies and porch; both soffit areas go into sheathing and WRB.
  • Attic draft stop separate from fireblock, by roof plan zones, row in Gable Walls; do not copy it from the shear total.
  • Parapets per the details, wrapping around the rim, real cut layout, coping on its own row or in Drip Edge.

docs.title: Beams, posts, stairs
docs.text:
• Every beam mark on every floor where it is shown; PSL under beam ends per the schedule.
  • The beam name in the app carries the length rounded by the Beam tool: up to 8' round up to the whole foot, longer to the even foot.
  • Cap and base for every post per detail; a continuous post once, on the top floor it supports.
  • Nailer on a steel beam: 3x DF on top, 2x on the bottom separately; bolts per the beams of their own floor.
  • Bolts, washers, nuts with separate formulas; one washer per bolt, two when there is wood on both sides; nails are not counted; screws need no washers or nuts.
  • Multiply stairs by the number of stairs; two flights - 2x12 stringers, not the LVL from the template; 2x12 Tread and 1x8 Riser.
  • Do not forget small structures: roof hatch curb, mechanical platforms, sign backing, trash enclosure, railings with hardware; kitchen and bath blocking.

docs.title: Balconies and porch
docs.text:
• Posts outdoors are always P.T.; under a roof, regular. Composite railing as a system, painted wood railing by component; two posts per balcony.
  • Porch is counted separately from balconies; fill porch SQFT on the Front Page even when the porch is under a balcony.
  • Porch ceiling joists + ledger + hangers are required; framing not shown - a note. Full list: Balcony, porch and holdown blocks.

docs.title: Doors
docs.text:
• Unit entry doors from the corridor are usually fire rated: 3070 Entry, 2670 FCW, 3070 HM C-lbl; row format 3070 1 unit MARK FIRE LABEL.
  • Doors wider than 4' as double: 5070 = (2)2670. Hardware numbers do not go into the takeoff.
  • Casing in LFT on three sides of the door; interior door jambs are counted as points by unit, grouped by the adjacent wall section (a point at 2x6 = 2x6 jamb).

docs.title: Interior trims
docs.text:
• Room schedule: wood base only (Wd); exclude tile base.
  • Corridors, lobbies and other common areas separately: the trim type can differ from the units.
  • Crowns are included when interior trim scope is active. Trims not specified - not specified, do not make them up.

docs.title: Formatting and output
docs.text:
• Floors separately, even identical ones; section header 4th Floor Framing List is the same as 3rd Floor instead of a note.
  • Units: LFT, not FT; caps, bases, connectors in pcs. The label matches the calculation; E = the correct sheet or detail; inches with the " sign.
  • A different grade on its own row; copied detail labels corrected; Schedule, not Shedule; floors 1st, 2nd, Loft.
  • Material from a separate spec gets the note per customer note. Delete unused rows, except formulas that feed the wall calculation.
  • Do not swap count and length for joists; for duplexes and repeated buildings, check the multipliers twice.
  • Full check before delivery: especially items with very large quantities, and "is anything doubled".

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Common mistakes, QA checklist, Client rules
  • Formulas and factors, Notes in DFL, Hangers

docs.title: Balcony, porch and holdown blocks in the DFL
docs.text:
Here: how to lay out a balcony block, a porch block and a holdown block in the workbook the way it is done in delivered jobs. A block = a header with a fill, notes under it, rows with formulas, white blank rows between groups. A block is inserted as a copy of a reference (the template's block #1 or a block from a previous delivery), not typed by hand.

New group formatting rules (November 2026)

A group sits inside Framing, preferably right after the framing list of its floor. Decking, railing and trims come right after the framing under their own headers. Notes go only under a header. Full rule with a diagram: File format, groups.

Balcony framing: ledger at the wall, joists with hangers, beam on posts, box or rim around the perimeter. Each element is its own row in the block.

docs.title: Before the blocks
docs.text:
1. A second block in the same workbook: Duplicate Block copies it with its own units. The first block: open a delivered job with a similar balcony or porch and see how the block is laid out there.
  2. Count the types separately: balconies by size and number of posts, porch separately from balconies (a porch has its own count, it does not mirror the balconies). The number of instances comes from the doors on the floor plans, multiplied by the floors, cross-checked against the deck joist callouts on the S plans: a door without wood joists means a concrete or truss balcony, which is a different block.
  3. Take the takeoffs from OurPlanCore: areas sqfts/blcny, sqfts/porch, block points (one takeoff per type, a point per instance, xN in the name), holdowns from shear walls/<floor>/holdowns.
  4. Read all connection details on S to the end: beam to post, floor edge, beam to beam.

docs.title: Block formatting
docs.text: Element How Balcony header ="#N Upper Balcony List W' x D' "&G&" unit"&H, fill A:B, bold black; the template fill is FABF8F, in the reference books group headers are green 99CC00; use green for a new header (what is not settled yet); a terrace over a garage is Upper Balcony/Terrace List Porch header #N Porch Framing List W' x D', fill A:B green 99CC00, bold black Ground deck header must contain Deck and Frame or Framing, plus the level and location: Rear Ground Deck Frame, Ground Deck Framing List (left). The program does not recognize Rear Deck Text in the header only in A, columns B-F empty; put the detail or sheet in a note under the header Several of the same type state the location: which balcony is where, which porch Units G of the header = number of instances; area rows parse W and D from the header and multiply by the header's G Notes under the header, not above it; prefix and yellow fill (Notes) Decking, railing, trims right after the framing, each under its own header row: Balcony Railing, Ground Deck Decking (rear), Canopy Trims, Decking and Railing, Porch Trims Blank rows white, formatted from a white blank row; fill only on notes and the header Zeros delete rows with C = 0 and empty template rows

docs.title: Balcony block
docs.text:
Row How to count Source Posts P.T., per the plan: usually 2, a corner or recessed balcony may carry 1 plan, S detail Post Bases model per detail (ABA66Z, ABU66 Zmax) S detail Post Caps by beam plies: 3-ply BCS2-3/6 Zmax, 2-ply BC46 Zmax; model per schedule, not the default S detail, schedule Beam front and sides plies as the leading multiplier in C (=3*..., =2*...); beam codes from the project legend (example: balcony 2x12 P.T. B3/B4, porch 2x10 B1/B2) beam schedule Ledger + screws screws SDWS22400DB, 3 per point (=CEILING(...,3)) ledger detail Box only if the beam is not flush; a flush beam replaces box and rim S plan Joists 2x12 P.T. or 2x10 P.T., count W*12/16+1; a long board in D (14') and /2 in C, do not multiply short D values S plan End Joists the outer joists in a different size, hangers LUC210 Zmax (concealed flanges) S detail Hangers LUS210 Zmax joist to ledger; HUC212-2 Zmax beam to beam; LVL beam HUC410 Zmax S details Beam to post connections ML210Z, HL33Z, through bolts + washers + nuts, SDS: each on its own row, E = detail S details Decking under its own header; 2x6 DuxxBak, SQ FT, E = detail; 5/4x6 only on a terrace over a garage (there: subfloor 3/4" Ply + sleepers 2x4 P.T. + 5/4x6) A detail Fascia, Soffits, Post Wrap, flashing under the trims header (Balcony Trims), only if trim is in scope; Frame only: do not insert scope

Concrete and truss balconies (living space below, LW concrete) are not part of the wood block: bases = 0 on those stacks and a counted separately note.

docs.title: Railing
docs.text:
A balcony always has railing: either as a system or by component, per the detail. Do not mix them on one balcony. Railing rows go right after the framing under their own header (Balcony Railing or a shared Decking and Railing), with the note about the system under it.

Type Rows Composite, Azek, system note about the system + Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T. (=2*G, two per balcony) + Post Sleeve + Post Cap + Rail sections 6' (front and sides as separate rows) Wood painted, by component Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T. (=2*G) + Balustrades =EVEN(G*2.2) + Rails (top & bottom) =EVEN(G*2.2) + Cap Rail =EVEN(G*1.1), where G = railing LF x units Aluminum, metal note Note: Aluminum railing materials are by others; verify components.; material is not counted

System types and what they include: Rails & Decking.

docs.title: Porch block
docs.text:
• Ceiling Joists 16" o.c. + ledger + hangers are required and go separately from the rafters.
  • Porch framing not shown on the drawings: a note right under the header: Note: Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify.
  • A porch over a balcony with a truss roof: only Posts + Beams (+ caps), units = stacks, remove the template's rafters and ridge.
  • Porch ceiling as one row 5/8" Gyp, the two layers built into the formula (*2), not two rows.
  • Rafter block of a real porch roof: box + ledger + sub fascia, ridge beam per detail.
  • Exterior posts of a porch, balcony and railing are always P.T.; a porch or balcony under a roof (enclosed) is regular framing, not P.T. Exterior hardware Zmax (Hangers).

docs.title: Holdown block
docs.text:
Location: in the wall section of the floor whose shear walls the holdown serves (1st Floor Walls, 2nd Floor Walls), not in the Framing List. The block goes at the end of the section: after the last Tape row (under Box Sheathing), with a blank row before and after.

Row C When Holdowns (1) btm =G to concrete, bottom level, as drawn on the plan Holdowns (2) btm top =G*2 through a wood floor: one below, one above
  • B = model per the SW schedule (HDU5-SDS2.5), G = number of points from OurPlanCore, E = SW mark (SW-2). One row per model.
  • A holdown over a beam does not need a transfer holdown below (client instruction); do not delete hardware the engineer shows explicitly. Threaded rod only if shown.
  • Holdowns not marked on the plan: TBD HD + note Note: Locations of shear walls and holdowns are assumed; verify.
  • Shear wall anchors: A as text SW Anchor Bolts 12" o.c., B the size from the anchorage schedule (1/2" Ø x 4" emb Titen HD), E the SW mark, spacing in H from the sill and sole plate anchorage table; washers as one row =SUM(...) with the model (BP1/2-3). Do not replace a wedge anchor with Titen HD without a basis; count only for 1st floor SWs to concrete; a double-sided SW gets double anchorage. Details: Anchor Bolts, Shear Wall.

Holdown at the base of a shear wall stud, anchored into concrete: the Holdowns (1) btm row. Photo: Thester11, CC BY-SA 3.0, source

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A balcony block without its own unit multiplier, or with a multiplier from another block.
  • A note above the block header; decking and railing directly under the framing header; the group moved to the end of the worksheet.
  • Porch mirrored from the balconies instead of counted separately; porch SQFT on the Front Page empty.
  • Three posts per railing instead of two; system and component railing mixed.
  • Balcony hangers without Zmax; cap BCS2-3/6 on everything regardless of plies.
  • One holdown through a wood floor instead of two; the model not from the table of its own building.

All mistakes: Deck, porch, balconies, Shear walls and holdowns.

docs.text:

Joists 16" o.c.            2x12 P.T.          =CEILING((7*12/16+1)/2,1)*G   LFT  S4.1
Hangers                    LUS210 Zmax        =CEILING(10*G,2)         pcs   7/S4.1

Balcony Decking and Railing                        (its own header)
Note: Railing is composite per A6.2; posts, sleeves, caps and rail sections counted.
Decking                    2x6 DuxxBak        =CEILING(12*7*1.1,10)*G  SQ FT 5/A5.5
Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T.    4x4 P.T.           =2*G       pcs   4'
Rail sections 6'           6' Rail section    =EVEN(19/6*G)  pcs

docs.title: How the DFL workbook works
docs.text:
Here: what the working Excel workbook (Detailed Frame List) is made of, what columns it has, in what order the sections go, how rows are tied to takeoffs in OurPlanCore, and how to format the file so the processing program reads it correctly.

New formatting rules (November 2026)

The worksheet is now read by a program: it goes by color, prefixes and words. The main changes: a note without a prefix gets lost, any colored material row counts as an option, a note above a header goes into the previous block. Everything with examples: Source file format.

The Detailed Frame List worksheet: on the left the delivered table A:H, on the right the work areas (export from the app, wall matrix, spec cells, height calculator, lookup tables). Rows are inserted only in A:H.

docs.title: What is where on this page
docs.text:
• Section order

    Which section follows which: a floor's framing, its blocks, its walls, the next floor.

    See the order

  • Columns and areas

    What to write in A:H and what is calculated on the right.

    Columns A:H, work areas

  • Notes

    Important, Note, Comment: where they go and what they look like.

    Notes

  • Options and color

    A colored row drops out of the main list, an orange one goes to review.

    Options, revision

  • Balconies, porches, decks

    How to name a block and where decking, railing and trims end up.

    Groups, where a block goes

  • Before sending

    13 items worth going through before delivering the file.

    Checklist

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
The DFL (Detailed Frame List) is an Excel workbook that holds all the material for a building: one workbook per building (Bldng#A.xlsm, Bldng#B.xlsm), the file name equals the Job Name on the Front Page. The workbook is made from the TemplateCom.xlsm template (it is in the app's updates folder) and already contains all the formulas, macros and the notes library. The client gets the processed .xlsx (formulas in A:F converted to values) together with a PDF of the takeoff sheets.

Worksheet What is on it Front Page Customer, Contact, Date, Total pages; areas by floor (Basement, 1st, 2nd, Loft), separate Porches and Balconies rows; Total SQFT Detailed Frame List the main worksheet: header, main notes, material table by section, work areas on the right Standarts library of notes and row labels (Labels), where the canonical wording comes from Mat List material list by family (sizes, grades)

docs.title: Columns A:H (delivered)
docs.text:
Column What is in it Example A Description: the row label, as in the template (Labels) Studs Ext 16" o.c., Box Sheathing, Holdowns (2) btm top B Size / spec: member size, product, hardware model 2x6 P.T., (2) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, 7/16" Zip, HHUS410 Zmax SK30 R C Quantity: always a formula from G and H, never a number typed by hand =CEILING(G41/32*1.1,1) D Unit: LFT, SQ FT, 4x8, pcs, 50' rolls. Write LFT, not FT LFT E Source or explanation: sheet and detail, wall mark, stud height, purpose 8/S3.0, SW-2, 11' 8 3/8", for Ext Walls F Door or cased opening type tag, trim material type; the program ignores color in F, so it is used to mark a row (File format). Also wall mark tags Type A, IL326, IW2 G Takeoff from OurPlanCore: LF, SF or number of points =K37 H Formula parameter: spacing in inches, number of plies, height 16, 2

Wall height lives in E of the stud row (to 1/8"); wall names in the app use decimal feet. The SW mark and the source sheet also go in E, not in a note: a fact in the row means no note is needed (Notes in the DFL).

docs.title: Work areas on the right
docs.text:
The worksheet uses up to 79 columns. Only A:F are labeled in the header, so the right side looks empty, but that is where heights, LF by wall type and hardware selection are calculated. Read the row in full.

Area Columns What is there Export from the app J:N J the takeoff name as in the tree (ext 2x6 10.70, 4/S523), K the number, L the unit, M flags for rim/blocking/hangers (r, rb, b48, h16, l, bd, bft) Wall matrix O:AB LF by wall type and floor (Ext2x6, Cor2x6, Dem2x4...), filled by macro A3 from J:N; the Floor Walls rows reference it Spec cells O2:P6, O7:P8, R2:S7 O3 wall sheathing, O4 WRB, O5 Zip, O6 Zip Tape, O8 subfloor; R3 main roof, R4 overframes, R5 metal, R6 flat, R7 shingles. Next to them P and S: the source sheet as a bare reference: S3.0, 8/S3.0, A3.0 S2.5 Height calculator AE:AV floor, truss depth, deductions (slab, beam, curb), resulting stud height Lookup tables AW:BH rows 2-20: joist and beam to hanger model, steel beam to header; below that, hangers count by floor Per-row notes BR assumptions and flags for the row (Note: Trusses by others)

Spec cells are filled in from the PDF when the job is created, not before delivery: the E cells of the sheathing rows pull them with formulas (=$P$3, =S3), and one cell spreads across the whole worksheet. No source: leave per page and put the assumption in a main note. Details: Notes in the DFL, spec cells.

Insert rows only in A:H

A new row is added as cells A:H with a shift down (the Ctrl+W macro), not as a whole worksheet row. A whole row shifts the right-hand areas, and the height and wall matrix formulas stop matching the data. Deleting is also only A:H with a shift up (Ctrl+Q). Macros and hotkeys.

docs.title: Section order
docs.text:
The Detailed Frame List worksheet reads top to bottom, the way the building goes up.

In short

Foundation, 1st floor framing, 1st floor blocks, 1st floor walls, 2nd floor framing, blocks, walls and so on to the top. Then loft, gables, parapets, shafts, Wall Materials, roof, trim.

Fill in the template as usual: its sections are in a different order, and Process Excels makes the right order in the finished copy.

All sections and blocks top to bottom in the finished file, in construction order.

docs.title: What a section is made of in Excel
docs.text:
A section takes columns A:H and runs from its header to the header of the next section.

What What it looks like in Excel Example Header bold text in A, colored fill, B-F empty. One blank row before it, no blank row right under it 1st Floor Walls Note under the header right under the header, yellow fill on A:F Note: Floor Trusses are by others Material rows A label, B size or product, C quantity, D unit, E sheet or detail Bracing Ext Walls, 2x4, 76, 14 Row group rows of one assembly go together, one blank row between groups hangers right after their joists Note inside a section above the rows it refers to, bold without fill, a blank row above it Note: Optional garage headers added; verify Stair count bold row without fill, number in G, ending in H Note: 2 Stairs, G 2, H s

The header color hints at the kind of section:

Color Which sections Yellow FFFF00, A only Foundation Walls, floor walls, Gable Walls, Truss Heel, Parapet Walls, Shaft walls, Interior Doors&Trims Green 99CC00, A or A:B framing lists, framing of balconies, porches, decks and canopies, Wall Materials, Roof Frame list, Roof System Misc Light green CCFFCC, A only group decking, railing and trims, Soffits and Fascias, Exterior Trims, Siding

Framing ends here framing/roof framing, sqfts/rf 6, sqfts/flat, eves rakes/eves, eves rakes/rakes 14 Roof Products, Soffits and Fascias, Exterior Trims, Siding only if trim is in scope trims, siding 15 Interior Doors&Trims only if in scope; bold labels without color by floor 1st Floor, 2nd Floor trims, units

Sections not needed for the scope are removed by the macros A9_Fame_only (framing only) and A9_1_wall_panel (panel building), and empty and zero rows are deleted before delivery.

docs.title: What it looks like on the worksheet
docs.text: Two floors in the finished file: framing, the floor's own block, walls, the next floor's framing. Sample data.

docs.title: Template and finished file
docs.text:
In the template everything is arranged by type of work: all walls first, then all framing, blocks at the very end. In the finished file the same content is arranged by floor.

Template, where you fill in Finished file after Process Excels Foundation Walls, Basement Floor Walls the same 1st, 2nd, 3rd Floor Walls in a row 1st Floor Framing List, 1st floor groups, 1st Floor Walls Gable Walls, Truss Heel, Parapet Walls, Shaft walls, Wall Materials 2nd Floor Framing List, 2nd floor groups, 2nd Floor Walls 1st, 2nd, 3rd Floor Framing List in a row, Loft Framing List 3rd Floor Framing List, groups, 3rd Floor Walls, Loft Framing List Roof Frame list, Roof System Misc Gable Walls, Truss Heel, Parapet Walls, Shaft walls, Wall Materials balcony, porch, deck, canopy blocks Roof Frame list, Roof System Misc Roof Products and trim the same

Do not rearrange sections by hand

Formulas and the right-hand areas are tied to the template rows. Process Excels moves only columns A:H and only in the finished copy; the working workbook stays as it is.

Quantities do not change

After the move, the program checks all materials, the Front Page and the Mat List. If something does not match, the file is not created. What changed is recorded in the dfl_rules_report.txt report next to the finished files.

Rows J:L stay where they are

In the finished file, for moved sections they no longer sit next to their rows. The G-to-K references are correct, but checking takeoffs is easier in the working workbook.

docs.title: Where a block goes
docs.text:
Put the level in the block name

The program takes the block's floor from the header. No level: the block goes to the 1st floor.

In the block name Where it goes Example floor number after that floor's framing list #1 1st Floor Balcony List, 2nd Floor Porch Framing List Upper after 2nd Floor Framing List #1 Upper Balcony List no level, or Ground after 1st Floor Framing List Front Porch Framing List, Ground Deck Framing List (left), Rear Canopy Framing List Roof before the roof sections Roof Deck Framing, Side Roof Framing List

Several blocks on the same floor go in the order they were in the template. Decking, railing and trims go right after the framing of their block.

docs.title: Special cases
docs.text: Case What the finished file will have First floor on a slab 1st Floor Framing List stays with one note Note: First Floor is on the concrete slab, the 1st floor blocks come after it Concrete first floor 1st Floor Walls Materials at Concrete in place of the 1st floor walls, then 2nd Floor Framing List Identical floors the headers 4th Floor Framing List is the same as 3rd Floor, 3rd Floor Walls is the same as 2nd Floor Walls go in the same order as regular ones One list for two floors 1st - 2nd Floors Framing List goes before 1st Floor Walls A floor has framing but no walls of its own the framing list goes after the walls of the floor below No framing list for the floor in question the block goes after the nearest framing list below The building has no framing list at all blocks go before the roof sections

docs.title: How OurPlanCore takeoffs become rows
docs.text:
The XL strip in the app writes takeoffs into the workbook and runs the workbook's macros (details on the buttons: OurPlanCore, Estimating and export). The general flow is the same for all buttons:

  1. A takeoff from the tree goes into the J:N work area next to its section: name in J, number in K, unit in L.
  2. A workbook macro spreads J:N into A:H rows: A3 calculates walls into the O:AB matrix, C_BeamsSort, C_JoistsSort, C_HeadersSort, C_PostsSort write the framing rows, C_RimBoardBlockingHangers expands the M flags into rim, blocking, hangers, ledger.
  3. G of the row keeps a link to the takeoff (=K37), C calculates from G and H. So a takeoff corrected in the app and exported again changes the quantity by itself.
XL button What it takes from the tree Where it goes in the workbook SF sqfts/1st, 2nd, base, rf 6, flat, blcny, porch Front Page, subfloor, roof areas by pitch WL walls/<floor> floor walls/* O:AB matrix, Floor Walls rows (studs, plates, bracing, sheathing) GB, TH, PP, E/R gables, trussheel, parapets, eves rakes Gable Walls, Truss Heel, Parapet Walls, Roof Products OP openings/<floor>/WxH d gd Ext. Headers by width (up to 48", 60", 72", over 72"), flashing SH, SW, SHF, UN sheathing from J or the legend, shear walls, shafts, units A7 sheathing, Holdowns into the floor's wall block, Shaft walls, units table FR (= PS, BM, HD, JS, DT, ST) framing/<floor> framing/posts, beams, headers, joists, details, stairs the floor's Floor Framing List; headers into the wall block of the floor below; details into J:M with flags BL sqfts/blcny, sqfts/porch blocks #N Upper Balcony List, #N Porch Framing List LG project legend H5 - (2) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL (size by code), 4/S523 = b24 (detail flags), wall sheathing = 7/16" Zip no insulation

Beam, post and header codes (H5, B2, C5) without a legend go into the workbook as a code instead of a size: fill in the legend before export, per the project schedule.

docs.title: Front Page and SQFT
docs.text:
• Floor areas come from sqfts and go to the Front Page row by row; the floor above the last full floor is written Loft, not 5th.
  • Porches and Balconies have their own rows. A porch over a balcony does not cancel the porch row: fill in both.
  • Customer, Contact, Date, Total pages filled in before delivery; Total SQFT is not 0.

docs.title: Source file format
docs.text:
Here: how to format the file before sending it for processing. The rules come from the estimator guide (November 2026) and its two reference files.

Why. The processing program builds a summary list from the worksheet and assigns product codes to materials. It does not understand what rows mean and relies on color, prefixes and keywords. Extra text in a header or a colored row changes the result: the material ends up in the wrong group or drops out of the main list. A well-formatted file is processed in a few minutes instead of half an hour.

You already do most of this. Only two things are really new: three note levels and the new color logic.

Automation does not replace these rules

When the file is processed (Process Excels, Merge DFL), automation can fix some of the formatting. But only the estimator knows what counts as an option, what level a note has and what type a door is, so the estimator follows the rules.

docs.title: Section and subsection headers
docs.text:
Header: bold text + colored fill + name in column A + columns B-F empty. A blank row before the header.

  • Bold alone is not enough: a bold row without fill counts as a regular row.
  • Text in B-F, even one word, breaks the header. Put the explanation in a note under it.
  • Section names are standard (as in the template). Subsections inside Framing can be named as needed, same formatting.
  • A bold label without color inside a section is fine as a regular row: 1st Floor among the doors, Living rm Trims: before a group of panels.

A correct header, one with text in B, and one without color.

Colors in the reference files (the guide does not set a specific color, the fill itself is required):

Color Where in the reference files Yellow FFFF00, A only Foundation Walls, Shaft Walls, 1st Floor Walls, Interior Doors&Trims Green 99CC00, A or A:B framing lists, group framing (Porch Framing List 4pcs, Ground Deck Framing List (left), Pergola 4 pcs), Roof Frame list, Roof System Misc Light green CCFFCC, A only Decking, Decking and Railing, Porch Trims, Pergola Trims, Soffits and Fascias, Exterior Trims, Siding

docs.title: Groups: deck, porch, balconies, canopy
docs.text:
The framing, trims, decking and railing of these structures sit inside the Framing section as subsections, right after the Framing List of their floor: a 2nd floor balcony after 2nd Floor Framing List, a porch and a ground deck after 1st Floor Framing List, a roof deck before the roof. Groups moved to the very end of the worksheet get added up wrongly with the other material and have to be sorted out by hand.

  • Ground deck framing: the name must contain Deck and Frame or Framing, plus the level and location. Right: Rear Ground Deck Frame, Roof Deck Framing, Ground Deck Framing List (left). Wrong: Rear Deck.
  • Trims, Decking, Railing: each block gets its own header row, not directly under the framing header. Right: Balcony Railing, Ground Deck Decking (rear), Canopy Trims, Decking and Railing, Porch Trims. Wrong: Ground deck, Balcony deck, Ground Rail.
  • If there are several balconies, porches or decks, state the location: which one is where.

Ground deck group: framing with a note, then decking and railing under their own headers.

What it looks like in the reference file:

First Floor Framing List                  green
Ground Deck Framing List (left)           green, A:B
Note: All Deck frame is assumed to verify yellow, A:F
Posts, Post Bases, Post Caps, Beams, Ledger, Joists, Hangers, Stringers, Flashing
Decking and Railing                       light green
Note: Decking is composite per elevation  yellow, A:F
Note: Railing per detail page A4.04       yellow, A:F
Decking, Posts at Rails, Post Sleeve, Post cap, Rail sections, Post Wrap, Deck Fascia, Lattice
1st Floor Walls                           yellow

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
A note = a row with a prefix in A, columns B-F empty. Per the guide all notes have a yellow fill, and a row without it does not make it into the final file as a note. Our practice:

  • In the worksheet header (above Description): Important: red bold on yellow, a regular Note: red bold without fill.
  • Right under a section header: yellow fill on A:F.
  • Inside a section above its rows, and the count row Note: 2 Stairs: bold without fill, as before.
Prefix When Look Examples Important: a global decision: if the client misses it, the price shifts a lot. The program moves these notes to the top of the final worksheet red bold on yellow EWP by others, trusses by others, addition only, part of the building is existing, two sheathing systems Note: important, but the price does not change for the whole worksheet black on yellow, bold in the reference files client and plan disagree, a different LVL size assumed Comment: a passing remark about one small element black on yellow, bold in the reference files where the headers came from, client and plan agree

A simple level check: what happens if the client does not read it? Half the building counted for nothing or not counted: Important. One product instead of another: Note. Nothing significant: Comment.

Important, Note, Comment and a note continuation. At the bottom: rows that will not reach the final file.
  • Continuation: the next row right below, no prefix, the same yellow fill, B-F empty. A second note with a prefix also works.
  • Placement: always under the header of its section. The program reads everything under a header up to the next header; a note above a header goes into the previous block. This applies to notes about balcony railing and decking too.
  • A note above an option block goes right above the colored rows, inside its own section (Options).
  • Be specific: when the file is assembled, duplicates are removed and similar notes are merged. The note gets separated from its block and must read on its own: not No changes in this area, but No changes for the 1st floor walls. If the note is obviously about the floor of its subsection, the floor need not be repeated, but the text must stay clear outside the worksheet.
  • Pages and details in column E: leave them as they are: that is comment level, they do not go to the final worksheet.

A note under the header and above the header; vague and specific text.

How to write the text itself and when a note is not needed: Notes in the DFL.

docs.title: Options and color
docs.text:
The color logic has changed

Any colored material row now counts as an option and is excluded from the main list. The only exception: orange. Do not color materials for any other reason.

An option is defined by the fill color of the whole row, not by the word optional. Without color the row goes into the main list as required material, even if A or E says optional.

  • Color: one color per option, not white and not orange, light so the text is readable.
  • Uniqueness: within a section, one color = one option. Two blocks of the same color in one section merge, whatever they are called. In another section the same color is processed independently.
  • Different options: clearly different colors (blue and green, not two shades of pink).
  • A blank row inside a colored block stays in the block if the color continues.
  • End of the block: the color changes, turns white or disappears, or a header comes up.
  • Name: optionally a row above the colored rows, B-F empty: Option 1, Optional Railing, Option Cupola. Without it the program names them Option 1, Option 2.

One block with a blank row inside, two colors, a scattered option, named options, an orange row.

Typical cases from the reference files:

Case How it is formatted The plans show two sheathing systems Important: Two options of wall sheathing cited..., below it Wall Sheathing (opt.1) and Tape in one color, Wall Sheathing (opt.2) and Vapor barrier in another The whole roof is in question Note: Roof materials optional, verify if apply, all rows of the section in one color Old part of the building Note: Optional for existing, verify if apply, soffits, fascia, frieze for that part in one color A door is not listed in the schedule Note: Door not listed, verify if apply, the row in color

Existing part. If the plan makes it clear that everything is new, count and write it as is. If old roofing, siding or trims remain and there is doubt: the new part as regular rows, the old part as a separate option block in one color, plus a note on what was counted.

Marking without an option:

  • A row for review: orange FABF8F (draws the reviewer's attention).
  • Any other visual mark: color only in the column F cell, the program ignores it.

docs.title: Review and revision
docs.text:
In a revision, do not color whole rows: they will become options.

  • A value changed: color only that cell (or the several cells that changed), any color.
  • A row added or changed entirely: color only in column F.

Changed cells and a new row; a whole row in color is wrong.

docs.title: Microgroups
docs.text:
Post wraps, panels, corner boards and similar assemblies are often ordered pre-made, so their materials are kept together and not mixed with the rest. A group is defined by its first row.

  1. The row above the group: blank, a label or a header. It cannot be a material row.
  2. The first row starts in A with the group word: Corner Board, Panel, Planter Box, Post Wrap, Pilaster Wrap, Column Wrap, Lattice. Any description after that. B-D as usual.
  3. End: a row where A, B and C are empty, or a header.

No separate header is needed. Add a picture for a complex assembly (column, panel) so the client can choose: build it or buy it complete.

A Panel group after a label, a Post Wrap group after a blank row; wrong: a group right under a material row.

docs.title: Individual rows
docs.text:
What Rule Right Wrong Hardware a specific name in A; the location, if critical, after the name Hangers, Bolts, Washers, Ties, Post Caps, Anchor Bolts Beam-to-Post, Opening, Stud, Hardware, Metal, Misc. Insulation the full word in column B, otherwise it lands in another group Batt Insulation R-21, 1-1/2 Rigid Insulation Batt R-21, 1-1/2 Rigid, Insul. Flitch beam the steel plate as a separate row right after the wood beam (in the reference file also under Ridge) Beam (4) Dropped + Steel plate (1), B 1/4x14 the plate at the end of the list Detail with a picture pictures in order (Detail 1 or Det. 1), the material row has the reference in B 22x42x6, det. 2, 3" Crown, det.1 a picture without a number, reference only in E Doors, cased openings different types: a tag in F starting with the word Type; the physical kind and rating stay in B F Type A; B 21080 pocket, 2880 FR s/cl A without the word Type Trim with a material type different material types in F B 3", F IL326, MD-01 type lost, everything merged into one 3" crown

Sheet references without a picture (1/A423, 2/pA421) stay in E, as before.

Flitch beam, Insulation, a detail with a picture, door and trim types.

Additions from reviewing the guide:

  • Trim with a mark on the plan: the mark can go right in B instead of the size, since it is the product name. If you write the size in B, the mark goes in F.
  • Similar profiles of the same size (two 6" crowns): they will be added together when the file is assembled. Write 6" Crown, det.1 and 6" Crown, det.2, with a picture whose arrow points to the right profile. Write the same profile the same way in different details, so it adds up.
  • Length with steel: at 14'5" the steel plate is 15, the wood beam may be 16.
  • Commercial doors: public areas and corridors separately from doors inside units, state the rating. Glass doors are not always labeled as such: when in doubt, (glass?) in B.
  • Roofing: if the plan clearly shows the whole roof as new, say so and do not make it an option.

docs.title: Checklist before sending
docs.text:
• 1. Headers: bold font, colored fill, B-F empty. Bold alone is not enough.
  • 2. The name of a deck's framing contains Deck and Frame or Framing.
  • 3. Each Trims, Decking, Railing block has its own header with the right name, and does not sit directly under the framing header.
  • 4. Important, Note, Comment have the right prefix, yellow fill, B-F empty. Important ones are bold red.
  • 5. Option rows: a color unique within the section, not orange and not white.
  • 6. Materials are not colored for any reason other than options. Orange to get the reviewer's attention; in a review, color in F or in the changed cell.
  • 7. Post Wrap, Panel, Corner Board, Planter Box, Lattice: the first row starts with the group word; above it a blank row, a label or a header.
  • 8. Every insulation row has the word Insulation in B.
  • 9. Hardware has a specific name in A, not Hardware, Metal, Misc.
  • 10. Flitch beam steel plates as a separate row right after the wood beam.
  • 11. Material rows that belong to a detail picture reference it in B.
  • 12. Door and cased opening type tags in F, starting with the word Type.
  • 13. Exterior and interior trim: different material types in F (MD-01).

docs.title: What is not settled yet
docs.text:
These are questions we do not have an answer to yet. What is written here is not a rule, just what is known today.

Question What is known Which exact color counts as orange the guide gives no color code. For a review mark we use FABF8F. Light peach FCE5D7 appears as an option in the guide's picture, so do not use peach shades for options. Make group headers green 99CC00, as in the reference files Notes without yellow the reference file has a red Note: without fill at the top, while the guide text says rows without yellow get lost. We do it as described in Notes. If such notes start disappearing from the final worksheet, we will change the rule More than half the worksheet changed not described in the guide. As before: one note in the header, no highlighting

Where the review session and the guide disagree, the guide wins:

Topic At the review session In the guide Header color "just for style" required One color per option across the whole worksheet within a section Wall insulation Wall Insulation in A and the word in B only the word in B Group keywords also Flower Box Pilaster Wrap, Column Wrap, Lattice; no Flower Box Floor in a note once "not needed if the note is in the floor's subsection", another time "write the floor" example No changes for the 1st floor walls Comment: - text and reference file: yellow fill; in one of the guide's pictures it has no fill

docs.title: Pre-delivery check
docs.text:
• Units in D (LFT, pcs, SQ FT, 4x8), the label matches the calculation (Plates (2) with H = 2).
  • C is a formula from its own block everywhere: its own header, its own unit multiplier, its own floor; no references to another block after copying a floor.
  • Spec cells O/P and R/S filled in; E of the sheathing rows shows the sheet, not formula text.
  • No junk in the calculation area in any column, not only A:H (a letter in O gives #VALUE!).
  • Zero and empty template rows deleted; notes do not contradict rows.
  • The measured area made it to Excel and was updated after edits in the app.
  • Processed .xlsx checked against the .xlsm: notes and rows in place.
  • Formatting checked against the file format checklist: headers, notes, options, groups.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Copying a whole floor with formulas that look at another floor or someone else's header.
  • A quantity as a number instead of a formula: it will not update on the next export.
  • Inserting a whole worksheet row instead of A:H: the right-hand areas shifted.
  • FT in D, 5th instead of Loft, porch SQFT on the Front Page not filled in.
  • Spec cells left until delivery: half the E cells reference per page.
  • A note without the Important:, Note: or Comment: prefix: it will not make it into the final file.
  • A note above the block header: it goes into the previous block.
  • (optional) as a word without color: the option goes into the main list as required material.
  • A whole row colored in a revision or "for personal use": it becomes an option and disappears from the main list.
  • A block without a level in its name: it goes to the 1st floor, even if it is on the 2nd.

All workbook mistakes: Common mistakes, Excel DFL and notes.

docs.title: E-Wood tab in Excel
docs.text:
Here: what each button on the E-Wood tab does, how to copy a block and insert a shared one, what each line of the Check report means, and what is applied where at delivery. The same instructions are in a PDF, opened by the More > Instruction button on the tab. The rules for the rows themselves are in How the DFL workbook works.

E-Wood tab, left part: Book, Order, Finish, Calculate

Right part: Insert, Structure, Clean, More. In a narrow window Excel collapses the groups on the right into one button, with the same macros inside.

The tab is installed on the computer once and works with any DFL workbook. The workbook itself and the macros inside it do not change.

Workbook path. Sort Blocks and Notes + Look change the open workbook, Fix and Process make a copy.

Undo

Sort Blocks and Notes + Look first save the workbook and put a copy in _ewood_backups, and leave the result unsaved. Don't like it: close the workbook without saving. Ctrl+Z does not undo regular macros, that is how Excel works.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
One file installs the tab, the tools, the rules and the instructions. Only Excel 2010 or newer is needed, no admin rights and no Python.
  • Update: the same steps with the new file. Remove: the same file, Uninstall button.
  • The DeepSeek key is stored for the Windows user and does not go into the installer. Without it everything works except the English check in Fix and Improve Note.
  • While a button is running, the status bar at the bottom says what Excel is busy with. There are no windows; a message appears only if something went wrong.

docs.title: The tab by group
docs.text: Group What is in it Book the template of the open workbook: Template A:H, Template A:G (old), Template A:F (old), Template unknown, Not a DFL book Order work on the open workbook: Sort Blocks, Notes + Look, Check Finish work on the saved file and make copies: Fix Numbers, Fix Links, Merge DFL, Process Excels Calculate calculation from takeoffs: Run First 6, A1 ... A9 Insert Duplicate Block, individual rows, the Insert Block and Metal Studs menus Structure sorting beams, posts, headers, joists, details, and sums Clean deleting zeros and gray rows, clearing tables More Improve Note, Check English, date, multiply, instructions, report, key, About

docs.title: Three templates
docs.text:
The tab detects the template from the workbook contents. It decides which columns may be moved.

Template Rows What works TemplateCom A:H everything 0.Template 05.23 A:G Order, Finish, More and macros that do not care: A1 Units, Trims, Sum Same, Sum Windows, 2400 @48, Insert Cells, Delete Cells, No Validation, Improve Note, Multiply 1.Template A:F the same unknown no Description row Finish, More and the same macros, Order grayed out not a DFL no worksheet the hotkeys belong to Excel again

The other buttons are grayed out on old templates and their hotkeys are not taken: such a macro would write over the table on the right. On old templates the rules move rows only within their own range.

docs.title: Calculation from takeoffs
docs.text:
Usually the A macros are run by OurPlanCore through the XL strip buttons. Here they are needed to recalculate one group. Select the list in J:L.

Button Hotkey What it does Run First 6 A2 ... A6 in a row, A1 last, on the selected list in J:L. A full manual run; usually OurPlanCore does it. A1 Units Units table by floor from the selected takeoff rows. A2 SQFT Floor, gable and truss heel areas, roof pitches. A3 Walls All Walls of all floors from J:L into the O:AB matrix and the Floor Walls rows. (2) in the name multiplies the length. A3 Walls One The same for one floor. A4 Parapet Parapet table. Select 2 columns: text and LF length. A5 Openings Openings by width into header and flashing bins. Select 2 columns: text and quantity. A6 Eaves Rakes Eaves, rakes, returns and canopy. Select 2 columns: text and LF length. A7 Sheathing Based on the text in J above the Floor Framing List (Zip, OSB, no insulation) keeps the right sheathing rows and writes the spec cell. A8 Split Suffixes Splits a wall name into a base for A3 and a suffix with the detail. A9 Wall Panel Panel building scope: the panel rows stay in Floor Walls. Do not rerun on a filled workbook: it deletes rows. A9 Frame Only Frame scope: removes the trim blocks. Do not rerun on a filled workbook: it deletes rows.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Button Hotkey What it does Beams Ctrl+Shift+B Beams from mark and length pairs into Beam rows, with a legend at the end of the selection. Posts Ctrl+Shift+P Posts by mark, with code and grade in E. Headers Ctrl+Shift+H Headers into width bins: up to 48", 60", 72", over 72". Joists Ctrl+Shift+J Joists from count and length pairs. Identical lengths are added together. Rim Blocking Rim, ribbon, blocking, hangers, screws, ties, anchor bolts and ledger by the flags in M. Trims Trim of one element, multiplied by the quantity. Sum Same Ctrl+Shift+F Adds up identical rows. Select 3 columns: label, number, unit. Sum Windows Adds up values next to openings for A5. 2400 @48 Fills in values from a 2-column list: key and value.

Rows by Color Ctrl+Shift+D Deletes the template's gray placeholder rows. Clear Color Gray fill turns white. Clear Wall SQFT Clears wall areas before a new calculation. Clear Parapet Clears the parapet table. No Validation Ctrl+Shift+V Removes drop-down lists.
