docs.title: Duplicate Block
docs.text:
A second balcony, porch or canopy almost always repeats the first one: a copy from the same workbook matches 76-91% of the rows. Copying by hand leaves references to another block, and the quantity is calculated from someone else's units. This button copies correctly.

Button Hotkey What it does Duplicate Block Copies the block under the cursor right below it: next number, its own units, links to takeoffs cleared.

Six steps. At the end, Check shows anything that still uses someone else's units. Before: block #1After: copy #2

Balcony block in the template: header with units in G, rows, green Decking and Balcony Trims inside the block.

The copy landed under the block after one blank row: number #2, its own units, the same rows and subsections.

The copy's formulas calculate from its own header and its own rows (C in block #1 and in the copy):

Block #1 Copy #2 =CEILING((G1814)*1.1/32,1) =CEILING((G1862)*1.1/32,1) =CEILING((G1814)*1.1,10) =CEILING((G1862)*1.1,10) =CEILING((G1841)*1.1,10) =CEILING((G1889)*1.1,10) =EVEN(G1843*2.2) =EVEN(G1891*2.2) What How Boundaries a block with units in the header's G is copied whole, together with the green Decking and Trims, up to the next header. Cursor on the green header itself: only that subsection, the units stay from its block Number #2 Upper Balcony... becomes the next free number of this kind. Without # the name stays as is, rename it yourself Units all $G$ references to the header in the copy point to its own header. So does the header reference in H, so the Decking area reads the size from the new header Links to takeoffs a G linking outside the block (=K36) is cleared: that is the old block's takeoff. C becomes 0 until you link a new one Numbers in G typed-in numbers are copied. The status bar says how many. Check them What it leaves alone everything to the right of A:H stays in place, the clipboard does not change, one blank row before and after the copy

The button does not check the block against the drawing

The copy's posts, beams and hangers are the same as the source's. Check them against the plan.

docs.title: Insert Block
docs.text:
A menu for blocks that have no sample in this workbook. Balconies, porches and canopies do not exist in a generic form: a generic version guesses 0-18% of the rows. For them use Duplicate Block or a block from a similar project. The menu rows come from delivered workbooks: only what holds from project to project.

Button Hotkey What it does Balcony A balcony block from the command b 12x30 or b 12.5x6.5 u2 (width, length, units). The command is taken from the active cell if that is what it holds, otherwise the program asks. Shaft Walls Two blocks at once: Shaft walls (CH + J) and Shaft Fire walls (H + C). Delete Zeros removes the unneeded one. Decking + Wood Railing Decking, Posts at Rails, Post Cap, Balustrades, Rails, Cap Rail. For wood railing. Decking + Cable Railing Decking, Posts at Rails, Post Sleeve, Post Cap, Cables, Cap Rail. For cable railing. Decking + Sleeve Railing Decking, Posts at Rails, Post Sleeve, Post Cap, Rail sections. For pre-made sections on sleeves. Pavers Pavers header, a by others note and a Pavers row. Jambs A Jambs row, G is taken from Perimeter Total in the openings table. Writes the Wall Materials header only if the workbook does not have one. Bolts Four rows: Blocking, Anchor Bolts, Washers, Nuts. Spacing and layers in H, G empty.

How they write:

  • Where: into the selected row; whatever was below shifts down. Only A:H. Blank rows before and after are added automatically; no blank row under a header.
  • Nothing is typed into G: while G is empty, C = 0, and Delete Zeros removes whatever was not needed. The macro used to put G=50 or 174, and such numbers went to the client as takeoffs.
  • Count: =0*$G$<header>. Replace 0 with the quantity per block. Sleeves and caps repeat the number of posts, Rails and Cap Rail repeat the length of the row above.
  • Units: inserted inside a block with units, the formulas pick up the $G$ of its header by themselves. Outside such a block there are no units.
  • Look: a regular material row, black text, black grid, gray G:H, header color as in the templates.

What each item writes (on a copy of the template, G not filled in yet, so C = 0):

Decking, posts, sleeves, caps, cables in 9 rows, cap rail.

Decking, posts, sleeves, caps, pre-made railing sections.

Blocking, Anchor Bolts, Washers, Nuts. Spacing and layers in H, labels are built from H, G empty.

Other inserts:

docs.title: Sort Blocks and Notes + Look
docs.text:
They work on the open workbook. First they save it and put a copy in _ewood_backups next to the workbook, then make the changes and leave the result unsaved. Closing without saving means undo. Report: _ewood_backups\<name>_report.txt.

Button Hotkey What it does Sort Blocks Order: blocks to their floor, construction order, Decking and Railing headers, deck names, microgroups, one blank row each. Notes + Look Formatting: notes, headers, colors, grid, options, size formula, CEILING. Check Changes nothing. Makes a list of what a person has to decide and opens it.

Sort Blocks, order:

  • blocks go right after the framing list of their floor, trims after their block, Roof Deck and Side Roof before the roof;
  • construction order: 1st Floor Framing List, 1st Floor Walls, 2nd Floor Framing List and so on;
  • Decking and Railing get their own header, deck framing gets the Ground level; no location: that goes into the report;
  • washers in Foundation Walls go under their anchors, microgroups start after a blank row, one blank row at a time, none under a header.

Notes + Look, formatting:

  • notes: prefixes, notes under the header of their section, Important: on top, drawing status first, color by placement;
  • headers: colors, text from E moved into a Comment: under the header, color under all of the text;
  • rows: material black without fill, options in their own color, review marks in F, black grid A:F, gray G:H, height, alignment;
  • formulas: the block size formula reads the same in any language, CEILING.MATH is written as CEILING. If the number would change, the row stays and goes into the report. Gable screws stay as they are.

While the button is running

Do not copy anything in other programs: rows are moved through the clipboard, and there is only one per computer. If a copy collides, the check will see it and the workbook will go back to its saved state. Nothing is lost.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
Changes nothing. Each line of the report: worksheet row number, code, and what is wrong. These are candidates: a person decides, from the drawing. A row you checked and kept will keep showing up: an empty list is not required.

First what changes numbers, then the rest.

This is what report lines look like (example):

r129 BLOCK-REF: C counts the units of r110 '#1 Upper Balcony/Terrace List 10.5' x 5.5' 4 units', this block starts at r128 (Beams (2) and 10 more rows)
r332 POST-COUNT: 14 post bases against 28 posts in this block (#1 Upper Balcony/Terrace List 17' x 6' 14 units)
r181 ROUNDING: 30 pcs, CEILING to 10: under 50 canon rounds to 2, unless that many go per point (Ties 24" o.c.)
r3 SPEC-CELL: P3 still says 'per page': fill it from the plans
r81 STOCK: D=9: over 8 ft only even stock, 10 (Studs Ext | 2x8)
r20 C-ZERO: C is 0: delete the row with Delete Zeros (Anchor Bolts 48" o.c.)

To find a row: Ctrl+G and the address, for example A129.

Code What it means What to do BLOCK-REF the row counts the units of another block; the block was copied by hand replace $G$ with the header of its own block, unless there is a reason BLOCK-UNITS C is not multiplied by the block's units, while other rows are multiply, or leave it if it is a total for the whole building POST-COUNT Post Bases and Posts in the block do not match check against the plan, some posts may have no base SAME-BLOCK two blocks are identical per unit one block, add up the units G-DEFAULT G equals what the macro used to enter by itself (50, 100, 174) enter the takeoff or clear it JL-ORPHAN a detail is measured in J:L, but no row uses or mentions it write a row with the sheet in E, or a note on why not ERR-CELL an error #REF!, #VALUE! or other in any cell of the worksheet find the cause: an error on the right can zero out a row SPEC-CELL a spec cell still says per page, TBD or assumed fill it in from the drawing; an item the building does not have may stay C-ZERO C = 0 Delete Zeros or enter G ROUNDING under 50 pieces, not rounded to 2 round to 2, unless the hardware goes N pieces per point STOCK odd length over 8 ft the next even length C-CEILING CEILING.MATH in C Notes + Look or Fix rewrites it automatically FORMULA-LOCALE the size formula reads wrong in another language Notes + Look, Fix and Process rewrite it automatically NOTE-LEN note longer than 80 characters, ceiling 100 a second Note: row NOTE-EQ, NOTE-ABBR an = sign in the note, abbreviations shtg, btm pl, o/ full words NOTE-GLUE, NOTE-RANGE sheet attached with a dash, a sheet range with a hyphen per <sheet>, S203 thru S206 PLACEHOLDER a leftover placeholder: per page or an ellipsis at the end fill it in or delete it E-DOUBLED, E-TEXT a doubled member described in E, a sentence in E (2) at the end of A; E holds only the sheet or mark B-LVL, B-GRADE, B-APA how LVL, lumber grade and APA are written in B 1 3/4 x 14 LVL; grade and APA are not written B-ZMAX, B-TBD ABU66Z, TBD from the template model, space, Zmax. DTT2Z, TBD HD, TBD Decking do not count A-NAME, A-STUDS hardware has no real name, Studs outside Floor Walls a real name; outside Floor Walls write Frame NO-DESCRIPTION column A has no Description row template unknown, restore the row

docs.title: Fix, Merge, Process
docs.text:
They work on the file on disk and ask whether to save changes. The workbook itself does not change; the result goes into a separate folder next to it.

Button Hotkey What it does Fix Numbers A copy of the workbook: rules, English check, links turn into numbers. Folder fixed_numbers, .xlsx file. Fix Links A copy of the workbook: the same, with live formulas. Folder fixed_excels, same format. Merge DFL Summary worksheet <name>_DFL_summary.xlsx next to the workbook. Process Excels All workbooks in this folder into processed_excels, links turn into numbers. This is the delivery file.

What is applied where:

What Sort, Notes Fix Process, Merge Notes, block order, headers, colors, review marks, blank rows yes yes yes Size formula in all languages yes yes yes Grid, row look, color under all text, 92D050 to 99CC00, CEILING yes yes no Washers under anchors yes no no English and typos, DeepSeek no yes no Links to numbers no Fix Numbers Process

English check in Fix. DeepSeek rewrites the notes, a second pass rejects any change of meaning, numbers and marks stay. In labels it fixes typos based on past jobs. B and product codes are only shown in the report. Inaccuracies go into the report as [check]. Without a key notes are not checked; the report says so, and the rest gets done.

If the check failed: a material row was lost, or Front Page or Mat List values or pictures changed. The workbook is not created; the reason is in the report. For Process, the report dfl_rules_report.txt and SQ FT.txt are in processed_excels.

docs.title: Header colors
docs.text:
As in the 0.Template 05.23 and 1.Template templates.

Color Where FFFF00 walls: Foundation Walls, Floor Walls, Gable Walls, Parapet Walls, Shaft walls, Interior Doors&Trims 99CC00 framing: Floor Framing List, balconies, porch, deck, Roof Frame list, Roof System Misc CCFFCC inside blocks and trim: Decking, Balcony Trims, Porch Trims, Pavers, Roof Products, Soffits and Fascias, Exterior Trims, Siding FABF8F orange only calls the reviewer. Wall Materials and Ceiling Materials in the working workbook use it for now. At delivery the orange header becomes 99CC00, for Shaft walls FFFF00

Light green 92D050 on a header is changed to 99CC00 by Fix and Notes + Look.

docs.title: Two languages
docs.text:
Excel and Windows can be Russian or English. The tab gives the same cells on both: numbers in formulas and labels are read the same way, not according to the computer's settings.

  • The block size formula used to read 10.3 according to the computer's region: in another language it came out as 0 or billions. Now TemplateCom, TemplateResidential and the Balcony macro use the new formula. Old workbooks are fixed by Notes + Look, Fix, Process and Merge.
  • If a value was wrong, the report will have [warn] with the row number: look at that block.
  • Another computer behaves differently: press More > About and send what it says. It shows the language and separators.

Tested on an Excel that behaves like an English one. A real English Excel has not been tested.

docs.title: Excel macros and hotkeys
docs.text:
Here: which VBA macros are built into the TemplateCom.xlsm workbook, what each one does, when to run it and in what order. These are not standard Excel shortcuts: the macros work only in a workbook with macros enabled.

The XL strip in OurPlanCore writes takeoffs into the workbook and runs the calculation macros itself. The other macros are run in Excel with a hotkey or through Alt+F8.

E-Wood tab

All these macros, plus the order, check and delivery buttons, are collected on the E-Wood tab, which installs from a single file: E-Wood tab in Excel. Some insert macros work differently from the tab than from the workbook: that is noted where it applies.

The macro does nothing

  1. The open workbook is made from the TemplateCom.xlsm template (a copy is in the app's updates folder), not someone else's file.
  2. Macros are enabled: File > Options > Trust Center > Macro Settings.
  3. The cursor is in the right place: insert macros work from the selected row, calculation macros from the selected range.
  4. The hotkey did not work: Alt+F8, pick the macro by name.

docs.title: Hotkeys
docs.text:
Hotkeys checked against the macro source code. Macros without a hotkey are run through Alt+F8 or a button.

Hotkey Macro What it does Ctrl+Shift+B C_BeamsSort beams from "mark and length" pairs into Beam rows Ctrl+Shift+J C_JoistsSort joists from "count and length" pairs into Joists rows Ctrl+Shift+H C_HeadersSort headers into width bins up to 48" / 60" / 72" / over 72" Ctrl+Shift+P C_PostsSort posts by mark with a legend Ctrl+Shift+F C_SumTheSameValues add up identical rows (key: label + unit) Ctrl+M Y_MultiplySelectedCells multiply the selected cells by an address (for example, by the header's G) Ctrl+Shift+I Y_Improve_Note rewrite a note's text following the samples on the Standarts worksheet (check the result by eye) Ctrl+Shift+T Y_CheckEnglish check the English in the selection Ctrl+Shift+O Y_InsertDate insert the date Ctrl+Shift+V Y_noValidation remove drop-down lists (data validation) Ctrl+W / Ctrl+Q Y_InsertCellsUp / X_DeleteCellsUp insert / delete cells A:H with a shift. Only this way, never a whole worksheet row Ctrl+E B_DeleteZeroRowsOnlyIn_AtoH delete rows with a zero quantity (A:H only) Ctrl+Shift+D X_DeleteRowsByColor delete the template's gray placeholder rows Ctrl+T B_FrameOC_InsertOneRow insert a Frame N" o.c. row under the selected one Ctrl+R B_Plate2_InsertOneRow insert a Plate (2) row under the selected one Alt+F8 B_BoltsAdd, C_TrimsCalc and the rest no hotkey Jumping between sections (Ctrl+F1 ... Alt+Shift+F9)

Some workbooks assign hotkeys on open that jump to a section header: Ctrl+F1 ... Ctrl+F5 1st ... 5th Floor Walls, Ctrl+F6 / Ctrl+F7 Gable Walls #1 / #2, Ctrl+F8 Parapet Walls, Ctrl+F9 Wall Materials, Ctrl+F11 / Ctrl+F12 Foundation / Basement Floor Walls; Alt+F1 ... Alt+F4 1st ... 4th Floor Framing List, Alt+F5 Loft Framing List, Alt+F6 / Alt+F7 Roof Frame list / Roof System Misc, Alt+F10 Roof Products, Alt+F11 / Alt+F12 Soffits and Fascias / Exterior Trims; Alt+Shift+F1 Interior Doors&Trims, Alt+Shift+F2 Drywall & Insulation, Alt+Shift+F8 / Alt+Shift+F9 balcony / porch by fill. The jump finds the header by its exact text.

Being verified

The current macro source code has no navigation module; if the hotkeys do not jump in a workbook, that is not a bug.

docs.title: Workbook order of work
docs.text:
1. In OurPlanCore: the LG legend is filled in (beam, post and header codes, detail flags, sheathing), then ALL or the needed buttons of the XL strip.
  2. In Excel: check that everything from the tree arrived (the export warning lists skipped takeoffs), fix J:N.
  3. Structural sorts, if something was entered by hand: Ctrl+Shift+B, Ctrl+Shift+J, Ctrl+Shift+H, Ctrl+Shift+P, then C_RimBoardBlockingHangers.
  4. Balcony, porch, holdown, bolt and jamb blocks (Blocks).
  5. Cleanup: Ctrl+Shift+D gray rows, Ctrl+E zeros, Ctrl+Shift+V validation.
  6. Final: Ctrl+Shift+O date, Ctrl+Shift+T English, notes per the rules, Front Page filled in, then the processed .xlsx.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Inserting a whole worksheet row instead of Ctrl+W: the right-hand areas shifted.
  • A9_* rerun on a filled workbook: it deleted needed rows.
  • C_BeamsSort without a legend: B shows the code H5 instead of the size.
  • A balcony block inserted by the macro on top of the template #1: two blocks.
  • A quantity typed in as a number after a macro: it will not update on the next export.

All workbook mistakes: Common mistakes, Excel DFL and notes.

docs.title: Formulas and factors
docs.text:
Here: the multipliers and column C formulas used in the workbook, and how studs differ from joists. Formulas are given in the English locale (CEILING, EVEN); in other locales Excel shows localized function names with ; between arguments, the meaning is the same.

Studs and joists use different tables

Studs and joists share the same o.c., but the multipliers differ: studs follow the owner's rule (a stud per foot plus waste), joists follow geometry (12 / spacing). Do not mix up the tables.

docs.title: Stud spacing factors
docs.text:
The canon for studs. At 16" o.c. count one stud per foot of wall plus 10 percent waste, not the geometric 0.75: this covers corners, T-intersections, jack, king and cripple studs at openings, and cutoffs.

Spacing Factor (pcs / LFT) Where it comes from 12" o.c. 1.4667 1:1 scaled 16 to 12 (x1.333) plus 10% waste 16" o.c. 1.1 1:1 plus 10% waste 24" o.c. 0.625 0.5 plus 25% waste
  • pcs = wall LFT x factor; stud height in column E of the row, to 1/8" (floor-to-floor minus subfloor, minus floor framing, minus plates).
  • Bearing walls as Extra: the main line with the regular factor, extra plies on a separate double extra row, subtract the base from the regular studs. Extra factors: 16" o.c. 0.75, 24" o.c. 0.5 (without the base row's waste).
  • A double wall = two frames only if the plan shows two frames; staggered corridor 2x4 = two rows at 16" o.c., 2x6 plates.

docs.title: Joist spacing factors
docs.text:
Joists, rafters and floor trusses follow the true center-to-center geometry, with no stud waste.

Spacing Factor (pcs / LFT of width) 12" o.c. 1.0 16" o.c. 0.75 19.2" o.c. 0.625 24" o.c. 0.5
  • pcs = span width LFT x 12 / spacing + 1 (an end joist for each run).
  • From OurPlanCore, joists come as "count / length" pairs from J Area: identical lengths are added together, a length over 8' that is odd gets +1 (the C_JoistsSort rule); short ones up to 7' go onto a double-length board (90 x 6' = 45 x 12', E shows 90 pcs 6'). Extra joists of the same length are added to the main row.
  • Hangers for joists: at both ends of each joist, by assembly; piece hardware under 50 rounds to an even number.

docs.title: Rim, ribbon, blocking, ledger
docs.text:
Item Unit Factor Rim Board, EWP jobs LFT 1.05 Rim Board, other jobs (residential, COM) LFT 1.1 Blocking, Ribbon, Ledger, Blocking for Drywall, bracing along walls LFT 1.1 once in the formula
  • Rim and blocking stay in LFT and are not divided into 16' pieces, unless the output explicitly requires pcs.
  • Top chord bearing trusses: instead of a ribbon board, blocking between trusses, often (2) 2x6.
  • Blocking at spacing is counted in pieces: formulas below.

docs.title: Blocking factor by type
docs.text:
Type Pieces per bay factor Flat 2 Diagonal 2.5 Vertical 1.5 ... 2

Walls 10' and taller get two rows of blocking. Kitchen: 2x6, 4 pieces at 14' per kitchen; bath: 1 piece at 14' per bathroom. Kickers only where the detail shows them.

docs.title: Column C formulas by row type
docs.text:
Row type C D 4x8 panels (sheathing, subfloor) =CEILING(G/32*1.1,1) 4x8 Linear stock by stock length =CEILING(G/D,1) (D = 14 or 16) LFT Plates =EVEN(G*H*1.1) (H = number of plates) LFT Studs =CEILING(G*1.1,1) at 16" o.c. pcs Hardware at spacing (anchors, ties, hangers) =CEILING(G*12/H*1.1,2); at 50 and more the template's own significance ,10 or ,1 pcs Screws at trusses =CEILING(...,3) pcs Washers =C<anchor row> or =SUM(...) as one row per group pcs H-clips by decking thickness and support spacing: PSCL at 16" = 6 per sheet, not "4 per sheet"; not needed with T&G or with decking thicker than the spec threshold pcs Truss bracing 2x6 by default, a row every 10'; =CEILING(G/4/D,1) over the whole area under the roof, including the garage pcs Panel adhesive =C<subfloor>/3 tubes Resilient channels =CEILING(area*12/spacing*1.1,10), only where the wall type shows them LFT Holdowns =G to concrete, =G*2 through a wood floor pcs Double-sided shear wall G = sum of the two faces, no extra x2 SQ FT

Formulas look at their own block: their own header, their own unit multiplier, their own floor. A copied floor with references into another block is the most common workbook mistake.

docs.title: Roofing
docs.text:
The pitch is applied once: plan area x sqrt(1 + (rise/12)^2).

Pitch Factor 4/12 1.054 6/12 1.118 8/12 1.202 12/12 1.414

Pitch from the sheet, each building has its own (garage 4/12 with the house at 6/12). The number in the name rf 6 is the rise per 12.

docs.title: Rounding
docs.text: What Rule Piece hardware under 50 up to an even number (significance 2) 50 and more template significance: ,10 for large ties and screws, ,1 for panels and strips Lumber, panels, pipes whole numbers, rounded up; 2.75 and 9.6 never appear in C Waste once: if G already includes 1.1, C has no second 1.1

docs.title: Shaft Walls
docs.text:
Shaft walls go in a separate block, even when the building walls are panels by others. Material from the wall type and the detail: it can be 2-1/2" CH + J-channel or 2" H + C-channel. Stock LF is usually 12; panels in the worksheet as 2x12 Panels.

2-1/2" CH + J:
1" Shaft Panels        = CEILING(LFT * 1.1 / 24, 2)
CH-channels vertical   = CEILING(LFT * 0.5 * 1.1 / Stock LF, 2)
J-channels horizontal  = CEILING(Horizontal LFT * 1.1 / Stock LF, 2)

2" H + C:
1" Shaft Panels, 2 layers = CEILING(LFT * 2 * 1.1 / 24, 2)
H-channels vertical       = CEILING(LFT * 0.5 * 1.1 / Stock LF, 2)
H-channels horizontal     = CEILING(Horizontal LFT * 2 * 1.1 / Stock LF, 2)
C-channels perimeter      = CEILING(Perimeter LFT * 1.1 / Stock LF, 2)

Dropped ceiling metal joists: 12" C-type = Area * 0.75 * 1.1 LF.

docs.title: Order-of-magnitude check
docs.text: If a number looks odd, compare it with what is typical for a similar building: Quantity benchmarks. This is a sanity check, not a norm; a discrepancy means "open the detail and the units", not "fix it to the average".

docs.title: Hangers
docs.text:
Here: how to pick a hanger by condition (what it carries, what it sits on, which mount, any skew or firewall) and how to write the model in the DFL. A hanger is picked by the condition and the project schedule, not by eyeballing the name.

Pick in 30 seconds

  1. Identify the member: Beam / LVL / PSL / GL, TJI, LPI, double joist.
  2. Identify the mount: Face Mount, Top Flange, Concealed Flange.
  3. Check the depth: joists deeper than 16" usually go to HIT, not ITS.
  4. Check skew and slope: ITS is not skewable.
  5. Check special conditions: firewall and double gypsum, Cedar, glulam, shear wall.

Selection flow: mount condition first, then depth, skew and special conditions.

docs.title: Quick pick
docs.text:
• Face Mount

    The hanger hangs on the side face of the support. Usually HU, HHUS, HGUS, IUS, MIU, SUL / SUR.

  • Top Flange

    The hanger sits on top of the support. For joists it is ITS / MIT, for beams WP, GLT / GLTV, LBV.

  • Concealed Flange

    The flange is hidden inside the connection: HUC / HUCQ, LUC. Do not quietly swap this hanger for a regular face mount: check the detail and fasteners.

  • Skew / Slope

    There is an angle - do not use ITS. Face mount: SUL / SUR (45 degrees), other angle LSSR; top flange: LBV ... XL45 / XR45; LPI slope and skew: LSSU / LSSUH / LSSUI.

  • Deep Joist

    Joists deeper than 16" - the HIT family, for example HIT420. ITS only up to 16" inclusive.

  • Firewall / Double Gypsum

    DHU / DGU only where joists hang through firewall double gypsum: stairs, elevators, shafts. A regular demising wall, where the gypsum stops under the floor framing, gets ITS.

docs.title: Critical rules
docs.text:
• ITS - top flange for I-joist only and only up to 16" deep; there is no skewed ITS.
  • Skewed top mount: WP / HUTF / LBV per detail; skewed face mount: SUL / SUR / HSUR.
  • EWP (LVL, PSL, GL, TJI, LPI): keep the exact family and section, do not turn it into a generic hanger.
  • Model per the detail: the detail says U210-2 - write U210-2, not LUS210-2.
  • Hangers on both ends of every joist, counted by assemblies on the plan, not by purchase boards after the cut list; whole pieces only.
  • Exterior and on P.T. - Zmax. H2.5A ties to trusses under the sheathing - no Zmax unless the detail says otherwise.
  • Repeated area (units x N): check that the hanger count repeats as many times as the framing.
  • The project schedule wins over the tables below; the tables are a hint, not a replacement for the engineer's detail.

docs.text:
Column B format, as in delivered jobs.

Rule Do Don't Zmax as a separate word after the model ABU66 Zmax, LUS210 Zmax, HHUS410 Zmax SK30 R ABU66Z, LSSR28Z, LUS210Z Angle and hand as the suffix SK<angle> <L or R> HHUS410 Zmax SK30 R, HU612 Zmax SK60 L skew 30 deg, special order, HDG in B Skewed on sawn 2x: SUL left hand, SUR right hand, a separate row for each hand and each angle SUL28 Zmax 12 pcs, SUR28 Zmax 16 pcs; angle in E skewed 30° one row "all skewed as one SKU" LSSR only for an angle outside the SUL / SUR range LSSR28 Zmax, E skewed 60° LSSR on all skewed Fire hangers only over stair, elevator, shaft walls DHU210-2 with E = detail DHU on a regular demising wall Ties H2.5A without Zmax to trusses; H3 on both sides of the truss if the detail says so; spacing = truss spacing; all bearing lines H2.5A Zmax under sheathing, ties only on exterior walls Quantity pcs, by assemblies, whole; under 50 - round up to even by boards after the cut list

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Hangers not on both ends, or counted by purchase boards instead of assemblies.
  • No Zmax on the exterior; bases are Zmax but hangers are not.
  • LUS210-2 instead of the model from the detail; ITS on a skewed condition.
  • All skewed on one row without splitting by hand and angle.
  • DHU on a regular demising wall; ties not on all bearing lines or not at truss spacing.

All mistakes: Floor framing and beams.

docs.title: Final check
docs.text:
• Family, size, skew, top or face mount, support condition checked against the detail.
  • The schedule on the plan wins over the default table.
  • The connection looks non-standard - open the detail, do not guess from the thumbnail.
  • Repeated areas: the count repeats as many times as the framing.

docs.title: How to check a rule
docs.text:
1. Find the sheet, schedule, detail or spec section of your own project.
  2. Check whether the rule applies to this material, connection and scope.
  3. For a product, open the manufacturer's page for the right series.
  4. When sources conflict, write down both sheets and the decision made in a note (Notes in DFL); do not hide an assumption by swapping the material.
  5. After the calculation, go through the QA checklist.

docs.title: Jobs and saving
docs.text:
Here: the start screen, how to create or open a job, add a PDF or another job to it, what the .ourplan file is, how autosave works, what to do if a job did not save or is already open in another window, and where a job takes up space. Needed at job intake, for a revision and before handing a job over.

In short

A job is one .ourplan file. Copy and hand it over only after Save: Saved hh:mm:ss in the status bar. Old folder-based jobs keep the folder format: for them, copy the whole folder.

Everything about jobs is in one menu, Main > Open / Import. Ctrl+O opens the same menu.

docs.title: Open / Import menu: reference
docs.text:
Menu item What it does Open project... job picker window: job folders on the left (SOURCES, + Add folder), a name filter, a list with dates; at the bottom Open, PDF project, Blank project, links Sample, Open project file... for an .ourplan outside the folders, Manage folders...; the Remove folder button removes the selected folder from the SOURCES list, the files on disk stay Blank project - start empty name, location for the .ourplan; sheets are added later via Page > Add Pages or Blank Sheet New project from a folder of PDFs... a folder of PDFs (with subfolders), job name, .ourplan file; sheets go into Pages/00. imported Import PDF Takeoffs... a PDF with someone else's takeoff annotations, for old jobs (import) Sample job (demo to explore) a demo job with no client data (demo tour) Import into the current job > ... add a PDF, a folder of PDFs, another OurPlanCore job or a PlanSwift project to the open job (below) Undo Last Page Sort, Undo Last Page Operation undo the last sort or sheet operation (import, move) Project Data Recovery... recovery of protected job files (if something went missing) Manage job folders... add or pick the folder where jobs are kept

Ctrl+Shift+O opens the list of recent jobs. A job from intake already comes with sheet names, folders and W/F/S/U dots, so a newcomer usually needs only Open project....

In the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) the same items have shorter names: Open / Import, Open Project File, Open Recent Job, Open Jobs Folder (pick a jobs folder, it is added to SOURCES and its job list opens), New PDF Job (a job from a folder of PDFs), Blank Job, Create Sample Job. The Show Main View command returns to the sheet from Settings or Sheet Manager, like clicking the Main View tab.

docs.title: Start screen
docs.text: The card in the center of the window is visible while no job is open. The Open / Import menu on the Main ribbon works here too. Tile What it does Open a recent job / Recently used list of recent jobs, like Ctrl+Shift+O New blank job / Start empty an empty job: name and location for the .ourplan, sheets are added later New job from PDFs / Import a folder of drawings a job from a folder of PDFs (steps) Open sample job / Explore a demo creates and opens the demo job (demo tour)

docs.title: How to open a job
docs.text:
Why: to continue working on a job from the jobs folder or from a file.

  1. Press Ctrl+O or Main > Open / Import > Open project... (on the start screen, the Open a recent job tile).
  2. Pick the source folder on the left; if needed, type part of the name in the filter.
  3. Click the job in the list and press Open. A file outside the job folders opens with the Open project file... link.

Result: the job name in the window title and the status bar, the sheet folders expand in Pages, the status shows Save: Saved.

In Lite, double-clicking an .ourplan file does not launch the app: Lite does not register itself as the program for these files. Open the job as described above, or drag the file into the window (Lite vs full version).

docs.title: How to create a job from PDFs
docs.text:
Why: a new job from the client's drawing folder. You need: a folder of PDF sheets (subfolders are fine).

  1. Press Main > Open / Import > New project from a folder of PDFs... and pick the drawings folder.
  2. Type the job name in the format <number>. <name> (the number at the start is needed by the In Progress button and the pipeline) and a location for the .ourplan file.
  3. In the Import PDF Options window leave the raster checkbox on (below) and confirm.
  4. Wait until the sheets land in Pages/00. imported.

Result: the job is open, sheets are in 00. imported with names Page N or names read from the title block. Next: Name+Scale and sorting into folders: Sheets.

docs.title: How to add a PDF or a job to the open job
docs.text:
Why: a new sheet set for a revision, missing sheets, buildings from different jobs. You need: the right job open (its name in the window title): the import goes into it.

Route What is added Where Import into the current job > PDF file(s)... or Page > Add Pages one or more PDFs, with confirmation of sheet names Pages/00. imported Import into the current job > Folder of PDFs... all PDFs from a folder and subfolders, without asking about each one Pages/00. imported Import into the current job > OurPlanCore project... another job (.ourplan or a folder with Data.xml, Pages, Takeoffs) separate branches in Pages and Takeoffs (steps) Import into the current job > PlanSwift project..., Main > PDF Takeoffs old jobs: a PlanSwift project, takeoffs from PDF annotations (import) groups 01. planswift, from pdf Page > Blank Sheet a blank sheet of a given size (dialog with presets) the selected Pages folder

docs.title: How to bring in another OurPlanCore job
docs.text:
Why: to combine buildings from different jobs or bring an old job into a revision.

  1. Press Main > Open / Import > Import into the current job > OurPlanCore project...: the Import OurPlanCore into Current Job window opens, the Destination line shows the open job's name.
  2. Choose Choose .ourplan file... or Choose project folder... (a folder with Data.xml, Pages, Takeoffs).
  3. Read the number of sheets, takeoffs and measurements in the dialog and type the name for the new branches in the Folder name in Pages and Takeoffs field (for example REV 2).
  4. Press Import.

Result: everything is added as separate folders in Pages and Takeoffs; existing content and job settings are not touched; importing again gives another branch. Crop links to sheets of the other job are not reassigned on import. To undo any import: Open / Import > Undo Last Page Operation.

docs.title: The .ourplan file and the working folder
docs.text:
• A job is stored as one .ourplan file. On opening, the app unpacks it into a working copy and works with that; Save packs the file back.
  • The job name is shown in the window title, the status bar and the recent list. If the file was renamed in File Explorer, the new file name is shown; nothing is written inside the package.
  • Save As... (Ctrl+Shift+S, the Save As button on the Main ribbon or the Export menu in Takeoffs) creates a new .ourplan in the chosen location and keeps the format of the open job. Do not change the extension or format by hand.
  • Moving to another computer: copy a successfully saved .ourplan. In the full version, through a shared Workspace the job opens without copying: Workspace.

docs.title: Autosave and the Save status
docs.text:
Measurements are written to the working copy right away, the .ourplan file is updated in a separate step. Copy only the file after a successful Save.

Saving happens in two steps:

  1. Every measurement and tree edit is written to the working copy right away.
  2. The .ourplan file is rebuilt automatically after a few seconds of inactivity, at least every couple of minutes, and on Ctrl+S.
Status Meaning Save: Saved 14:32:10 the file was updated at this time; safe to copy Save: Pending there are changes not yet written to the file Save: Saving... writing in progress; do not close the app Save: Failed with the time of the next attempt the write failed; the work stays in the working copy. The app retries after 30, 60 and 120 seconds, then every 5 minutes until it saves. Ctrl+S starts an attempt right away; copy the .ourplan only after Save: Saved Save: Protected data - open Project Data Recovery the job file cannot be read or is damaged; a temporarily unavailable file is checked again by the app, a damaged one needs manual recovery

Retry intervals can be changed in Settings > Autosave Recovery: After first failure, After second failure, After third failure, After later failures in seconds. Defaults are 30, 60, 120, 300; 5-3600 seconds are allowed, in non-decreasing order. The category has Apply, Reset, Save global default, Save as this job and Clear job override.

docs.title: How to hand over or copy a job
docs.text:
Why: a copy on another drive, handing over to a coworker, a restore point before a risky edit.

  1. Press Ctrl+S and wait for Save: Saved hh:mm:ss.
  2. Copy the .ourplan under a separate name or to another drive (for an old folder-based job, the whole folder).
  3. Open the copy itself and check a few sheets, measurements and the export.
  4. Keep the previous copy until the result is checked.

Result: the working copy and the backup match. A message about local recovery means the data is only in the working copy and the file has not been updated yet. .snapshots inside the job stores metadata snapshots; it is not a backup of PDFs, settings or the app.

docs.title: If a job did not save or something went missing
docs.text: Symptom What to do Measurements are not on screen check the active sheet, the takeoff's visibility (the dot at the sheet in Pages, H), the selected job; for an old folder-based job Setup > Repair page links. Do not redraw until the cause is clear Save: Failed keep the app open; it will retry saving by itself, and Ctrl+S tries right away. Wait for Save: Saved; if the error persists, Save As... to another location. Do not delete the working copy Save: Protected data if the file is temporarily locked, the app checks it every 30 seconds and lifts the protection only after successfully loading the same data. If the file is damaged or the protection stays, open Open / Import > Project Data Recovery... and choose Retry reading or Restore from copy... from a known good copy; after recovery the app rereads the data The .ourplan file does not open accept the offer to open the saved local recovery; Project Data Recovery does not repair the archive Save failed after moving a sheet between folders fixed in the current build; if it happens again: Troubleshooting No space when opening the app needs space for the working copy; free up disk space outside the job and recovery folders A quantity changed unexpectedly check the sheet scale, units, the active sheet and which takeoff the measurement belongs to; auto-scale must be checked against a known dimension

docs.title: If the job is already open in another window
docs.text: While a job is open, the app keeps an owner mark on it and refreshes it every 5 seconds. A second OurPlanCore window or a second computer opening the same file gets the Job Is Already Open window: job path, Owner, Machine, Process, Started, Heartbeat, Version.

docs.title: How to open a job held by another window
docs.text:
Why: to view or take over a job without corrupting it with two simultaneous writes.

  1. Read Machine and Heartbeat. If the owner is another window of yours, save and close it, then press Retry.
  2. You only need to look: press Open Read-Only. The window title shows [READ-ONLY], saving and editing are disabled.
  3. The owner crashed or hung, the mark has not been refreshed for 30 seconds: the badge changes to STALE LEASE and the Take Over button becomes available. Press it and confirm in the Confirm Risky Take Over window.
  4. If in doubt, press Cancel, and opening is canceled.

Result: the job is open for writing (after Retry or Take Over) or read-only.

Take Over while the owner is alive

If the other window is actually working, two windows write to one job and can corrupt it. Take over only when you know for sure the owner is closed or hung.

docs.title: Raster on import and Sheet Manager
docs.text:
In Import PDF Options, the Build readable raster cache and strict black-line snap index checkbox prepares a raster of the sheets and an index of black lines for PDF Snap. It takes longer and uses space, but sheets open faster and Ctrl+F3 snaps to lines. The choice is remembered. For sheets already imported, the raster is prepared in the Sheet Manager tab (a module): select the sheets, Prepare, then First On (steps). Otherwise, scans without a text layer are not named or scaled automatically.

In Sheet Manager, the Options... button opens the raster format: Auto (default, WebP where possible), WebP or PNG for difficult PDFs that look like scans. The set of DPI buttons is edited in Settings > Defaults, section Sheet Manager raster DPI presets (Settings).

docs.title: Project Storage
docs.text: Analysis buttons at the top, the report by section below. The analysis only reads the job.

docs.title: How to check where a job takes up space
docs.text:
Why: to understand why an .ourplan grew large and safely compact what can be compacted. You need: the job open; for compacting, not read-only.

  1. Open Settings > Project Storage and press Analyze project.
  2. Read the report sections (table below). The analysis does not change any files.
  3. Press Preview safe compact: the Safe compact preview section shows how much space compacting will free.
  4. If the savings are above zero, press Compact snap.json... and confirm. Only formatting whitespace in the snap.json snap indexes is compacted; PDFs, raster, recovery history, takeoffs and measurements are not deleted.

Result: the status shows Compacted N file(s); saved ...; for a fresh report press Analyze project again.

Section What it shows Project format new jobs are always one portable .ourplan file; old folder-based jobs stay folders and are saved in place Current project name, number of files and total size Storage breakdown size by group: job data, sheet raster (rebuildable), recovery history, duplicate source PDFs, PDFs not referenced by a sheet, PDFs to review, other Safe compact preview how much of snap.json can be compacted and how much that saves Review-only findings duplicate source PDFs, PDFs not referenced by a sheet, external sheet dependencies. For information only: nothing is deleted here, such files may be needed for recovery Details the first lines of findings: DUP (duplicate), REVIEW (review), WARN (warning)

This is not a cleanup of recovery data and caches on the computer. Unused raster variants of the selected sheets are removed by Clean in Sheet Manager; for all sheets on app close, the Clean unused raster cache on close checkbox in Settings > Defaults (the active raster and snap index stay).

What is inside a job (advanced) 

Data.xml                     job card
sources/                     source PDFs
Pages/.../<sheet>/
  Data.xml, source.json      name, source, scale
  source_pdf.json            metadata for Name/Scale
  takeoff_routing.json       the sheet's W/F/S/U dot
  annotations.json           markup, Hide masks, crops
  layers.json, raster/       PDF layers, raster
Takeoffs/.../<takeoff>/
  Data.xml, measurements.json
AI_Context/settings/         settings of this job (routing, shortcuts, modules)
AI_Context/project.md        job notes for AI: observations and AI answers
AI_Context/*-trash           undo bins for Merge and the agent
3D_Context/walls_model.json  3D model
bookmarks.json, import_reports/
The folder on disk may have a technical name; the visible name is stored in Data.xml. Do not edit job files by hand while the app is running. The exception is AI_Context/project.md, the log of AI observations and answers for the job: with the AI module (full version), right-click a sheet, Open Project Context opens it in Notepad. The app only appends to the end, so your own notes there are kept.

docs.title: OurPlanCoreCli: the pipeline console
docs.text:
A separate program with no window, used by the intake and delivery pipeline; the estimator does not run it but sees the result: the job arrives already with sheet names, folders and W/F/S/U dots, and at delivery the PDF is assembled by building. It is not related to the full version's AI terminal.

Command What it does Options create a new .ourplan from PDFs; with --base-project, a revision package on top of the original job --name, --package, --pdf (several), --raster-dpi (150), --no-raster, --base-project, --import-folder REV, --report inspect a report on the package's sheets, folders and measurements --package, --report apply-sheets apply sheet names, folders, scale and dots from JSON; makes a backup of the package --package, --sheets, --dry-run, --report export-pdf a PDF with only the sheets that have measurements; --grouping auto splits by building based on the green dot, --grouping single makes one file --package, --out, --grouping, --dry-run, --overwrite, --report excel-plan an Excel export plan based on the tree --package, --scope <path under Takeoffs>, --report

Each command prints one JSON; exit codes: 0 success, 1 command error, 2 invocation error. Commands that change the package refuse to run while the app is open: Refused to ...: OurPlanCore is running. Close it first. The export takes the PDF Output settings from the job: Opac, the legend and its groups, overlays, crops and masks.

docs.title: 3D roof
docs.text:
Full version only

OurPlanCore Lite has no 3D module: no 3D tab and no Roof Base. In Lite, the roof is measured with roof plane areas with the pitch in the name (Roof) and edges with lines (Ridge / Valley / Hip). How the versions differ: Lite vs full version.

Here: how to turn roof plane and eave areas into a 3D roof on the 3D tab, set the pitch of edges, add overhangs and rafters, and pull ridge, hip, valley and eave lengths from the model into the Takeoffs tree. You need it on a complex roof (L, U, several pitches, dormer) when the plan does not show where hips and valleys run, and when the client asks for edge lengths. A simple gable roof is measured without 3D: an Area per roof plane with the pitch in the name (Roof). Walls in 3D, the general viewer and the archived Massing: 3D and Massing.

Demo on a real job: select the roof area rf 4, 3D > Auto builds a hip roof; a second roof from a second area, picked in Roof Mesh.

The 3D ribbon (Build, Rafters, Viewer), the scene window and the side panel: Default pitch, the Roof Edge block, the Roof Mesh list, the Roof Qty tabs and the log.

docs.title: How the model works
docs.text:
Concept What it is Where it comes from Roof Base the roof outline in plan, the base of the model selected Areas: rf 6, rf mtl 4, flat from sqfts, or any area from the sheet Edge a side of the outline; an edge has the properties Defines Slope, Pitch, Overhang created with the Roof Base, one per side of the outline Eave an edge with Defines Slope: a roof plane rises from it at the given pitch you set it, or Auto sets it on all edges Rake an edge with no slope: gable end uncheck Defines Slope Roof Mesh, group the generated roof of one base; a job can have several (main house, garage, dormer) each Roof Base makes its own group, the active one is picked in the Roof Mesh list Ridge, Hip, Valley the seams between roof planes calculated by Generate Roof Rafters rafters on the faces Pick Faces or Whole Roof

The model is stored in the job (3D_Context/walls_model.json) and survives closing; a roof plane's color comes from the color of the source Area takeoff. The generator builds the roof "by footprint" like Revit: each eave edge rises at its own pitch, the edges meet in hips and valleys at one height. The roof stays a draft for checking: it knows nothing about windows, second-level roof planes or cutouts.

docs.title: How to build a roof from roof plane areas
docs.text:
What for: see the ridge, hips and valleys on a complex outline and get their lengths. Needed: the 3D module is on (Settings > Modules), the roof plan has roof plane Areas with the sheet scale set.

There are two ways. Auto builds a full hip roof right away: all outline edges become eaves with one pitch. Roof Base creates only the outline, and you set the edge pitches yourself. On one area, pick one way: Auto with a selected area always creates a new group, and after Roof Base on the same area the model will have two roofs.

The fast way, Auto:

  1. Open sheet a105 rf and select the roof plane areas on the sheet with the Select tool (or the takeoffs rf 6, rf mtl 4 in Takeoffs).
  2. Open the 3D tab and type the default pitch in the Default box of the side panel: 6/12, 4 or 0.333.
  3. Press Build > Auto. Status: 3D Auto Roof: Roof 1, full hip from N eave edge(s), pitch 6/12, generated M roof mesh face(s).
  4. For gables, switch the needed edges to Rake (below) and press Generate Roof.

The manual way, Roof Base:

  1. Select the roof plane areas, as in step 1 above.
  2. Press Build > Roof Base (or right-click the sheet, 3D > Create Roof Base from Areas).
  3. Read the status: 3D Roof Base: created Roof 1, 1 base layer(s), N selectable edge(s). Select slope edges and apply pitch. The outline appears in the scene as a flat slab, all edges are Rake for now, edge selection mode is on.
  4. Set the pitch on the eave edges (below) and press Generate Roof.

Result: status Roof generated: Roof 1, N mesh face(s) with area and length totals; in the scene, roof planes in the takeoff color, seams as single lines. Viewer > Iso, Top, Front, Fit turn the camera.

Tips

  • Auto with nothing selected takes all rf and roof takeoffs of the job and builds a new group from them. If there are no such takeoffs but a Roof Base already exists, Auto sets the pitch from Default on all its edges. The status select RF/roof area takeoffs first means there are neither takeoffs nor a base.
  • The Auto and Wall buttons rebuild walls and slabs but leave the created roofs and their edge settings in place.
  • An area without a sheet scale is skipped, with a counter in the status: set the scale and repeat.
  • Several roofs (house and garage): a separate Roof Base for each area, the active group is picked in the Roof Mesh list.

docs.title: How to set edge pitch
docs.text:
Demo: Roof Base, edge selection, Defines Slope at 6/12 pitch and Save Edge(s), one edge at 12/12, Generate Roof.

What for: different pitches on roof planes, a gable instead of a hip, an overhang of the right width. Needed: a Roof Base exists.

  1. Press Build > Select Edge (status on the sheet: 3D Roof Edge Select: click a roof base edge...).
  2. Click an edge on the sheet; Ctrl or Shift with a left or right click adds edges to the selection (a right click with the key does not open the sheet menu). A Pitch window opens next to the edge (with several edges, Pitch x3).
  3. Type the pitch 6/12, 4 or 0.333 and press Enter: the edge became an eave with that pitch. Esc closes the window without changes.
  4. For a gable, open the Roof Edge block in the side panel, uncheck Defines Slope (eave) and press Save Edge(s); right-click on the edge does the same: 3D > Set Edge as Rake. Back: Set Edge as Eave + Pitch 6/12.
  5. Type Overhang in (overhang in inches, for example 12 or 24) and press Save Edge(s): the roof plane extends past the wall by that amount.
  6. Press Generate Roof.

Result: status 3D Roof: saved edge properties to N edge(s) and then Roof generated; the Roof Edge block shows the pitch and overhang of the selected edge, gable edges do not raise a roof plane.

The 3D sub-tab next to Takeoffs: the Roof Base, Select Edge buttons, the Default box, the Roof Edge block with the Defines Slope (eave) checkbox, Pitch, Overhang in and Save Edge(s), below it the Roof Mesh list with offset sliders.

Tips

  • The error invalid edge pitch means a wrong format: only 6/12, 4 or a decimal rise per foot.
  • The pitch can be taken from finished eave lines: select the takeoffs eve 24 main in Takeoffs and apply them to the base edges from their 3D menu; matching edges get the pitch from the Default box (status matched N roof edge(s) from selected eave line takeoff(s)).
  • The same actions are in the right-click menu on an edge on the sheet, the 3D submenu: the header Roof Edge - <type> | <pitch>, then Add Edge to Selection (on an already selected edge, Remove Edge from Selection) adds the edge to the selection without Ctrl, Set Edge as Eave + Pitch ... and Set Edge as Rake apply to all selected edges.
  • Clear the edge selection: right-click the sheet, 3D > Clear Edge Selection; turn the mode off: Select Edge again or any sheet tool (Line, Select, Pan...).

docs.title: How to move a roof and work with groups
docs.text:
What for: the roof and the walls were drawn from different sheets and do not line up; the job has several roofs; the roof of a low building landed at the height of the tallest one.

  1. Pick the group in the Roof Mesh list of the side panel (status 3D Roof: selected Roof 2): pitch, move, reset and delete act on it.
  2. Press Move Roof and drag the roof in the 3D window: the gizmo moves it along an axis, status dragging Roof 2 on X-axis; the motion is slowed down for precise fitting.
  3. Press Reset Pos to put the roof back where it was built.
  4. Delete an extra group with the delete button by the Roof Mesh list; the whole roof together with its edges is removed with right-click on the sheet, 3D > Clear Roof Base.

Result: the roof sits on the walls, the list has only the groups you need.

docs.title: How to get rafters and check lengths
docs.text:
Demo: 24" spacing, 2x8 member, Whole Roof; the status shows the rafter count and the linear footage.

What for: estimate the number and lengths of rafters per face, see the member depth under the roof plane. Needed: the roof is generated (Roof Base, edges, Generate Roof), otherwise the status is Rafters: generate the roof first.

  1. In the Rafters group, pick the spacing in the first list (tooltip Rafter spacing o.c.: 12", 16", 19.2", 24", measured horizontally along the eave) and the member in the second (tooltip Rafter member size: 2x6, 2x8, 2x10, 2x12; the member depth goes down from the roof plane, the walls are trimmed to the bottom of the rafters). Default 16" and 2x10.
  2. Press Whole Roof for all faces, or Pick Faces and click faces in the 3D window to turn rafters on one at a time.
  3. Read the status: Rafters 2x10 @16" o.c.: 86 pcs, 1240 ft (4 face(s)) - 24 @ 18.5 ft, ...: count, total length and a breakdown by length.
  4. Check the lengths against the section: rafter length along the slope equals the horizontal run times the pitch factor, plus the overhang.
  5. Press Clear to remove the rafters.

Result: the rafters show in the scene under the roof planes, the walls are trimmed to their bottom edge, the numbers are in the status and the 3D log.

docs.title: What the 3D roof gives to the tree
docs.text:
What for: seam lengths and roof plane area as takeoffs you can check and use.

  1. In Takeoffs, select the folder for the result (otherwise the takeoffs go to the root or to the green-dot building).
  2. Press Roof Qty in the side panel: the tab shows Sloped and Plan area in SF, Ridge, Hip, Valley, Eave lengths in feet and the number of faces.
  3. Press Roof Takeoff.

Result: status 3D Roof Takeoff: created N reviewable takeoff item(s) and new takeoffs in the selected folder:

Takeoff Type What is inside Roof Eave Line edges with Defines Slope, length in plan Roof Ridge, Roof Hip, Roof Valley Line the seams the generator found Roof Area (plan) Area the base outline in plan

The Notes of each takeoff have a summary: Generated from 3D roof. Sloped ... SF, plan ... SF, ridge ... ft, hip ... ft, valley ... ft, eave ... ft. The measurements sit on the sheet where the base is and go into its legend.

Link with Excel and the DFL: these takeoffs are a check, not a replacement for the canon. The workbook gets the takeoffs the XL strip reads: roof planes rf 6 from sqfts (the SF button calculates roofing by the pitch in the name), eaves eve 24 main and rake 12 main from eves rakes (the E/R button, overhang in inches from the name). Roof Eave lengths from 3D are checked against the eve total, Roof Hip and Roof Valley help check hips and valleys in the roof details; after checking, the 3D takeoffs can be deleted or kept in a separate 3d check folder so they do not get into the export. Measuring rules: Roof, Eve.

docs.title: Roof guide mode keys
docs.text: For manual guides on the sheet (when the base does not give the seam you need): R Ridge, H Hip, V Valley, E Eave, K Rake, P Pitch; Backspace or Ctrl+Z back, Esc cancels the line or exits. Two clicks create a guide, Snap and Ortho work. The full key list: Keyboard shortcuts.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Change the pitch of one group
  1. Pick the group in Roof Mesh (for example Roof 2, the garage).
  2. Select Edge, Shift and clicks on all garage eave edges.
  3. In the Pitch x4 window type 4/12, Enter.
  4. Generate Roof: only this group is rebuilt, the main house does not change.
Dormer as an extra group
  1. Draw an Area along the dormer outline on the roof plan (rf dormer 8).
  2. Select it, Roof Base: Roof 2 appears.
  3. Select Edge: make the front dormer edge Rake (gable), leave the sides as eaves at 8/12, Generate Roof.
  4. Move Roof to lift the dormer onto the main roof plane if it sat lower; check in Iso.
  5. The generator does not cut the dormer's intersection with the main roof plane: the valley along the joint is measured on the plan by hand.
Get rafters and check lengths
  1. The roof is generated; in Rafters pick 16" and 2x10.
  2. Whole Roof, read the status with the breakdown by length.
  3. Check the longest group against the section; a difference bigger than the overhang means a wrong edge pitch or the wrong Overhang.

docs.title: Limits and common mistakes
docs.text:
• The generator builds the roof from the outer outline: cutouts, a second level of roof planes, dormer intersection with the main roof, fascia and true overhangs at hips and valleys are planned (ideas).
  • A self-intersecting outline is straightened to a convex hull: extra areas in the scene mean a crooked Area outline on the plan.
  • Different pitches on neighboring eaves meet correctly, but check the result in Iso: a gap along a seam is a sign of an edge with no pitch that should be an eave.
  • Roof Base with no area selected just shows the status select area measurements or RF/roof area takeoffs first.
  • The roof is placed at the highest point of the model: the top of the tallest walls, level or slab in the whole job. In a job with buildings of different heights, the roof of the low building will float above its walls: lower it with Move Roof along the vertical axis (groups) and check in Front.
  • Roof ... takeoffs from 3D got into the Excel export: keep them in a separate folder or delete them after checking.
  • 3D does not replace Areas per roof plane with the pitch in the name: SF in Excel reads rf 6, not Roof Area (plan).

docs.title: 3D and Massing
docs.text:
Full version only

OurPlanCore Lite has no 3D module, and it cannot be turned on. How the versions differ: Lite vs full version.

Here: the 3D tab, which is off by default: walls and slabs from measurements, the general viewer, and the honest status of the old AI Massing. You need it when you want to see a building in 3D or when someone asks "what about 3D". The roof in 3D is described separately: 3D roof. The Sheet Manager, Takeoff Manager, Report Builder and Materials tabs: Managers.

Demo: the 3D tab on a demo job: walls, a slab and a gable roof; rotating with the mouse, the Front and Iso views.

docs.title: Status in short
docs.text: What Status in 3.0 Where 3D walls and slabs from measurements works, no AI Settings > Modules > 3D, the 3D tab 3D roof from edges, Roof Qty, Roof Takeoff, rafters works 3D roof AI 3D Massing (Build 3D Draft, Review, Accept) turned off in code since May 2026, archive nowhere

docs.title: How to turn it on and what is on the tab
docs.text:
1. Open Settings > Modules, check 3D, press Save global default (or Apply until restart).
  2. A 3D tab appeared in the mode bar; a 3D sub-tab appeared under Takeoffs.
  3. To get to them without the mouse, open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P): Show 3D Viewer opens the 3D tab in the mode bar, Show 3D Tab selects the 3D sub-tab next to Takeoffs.
Demo: Settings > Modules, the AI and 3D checkboxes, Apply and Save global default; the 3D tab appeared in the mode bar. The 3D ribbon (Build, Rafters, Viewer), the scene window and the side panel with edge pitches and the log. Group Button What it does Build Auto walls from Line, slabs from sqft Areas and roofs from RF Areas, if there are any Build Wall wall prisms from the selected Line takeoffs Build Roof Base, Select Edge, Generate Roof roof: 3D roof Rafters Pick Faces, Whole Roof, spacing, member, Clear rafters: 3D roof Viewer Fit, Iso, Top, Front, Reset camera

The model is stored in the job (3D_Context/walls_model.json) and survives closing; it can be rebuilt at any time, and it does not change the measurements.

docs.title: How to raise walls and slabs
docs.text:
What for: see the building in 3D and check that the wall heights in the names agree between floors. Needed: walls drawn as Line with the height in the name (ext 2x6 9.09), floor areas as Area in sqfts.

  1. Select the wall takeoffs in Takeoffs (or nothing, if you need the whole building).
  2. Open the 3D tab and press Build > Auto: walls from all Line takeoffs, slabs from sqft Areas, a roof from RF Areas if present. Or Build > Wall for the selected lines only.
  3. Press Viewer > Iso, then Fit.
  4. Click a wall in the scene: the Details block of the side panel shows its height and thickness; type Height ft and Width in, press Apply Wall for one segment or Apply Group for all segments of the takeoff.

Result: floors are stacked by wall height, slabs sit at floor levels, walls are trimmed to the rafters if a roof with rafters is already built. The status 3D viewer ready... changes to the number of walls built.

Tips

  • The wall height is taken from the takeoff name in feet: a wall without a number gets the default height and the floor "sags". This is a handy name check before Excel.
  • Edits in 3D (height, thickness) live in the model and do not change takeoff names or the tree.

docs.title: Massing: what is turned off and why
docs.text: The old AI 3D Massing workflow (the Build 3D Draft, Review Roof / Openings, Accept 3D buttons) has been turned off in code since May 2026 and does not show in the interface. The AI model drafts needed a manual check of every wall and roof, while the deterministic roof from edge pitches gives the same result with no network and no surprises. The code stays in the repository as an archive; removing it is on the plan. If old notes mention "AI massing", they mean this archive.

docs.title: AI console: Claude, Codex and DeepSeek terminals
docs.text:
Full version only

OurPlanCore Lite has no terminal: no >_ button, no palette command, no Settings > Terminals. How the versions differ: Lite vs full version. The rest of the full version block: AI in the app.

Here: the >_ panel with Claude, Codex and DeepSeek terminals inside the app window, what they know about the job (the ctx line, the context file), how to send the assistant a sheet crop, how it edits the open job through Agent Bridge and how to continue a conversation on a second computer. You need it when you want to ask the assistant about the current sheet, get notes from a schedule table or hand it routine work in the tree without leaving the app. The other AI features (AI Crop Notes, AI Manager, title block reading, Agent Bridge settings) are on AI in the app.

Demo: the >_ button opens the console: pick Codex or Claude, the Quick / Balanced / Deep level, a context line with the job and the sheet.

The >_ panel to the right of the sheet: the Codex / Claude switch, Run and Attach, the ctx line with counters, context buttons and the Git Bash terminal itself inside the window.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
• Git for Windows (Git Bash, mintty.exe): the terminal lives in it.
  • The assistant CLI (claude or codex) is installed and you have logged in once on this computer.
  • Without Workspace: launch shortcuts in Settings > Terminals (by default Codex - E-Wood (bash).lnk and Claude - E-Wood (bash).lnk on the desktop; a mintty shortcut or an E-Wood bash launcher with the single line start mintty works). With Workspace on, no shortcut is needed: the app starts mintty from the managed folder itself (Workspace).
  • For edits in the job: Settings > Agent Bridge > Enable local assistant access (Agent Bridge). For crops into the console: the AI module.

docs.title: How to run the assistant in the window
docs.text:
What for: Claude or Codex next to the drawing, with live job context. Needed: Git Bash and the assistant CLI installed (above).

  1. Press >_ on the right command strip (palette command Codex / Claude / DeepSeek Terminal): the panel opens to the right of the sheet.
  2. Pick the Claude, Codex or DeepSeek profile. DeepSeek runs through the local Codex CLI; requests sent are billed through the API.
  3. Pick the effort in the list: Quick for questions about the sheet, Deep for a breakdown.
  4. Press Run and wait for the status Connected - context sent at startup; the assistant briefly confirms the job and the sheet.
  5. Type the task in the terminal.

Result: the conversation runs in the panel, the ctx line shows the job and the sheet; the X hides the panel, the conversation continues.

docs.title: Panel: buttons
docs.text:
Panel width is 340-900 px: drag the left edge or set it in Settings > Terminals > Panel width (460 by default); in a narrow window the panel gives way to the drawing.

Element What it does Codex / Claude / DeepSeek profile: each has its own terminal, switching does not break sessions Run start or continue the assistant (Run / resume using the selected E-Wood shortcut); with Workspace it starts claude --continue or codex resume --last, that is, it continues the last session, otherwise a new one Attach pick up an already open Git Bash or mintty window: a menu with the window list and Refresh; after connecting, press Paste context Quick / Balanced / Deep / Provider default the Reasoning effort for the next launch list: reasoning effort for the next launch, low, medium, high or the provider default; for a connected session the list is inactive, it runs on its own settings ctx <job> <sheet> what is in the context now (below) Context open the live context file in the default editor Paste context paste the connection message into the terminal without Enter: read it and send it yourself when the assistant is free AI Inbox expand AI Inbox at the bottom of Main View AI Crop + draw a crop on the sheet and hand its PNG to the context (below) the Detach arrow (Detach terminal to its own window) detach the terminal into its own window; the conversation continues (Detached - conversation continues in its own window); active only with a connected session gear Settings > Terminals three dots (Terminal actions) only on a narrow panel (under 390 px): instead of the arrow and gear, a menu with Detach to window and Settings > Terminals; button captions get shorter (Inbox, Crop +), the counter line hides X (Hide panel) hide the panel; both conversations keep running

The status line under the buttons guides you step by step: Choose Run or Attach, Starting Claude..., Connected - context sent at startup, Connected - startup context disabled, Context pasted - submit it in your assistant when ready, AI crop saved - available in context and AI Inbox. An error is written there too and in the window status bar with the Terminal: prefix.

docs.title: What the assistant knows about the job
docs.text:
While the panel is open, the app checks every two seconds whether something changed (sheet, selection, bookmark, an AI Inbox entry, job files) and rewrites two files in the app profile (%LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore\terminals\<process number>\), not in the job:

File What is inside context-summary.json a short summary: job, current sheet (name, PDF, scale), the selected bookmark or crop with the path to the PNG, the selected Inbox request, counters, the Agent Bridge descriptor, a link to the full file context.json the full index: all sheets (pages), all takeoffs (takeoffs), bookmarks with PNG (bookmarks), crops (ai_crop_bookmarks), Inbox requests and responses (ai_requests), selected measurements, markup of the current sheet, read-only, package path, a bridge block with the session and instructions

The ctx line shows the same in short: <job> <sheet> and counters PDF (sheets), TO (takeoffs), BM (bookmarks), Crop (AI crops), Inbox (requests); with a bookmark selected, BM: <name> is added. No project open means there is no job and the context is empty.

Checkboxes in Settings > Terminals decide what goes into the file: Include bookmarks and their PNG crop paths, Include AI Inbox, requests, responses and AI crops. The checkbox Start with current sheet / crop and a short index; load details on demand (on) sends the assistant the summary instead of the full file: it reads details as the task needs them and answers faster. When the app closes, the file is left with state: app_closed, and the assistant knows the bridge is invalid until the next opening.

docs.title: Connection message
docs.text:
On Run with the checkbox Give new terminal sessions the live plan context, the assistant gets the text from Settings > Terminals > Context message as its first message; {context} in it is replaced with the path to the context file. The built-in text asks it to: read the file now and before every task on the plan, open bookmark and crop PNGs with the image-reading tool (a path by itself is not evidence), check the job and the time in the file, make edits only through Agent Bridge, and answer the connection itself with a short confirmation of the job and the sheet, then wait for a task. With Workspace, the shared folder path, the memory index _agent-memory/MEMORY.md and the rules _rules/global.md are added, without loading the whole knowledge base.

The text is edited in the settings (up to 12000 characters, {context} is required); Reset restores the built-in one. Paste context pastes the same message into a session that is already running, without sending it.

docs.title: How to send a sheet crop to the console: AI Crop +
docs.text:
Demo: AI Crop + and a frame over part of the plan: the crop goes into the console context and into AI Inbox.

What for: the assistant sees a table or detail as an image instead of guessing from text. Needed: the AI module is on, the job is not read-only, the terminal is connected.

  1. Open the sheet, press AI Crop + (needs the AI module and a job that is not read-only). Status: Drag a crop on the sheet - Esc cancels.
  2. Drag a frame over the schedule table, detail or title block.
  3. The app saves the crop PNG into the job, creates a terminal_crop observation and an AI Inbox request with the text "read the crop in the context of the plan and wait for a task". The entry is selected in Inbox right away and goes into the context as the selected crop.
  4. Tell the assistant in the terminal what to do with the crop: "list the notes from this table", "which header mark is over opening 3". It opens the PNG from the path in the context.

Result: the status AI crop saved - available in context and AI Inbox, the entry is selected in Inbox, the ctx line shows Crop one higher.

The selected bookmark (B, K, the Bookmarks tab) and the selected AI Inbox entry go into the context the same way: just select it before asking. The item Use in Codex / Claude / DeepSeek terminal in the AI Inbox entry menu does this in one click: it opens the >_ panel and refreshes the context with that entry right away. Into a conversation that is already running you need to pass it with the Paste context button; a new session gets it on Run.

docs.title: Job edits through Agent Bridge
docs.text:
The assistant does not touch the job files. The bridge block of the context holds the session of the open job and the path to the client agent_bridge.py (the Tools\AgentBridge folder next to the EXE). The order on its side: inspect (a tree snapshot and revision), apply with that revision (create, rename, move, copy, delete folders and takeoffs, add measurements), save, on error undo. Changes show up in the tree and on the sheet right away, deleted items go to AI_Context/agent-trash.

What the estimator should check after the assistant's work: the tree (names per the canon, folder, measurement type), Total of new takeoffs, Ctrl+S. If the bridge is off or the job is read-only, the assistant answers that it cannot make edits; turn on Settings > Agent Bridge. Bridge limits (it does not set the page scale, only launches palette commands, one agent per session): Agent Bridge.

docs.title: Conversations and a second computer
docs.text: With Workspace on, sessions started from the panel are archived automatically. Settings > Workspace > Conversations: Continue selected opens a separate branch of the saved conversation (Claude continues the transcript with --resume --fork-session, Codex imports a copy of the history and continues it), Setup on this computer installs the shortcuts and checks the CLI, Import a Claude / Codex conversation picks up a conversation started outside the app. Before opening another conversation, detach the current terminal: Detach the current terminal before opening another conversation; it will keep running. A conversation over 256 MB is skipped with a warning. The server address and the assistant logins live on each computer separately.

docs.title: Settings > Terminals
docs.text:
Shortcuts, profile, width, effort, four context checkboxes and the connection message text. Field What it sets Codex shortcut, Claude shortcut a shortcut or launcher (.lnk, .cmd, .bat, .exe), Browse...; order: this job, global, the E-Wood shortcuts on the desktop Default profile which terminal is selected when the panel opens Panel width 340-900 Reasoning effort for new sessions Quick, Balanced, Deep, Provider default Start with current sheet / crop and a short index; load details on demand summary instead of the full file Give new terminal sessions the live plan context send the connection message on Run Include bookmarks and their PNG crop paths, Include AI Inbox, requests, responses and AI crops what the context contains Context message a template with {context}

Buttons Apply (until restart), Reset, Save global default, Save as this job, Clear job override; the line under them says what applies: Using global / built-in defaults, Using this job's override, Applied for this session.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Ask about the current sheet
  1. Open s201 2nd, select the questionable detail with the Select tool (the selection is in the context too).
  2. >_, Claude, Quick, Run; wait for the short confirmation of the job and the sheet.
  3. Type: "what is the detail under the selected measurement and which floor does it belong to".
  4. Check the answer against the sheet; if in doubt, Deep for the next session.
Send a schedule crop and get notes
  1. Open the schedule sheet a901 win sch, AI Crop +, drag a frame over the table.
  2. In the terminal: "list the Tag - Size rows from this crop for the opening notes".
  3. Check the rows against the table and paste them into the takeoff Notes or into the DFL. The format of the compact lines from AI crop here -> note is set by Settings > AI Crop Notes (AI in the app).
Ask it to create takeoffs through the bridge and check
  1. Settings > Agent Bridge, turn access on; open the sheet you need, put the green dot on the building.
  2. In the terminal: "create takeoffs in framing/2nd floor framing/posts for the posts from the S2.1 schedule, names per the canon, Count type".
  3. The assistant runs inspect, apply, save; the takeoffs appear in the tree.
  4. Check the folder, names, Total, remove extras, Ctrl+S. Not right: ask for undo or Ctrl+Z in the tree.
Continue a conversation on a second computer
  1. On the first one: Ctrl+S, Settings > Workspace > Sync now, wait for Synced.
  2. On the second one: open the job via Projects > Open selected, Settings > Workspace > Conversations, pick the conversation, Continue selected.
  3. The >_ panel opens with a branch of that conversation; the context is already local, from the open sheet.

docs.title: If the terminal does not start
docs.text:
Message What to do Terminal shortcut was not found. Choose it in Settings > Terminals. point to a shortcut with Browse... or turn on Workspace Install Git for Windows (Git Bash), then try Run again. install Git for Windows; Settings > Workspace has the instructions Choose a Git Bash / mintty shortcut, or the E-Wood Bash launcher., This launcher has additional batch commands... the shortcut does not lead to mintty, or the launcher is more than the single line start mintty; pick a direct mintty shortcut Assistant CLI not installed. Open Settings > Workspace > Setup on this computer. the terminal has no claude or codex: install the CLI and log in The terminal did not expose its window. Use Attach if it opens later. the window opened separately: Attach, pick it in the list This terminal is already connected. the session is already running; type into it, or Detach and Run again Context update failed: ..., context_unavailable in the file the context was not built; switch the sheet and press Context again; on sheets with crops this was fixed in 2.2.36

Everything else: Troubleshooting, terminal and Agent Bridge.
