docs.title: AI in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Full version only

This page opens the "AI, terminal and 3D (full version)" block. OurPlanCore Lite, which estimators run, has no AI module, terminal, Workspace or 3D; Settings > Agent Bridge is in Lite. How the versions differ: Lite vs full version.

Pages of the block: AI in the app (this one), AI console and terminal, Workspace, second computer, 3D roof, 3D and Massing.

Here: every place where OurPlanCore 3.0 calls a model or an external agent: notes from crops and their format (AI Crop Notes), reading sheet title blocks, AI Inbox and AI Manager in short, Agent Bridge. You need it when you want to speed up routine work while every AI result stays under the estimator's review. The Claude and Codex terminals in the app window, with all their buttons, context and scenarios, are described separately: AI console.

docs.title: What there is and what it needs
docs.text:
Tool What it does Online What to turn on AI crop here -> note a crop of a table or detail becomes a takeoff note yes AI module, OpenAI key in AI Settings AI Crop Notes the format of Tag/Size lines in such notes no Settings > AI Crop Notes AI Inbox and AI Manager request queue, responses, observations, markers yes AI module Similar with AI double-check advice on which symbol was picked yes AI module, checkbox in the Similar dialog OCR on Name reading the sheet number without a text layer (Tesseract) no always works; Lite has no OCR AI from the title block image a sheet name that text and OCR could not read yes checkbox in Settings > Auto Rename / Scale >_ terminals (AI console) Claude or Codex in the right panel with live plan context yes Git Bash and the assistant CLI, log in once Agent Bridge an agent edits the open job through the app no (local) Settings > Agent Bridge; also in Lite

The OpenAI key is set in the AI Settings dialog (a button on the tool strip, in AI Manager or the OpenAI Settings palette command); it is saved to the Windows user environment variables and is not written into the job. The default model is gpt-5-mini, the model list is in the same place. Everything marked "yes" goes to the network as sheet crops: keep that in mind with other people's drawings.

docs.title: AI crop and AI Crop Notes
docs.text: Tag/size separator and preview: the pasted text on the left, how it will land in the note on the right.

docs.title: How to get a note from a table crop
docs.text:
What for: schedule rows in the takeoff Notes without typing them by hand. Needed: the AI module, a key in AI Settings, a takeoff selected in Takeoffs.

  1. Right-click the sheet and choose AI crop here -> note (outline an area) or AI quick box here -> note.
  2. Wait for the answer in AI Inbox: the app reformats a schedule answer like Tag - Size into compact lines HP1 (2) 2x8 without repeated headers and table lines.
  3. Check the lines against the table on the sheet.

Result: a note in the Notes of the selected takeoff; the raw answer stays in AI Inbox.

Settings > AI Crop Notes: Tag/size separator, a preview (Preview - paste the recognized text on the left), the Original tables checkbox, Reset, global and per job. Other note text is not touched.

The other items of the same AI Assist submenu: Save AI crop here, Save AI marker here (a symbol sample, below), Ask AI about this point / area, Read text near point, Save observation here, Add as pending check, Suggest takeoff item here, Trace wall from this point, Trace closed area, Check missed takeoffs on this page. On a measurement: Save measurement AI crop (a crop around the measurement with its description goes to AI Inbox, the model is not called), Save measurement as AI marker (the measurement as a sample), Explain measurement, Find Similar, Link to observation, Create note from measurement. The Trace commands work deterministically from the PDF geometry and show a preview before applying.

docs.title: AI Inbox and AI Manager
docs.text:
AI Inbox is a panel at the bottom of Main View (AI module): the job's observations, crops, model requests, responses and markers, newest on top; a request has a status at the start of the line: [pending], [running], [done], [failed]. AI Manager is the same feed as a separate tab with the Run AI, Run New, Retry Failed buttons and marker sets (below). AI output is a draft, not measurements: it gets into the tree only after review (below). Everything is stored in the job, in the AI_Context folder.

The AI Inbox header: entry counter, two marker filters, More, Run AI, + Add and the collapse arrow. Right-click on an entry opens the action menu. Element Where What it does arrow in the header (Toggle AI Inbox) AI Inbox header; palette command Toggle AI Inbox collapse the panel to the header or expand it Show AI Manager palette command open the AI Manager tab the Filter AI markers by type list header All inbox - all entries; All markers - only markers; a type (window_sample, door_sample, roof_edge_sample, ignore_area and others) - only markers of that type the Filter AI markers by sample kind list header Any sample, positive, negative, ignore: which kind of markers to show Run AI header send the selected request; if it is not waiting to be sent, the first waiting one in the queue More header Run New Bookmarks, Retry Failed Bookmarks (batch), Create Marker Set, Manage Marker Sets..., Export Marker Context (entry menu) + Add header your own observation note for the current sheet Enter the selected entry the Observation Details window

docs.title: The AI Manager tab
docs.text:
AI Manager is the same feed as a separate mode bar tab, with a table Type, Page, Observation, Quality, Time. It opens with the palette command Show AI Manager when the AI module is on.

Group Buttons Setup AI Settings, + Add, Refresh Review Open Details, Go to Page, Run AI Batch Run New (all new requests from bookmarks), Retry Failed Markers Create Set, Marker Sets, Export Markers

What goes into Inbox: crops AI crop here -> note and AI quick box here -> note, observations Save observation here, Add as pending check, Suggest takeoff item here, trace requests Trace wall from this point, Trace closed area, Check missed takeoffs on this page (tracing), crops from the AI console AI Crop + (console). A marker is a verified symbol sample; Find Similar From Marker works from it. AI output in Inbox is a draft, not measurements: it gets into the tree only after confirmation. The key and model are set in the AI Settings dialog; the format of notes from crops in Settings > AI Crop Notes (above).

docs.title: How to send a request to the model
docs.text:
What for: get an AI answer for a crop, point or measurement waiting in Inbox. Needed: the AI module, an OpenAI key in AI Settings, a job that is not read-only.

  1. Select an entry with the [pending] or [failed] status in AI Inbox.
  2. Right-click and choose Run AI Request (or the Run AI button in the header).
  3. Read the Review AI Attachments window: it lists the job files (crops, layers) that will go to the network. Press Yes.
  4. Wait for the run to finish: the entry status becomes [done] or [failed].

Result: the answer shows in the Observation Details window (Enter on the entry) as AI Request, AI Response and AI Action Draft blocks. If the answer has points, review the draft (below).

docs.title: How to save a symbol sample: a marker
docs.text:
What for: show the AI what the symbol you need looks like (window, door, roof edge), so it can look for the same ones later. Needed: the AI module, a job that is not read-only.

  1. Right-click the symbol on the sheet and choose AI Assist > Save AI marker here; on a finished measurement, AI Assist > Save measurement as AI marker.
  2. Pick a Marker type from the list or type your own.
  3. Pick a Sample kind: positive - this is what you need, negative - similar but not it, ignore - do not look at this area.
  4. If needed, fill in Value / measurement text (size, mark) and Note, press Save.

Result: a crop around the point is saved, the marker shows on the sheet and as an entry in AI Inbox, status Saved AI marker <type> on <sheet>. Find Similar From Marker works from a marker: a request with the marker crop and a crop of the neighboring sheet area is queued, and the answer comes back as an action draft.

docs.title: How to review an AI action draft
docs.text:
What for: turn the points the AI found into measurements only after your own review. Needed: the entry has an answer with points (after Run AI Request, Find Similar From Marker or a manual answer).

  1. Right-click the entry and choose AI Response > Preview Action Draft: the app opens the sheet and draws the draft points over the drawing.
  2. Choose AI Response > Review Action Draft: a window with candidate rows opens.
  3. Check the correct rows in the Accept column (buttons Accept Selected, Reject Selected, Accept Valid, Reject All; Preview Selected shows the selected ones on the sheet).
  4. For each accepted row, pick a Target Takeoff: an existing takeoff or New AI Line Item, New AI Area Item, New AI Count Item.
  5. Press Apply Accepted, then clear the preview points: AI Response > Clear Action Preview.

Result: the accepted candidates became measurements in the chosen takeoffs, the draft is marked reviewed; accepted and rejected rows are remembered as marker feedback.

Add Manual AI Response (in the Observation Details window, the AI Response button) lets you type an answer by hand, for example one you got in the assistant console: it is saved as finished (done), and an action draft is built from it right away.

docs.title: How to send crops in a batch
docs.text:
What for: collect crops while reviewing sheets and send them to the model in one run.

  1. Right-click an entry with a crop and choose Crop > Bookmark Crop For Batch AI: status Bookmarked crop ...; Run New will send it to OpenAI.
  2. Repeat for other crops.
  3. Press More > Run New Bookmarks in the AI Inbox header (Run New in AI Manager): the new bookmarks go to the model one by one.
  4. Retry the failed ones: More > Retry Failed Bookmarks (Retry Failed).

Result: status Processed new crop bookmarks: N done, N failed, N total, answers in Inbox. If an answer found candidates with points, the app adds a new crop bookmark for each by itself (one level deep, no duplicates nearby); the next Run New sends them.

docs.title: AI Inbox entry menu: reference
docs.text:
All entry menu items and Observation Details window buttons Item Submenu What it does Open Details - the Observation Details window with the entry text, request, response and draft Go to Page - open the sheet the entry belongs to Run AI Request - send this entry's request to the model (above) Open Crop Crop show the crop PNG in a viewer Open Crop Folder Crop open the job's crop folder in File Explorer Bookmark Crop For Batch AI Crop a bookmark for a batch run (above) Edit Marker Marker the same window as when saving a marker: type, sample kind, value, note Delete Marker Marker delete the marker after confirmation; the crop and the log stay in AI_Context Find Similar From Marker Marker queue a search for similar items from the sample Create Marker Set From Filter Marker save the markers under the current filters as a named set (name and Description / use); same as More > Create Marker Set Manage Marker Sets... Marker the list of sets: Apply Filter (set the set's filters), Rename..., Delete (deletes only the set file), Open JSON Export Marker Context Marker export the visible markers under the filters to JSON for an external agent and open the file Hide This Marker Type Marker hide markers of this type on the sheet; remembered for the job Show All Marker Types Marker bring all hidden types back onto the sheet Add Manual AI Response AI Response type an answer by hand (above) Preview Action Draft, Review Action Draft, Clear Action Preview AI Response show, review and clear the action draft (above) Apply Sheet Metadata Response AI Response apply the model's answer on the sheet name and scale (below) Open Request JSON and others Files the entry's service files in Notepad Open Project Context - the job log project.md: all observations in a row, in Notepad Use in Codex / Claude terminal - hand the entry to the assistant in the console (AI console) Refresh Inbox - re-read the list from disk

Observation Details window buttons: Go to Page, Open Crop, Request JSON, Run AI, AI Response (manual answer), Project Context (job log), Close.

docs.title: AI when reading sheet names
docs.text:
The Name button (and Name+Scale) looks for the sheet number in the text of the whole plan set. If there is no text layer, the built-in OCR works (the right strip of the title block, the bottom strip, a learned location). If that did not give a number either, the sheet can be handed to the model: Settings > Auto Rename / Scale, the checkbox Read title blocks the PDF text cannot name with AI (online; AI module and OPENAI_API_KEY).

  • No more than 80 sheets per run; answers are cached in the job (AI_Context/cache/sheet_vision), title block images are deleted after the request.
  • The result shows in Sheet Manager: the Name Source / Name Conf., Why columns.
  • The Kept column in the rule table is learning without AI: how many times a name with that tag stayed final when jobs were opened.

A manual request for selected sheets (Sheet Manager and AI modules):

  1. Right-click a sheet or folder in Pages and choose PDF Metadata > Queue GPT Metadata Fallback.
  2. Read the summary in the window: the app takes only sheets where PDF parsing did not find the number, title or scale (or there is no text at all) and that do not have such a request yet; for each one it saves a title block crop (from the Crop Hints regions, if set) and queues a request in AI Inbox.
  3. Send the requests: Run AI Request on an entry or AI Fill in Sheet Manager (it queues, sends and writes the answers into the sheet table by itself).
  4. Apply the answer per entry: right-click > AI Response > Apply Sheet Metadata Response, check the Rename checkboxes and the Scale Action column in the preview window, press Apply.

Result: the sheet name and scale are updated only where the checkboxes were left on.

docs.title: Claude and Codex terminals
docs.text: The >_ button on the right command strip opens a panel with Git Bash inside the app window: the assistant sees the job, the sheet, the selection, bookmarks and crops through a live context file, and edits the job through Agent Bridge. Panel buttons, the ctx line, AI Crop +, Settings > Terminals, scenarios and what to do if the terminal does not start: AI console.

docs.title: Agent Bridge
docs.text:
Two switches: local assistant access and permission for palette commands.

What it is. A channel through which an external agent (Claude Code, Codex) edits the open job with the app's own hands: changes show up in the tree and on the sheet right away, a recovery log is kept, deleted items go to AI_Context/agent-trash. The agent does not touch job files behind the app's back: if you rewrite Takeoffs on disk and press Refresh, the app overwrites it with its in-memory state.

Who it is for. The owner and the agents that help with measuring; the estimator presses nothing in the window except turning it on.

Where it is turned on. Settings > Agent Bridge: Enable local assistant access and Allow all registered palette commands (some require interaction); Apply, Reset, global and per job. Off by default.

What it can do. The client agent_bridge.py is in the Tools\AgentBridge folder next to the EXE, commands: sessions, ping, status, commands, inspect, context, save, refresh, refresh_pages, reload, apply, undo, palette. Through apply the agent creates, renames, moves, copies and deletes Takeoffs folders and takeoffs, changes takeoff properties, adds and replaces measurements. Every batch needs a revision from inspect; on a conflict a new inspect is needed. save waits for the batch to be actually saved and reports the result, undo rolls back the agent's last batch.

What it cannot do. It does not set the page scale; it only reads and refreshes sheets; it only launches palette commands (dispatched, no result) and does not bypass modules or read-only; it does not work while a modal window is open or a drawing gesture is unfinished; a timeout is not a reason to repeat the request with a new ID. One agent per session of the open job.

The rules for how the agent works with the tree (names, move instead of create+delete, measurement types) are in the owner's skills; for the estimator one thing matters: after the agent's work, check the tree and press Ctrl+S.

docs.title: What AI does not do
docs.text:
• It does not replace the scale or the check against a known dimension.
  • It does not count for you: Similar, AI crop, Trace give candidates you have to confirm.
  • It does not read closed jobs: the bridge and the terminals work only with the open job.

docs.title: Multiple buildings
docs.text:
This page covers how to run a job with several buildings in one file: a folder per building in Takeoffs and in Pages, the green and red dots in the Takeoffs header (where new measurements are written), how the W/F/S/U sheet dots work inside the selected building, copying identical buildings, a separate Excel workbook and a separate PDF per building. You need it on every job with more than one building: townhouses, a house with a garage and storage, a complex of buildings A, B, C.

Demo on a job with several buildings: the green dot on a building folder sends new measurements into it, the red dot returns to the Takeoffs root.

Three buildings A, B, C: each has its own walls, sqfts, framing. The green marker on B says new measurements go into it.

docs.title: A folder per building
docs.text:
• One building: the roots walls, sqfts, framing... sit right in Takeoffs; do not create a Main folder.
  • Several buildings: a folder for each, with the regular canonical tree inside. Names per the plans or by role: A, B, C; Main, Grge, Storage, Clubhouse; Bldng A. The building name repeats in Pages, in the Excel workbook and in the PDF name, so pick it once and keep it short.
  • More > Auto Tree builds the building tree when the building folder is selected; New Folder under the building adds whatever is missing.
  • In Pages the building also gets its own folder with the same name; shared sheets (complex elevations, details, specs) stay in 00. imported/.... Canonical folders: Takeoff tree and sheet names.

Identical buildings (a mirrored townhouse, a repeated typical house) are measured once, then copied (below).

docs.title: Green and red dots
docs.text:
Two dots to the left of the tree refresh button. The tooltip shows the current root: Current: B or Current: Takeoffs root.

The dots set the root for new takeoffs: which building receives measurements, New Item, Beam, Openings and pasted New takeoffs.

Dot Tooltip What it does green Use selected folder as root the selected folder becomes the root; it gets a green marker, status New takeoffs -> B red Use Takeoffs root the root is the whole Takeoffs again; status New takeoffs -> Takeoffs root

docs.title: How to pick the building for new measurements
docs.text:
Why: everything you draw next goes into this building's folders. You need: the building folders created in Takeoffs.

  1. Select the building folder in the tree (B).
  2. Press the green dot in the Takeoffs header. With no folder selected the status will tell you: Select a Takeoffs folder, then press the green dot.
  3. Measure: all new takeoffs go inside B; the sheet dot picks the floor and branch.
  4. For another building, select C and press the green dot again. For complex-wide takeoffs press the red dot.

Result: folder B has the green marker, status New takeoffs -> B, the tooltip on the dots reads Current: B; in the New Item dialog the path starts with B/.

The choice is stored in the job and follows the folder when it is renamed or moved; it is restored when the job is opened. Existing takeoffs do not move when the root changes; Record continues its takeoff in any building. If the root points to a deleted folder, creation is blocked with a message: press the red dot and pick the building again.

Without the green dot the building comes from Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Building root (the default building for the job; with Save as this job it is also written to the dot of the open sheet), and if that is empty too, the Takeoffs root. In the New Item dialog the target path is visible before creation; in the paste dialog, the line Root: Takeoffs/B.

docs.title: Sheet dots inside a building
docs.text:
The W/F/S/U sheet dot picks the branch and floor, the green dot picks the building: sheet a201 2nd with the W 2 dot under root B gives B/walls/2nd floor walls, under root C gives C/walls/2nd floor walls. Name rules (eve, prpt, gable, Openings) are also counted from the root: B/eves rakes/eves, B/openings. Rule order: Names and auto-routing.

A sheet shared by two buildings (one plan with buildings A and B side by side): measure building A with the green dot on A, then switch to B and measure the other half from the same sheet. A sheet copy for the second building is needed only when the buildings cannot be told apart on different sheets, or for a separate PDF (split by sheets).

docs.title: How to copy a building
docs.text:
Why: do not draw identical or mirrored buildings a second time. You need: building A measured, folder B created, building B sheets in Pages.

  1. On a building A sheet, select the measurements with the Select tool (Ctrl+A for everything on the sheet), Ctrl+C.
  2. Select folder B, green dot. Open a building B sheet (with identical plans, a sheet copy or the same sheet).
  3. Ctrl+V, in the Paste Measurements dialog pick New takeoffs; the line Root: Takeoffs/B. shows the target building.
  4. The copies go into the same folders as the sources, only inside B: A/sqfts to B/sqfts, A/framing/2nd floor framing/details to B/framing/2nd floor framing/details, Openings to B/openings. On a sheet with a different dot of the same row only the floor changes.
  5. Check the B tree, fix whatever differs (a different opening size, an extra post), Ctrl+S.

Result: B has the same folders and takeoffs as A, with measurements on the building B sheets; the A totals did not change.

Same takeoffs is not what you want when copying between buildings: it adds the measurements to the source takeoffs of building A. The Copies keep their source folders checkbox in Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing turns off the folder mirroring; then copies follow the sheet dot. Copying whole tree folders: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V in Takeoffs carries takeoffs without the measurements of another sheet, so for a building you copy measurements from the sheet. Details: copying.

docs.title: How to export an Excel workbook per building
docs.text:
Why: each building has its own DFL with the wall matrix and framing lists. You need: copies of TemplateCom.xlsm per building, Excel open with macros enabled.

  1. Each building gets its own copy of TemplateCom.xlsm: workbook names by building (Bldng A.xlsm, Bldng B.xlsm), workbook name equals the Job Name on the Front Page.
  2. Open the building workbook, activate Detailed Frame List.
  3. In Lite: click a cell, select a folder or takeoff of this building in Takeoffs and press Excel, Value or Link to Excel. For Auto Link put the green dot on the building: it takes only that building's takeoffs.
  4. In the full version, instead of step 3: select one building folder and press ALL on the XL strip. A selection from two buildings is not accepted: Excel ALL found more than one building/root in the selection. The LG legend is per workbook: the beam and post codes of that building.
  5. Repeat for the next building with its workbook.

Result: the building workbook is filled with the numbers of this building only. The Lite buttons and the XL strip: Export to Excel.

docs.title: How to get a PDF per building
docs.text:
From the window: the building has its own sheet folder in Pages; in Export PDF tick it with one checkbox; on a shared sheet hide the other building's takeoffs (H on the building folder in Takeoffs), export, name it <job> Bldg A.pdf, restore visibility and repeat (PDF and delivery).

With the pipeline: OurPlanCoreCli export-pdf --grouping auto splits the PDF by building on its own: it takes the saved green dot choice, exports each sibling building branch as a separate file, and on a shared sheet prints only that branch's measurements. With no root selected (red dot) you get one file; --grouping single forces one file; measurements outside the building folders stop the export with a message. Before delivery: Ctrl+S, green dot on the building, save again (pipeline).

docs.title: Example: a job with three buildings A, B, C
docs.text:
Pages/
  00. imported/   shared: a001 n, a901 win sch, s501 d
  A/  a101 1st, a102 2nd, s101 1st, s102 2nd, a105 rf
  B/  copies of the A sheets (same building, mirrored)
  C/  a301 1st, s301 1st, a305 rf

Takeoffs/
  A/  sqfts, walls/1st floor walls, framing/1st floor framing/..., openings/1, eves rakes
  B/  same, pasted as New takeoffs from the A sheets, openings fixed
  C/  sqfts, walls, framing, openings, eves rakes

Workbooks: Bldng A.xlsm, Bldng B.xlsm, Bldng C.xlsm; PDFs: <job> Bldg A.pdf, ... B.pdf, ... C.pdf.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Forgot to switch the green dot: half a day of measurements went into A instead of B. Move them by folders (Ctrl+X, Paste Into Folder); measurements and colors are kept. Check the Current: tooltip on the dots before starting a new building.
  • The green dot is on a building while a shared complex sheet is being measured: complex takeoffs ended up inside the building. For shared ones, the red dot.
  • Pasting Same takeoffs between buildings: building B measurements were added to the A takeoffs, the A totals grew. Ctrl+Z, paste again as New takeoffs.
  • ALL in Excel with two buildings selected or with all of Takeoffs selected: the export stops; select one building folder.
  • One PDF for all buildings: the client cannot tell what is what; export by building folders or with the pipeline.
  • A Main folder in a single-building job: an extra level; Excel and the pipeline expect the roots right in Takeoffs.

All sheet and tree mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.title: OurPlanCore - what's new
docs.text: This page lists what went into OurPlanCore 3.0: the new 3.0 releases first, below them what accumulated in builds 2.2.6-2.2.42. You need it to see which feature was missing in an older version and where to read about it. Releases 3.0.4-3.0.26 are not written up here yet.

• TemplateCom.xlsm template: the formula for the balcony and porch block size now reads the same on a Russian and an English computer (Two languages). The numbers in the template did not change.
  • Writing to a closed workbook: a timeout is now reported as usual; before, it could end in a thread error.

• Auto Link: a button next to Link to Excel, DFL only. One click links Sure takeoffs (the label in J equals the name, the number matches) and Probable ones (the number matches one to one in column K, with no name) right away. Cell values do not change, the workbook is not saved. Windows, doors and other openings, joists, unnamed points, small unnamed whole numbers are skipped. Ambiguous ones are linked in the result window, where Undo This Auto Link also is. Look at the result window right away: a Probable can land on someone else's row with the same number. Also in Lite. Auto Link
  • Reset All Links: removes all links of the job after a prompt, cannot be undone, the values in the cells stay. Names leave open workbooks right away, closed ones at the next opening or right away with a second button. Reset All Links
  • Unlink for a closed workbook: the hidden name now goes away when the workbook is opened while this job is open, instead of staying until Remove All Links.

• Link to Excel: a button next to Value and Excel writes the number of one takeoff into the active cell of the open workbook and keeps it there. The link goes only from OurPlanCore to Excel; inserting rows does not break it. A closed workbook is updated on Ctrl+S or with Update Links. States Linked, Pending, Conflict, Broken, the All Excel Links... list, settings Settings > Excel Links. Before the workbook goes to the client the links are removed: Remove All Links from This Workbook.... Also in Lite. Link to Excel

• PDF export by default puts measurements in as separate objects that can be edited in Adobe Acrobat; the look stays as in OurPlanCore. In Acrobat lines, areas and labels move; Count points and joist areas do not, and the legend is the same type as the points and should not move (it was not tested separately). Adobe does not recalculate labels and the legend. To turn it off: PDF Output > ADOBE > Editable, settings Settings > PDF Editable Export. Also in Lite. Editing the PDF in Adobe

• The sheet legend is split by default into blocks by the current Takeoffs folders. On framing Posts, Beams, Details come first; SQFTs after the other measurements. The order and names are edited in Settings > Sheet Legend globally or per job. The button next to the crop lock turns off the automatic blocks on one sheet; manual groups stay available. Sheet legend
  • On an F sheet, a Count/Points ending in Post goes to framing/<floor>/posts, a name ending in Stair with any tool goes to framing/<floor>/stairs. Names and auto-routing
  • Crop to Sheet places crops from the top left corner to the right, then below, with margins and without overlap. If a whole crop does not fit, it is not added; the status suggests a larger or a new sheet. Crops
  • On an error, autosave retries after 30, 60 and 120 seconds, then every 5 minutes until it succeeds; the intervals are edited in Settings > Autosave Recovery. A temporarily unreadable file is checked every 30 seconds; the protection is lifted only after the data loads successfully. A corrupted file stays protected for manual recovery. Saving

Fixes found while recording the clips for this section. Rollback: the ourplancore.exe.3.0.1-*.bak file next to the EXE.

  • Fit (F) puts the sheet in the middle of the work area, not in the top left corner.
  • Autosave: if the job file changed while the app was writing the .ourplan, it retries by itself. Before, such a race stopped autosave until a manual Ctrl+S (Save: Failed). Saving
  • A sheet file that is briefly busy with another write is reread by the app instead of being declared Save: Protected data right away.
  • 3D: the rf 6, rf 4 roof area sits on top of the walls; before, the pitch digit was read as a floor number, and the slab hung several floors higher. Already saved models are fixed on opening.
  • 3D roof: any sheet tool turns off edge selection; Ctrl or Shift with a right-click add an edge without the sheet menu; Auto and Wall no longer break Roof Base groups. 3D roof
  • A large sheet no longer stays white after the 3D tab, and undo (Ctrl+Z) survives switching to the 3D tab and back.

Fixes found while shooting the screenshots and clips for this section on the sample job. Rollback: the ourplancore.exe.3.0.0-*.bak file next to the EXE.

  • Open sample job works again. The sample is laid out as in real work: sheet copies with the W, F, S and U dots, a tree per the canon, each takeoff on its own sheet, a gable roof from sqfts/rf 6, the saved 3D model visible right away. Sample job
  • The default tree folder is basement floor walls (was basement foor walls).
  • New Takeoff Item: the measurement type shows Line, not the record text.
  • A new blank sheet gets a W/F/S/U dot from its name; Duplicate Page gives the copy a unique name and does not carry over the dot.
  • PDF Output > Preview keeps the sheet's legend groups.
  • Batch Overlay: column headers in English, with tooltips.
  • Ctrl+Z from the ribbon also undoes a Hide mask that was just drawn.
  • The XL strip and the command strip scroll with the wheel in a short window.
  • The tiles of the start card respond to a normal click.

Release 3.0.0 is build 2.2.42 plus one fix: the Workspace sync no longer gets stuck on a dialog transcript that is too large (a file over 256 MB is skipped with a warning, the other dialogs sync). Window title: OurPlanCore 3.0.0 - <job>. One install in the updates folder Desktop\updates\OurPlanCore, the rollback is the .bak file next to the EXE. Below is everything that accumulated since 2.2.7 and went into 3.0.0; what 2.2.6 and 2.2.7 themselves brought (a single .ourplan file, autosave, Project Data Recovery, live Preview, key editor) is in the 08/15-09/06 section.

docs.title: Where a new takeoff goes
docs.text:
• W/F/S/U dots under the Scale label: one dot per sheet decides the folder and floor for any tool; status Route: W 2nd. The dot is set automatically from the sheet name (a is W, s is F, a final u is U), and there is a Route sheets without a dot now pass.
  • Takeoff Name Routing: rules by name and tool (eve, rake, gable, prpt, trussheel, Openings) beat the sheet dot.
  • Green and red dots in the Takeoffs header: the building for new takeoffs; New takeoffs paste goes into it, copies keep their subfolders (D3/sqfts to D4/sqfts).
  • Takeoff Colors: bft is always light gray; random colors avoid gray, black and white.
  • Details: Takeoff routing.

docs.title: Editing measurements
docs.text:
• Merge and Split of whole takeoffs from the tree (Ctrl+M, Ctrl+Shift+M): by section or by sheet, undo with Ctrl+Z in Takeoffs.
  • Break (Ctrl+Shift+B) and Break H/V (Ctrl+Shift+V): lines into segments, horizontal and vertical ones into separate takeoffs. Ends: Count marks at the segment ends.
  • H hides the takeoff of the selected segment, the highlighter moved to Shift+H. Keys work in the Russian layout.
  • Details: Editing takeoffs, Hotkeys.

docs.title: Sheets
docs.text:
• Crop to Sheet: details from several sheets onto one clean sheet at 100 % scale; rotate, mirror, opacity, order, lock, the not true scale badge.
  • Blank Sheet with size, units and presets; Change Sheet Size...; fast zoom on large blank sheets.
  • Hide: a white mask over the sheet, prints in the PDF. Area markup by box. PDF Output > Opac is the line opacity in the PDF.
  • Legend groups and Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space). Batch Overlay for all floors at once.
  • Sheet names across the whole set: tags rcp, demo, u, base, sch, in el, fin; OCR for scans; AI from the title block image; learning (the Kept column); sorting by the last word, rcp and demolition folders.
  • Details: Sheets: Crop to Sheet, Overlay, legend, Hide, Pages sheets.

docs.title: Excel and PDF
docs.text:
• The XL strip: new buttons SH, SW, SHF, UN, BL and the framing buttons FR, PS, BM, HD, JS, DT, ST; Framing no longer wipes the template, a repeat run works; details get M flags.
  • The "comments" dot on the Excel button: takeoff and measurement notes go into the export.
  • PDF: crops and masks print even without Markups, legend groups in the PDF, export by building through the pipeline.
  • Details: Excel export, PDF export.

docs.title: AI, workspace, pipeline
docs.text:
• Claude and Codex terminals in the window (>_) with live sheet context and Quick / Balanced / Deep effort.
  • Agent Bridge: an agent edits the open job through the app, with undo.
  • Workspace: a shared server for rules, skills, jobs and dialogs for a second computer.
  • AI Crop Notes: notes from a schedule in compact rows.
  • The In Progress button (Job Tracker module), importing an OurPlanCore job into the open one, the OurPlanCoreCli pipeline console.
  • Details: AI console, AI in the app, Workspace and modules, Managers.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings grew from 12 to 20 categories (Blank Sheets, Sheet Takeoff Routing, Takeoff Name Routing, Takeoff Colors, AI Crop Notes, Agent Bridge, Terminals, Workspace); 19 modules (plus Job Tracker). One principle everywhere: Reset, Save global default, Save as this job. Details: Settings: all categories.

docs.text: Until 2.2.8 the app ran on the stable 2.2.5 (07/22), and new work was built into a separate Preview with its own profile and shortcut. Since 2.2.10 there is no Preview: everything is installed into the main updates folder. What went in over those three weeks:

docs.title: Jobs and saving
docs.text:
• A single .ourplan file (08/17): the job became a portable package; on opening it is unpacked into a working copy, and Save packs it back. Old folder jobs open with the same Open project.... Jobs and saving
  • Save As with a format choice (08/20): a new portable file or a compatible folder copy; since 09/01 it is a single Save As... item (Ctrl+Shift+S) that keeps the format of the open job. Jobs
  • Unified job storage (09/01): one Open project... dialog with source folders, a filter and Open project file... for an .ourplan outside those folders; the Settings > Project Storage category with size analysis and Compact snap.json. Jobs, Settings

  • Data protection (2.2.6 Preview, 09/06): a corrupted or locked metadata file is not overwritten with an empty one, Open / Import > Project Data Recovery... with Retry reading and Restore from copy...; a log of sheet operations and Undo Last Page Sort / Undo Last Page Operation; raster caches are read on long paths too. docs.title: First steps: 10 lessons
docs.text:
A course on the OurPlanCore 3.0 demo job: from opening the app to PDF and Excel. Each lesson is one task from start to a visible result, 5-10 minutes. Lessons follow the estimator's order of work; details on each topic are on the pages of this section, linked at the end of each lesson. You can break the demo job: a new one is created with the Open sample job tile (demo tour).

What you need before you start: the app is installed and launches from the desktop shortcut (getting started); for lesson 9, Excel and a copy of TemplateCom.xlsm from the templates folder of the shared Dropbox folder (where the app is).

docs.title: Lesson 1. Open the demo job and look around
docs.text:
Demo: Open sample job on the start card creates the demo job; then the W, F, S and U sheets with their legends and the 3D tab (it exists only in the full version).

Goal: open the training job and learn where things are in the window.

  1. Launch the app and press the Open sample job tile (or Main > Open / Import > Sample job (demo to explore)).
  2. Wait for the status Sample project created: OurPlanCore Guide Sample.
  3. In the Pages panel on the left, expand the 00. Guide folder and click a floor plan: it opens as a tab in the center.
  4. Find the Takeoffs panel with the takeoff tree on the right, the tool strip at the bottom, and the status bar at the very bottom.
  5. Press F1: a shortcut cheat sheet over the window; close it with Esc.
  6. Press Ctrl+Shift+P, type fit, Enter: the sheet fits the window. The F key does the same.

Check yourself: the window title shows OurPlanCore Guide Sample, the status bar shows Scale: and Route:, the right mouse button pans the sheet, the wheel zooms.

Details: Getting started, window map.

docs.title: Lesson 2. Sheets: name, scale, sheet dot
docs.text:
Demo: Ctrl+D makes a copy of the sheet, F2 names it a101 1st sw, a click on the S/1 dot under Scale sets the route S 1st floor.

Goal: understand that a sheet has a canonical name, a scale and a W/F/S/U dot, and learn to set them by hand.

  1. Select a floor plan in Pages and read Scale: 1/8" = 1'0" (or 1:96) and Route: W 1st in the status bar.
  2. Press R (Ruler) and click both ends of a dimension string on the sheet: the tape length matches the labeled dimension, so the scale is right.
  3. Press F2 on the sheet, type the same name (a101 1st), Enter: the name in lowercase, the floor tag last; the W dot under the Scale header stays.
  4. Press Ctrl+D: a copy of the sheet with the same name appears next to it.
  5. Press F2 on the copy, type a101 1st sw, Enter, then right-click the copy and Move to Folder... if you want to put it in a separate folder.
  6. Open the copy and click the dot in row S, column 1, under the Scale header.
Demo: on a sheet with the wrong scale, F4 and entering 1/8" = 1'0"; the length in the legend is recalculated right away.

If the sheet has no scale: press S, click both ends of a known dimension, type the length (20' or 1/8" = 1'0"), Enter; for several sheets, select them in Pages and press F4.

Check yourself: on the copy the status shows Route: S 1st, on the original Route: W 1st; both sheets have a scale.

Details: Sheets (Pages), split by sheets, sheet names.

docs.title: Lesson 3. Routing: where a measurement goes
docs.text:
Demo on a real job: a wall on a W sheet goes to walls/3rd floor walls, a beam on an F sheet to framing/3rd floor framing/beams, a shear wall on a sheet copy with the S dot to shear walls.

Goal: see how the sheet dot and the takeoff name pick the folder in the tree by themselves.

  1. Open a plan with the W dot (a101 1st) and press L.
  2. In the New Takeoff Item dialog type the name ext 2x6 9.09 and read the destination line at the bottom of the dialog: walls/1st floor walls.
  3. Press OK, click two corners on the sheet and press C.
  4. Find the takeoff in Takeoffs: it is in walls/1st floor walls; the status shows Takeoff: ext 2x6 9.09 (Route: W 1st).
  5. Press L again and type eve 24 main: the destination line shows eves rakes/eves, even though the sheet is the same. The word eve in the name beats the sheet dot. Press Cancel.
  6. Open the copy with the S dot, press L, type SW1-1: destination shear walls/1st floor/shear. Press Cancel.

Check yourself: you can tell which folder a takeoff will go into before pressing OK, and you see it in the Route: field of the status bar.

Details: Names and auto-routing, Split by sheets and routing.

docs.title: Lesson 4. Walls: Line
docs.text:
Demo: L, name ext 2x6 9.09, route line walls/1st floor walls, clicks along the exterior wall centerline and C.

Goal: draw the exterior walls of a floor as one takeoff and continue it with Record.

  1. On a plan with the W dot press L, name ext 2x6 9.09 (purpose, size, height in feet), OK.
  2. Click along the exterior wall centerline corner by corner; Backspace removes the last point.
  3. Press C: the run is closed, the status shows Mode: Record ext 2x6 9.09.
  4. Draw the next disconnected run of the same wall: it goes into the same takeoff.
  5. Press Space to stop Record. Select the takeoff in the tree and press Space again: Record continues it when you come back to the walls later.
  6. For partitions of a different height press L and create a new takeoff 2x4 9.09: a new height or size means a new takeoff.

Check yourself: walls/1st floor walls has two takeoffs, ext 2x6 9.09 has sections by run under it, Total shows linear feet.

Details: Measuring tools, Line, Exterior.

docs.title: Lesson 5. Openings: Openings
docs.text:
Demo: O, a box around a window, name 4.0x4.0, the other windows with one click each; total 4 ea.

Goal: count windows and doors as size-named takeoffs, one point per opening.

  1. Press O on a plan or an elevation.
  2. Click two opposite corners of a box around the opening.
  3. In the dialog type the name 3.0x6.8 d: width by height in feet with one decimal place, suffix d for a door (gd garage door, lv louver); a window has no suffix, 4.0x4.0.
  4. Press OK: a point appears in the center of the opening, the takeoff goes into openings from any sheet.
  5. Repeat for the next opening of the same size: select the takeoff and Space, then the box; different marks of the same size = one takeoff.
  6. In Takeoffs create a folder 1 under openings (New Folder) and drag the floor's takeoffs into it.

Check yourself: openings/1 has the takeoffs 3.0x6.8 d and 4.0x4.0, Total equals the number of openings, the plan has one point per opening.

Details: Tools, Openings, Windows and Doors.

docs.title: Lesson 6. Areas: Area and Cut
docs.text:
Demo: A, the 1st floor outline and C; then X (Cut) with F9 (Box) cuts a bathroom out of the area.

Goal: take off the floor area and cut a shaft out of it.

  1. On a plan with the W dot press A, name 1st, OK.
  2. Trace the floor outline corner by corner, C closes it: the takeoff goes into sqfts.
  3. Press X (Cut), trace the outline of a shaft or stair opening inside the area, C.
  4. Read the takeoff's Total: the area went down by exactly the cutout.
  5. For a rectangular room press A, then F9 (Box) and click two corners.

Check yourself: sqfts has the takeoff 1st, the sheet shows an outline with a hole, Total in SF.

Details: Tools, Area, SQFT, Editing and snaps.

docs.title: Lesson 7. Framing on an F sheet: J Area and Beam
docs.text:
Demo: J, name 2x10 16", floor framing outline and the joist direction line; the app counts pieces and linear feet.

Goal: count joists by area and a beam with an order length on a structural plan.

  1. Open a structural plan with the F dot (s101 1st); status Route: F 1st.
  2. Press J, name 2x10 16" (size and spacing), OK, trace the joist area, C.
  3. Draw the direction line along the joists when the app asks; Shift keeps the direction on the axes.
  4. Read Total: pieces and linear feet, the takeoff is in framing/1st floor framing/joists.
Demo: B, two beam ends, name FB1; the app adds the length to the name: FB1 52.
  1. Press B, draw from support to support of the beam, type the mark FB1 in the dialog, OK: the app added the length in feet, rounded up (FB1 14), the takeoff is in .../beams.
  2. Press P, name C4 20, click the post symbol: the takeoff is in the root of framing/1st floor framing; drag it into the posts folder.

Check yourself: framing/1st floor framing has the folders joists, beams, posts with takeoffs; the beam has its length in the name, the joists have pieces in Total.

Details: Tools, J Area and Beam, Joist, Beam.

docs.title: Lesson 8. Check: legend, Hide, Total
docs.text:
Demo: two takeoffs under a sheet in Pages, right-click Legend Group > New Group; the legend on the sheet splits into walls and openings blocks.

Goal: make sure everything is in place on the sheet and in the tree before exporting.

  1. Turn on Display > Legend Show: a legend with this sheet's takeoffs appears on the sheet.
  2. Right-click the sheet in Pages, Organize > Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space): takeoffs are sorted by the first word of the name.
  3. Expand the sheet in Pages: under it are the same takeoffs as in the legend.
Demo: H hides the selected takeoff on the sheet, the visibility dot under the sheet in Pages brings it back.
  1. Select the 1st takeoff in Takeoffs and press H: the area disappears from the sheet, status Hidden 1 whole takeoff(s).
  2. Click the visibility dot next to the takeoff under the sheet in Pages: the area is back.
  3. Open the Estimating tab on the right: all takeoffs in one table with totals. Press Delete Empty in Takeoffs to remove takeoffs with no measurements.

Check yourself: the legend is readable, each takeoff has its own color, Estimating has no empty rows or zero totals.

Details: Takeoffs tree, PDF and delivery, legend.

docs.title: Lesson 9. Excel: the Excel, Value and Link to Excel buttons
docs.text:
Goal: send takeoff numbers into the DFL workbook and link one number to a measurement.

  1. Copy TemplateCom.xlsm from the templates folder of the shared Dropbox folder into the job folder under the building's name, open the copy in Excel, enable macros, activate the Detailed Frame List worksheet.
  2. In Excel, click the first free cell of the J:L list (from row 10).
  3. In OurPlanCore, select the walls/1st floor walls folder in Takeoffs and press Excel at the bottom left: the rows (name, number, unit) land starting from that cell. Value writes only the numbers of the same selection into one column.
  4. Click another cell in Excel, select the floor area takeoff in sqfts (for example 1st) and press Link to Excel at the bottom. Status: Linked <takeoff> to <workbook> <sheet!cell>: <number>, the takeoff row shows a chain icon.
  5. Select that takeoff, press Space and trace one more room: after a short pause the number in the linked cell goes up.
  6. Save the workbook in Excel yourself: the app does not save it.

Check yourself: J:L has wall rows with numbers in LF, the linked cell shows the same number as the takeoff's Total in the tree.

In Lite, the calculation from the J:L list (wall matrix, areas, openings) is run with the E-Wood tab buttons in Excel (Calculation from takeoffs). In the full version the XL strip does it: LG, then ALL exports the whole building and runs the workbook macros itself (XL strip).

Details: Export to Excel, How the DFL workbook works.

docs.title: Lesson 10. PDF and delivery
docs.text:
Demo: PDF Output > Preview; the sheet preview redraws when the opacity and legend size change on the ribbon.

Goal: get a PDF with only the sheets that have measurements, and check it before export.

  1. Press Ctrl+S and wait for Save: Saved hh:mm:ss in the status bar.
  2. Open the PDF Output ribbon and press Preview: the window shows the current sheet as it will print.
  3. Change Opac to 70 and the Legend size: the preview redraws.
Demo: Main > Export, check the sheets you need, Export; status Exported PDF (2 sheet(s)).
  1. Press Main > PDF > Export, check only the sheets with measurements in the dialog, leave Measurements and Legend checked.
  2. Press Export, name the file <job> Bldg A.pdf, save.
  3. Open the PDF and page through it: measurements and legend in place, no extra sheets.

Check yourself: a PDF with one or two sheets, wall lines do not cover the dimensions, the legend is readable.

Details: PDF and delivery, Workflow, delivery.

docs.title: Merge, Split, Break, Ends, Combine, Similar: step by step
docs.text:
Each editing operation is described here as a task: what to prepare, which steps, what to see in the status bar. The big picture (selection, vertices, Undo, the operations map, recipes that combine them) is on Editing measurements and snaps.

Tool strip: Merge, Split and the Combine list. Break and Ends sit further left, next to P Line.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text:
Button Key What it does Works with Merge Ctrl+M combines whole takeoffs (selection in the tree) or moves selected segments into another takeoff (selection on the sheet) Takeoffs, sheet Split Ctrl+Shift+M splits a takeoff by section or by sheet (tree); splits segments or marks off into a new takeoff (sheet) Takeoffs, sheet Break Ctrl+Shift+B each Line polyline falls apart into single-segment measurements Line Break with the H/V dot Ctrl+Shift+V segments go into <name> - Horizontal and <name> - Vertical Line Ends none Count marks at both ends of each Line segment Line P Line none Count marks along a Line at a set spacing Line Cut X, F9 box cutout in an Area, erasing a piece of a Line Area, Line Combine none Union, Subtract, Intersect, Remove Overlap, Divide for two or more Areas Area Similar none finds identical symbols on the sheet and on other sheets Count Transform none Flip H, Flip V, rotate, scale the selection all Repeat Line, Repeat Beam none a series of segments or beams without a dialog for each Line, Beam

All commands are in the palette Ctrl+Shift+P: Break Lines Into Segments, Break Lines Into Horizontal / Vertical, Count Points At Line Ends, Combine Areas: Union and so on. Keys that have no binding are assigned in the key editor. Merge, Split, Break, Ends, P Line, Combine require the Advanced Takeoff Tools module (on by default, Settings > Modules).

docs.title: Two modes of Merge and Split
docs.text:
• Takeoff rows selected in the Takeoffs tree (Ctrl or Shift on rows): whole takeoffs with all sections on all sheets are affected. This is how identical takeoffs from different floors are collected and a takeoff is split before Excel.
  • Measurements selected on the sheet with the Select tool (or a section under a takeoff selected in the tree): segments and marks are affected. This is how a wrong piece is moved into another takeoff or split off into a new one.

The tree takes priority: if takeoff rows are selected there, the button and key work on whole takeoffs, even if something is still selected on the sheet. A click on a measurement on the sheet brings back segment mode.

Undo for the tree: Ctrl+Z with focus in the Takeoffs panel, or right-click Undo Takeoff Merge / Split. Undo on the sheet: Ctrl+Z in the viewport.

docs.title: How to merge whole takeoffs
docs.text:
Why: one takeoff instead of several identical ones (2nd and 3rd floor walls with the same name). You need: two or more takeoffs of the same type (Count with Count, Line with Line, Area with Area, J Area with J Area).

The Merge Into Takeoff dialog: pick which takeoff stays; the others move into it as sections.
  1. Select the takeoffs in Takeoffs: click the first one, Ctrl or Shift + click the others.
  2. Click Merge, Ctrl+M or right-click Merge Selected Takeoffs....
  3. In the list pick the takeoff that stays: its name, folder, color, price and properties are kept.
  4. Click Merge.

Result: status Merged 3 takeoffs into ext 2x6 9.09 (12 sections). Ctrl+Z in Takeoffs to undo. Sections from all sheets moved into the chosen takeoff, the other rows disappeared. Geometry is not joined: lines stay separate segments, marks stay separate marks.

Demo: a wall segment landed in the wrong takeoff; Ctrl+M and Merge Into Takeoff move it into ext 2x6 9.09.

Tips

  • Takeoffs removed by a merge are kept in AI_Context/takeoff-merge-trash inside the job; Ctrl+Z in the tree brings them back while the session is open.
  • If the Merge Into Takeoff window shows only one row, the app merges without asking.

docs.title: How to move segments into another takeoff
docs.text:
Why: a piece of wall was drawn in the wrong takeoff. You need: the target takeoff already exists.

  1. Select (E), click the segment, Ctrl + click the other wrong ones.
  2. Press Ctrl+M.
  3. In the Merge Into Takeoff dialog pick the target takeoff, Merge.

Result: status Merged 2 segment(s) into ext 2x6 9.09, the segments took on the takeoff's color. Types do not mix: Merge/Split needs one measurement type at a time.

docs.title: How to split a takeoff by section or by sheet
docs.text:
Why: turn one takeoff on three sheets into three takeoffs for the DFL rows. You need: a takeoff with several sections.

Two modes: Each section into a separate takeoff and Separate takeoffs by sheet; the preview shows how many takeoffs you will get.
  1. Select the takeoff (or several) in Takeoffs.
  2. Click Split, Ctrl+Shift+M or right-click Split Selected Takeoffs....
  3. Pick the mode: Each section into a separate takeoff (default) or Separate takeoffs by sheet.
  4. Check the preview 1 takeoff(s) ... 3 takeoff(s), 2 new and click Split.

Result: status Split 1 takeoff(s); created 2 new takeoff(s). Ctrl+Z in Takeoffs to undo. The first group stayed in the original takeoff, the rest became neighboring takeoffs with the same name, folder and properties but a new color. Sections keep their sheet, scale and geometry; empty takeoffs do not change.

Demo: doors on two sheets in one takeoff, Ctrl+Shift+M, Separate takeoffs by sheet: two takeoffs, one per sheet.

Sorting takeoffs by sheet for Excel in detail: Split by sheets.

docs.title: How to split segments or marks off into a new takeoff
docs.text:
Why: part of the measurements should become a separate takeoff with a different name. You need: measurements selected on the sheet.

  1. Select, select the segments. For Count marks: Alt + click or a box around the marks you need.
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+M.
  3. In the Split Selected Measurements dialog (for marks, Split Selected Count Marks) enter the name of the new takeoff, OK.

Result: status Split 4 segment(s) into new takeoff ... or Split 3 Count marks into new takeoff .... The new takeoff sits next to the original one and gets its own color.

docs.title: How to break a polyline into segments
docs.text:
Why: move, recolor or place points on each segment separately. You need: a Line of two or more segments.

Break with the small H/V dot (filled = mode on) and Ends to the right.
  1. Select the lines on the sheet or a Line takeoff in Takeoffs (several are fine).
  2. Click Break or press Ctrl+Shift+B (right-click a line: Break Line Into Segments).
  3. With 200 or more segments, confirm the Break Lines Into Segments prompt.

Result: status Broke 2 line(s) into 9 separate segments. Ctrl+Z restores them. The total length did not change, the number of sections under the takeoff grew. If all lines are already single-segment: Nothing to break.

docs.title: How to sort segments into horizontal and vertical
docs.text:
Why: separate counts for horizontal and vertical members (bracing, trims). You need: a Line drawn, even a single segment.

  1. Select the lines or the takeoff.
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+V. Or fill the H/V dot on the Break button (status Break H/V is on) and click Break.

Result: status Broke 1 line(s) into 7 segments: 4 to bft - Horizontal, 3 to bft - Vertical. Ctrl+Z puts the lines back. Next to the original takeoff appear <name> - Horizontal (the original color) and <name> - Vertical (a contrasting color). The original takeoff stays, even if empty, so that Ctrl+Z can bring back the polylines.

Demo: Ctrl+Shift+V splits a wall into Horizontal and Vertical, then Ends places marks at the line ends.

Tips

  • Running it again adds segments to the same - Horizontal / - Vertical pair, no new pair is created.
  • In the Takeoffs tree Ctrl+Shift+V is Break H/V, while Ctrl+V stays Paste.
  • Diagonal segments go to the axis they are closer to.

docs.title: How to place points at line ends
docs.text:
Why: posts at beam ends, holdowns at shear wall ends. You need: Lines selected on the sheet or a Line takeoff in the tree.

Count Points At Line Ends: name of the new Count, the Merge points where segments meet checkbox, the Create button.
  1. Select the lines.
  2. Click Ends (right-click a line: Count Points At Line Ends...).
  3. Set the name (default <takeoff> End Points), keep the Merge points where segments meet checkbox: one mark at a shared corner instead of two.
  4. Click Create.

Result: status End points created: 14 Count mark(s) in beam End Points. Merged 3 shared corner(s). The new Count sits in the original takeoff's folder and becomes active; the tool switches to Count, so you can add marks by hand. Each source takeoff gives its own Count.

docs.title: How to place points along a line at a spacing
docs.text:
Why: fence posts, hangers, anchors at a spacing. You need: a Line selected.

  1. Select one line or several.
  2. Click P Line (right-click a line: Create Count Points Along Line...).
  3. In the Create Count Points Along Line(s) dialog enter Count takeoff name, Spacing, inches (default is the line's spacing or 16), keep the Include line end point checkbox.
  4. Click Create.

Result: a separate Count with marks along the line. The line stays and gives the LF. No Count points were created means the spacing is longer than the line.

Demo: select the partitions, P Line, name posts 2x4, spacing 48: the marks line up along the lines.

docs.title: How to cut an opening out of an area and erase a piece of a line
docs.text:
Why: shafts, stairs and openings must not be in the area; a line must not run through a garage door. You need: an Area or a Line on the sheet.

  1. Click Cut (X). For a rectangle turn on Box (F9).
  2. Click inside the area: it becomes the target (status Cut: click inside the Area you want to cut if you missed).
  3. Outline the cutout point by point and finish with C or a double click; in Box mode click the second corner.
  4. For a line: Select, pick the line, then Cut and outline the piece you are erasing.

Result: status Cut (polygon): 1 area changed ... or with the number of lines removed and added. A cutout can later be selected with a click inside it, moved, copied with the area or deleted with Del (the area stays).

Demo: X with F9 cuts a rectangle out of an area; the same move cuts a wall line at a door opening.

Cut with no target

If the first click was outside every area and nothing is selected, Cut cuts all lines on the sheet that the outline touches. Select the target before cutting.

docs.title: How to unite, subtract or separate areas
docs.text:
Why: overlapping areas, subtracting a balcony from a floor, splitting into parts. You need: two or more Areas on one sheet; the first one selected is the main one.

  1. Select, click the main area, Ctrl + click the others.
  2. Open the Combine list and pick the operation:
Operation Result Union one area from all selected Subtract subtract the others from the first selected; the others do not change Intersect only the common intersection remains Remove Overlap cut off the overlaps, the first selected stays whole; nothing is counted twice Divide split into non-overlapping parts plus a separate overlap area

Result: status Combine union: 2 area(s) merged into 1 and the like. Combine: the selected areas do not overlap means there is no intersection. For cutouts inside one Area, Cut is simpler.

Demo: click 1st, Ctrl and click the balcony, Combine > Subtract: the floor area shrank by the overlap.

docs.title: How to find identical symbols
docs.text:
Why: count one symbol (holdown, post, hanger) across the whole sheet or job in one pass. You need: a sheet open; an active Count or readiness to create a new one.

  1. Click Similar and drag a box around one symbol.
  2. Pick the threshold: Strict, Default, Loose; if needed, the Match rotated copies (90° / 180° / 270°) and Match mirrored copies checkboxes.
  3. For the whole job tick Search all sheets in this job: matches verified against the raster are added automatically; text-only candidates are only shown. No more than 80 other sheets per search.
  4. Check the marks: blue ones are added right away, orange weak ones are for review, gray check marks are already counted. Include candidates takes the weak ones too, Strong only takes only the reliable ones.
  5. Click Add N to <name>.

Result: marks in the active Count or in a new Similar Count. The Ask AI to identify the symbol checkbox works online and only suggests a name (needs the AI module and a key, that is, the full version; in Lite the checkbox is visible but disabled). More on searching across sheets: Similar across all sheets.

Demo: Similar, a box around a window, the Match rotated copies and Search all sheets checkboxes, Add. The wait for the cross-sheet search is cut out.

docs.title: How to mirror, rotate and scale the selection
docs.text:
Why: a mirrored unit, a rotated building, measurements from a sheet at a different scale. You need: measurements or markup selected on the sheet.

  1. Select, select the measurements (together with cutouts and markup if needed).
  2. Click Flip H or Flip V in row 2 of the strip: a mirror around the center of the selection.
  3. Rotation: drag the orange rotate handle on the selection frame (Shift gives 15° steps) or move the Rot slider; the arrow button next to it resets the slider to zero for the next relative rotation.
  4. Size: the orange corner handles scale from the center, the side handles stretch one side (Shift keeps the proportions); or use the Scale slider and the 1x field (type 1.25x or 125%, Enter).

Result: status Mirrored selection horizontal, Rotated selection 90 deg, Scaled selection 1.25x. A slider move is undone with one Ctrl+Z. The joist direction rotates together with a J Area. The keys Mirror selected objects horizontally / vertically are not bound by default.

Demo: a box around the measurements, Flip H, Flip V, the Rot slider; three Ctrl+Z bring everything back.

docs.title: How to repeat segments and beams
docs.text:
Why: a series of short segments or beams without picking the tool each time. You need: a sheet with a scale.

  1. Click the arrow button Repeat Line to the right of Line (or Repeat Beam to the right of Beam).
  2. For a Line, set the name of the new takeoff once. Every two clicks create a separate two-point segment in it.
  3. For a Beam, each pair of clicks measures the length, asks for the name and places a mark, then waits for the next beam.
  4. Press Esc or click the repeat button again to stop.

Result: status Repeat drawing stopped, a series of measurements in the tree.

Demo: Repeat Line, name blk 2x10, segments with pairs of clicks without switching tools, Esc finishes.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text:
• Merge does not join geometry: two walls end to end stay two segments with a combined total.
  • Split on the sheet and Split in the tree are different commands; look at where the selection is.
  • Break H/V creates a pair of takeoffs and adds to it on the next run.
  • Similar finds similar pictures, not the same purpose: a window and a door of the same shape can end up in one count. Check the orange marks.
  • Operations from the tree are undone with Ctrl+Z only with focus in the Takeoffs panel; operations on the sheet only with focus in the viewport.
  • Cut with no selected target cuts all lines the outline touches.

docs.text:
