docs.title: Editing measurements and snaps: how it all works together
docs.text:
This page collects everything you do with a measurement that is already drawn: how to select an object or its vertex, how to move, cut, merge, cut out, mirror and undo. The tables answer which tool and where, the recipes at the bottom show the operations together, the right-click menu items (copy, rename, delete on the sheet, in Takeoffs, Pages and Estimating) are collected at the end of the page, the detailed steps of each operation are on the Merge, Split, Break, Ends, Combine, Similar page, and snaps and tracing are on the Snap and tracing page.

Row 1 of the tool strip: drawing, Cut, Merge, Split, Combine, the Snap / PDF / Ortho / Box toggles. Row 2: Transform (Flip H, Flip V, Rot, Scale).

docs.title: Selection model
docs.text:
The Select tool (E key). There is one rule: Ctrl works with objects, Alt with vertices. Shift without Ctrl is reserved for Ortho (it holds a right angle temporarily).

Left: a click and a box with no keys replace the selection, with Ctrl they add an object, with Ctrl+Shift they remove it. Right: Alt toggles the blue handles of the selected object, Alt-click on the body takes all handles, Alt-click on empty space clears them. What I want Gesture What the status bar shows select one measurement click on a line, outline or mark Moving Line... while dragging select several with a box a box left to right takes what is fully inside; a box right to left takes everything it touches Selected N measurement(s) and M enclosed cutout(s) or ... touched cutout(s) add to the selection Ctrl + click or Ctrl + box Selected N measurement(s) and M cutout(s) remove from the selection Ctrl+Shift + click or box Removed N object(s) all measurements on the sheet Ctrl+A vertices of the selected Line or Area Alt + click on a handle toggles one, Alt + box toggles all handles in the box, Alt + click on the body takes all, Alt + click on empty space clears N handle(s) selected one Count mark click the mark and drag; no Alt needed a cutout (hole) in an Area click inside the cutout; Ctrl adds to the selection ... cutout(s) clear the selection click on empty space or Esc

What else selection on the sheet does: Del deletes the selected objects, the selected vertices or the selected cutouts (the parent Area stays); F2 or a double click on a measurement renames its takeoff; Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy to another sheet (copying); H hides the whole takeoff of the selected measurement on this sheet (visibility).

Sheet and tree. The selection on the sheet and the selection in the Takeoffs tree live separately. On the sheet you select segments, marks and cutouts of one page. In the tree you select whole takeoffs (Ctrl or Shift on rows) or sections under a takeoff. Merge, Split, Break and Ends look at where the selection is: if takeoff rows are selected in the tree, they work on whole takeoffs on all sheets; otherwise on what is selected on the sheet. Ctrl+Enter in the tree selects the section's measurements on the sheet.

docs.title: Editing vertices
docs.text: You need: the Select tool, a Line or Area measurement selected (blue handles visible).

docs.title: How to move a vertex
docs.text:
1. Hover over a blue handle of the selected measurement.
  2. Drag it. Shift while dragging keeps the move on one axis, Snap (F3) catches the vertex on the ends, midpoints and intersections of neighboring measurements.
  3. Release the button.

Result: status Editing Line vertex N, the takeoff's length or area is recalculated in Total.

docs.title: How to move several vertices at once
docs.text:
1. Select the measurement (or several measurements with a box).
  2. Alt + box around the corners you need: the handles become selected.
  3. Drag any selected handle; all selected ones move together. Shift holds the axis.

Result: status Editing N selected vertices. This is how the shared corner of two walls is moved in one go.

docs.title: How to add and remove a vertex
docs.text:
1. Right-click the line or outline at the right spot: the Insert Vertex Here item inserts a vertex into the nearest segment. Status Inserted Line vertex N.
  2. To remove an extra one: right-click next to it, Remove Nearest Vertex; or Alt + click on the handle and Del. A Line must keep at least two points, an Area three.
  3. To delete Count marks: Alt + click or a box around the marks, Del. If all marks of a measurement are selected, the whole measurement is deleted.

Result: Deleted N selected vertex/vertices. Ctrl+Z brings it back.

Demo: right-click a line, Insert Vertex Here, drag the vertex, then Remove Nearest Vertex.

docs.title: Undo: which one where
docs.text:
The app has several undos, each listens to its own focus.

Where the focus is Key What it undoes sheet (viewport) Ctrl+Z or Backspace the last geometry action on this sheet: drawing (point by point), move, vertices, Cut, Combine, Break, Transform, paste, delete, markup and the Hide mask, crops on the target sheet, overlay shift. Depth 80 steps; each sheet has its own stack, cleared when you switch sheets Takeoffs tree Ctrl+Z or right-click Undo Takeoff Merge / Split deleting takeoffs and folders, Merge and Split of whole takeoffs, in reverse order Pages tree Ctrl+Z or right-click Undo Last Page Delete only the last deletion of sheets and folders; another job or closing the app sends it to the Windows Recycle Bin Main > Open / Import Undo Last Page Sort, Undo Last Page Operation sheet sorting, job import

Not undone by Undo: renaming, moving a takeoff between folders, legend order and groups, placing a crop from the source sheet (delete it on the target sheet).

docs.title: Operations map
docs.text:
What I want to do Tool Key Where in the menu Page select, move, delete Select E, Del tool strip above move or delete a vertex handles, Alt Del right-click Insert Vertex Here, Remove Nearest Vertex above merge takeoffs or segments Merge Ctrl+M right-click in Takeoffs Merge Selected Takeoffs... Merge split a takeoff by sheet or section Split Ctrl+Shift+M right-click in Takeoffs Split Selected Takeoffs... Split split segments or marks off into a new takeoff Split on the sheet Ctrl+Shift+M Split on the sheet break a polyline into segments Break Ctrl+Shift+B right-click a line Break Line Into Segments Break sort into horizontal and vertical Break with the H/V dot Ctrl+Shift+V Break H/V points at line ends Ends none right-click a line Count Points At Line Ends... Ends points along a line at a spacing P Line none right-click a line Create Count Points Along Line... P Line cutout in an area, erase a piece of a line Cut X, F9 box tool strip Cut add, subtract, trim overlapping areas Combine none Combine list Combine find identical symbols Similar none tool strip Similar mirror, rotate, scale the selection Transform none (Mirror can be bound) row 2 of the strip Transform repeat segments or beams without a dialog Repeat Line, Repeat Beam none arrow buttons next to Line and Beam Repeat right angle, rectangle, snap to your own points Ortho, Box, Snap F8, F9, F3 tool strip Snap take walls off a vector PDF Trace Walls Inside Area, Layer Trace none right-click an Area, PDF Layers tab tracing

All commands are also in the palette Ctrl+Shift+P (Break Lines Into Segments, Count Points At Line Ends, Combine Areas: Union...). A key with no binding can be assigned in the key editor. Merge, Split, Break, Ends, P Line, Combine, Similar and wall tracing require the Advanced Takeoff Tools module (on by default, Settings > Modules).

docs.title: What works with what
docs.text:
Operation Line Area Count J Area Beam Openings move, Del, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V yes yes yes yes yes yes vertices (Alt, Insert, Remove) yes yes marks yes mark mark Merge of whole takeoffs yes yes yes yes like Count like Count Merge of segments on the sheet yes yes yes yes like Count like Count Split of a takeoff by section or sheet yes yes yes yes like Count like Count Split of segments or marks on the sheet yes yes yes, selected marks yes marks marks Break, Break H/V yes no no no no no Ends, P Line yes no no no no no Cut erases a piece cutout no cutout no no Combine no yes, 2 or more no yes, like Area no no Transform yes yes yes yes yes yes Similar no no yes no no no

Beam and Openings are stored as a Count with a mark, so for editing they behave like a Count: the mark can be moved, merged, split; the beam length and the opening size sit in the name. Merge and Split do not mix types: Line only with Line, Area with Area, Count with Count, J Area with J Area.

docs.title: Recipes together
docs.text: Each recipe runs from an estimator's task to a visible result. The PDF snap is not used in the recipes: it works unreliably (why); accuracy comes from Ortho, Box, Snap to your own points, zoom and editing vertices afterwards.

docs.title: How to trace a wall with right angles and close the outline
docs.text:
Why: a polyline along the wall centerline with no corners drifting by a fraction of a degree. You need: a sheet with a scale, the W sheet dot set.

  1. Click Line (L), give the takeoff a name (ext 2x6 9.09), OK.
  2. Turn on Ortho (F8) and Snap (F3).
  3. Zoom in on the first corner and click on the wall centerline.
  4. Move the cursor to the next corner: Ortho holds horizontal or vertical. On a diagonal run release Ortho with one press of F8 and turn it back on afterwards.
  5. To close, bring the cursor to the first point: the Snap highlight shows end; click. For an Area a click near the first point is enough, the outline closes by itself.
  6. Press C or double-click to finish the polyline.
  7. Check the corners: Select, drag the handles where the centerline drifted.

Result: a takeoff in walls/<floor> floor walls, Total shows the length. An extra point while drawing is removed with Backspace.

Demo: L, name ext 2x6 9.09, the route line walls/1st floor walls, clicks along the exterior wall centerline and C.

docs.title: How to break a line into segments and sort them into horizontal and vertical
docs.text:
Why: one bracing or trim polyline turns into two counts: horizontal and vertical feet. You need: a Line drawn.

  1. Select the lines on the sheet or the takeoff in Takeoffs.
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+V (or fill the H/V dot on the Break button and click Break).
  3. Read the status: Broke 1 line(s) into 7 segments: 4 to bft - Horizontal, 3 to bft - Vertical.
  4. In Takeoffs, bft - Horizontal and bft - Vertical appeared next to the original takeoff. The original takeoff is now empty: delete it or keep it.

Result: two separate totals. A regular Break (Ctrl+Shift+B) cuts into segments and keeps them in the same takeoff. Diagram: what Break and Break H/V do.

Demo: Ctrl+Shift+V splits a wall into Horizontal and Vertical, then Ends places marks at the line ends.

docs.title: How to merge segments from different takeoffs into one
docs.text:
Why: a wall is drawn partly in ext 2x6 9.09 and partly, by mistake, in int 2x4 9.09. You need: both measurements on one sheet.

  1. Select, click the segment in the wrong takeoff, Ctrl + click the other wrong ones.
  2. Press Ctrl+M.
  3. In the Merge Into Takeoff dialog pick ext 2x6 9.09, Merge.

Result: status Merged 2 segment(s) into ext 2x6 9.09, the segments changed to the takeoff's color. To merge two whole takeoffs, select their rows in the tree and press Ctrl+M: Merge of whole takeoffs.

Demo: a wall segment landed in the wrong takeoff; Ctrl+M and Merge Into Takeoff move it into ext 2x6 9.09.

docs.title: How to split a takeoff by sheet
docs.text:
Why: the rf 6 roof is drawn on three sheets, and the DFL needs a row per sheet. You need: a takeoff with sections on several sheets.

  1. Select the takeoff in Takeoffs.
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+M.
  3. In the Split Selected Takeoffs dialog pick Separate takeoffs by sheet; the preview shows 1 takeoff(s) ... 3 takeoff(s), 2 new.
  4. Click Split.
  5. Rename the copies (F2): rf 6 a105, rf 6 a106.

Result: three takeoffs with the same name and properties, the split-off ones got a new color. More on sorting by sheet: Split by sheets page.

Demo: doors on two sheets in one takeoff, Ctrl+Shift+M, Separate takeoffs by sheet: two takeoffs, one per sheet.

docs.title: How to cut an opening out of an area and erase a piece of a line
docs.text:
Why: a shaft or stair must not be in 1st, and a wall line must not run through a garage door opening. You need: an Area and a Line drawn.

  1. Click Cut (X). For a rectangular cutout turn on Box (F9).
  2. Click inside the area you are cutting: it gets selected, and the cutout goes only into it.
  3. Outline the cutout (in Box mode the second corner), finish with C or a double click.
  4. For a line: Select, pick the line, Cut again and outline the piece to erase. The line falls apart into pieces on both sides.

Result: status Cut (box): ... with the number of areas and lines changed, Total went down. If the first click was outside the area, Cut cuts all lines on the sheet that the outline touches: select the target first.

Demo: X with F9 cuts a rectangle out of an area; the same move cuts a wall line at a door opening.

docs.title: How to unite or subtract areas
docs.text:
Why: two roof slopes overlap, or a separately drawn balcony must be subtracted from the floor area. You need: two or more Areas on one sheet.

  1. Select, click the first area (it is the main one), Ctrl + click the others.
  2. Open the Combine list.
  3. Pick: Union to add into one, Subtract to subtract the others from the first, Remove Overlap to trim the overlap (the first stays whole), Intersect to keep the common part, Divide to split into parts.
  4. Compare Total before and after.

Result: status Combine remove overlap: trimmed 1 area(s) against the first-selected. Selection order matters: click first the area that must stay whole.

Demo: click 1st, Ctrl and click the balcony, Combine > Subtract: the floor area shrank by the overlap.

docs.title: How to place points at the ends and along a line
docs.text:
Why: posts at beam ends, studs or hangers at a spacing along a line. You need: Lines drawn.

  1. Select the lines (on the sheet or the takeoff in the tree).
  2. Click Ends. In the Count Points At Line Ends dialog keep the Merge points where segments meet checkbox, set the name, Create.
  3. Select the lines again and click P Line. In the Create Count Points Along Line(s) dialog set Count takeoff name, Spacing, inches (for example 96), the Include line end point checkbox, Create.

Result: two new Counts in the same folder, status End points created: N Count mark(s). Extra marks at joints are removed with Alt + click and Del.

Demo: select the partitions, P Line, name posts 2x4, spacing 48: the marks line up along the lines.

docs.title: How to find identical symbols on other sheets
docs.text:
Why: count one holdown or post on all floors in one pass. You need: an active Count or readiness to start a new one, a sheet open.

  1. Click Similar, drag a box around one symbol.
  2. In the dialog pick the Default threshold (or Strict if it catches too much), tick Search all sheets in this job. The search across all sheets takes tens of seconds even on a small job (about 35 s on the demo), and the Add button waits for it to finish: do not click again.
  3. Look at the marks: blue ones will be added, orange ones are weak, gray ones are already counted. When in doubt, click Strong only.
  4. Click the Add N to <name> button.

Result: marks added to the Count on the current and other sheets, the status lists what was added. The search looks for a similar picture, not the same purpose: check the orange ones.

Demo: Similar, a box around a window, the Match rotated copies and Search all sheets checkboxes, Add. The wait for the cross-sheet search is cut out.

docs.title: How to repeat drawing a series
docs.text:
Why: twenty short ledgers or ten beams without a dialog for each. You need: a sheet with a scale.

  1. Click the Repeat Line arrow next to Line (or Repeat Beam next to Beam).
  2. For a Line, set the name once. After that every two clicks give a separate segment in that takeoff.
  3. For a Beam, each pair of clicks measures a beam, asks for the name and places a mark, then waits for the next one.
  4. Press Esc to finish. Status Repeat drawing stopped.

Result: a series of segments or beams without switching tools.

Demo: Repeat Line, name blk 2x10, segments with pairs of clicks without switching tools, Esc finishes.

docs.title: How to mirror and rotate measurements
docs.text:
Why: a mirrored unit or a rotated building: copied measurements need to be turned in place. You need: measurements selected on the sheet.

  1. Select, select the measurements with a box.
  2. In row 2 of the strip click Flip H or Flip V: a mirror around the center of the selection.
  3. Rotation: drag the orange rotate handle on the selection frame (Shift gives 15° steps) or move the Rot slider; the arrow button resets the slider to zero for the next rotation.
  4. Size: the corner handles scale from the center, the side handles stretch one side (Shift keeps the proportions); or the Scale slider and the 1x field.
  5. Drag the selection into place.

Result: status Mirrored selection horizontal, Rotated selection 90 deg. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole slider move. Mirror keys are assigned in the key editor (Mirror selected objects horizontally / vertically).

Demo: a box around the measurements, Flip H, Flip V, the Rot slider; three Ctrl+Z bring everything back.

docs.title: How to fix a measurement that went into the wrong takeoff
docs.text:
Why: a wall was drawn while Record was active on someone else's takeoff, or on a sheet with the wrong dot. You need: to know where the measurement should go.

  1. Find the measurement on the sheet: click the wrong takeoff in the tree, Ctrl+Enter on the section highlights its measurements.
  2. If the right takeoff already exists: Select, pick the measurement, Ctrl+M, choose the right takeoff in Merge Into Takeoff.
  3. If the right takeoff does not exist: Ctrl+Shift+M, enter a new name in Split Selected Measurements. The new takeoff lands next to the original one.
  4. If the whole sheet was wrong (the wrong W/F/S dot): fix the dot under Scale, then drag the takeoff in the tree into the right folder or merge it with the right one via Ctrl+M on the tree rows.

Result: the original takeoff's Total went down, status Merged N segment(s) into ... or Split N segment(s) into new takeoff .... Where a new measurement will go: routing.

docs.title: How to close the corner of two walls drawn separately
docs.text:
Why: two lines meeting end to end leave a gap or an overlap at the corner, and it shows in the PDF. You need: both lines on one sheet.

  1. Select, click the first line, Ctrl + click the second.
  2. Alt + box around the corner: both end handles are selected.
  3. Drag one handle with Snap (F3) on: both points move together and stick to the end or intersection.
  4. If the lines are in the same takeoff and you want one segment instead of two, leave it as is: Merge does not join geometry, and the total length is already right.

Result: status Editing 2 selected vertices, the corner meets at one point.

docs.title: Break and Break H/V diagram
docs.text: Left: a polyline of five segments in the bft takeoff. Center, after Break: five separate segments in the same takeoff, same total. Right, after Break H/V: the horizontal ones went into bft - Horizontal, the vertical ones into bft - Vertical.

docs.title: Right-click menus: copy, rename, delete
docs.text:
The same actions as the keys and buttons above are in the right-click menus. The item name changes with the selection: with several rows Copy Selected replaces Copy Item, and on a Count takeoff Count replaces Section. Below, the items are grouped by where the menu is opened.

Right-click a measurement on the sheet Item What it does When you need it Copy Measurement puts the measurement under the cursor on the clipboard, like Ctrl+C; with a selection the item is called Copy Selected Measurements, with cutouts Copy N Cutout(s) move a measurement to another sheet Paste Measurements to This Sheet pastes the clipboard onto this sheet (with a number: Paste 3 Measurement(s) to This Sheet): the top left corner of the copied set lands at the click point, then the same Paste Measurements dialog as with Ctrl+V identical floor or building: copying Merge Segment..., Split Segment... move the measurement into another takeoff or split it off into a new one Merge on the sheet, Split on the sheet Takeoff Properties..., Section Properties... properties of the whole takeoff; name and note of one measurement (section) change spacing, color, height; mark one run Rename Section changes the section name, that is the row of this measurement under the takeoff in Takeoffs; does not touch the takeoff name. For a Count the item is Rename Count, for a measurement with no takeoff Rename Measurement, and it is disabled label a run (north wing) so you can find it in the tree Insert Vertex Here, Remove Nearest Vertex insert or remove a vertex vertices Delete Section deletes only this measurement after the prompt Delete this section from <takeoff>?; the takeoff and its other measurements stay. For a Count Delete Count, for a measurement with no takeoff Delete Measurement (disabled) an extra run; the whole takeoff is deleted in the tree Line and J Area items Break Line Into Segments, Count Points At Line Ends..., Create Count Points Along Line...; Use Area As Joists..., Delete Nearest Extra Joist and others Break and Ends, J Area menu

In a separate sheet window (Detach) the menu is shorter: Copy Measurement, Paste Measurements to This Sheet, Takeoff Properties..., Section Properties..., Rename Section, the J Area items and Hide on This Sheet / Show on This Sheet. The Delete Section, Merge, Split and vertex items are not there: that is done in the main window.

Right-click in the Takeoffs tree Where Item What it does takeoff Duplicate Item (Ctrl+D) a copy of the takeoff with the same name, properties and all measurements in the same folder, at the end of the list. The copy's measurements sit on the same sheets on top of the originals: before Excel, rename and move the copy or delete what is extra takeoff Delete item + measurements deletes the takeoff and all its measurements on all sheets after the prompt Delete "<name>" and all contained measurements?; Ctrl+Z in the Takeoffs panel brings it back takeoff, Clipboard submenu Copy Item, Cut Item, Paste Into Parent Folder copy or move a takeoff; to paste into another folder: right-click the folder, Paste Into Folder folder Delete folder + children deletes the folder with all its takeoffs and measurements; Ctrl+Z in the Takeoffs panel brings it back folder, Clipboard submenu Copy Folder, Cut Folder, Paste Into Folder, Duplicate Folder the same for a whole folder: move a floor into another building, multiply a floor tree Takeoffs root (empty space under the tree) Paste Into Root pastes what was copied or cut at the top level of the tree section under a takeoff Rename Section, Delete Section (for several: Delete 3 Sections) as on the sheet, but for the selected section rows

With several rows selected the items are called Copy Selected, Cut Selected, Duplicate Selected, Delete selected takeoffs. Cut and paste: measurements, color and legend order are kept. Copy and paste or Duplicate: the measurements are copied too.

Right-click in the Pages tree and Batch Rotate Where Item What it does sheet or folder, first line Undo Last Page Delete brings back the last deletion of sheets or folders, like Ctrl+Z in Pages; when there is something to bring back, the item reads Undo Delete: <name>. One deletion is kept: the next deletion, switching to another job or closing the app sends the previous one to the Windows Recycle Bin sheet Delete Page (several: Delete Selected) deletes the sheet after the prompt Delete page '<name>'? folder Delete Folder deletes the folder with everything in it after the prompt Delete folder '<name>' and everything inside it? sheet, Clipboard submenu Copy Page, Cut Page, Paste Into Parent Folder cut and paste moves the sheet, the measurements stay attached to it. Copy and paste gives a copy of the sheet (PDF, scale, markup) without measurements: measurements live in Takeoffs folder, Clipboard submenu Copy Folder, Cut Folder, Paste Into Folder the same for a folder of sheets sheet or folder, PDF Metadata submenu Auto Rename from PDF..., Auto Rename + Scale from PDF... the same as the Name and Name+Scale buttons of the Pages panel, for the sheets under the cursor and the selected ones: a preview of names (and scales), applied after OK (names) Page ribbon, Batch Rotate button Rotate Selected Left, Rotate Selected Right, Rotate Selected 180 rotates the PDF of all sheets selected in Pages (with no selection, the current sheet); measurements, cutouts, markup and the origin point rotate together with the sheet Right-click an Estimating row

Go to Page (with several rows Go to First Page) opens the measurement's sheet, Select on Canvas selects the measurement on the sheet, Section Properties... opens the section name and note, Rename Section and Delete Section work as on the sheet. With several rows selected these two items are called Rename Measurement and Delete Measurement and are disabled: renaming and deleting go one row at a time.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text:
• Merge does not join geometry: two lines end to end stay two segments with a combined total.
  • Cut with no selected target cuts all lines on the sheet that the outline touches. Make the first click inside the area or select the target in advance.
  • Combine looks at the selection order: the first selected area is the main one for Subtract and Remove Overlap.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes where the focus is: the sheet, the Takeoffs tree or the Pages tree. After switching sheets the sheet's undo stack is empty.
  • Break H/V on a repeat run adds to the existing - Horizontal / - Vertical pair instead of creating a new one.
  • Snap on a dense drawing catches on a neighboring measurement: turn off F3 or zoom in.
  • A click on a Count mark moves it right away, with no Alt: Ctrl+Z undoes an accidental move.
  • Duplicate Item and copying a takeoff in the tree copy the measurements too: on the sheet the copy sits on top of the original, and the Excel total doubles. Copy Page on the contrary copies the sheet without measurements.
  • Rename Section renames the measurement row, not the takeoff: the name for Excel comes from the takeoff (F2 on the takeoff row in the tree).

docs.text:

docs.title: Export to Excel
docs.text: This page covers how to move numbers from the Takeoffs tree into the DFL workbook. In Lite these are the Excel and Value buttons at the bottom left, a permanent link from a takeoff to a cell with Link to Excel, Auto Link for the whole DFL, resetting links, and Export > Export Excel to a file. The XL strip to the right of the sheet, which writes sections into TemplateCom.xlsm and runs the workbook macros by itself, exists only in the full version: it is described at the end of the page (XL strip). You need it after measuring, before working in the DFL.

docs.title: Excel in Lite
docs.text:
What Where What it does Excel bottom left rows of the selected folder or takeoff (name, number, unit) from the active cell of the open workbook (below) Value next to Excel only the numbers of the same selection in one column (below) Link to Excel next to Value the number of one takeoff into a cell; after that the cell updates by itself (below) Auto Link next to Link to Excel link takeoffs to the J:L list of a DFL workbook in one click (below) Export > Export Excel the Export menu of the Takeoffs panel export of the tree to an .xlsx file, columns J/K/L from row 10

Lite does not run the workbook macros: it has no XL strip. Run the calculation on the exported J:L list (areas, walls, openings, eaves) in Excel with the E-Wood tab buttons (Calculation from takeoffs). Make the building workbook from the template in the templates folder of the shared Dropbox folder (TemplateCom template).

docs.title: How to put one takeoff into a cell: Value and Excel
docs.text:
Why: drop a number or several rows into a finished workbook without macros.

  1. In Excel click the target cell in the open workbook.
  2. Select a takeoff or folder in Takeoffs.
  3. Press Excel at the bottom left: the rows (name, number, unit) are written from the active cell. Or press Value: only the numbers of the same selection in one column, to quickly fill G in existing rows.

Result: the data is in the workbook from the selected cell. The message Open Excel, open a workbook, click the destination cell means there is no active cell.

Button What it does Excel (bottom left) writes the selected folder or takeoff as rows (name, number, unit) from the active cell of the open workbook; no macros the dot on the Excel button (Include takeoff comments in Excel export) filled - the takeoff and measurement comments (notes) go into the export; off by default. Applies to Excel and Export > Export Excel; Value and the XL strip do not write comments, CSV and TXT always do Value writes only the numbers of the same selection in one column from the active cell Link to Excel writes the number of one takeoff into the active cell and keeps it there: below Auto Link DFL only: links all takeoffs whose numbers are already in the J:L list, at once: below Export > Export CSV / TXT / Excel export of the tree to a file Export > Export to Current Excel same as the Excel button

docs.title: How to add a comment to a measurement and send it to Excel
docs.text:
Why: a note for the DFL next to the number (verify on site, per S2.1) that travels to the workbook with the takeoff.

  1. Right-click the measurement (section) row under the takeoff in Takeoffs and choose Set Notes...; for several selected rows the item is called Set Notes for N Rows....
  2. Type the text, each line is a separate comment, press OK. A comment for the whole takeoff goes into the Notes: field of the takeoff's Properties... window.
  3. Click the dot on the Excel button at the bottom left so it is filled: status Excel comments are on: include takeoff and measurement comments.
  4. Click the target cell in Excel and press Excel.

Result: under the takeoff row come the comment rows (first the takeoff's, then the measurements'; duplicates are not repeated) and an empty row after them.

docs.title: How to keep a number in a cell: Link to Excel
docs.text:
Value writes the number once. Link to Excel writes the number into the cell and remembers the link: change the measurement and the cell updates by itself. One takeoff, one number, one cell.

One way only, from OurPlanCore to Excel

Editing the cell does not change the measurement. The app does not save the open workbook; you do. Until you press Link, the app does not touch Excel: a job without links leaves Excel alone.

The number goes from the takeoff to the cell. The icon color on the takeoff row shows the link state. Names in the diagram are examples.

Why: the number in the workbook follows the measurement by itself; no need to repeat Value after every edit. You need: version 3.0.28 or newer, the workbook open in Excel and saved as a file, the job not opened read-only.

  1. Select one takeoff in Takeoffs. A measurement row under a takeoff counts as that takeoff; a folder does not work, nor does an annotation takeoff with no quantity.
  2. In Excel click the cell you need.
  3. In OurPlanCore press Link to Excel at the bottom right, next to Value and Excel. The same command: right-click on the takeoff, Excel Link > Link to Excel, or the Ctrl+Shift+P palette. No default key.
  4. If the cell already has text, another number, a formula or another link, the app asks: Replace or Cancel.
  5. Read the status at the bottom: Linked <takeoff> to <workbook> <sheet!cell>: <number>. A chain icon appears on the takeoff row.
  6. Change the measurement and look at the cell: the number updates after a short pause.
  7. Save the workbook in Excel yourself.

Result: the takeoff number sits in the cell and follows the measurement. The value is the same one Value writes: same units and rounding.

The feature is new. On the first workbook, compare the cell with Total in the tree with your own eyes.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
What happened What happens the workbook is open the cell updates after a short pause. The active worksheet, selection and calculation mode in Excel stay as they were. A write from the app clears Excel's own undo (Ctrl+Z): a formula replaced with Replace cannot be brought back with undo Excel is busy or a cell is being edited the link waits (Pending), the app retries by itself the workbook is closed the link waits (Pending). The number is written when the job is saved (Ctrl+S; autosave does not count) or by Update Links: in a hidden Excel with macros off, with a copy of the workbook made before writing; then the write is read back from disk rows were inserted above the cell the link holds on to a hidden name _OPLink_... in the workbook, which follows the cell. The app does not guess the address the row with the cell was deleted, by hand or by a macro the link is Broken, nothing is written the takeoff was renamed or moved to another folder the link follows it. A copy of the takeoff has no link the takeoff was deleted the link is Broken, the cell stays as it is; Ctrl+Z in the app restores the link

Link and Unlink themselves cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z. The workbook copies are in the app profile: for Lite in %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\local\excel-link-backups, for the full version in %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore\excel-link-backups; there are none next to the workbook.

docs.title: States: the icon on the takeoff
docs.text:
State Icon What it means What to do Linked gray the cell has this takeoff's number nothing Pending yellow the new number is not written yet: the workbook is closed, Excel is busy, the workbook or file is read-only, the file is locked by another program or missing, the cell is protected, the joists have no direction set closed workbook: Ctrl+S or Update Links. The icon tooltip gives the reason Conflict orange the cell was changed by hand or a formula was typed into it. The app does not write over it Overwrite the Cell (the app's number on top) or Keep the Cell and Unlink (the cell stays, there is no link any more) Broken red the takeoff was deleted, the row or cell was deleted (#REF!), the hidden name disappeared from the workbook, the joists got a different number of lengths. Nothing is written a deleted takeoff comes back with Ctrl+Z. Otherwise Unlink and link again

The icon tooltip: state, workbook, worksheet and cell, last number written, reason.

docs.title: Joists: which number
docs.text:
A J Area takeoff has no single number (Value writes a line of text there), so Link asks which number goes into this cell:

Option in the window What it is Count of the 16 length: 45 pieces of this order length Length 16 the order length itself Total count, all lengths: ... all pieces, if there are several lengths Total length, all lengths: ... total length, if there are several lengths

For a second number, click another cell and press Link again. The link holds on to "length number N of M": if the number of lengths in the takeoff changed, the link becomes Broken and asks to be linked again; a wrong number will not get into the cell. The totals survive any such edit. Without a joist direction set, the app will not link: Set the joist direction before linking this takeoff.

docs.title: All job links: All Excel Links
docs.text:
To open it: right-click on a takeoff, Excel Link > All Excel Links..., or the Excel Links... command in the palette. The Excel Links window has the columns Takeoff, Workbook, Cell, Last value, State, Why.

Button What it does Go to Cell shows the cell in Excel, opening a closed workbook first Overwrite the Cell, Keep the Cell and Unlink visible when a link in Conflict is selected Unlink there is no link any more, the number stays in the cell. If the workbook is closed, its hidden name goes away when the workbook is opened while this job is open Update Links writes everything that is waiting, including to closed workbooks, and rechecks the hidden names of broken links. This button works with any settings. The same: Excel Link > Update Links or Update Excel Links in the palette Point to New Path... the workbook was moved or renamed. No new workbook is created Remove All Links from This Workbook... see below Reset All Links... removes all links of this job: see below

Before delivering the workbook to the client

All Excel Links..., select a link to this workbook, Remove All Links from This Workbook.... The numbers stay in the cells, the hidden names leave the workbook. All of them go, including those made by other jobs and OurPDF.

docs.title: How to link the whole DFL in one click: Auto Link
docs.text:
Why: the numbers are already exported to the J:L list, and linking each takeoff by hand takes long. You need: version 3.0.29 or newer (the same in Lite), a saved DFL workbook active in Excel, the job not opened read-only. OurPDF has the same button since 0.9.27.

Look at the result window right after pressing

There is no question before linking; the result window is the check. A Probable link can land on someone else's row with the same number, and the next measurement edit will write the new number there. Once you close the window, Undo This Auto Link is gone.

  1. In a job with several buildings, put the green dot on the building you need: Auto Link takes only its takeoffs. With no active building, all takeoffs of the job are taken.
  2. Press Auto Link at the bottom, next to Link to Excel. The same command: right-click on a takeoff, Excel Link > Auto Link (DFL), or Auto Link in the Ctrl+Shift+P palette. No default key.
  3. The links appear at once; the Auto Link window shows the result for each takeoff: Group, Takeoff, Number, Cell, Label in column J, Result, Why.
  4. Check every Probable row: the label in column J must be about this takeoff.
  5. Save the workbook in Excel yourself. Auto Link does not change cell values and does not save the workbook; it only adds hidden names. Close the workbook without saving and the names disappear, the links become Broken.

Result: the Sure and Probable takeoffs are linked; the rest are described in the window with a reason.

DFL only: an .xlsm, .xlsb or .xls workbook with a Detailed Frame List worksheet whose column A has the word Description in the first 150 rows. Another workbook: status Auto Link works only with a DFL, nothing else happens. Link to Excel works on any workbook.

What gets linked. There is only one target: constant numbers in column K of this worksheet, from row 2; the label is taken from column J. Formulas never count. Columns A:H, the blocks O:AB, O135:W147, O105:AL129, Z158 and beyond (the macros fill them from J:L), spec cells and other worksheets are never targets, even if the number matches.

Group When What happens Sure the label in J equals the takeoff name (case and spaces do not matter), the number matches, there is one such row linked at once Probable the label does not equal the name, but the number is one to one: it sits in exactly one K cell and no other participating takeoff has it (openings, joists and already linked ones do not count). The label of that row is not the name of another takeoff linked at once, check it by eye Ambiguous this number is in several cells or belongs to several takeoffs, the name does not decide it not linked: select the row in the window, pick the cell in the Cell column, press Link This Row Skipped the list below; the reason is written in the window row not linked

The number is compared at the rounding Value shows, and no looser. A cell with 162.504 matches 162.5 and keeps its value until the takeoff number changes. If you changed the measurement after exporting, the number is not in the list and the takeoff will be skipped.

What is skipped:

  • windows, doors and other openings: an openings folder above the takeoff, or the name window, windows, wind, wnd, door, doors, opening, openings, storefront, gd, lv, louver, words starting with окн, двер, проём (Russian for window, door, opening), an opening size with a dot like 3.0x6.7 d. A J row with such a label is not a target either. Manual Link to Excel works on them;
  • J Area takeoffs: they have more than one number; link them by hand with the question, as usual;
  • points (Count) without their own name in J: points are linked only by name, whatever the number. 240 without a name stays unlinked;
  • a small whole number without a name: a line or area with a whole number under 10 (threshold in the settings). With a name it gets linked;
  • zero and a takeoff with no number;
  • an already linked takeoff, a cell with another link, a formula in the cell, a list row with the name of another takeoff, the number not in the list.

When Probable gets it wrong:

  • a hand-typed J row with a different name and the same number, while the takeoff itself is not exported to the list yet;
  • a sum row (two takeoffs in one number) happens to equal a third one;
  • a takeoff of another building, when no active building is set and its number equals a row in this workbook;
  • two floors with the same area: one row is exported, and the second floor is not measured yet;
  • harmless: the takeoff was renamed after exporting, or the label was edited. The row is right, it is just Probable instead of Sure.

What to do. Undo This Auto Link removes all links of this window, including those linked in it by hand. Unlink removes one takeoff. The numbers in the cells stay, including those written after linking. A closed workbook loses the names the next time it is opened. Go to Cell shows the cell of the selected row in Excel.

What Auto Link does on a real workbook has not been checked yet: only on generated rows in template copies. On the first workbook, look through the whole window.

docs.title: How to remove all job links: Reset All Links
docs.text:
Reset All Links... removes all links of this job. The button is in the Excel Links window, Excel Link > Reset All Links..., or Reset All Excel Links in the palette. First a question with the number of links. It cannot be undone. The values in the cells stay.

  • Open workbooks lose this job's hidden names at once. The workbook is not saved; you save it.
  • Closed workbooks lose the names when the workbook is opened while this job is open. Without saving.
  • A second button, Remove Them and Clean the Closed Workbooks Now, appears if some workbook is closed. It cleans the closed workbooks at once, with a hidden Excel and a copy of the workbook, and removes all names from them, including those of other jobs and OurPDF.
Reset All Links Remove All Links from This Workbook Scope this job, all its workbooks one workbook Which names only this job's, except with the second button all, including other jobs and OurPDF Closed workbook at the next opening or with the second button at once, with a hidden Excel and a copy When to link the job again before delivering the workbook to the client

docs.title: Settings: Settings > Excel Links
docs.text:
Section header Link to Excel behaviour. There are Apply, Reset, Save global default, Save as this job, Clear job override.

Field Default Update an open workbook at once on; off: only Update Links writes to an open workbook Update a closed workbook when the job is saved on; off: waits for Update Links Backups kept per workbook 5, from 1 to 50 Delay before an open workbook is updated, ms 800, from 100 to 10000 Time limit for a closed workbook, seconds 180, from 15 to 1800; after it the app stops its hidden Excel, the links stay Pending Lines and areas: a whole number below this needs its name Auto Link section, 10, from 0 to 1000; points always need a name

OurPlanCore Lite has the same button, menu, window and Settings section. Lite has no XL strip. OurPDF has the same link.

docs.title: TemplateCom template
docs.text: TemplateCom.xlsm for Lite is in the shared Dropbox folder Office Folder\programs\templates; for the full version it is also in the update folder next to ourplancore.exe. Each building gets a copy (Bldng#A.xlsm); the workbook name equals the Job Name on the Front Page. Worksheets: Front Page (areas, Total SQFT), Detailed Frame List (the delivered columns A:H and work zones to the right: J:N export, O:AB wall matrix, spec cells O:S, height calculator), Standarts (notes library), Mat List. The A-series macros are run by the XL strip in the full version and by the E-Wood tab buttons in Lite (Calculation from takeoffs); the B, C, X, Y series by hotkeys in Excel. Details: DFL: how the workbook works, Excel macros and hotkeys, Standard notes.

docs.title: XL strip: full version only
docs.text:
Full version only

OurPlanCore Lite has no XL strip, nor the Settings > Excel Actions and Excel Rules sections or the Create Project Excel Workbook command. In Lite numbers go through the buttons above, and the workbook macros are run in Excel. How the versions differ: Lite vs full version.

The XL strip is a vertical strip of buttons to the right of the sheet. In the full version it is turned on and off in the settings: Settings > Modules, the Excel Integration module (on by default). The same module shows the Excel, Value, Link to Excel and Auto Link buttons; if the strip is not visible, check this checkbox first. In Lite the Excel Integration checkbox controls only these buttons; it does not bring back the XL strip.

Top of the strip: ALL and LG, below them the wall and area buttons, then framing starts (FR). In a short window the strip scrolls with the mouse wheel down to the lower framing buttons. Each button's tooltip says what it does. Demo: the AI Inbox is open and the XL strip got short; the mouse wheel over the strip scrolls it down to FR, PS, BM, HD and back.

docs.title: What you need before pressing
docs.text:
• Excel has the building workbook open, made from TemplateCom.xlsm (a copy of the template from the app update folder), macros enabled. The app looks for an open TemplateCom.xlsm workbook; if there is none, it takes the active macro-enabled workbook (.xlsm) that has a Detailed Frame List worksheet.
  • The Excel Integration module is on (Settings > Modules, on by default).
  • One building (a folder with roots) or one export folder (walls, sqfts...) is selected in the Takeoffs tree. For ALL a selection from two buildings is not accepted (multiple buildings).
  • The LG legend is filled with the job's beam, post and header codes (otherwise the workbook keeps codes instead of sizes).
  • The job is saved, Total checked on the large takeoffs.

docs.title: How to export a building with one button: ALL
docs.text:
Why: the whole building workbook in one run, steps in the right order. You need: the list above.

  1. Open the building workbook in Excel and activate the Detailed Frame List worksheet.
  2. In OurPlanCore select the building folder in Takeoffs (or the root for a single building).
  3. Press LG, type rows like H5 - (2) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, C4 - 6x6; the Add missing codes button adds empty rows for all job codes without a size; press Save for job.
  4. Press ALL. Read what the app will skip (takeoffs without a number, names not in the format) and press Continue.
  5. Watch the step label Excel ALL 3/12: Walls... and wait for the summary Completed: ... with the list of what was skipped. A step that could not run is listed and does not stop the rest (except the A-series macros: they stop the chain).
  6. Check the workbook: the wall matrix, Front Page, framing lists.
  7. Save the workbook in Excel yourself: the app does not save it.

Result: the building workbook is filled; if you fix a measurement in the app, repeat the relevant button, not the whole ALL.

ALL in order: UN, SF, WL (right after it SH and SW), GB, TH, PP, E/R, OP, SHF, then all of framing (FR), and at the end BL (off in ALL by default). What goes into ALL is set in Settings > Excel Actions.

docs.title: XL strip buttons: reference
docs.text:
The general scheme: the branch takeoffs are written to the J:L work zone of the worksheet (name, number, unit; first free spot from row 10), the app selects what it wrote and runs the workbook macro, and the macro lays the rows out into the delivered columns A:H. How the workbook works: DFL: how the workbook works; what each macro does: Excel macros and hotkeys.

Button Takes from the tree Writes in the workbook ALL the whole selected building all steps in the order above LG - opens the job legend for PS, BM, HD; the row wall sheathing = 7/16" Zip no insulation is needed by SH. The cross in the panel header (Hide the Excel legend panel) or pressing LG again closes it without saving: first Save for job, otherwise the edit is lost; Clear empties and saves an empty legend SF sqfts (sqft) J:L, macro A2_SQFT_calc: floor areas, Front Page, roof by pitch WL walls J:L with floor headers, strict order, macro A3_Walls_Calc_AllGroup: the O:AB wall matrix and the Floor Walls rows; then zero rows are deleted in A:H of the wall block (the template rows Flashing, Headers, Wall Sheathing, Insulation, Box Sheathing, Tape, Shear Walls, Holdowns stay) GB gables J:L, A2_SQFT_calc TH trussheel J:L, A2_SQFT_calc PP parapets J:L, A4_Parapet: three numbers from the tail of the name prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 E/R eves rakes J:L: eaves by descending LF, then rakes; A6_Eve_Rakes OP openings/<floor> the zone from Z158 by floor; for each floor C_SumNearWindowValues, then A5_Openings: headers by width buckets and flashing. The name must start with the size WxH, otherwise the takeoff is skipped with a warning SH the sheathing text from column J or the wall sheathing = ... row from LG A7_walls_sheathing: keeps one sheathing system (Zip, Ply, OSB), removes the extra rows; in ALL it runs right after WL SW shear walls/<floor>/shear and .../holdowns J:L; a Shear Walls row (interior; exterior ones take wall sheathing) and one Holdowns row for each holdown in the floor's wall block SHF walls whose name starts with shaft the Shaft walls block above the first framing list: panels, CH and J channels from LF times wall height UN units/<mark size> (Line) and units/<floor>/<mark> (Count) units table from cell AM3 (Settings): mark on 2x4 / 2x6 / half, count by floor, SUMPRODUCT totals BL sqfts areas named blcny, balcony, terrace, porch blocks #n Upper Balcony/Terrace List W' x L' N units and #n Porch Framing List for each size, as a copy of the template's #1 block BL separate from ALL

The balcony block macro writes formulas in localized notation and is built for the Russian-language Excel interface; that is why it is off in ALL and is run with the BL button. It is turned on in Settings > Excel Actions. What the blocks look like: Balcony, porch and holdown blocks.

docs.title: Framing
docs.text:
Button Takes Writes FR all of the building's framing all the steps below for each floor; a missing framing list (6th Floor Framing List, Balcony Framing List) is added from the nearest one PS framing/<floor> framing/posts Posts rows in the floor's framing list; size by code from LG (C_PostsSort) BM .../beams Beam rows; size by code from LG HD .../headers/ext, .../headers/int header rows in the wall block one floor down (the 2nd floor framing sits on the 1st floor walls); Wall Sheathing and the rows after it are not touched JS .../joists Joists rows; Extra joists of the same length are added into the row; joists up to 7' go on doubled stock (45 x 12' with the note 90 pcs 6') DT .../details detail rows in J:L under a label row, once; a flag in M by name (bft, bd, ledger gives l, ribbon rb, rim r, or name = flags from LG), then C_RimBoardBlockingHangers ST .../stairs stair rows before Subfloor; a repeat export replaces them Tree folder Framing list in the workbook Headers go to the block framing/1st floor framing 1st Floor Framing List Basement Floor Walls framing/2nd floor framing 2nd Floor Framing List 1st Floor Walls framing/3rd floor framing ... 8th 3rd ... 8th Floor Framing List the floor below framing/roof framing, loft framing Roof Frame list - framing/balcony, porch, canopy Balcony / Porch / Canopy Framing List -

Posts, beams and joists replace their rows in the list; the other template rows (Blocking, Rim, Hangers, Subfloor) stay; a second run does not break the worksheet. Flag codes and material overrides: Takeoff tree, detail codes.

docs.title: Repeat export
docs.text:
• Framing (FR, PS, BM, HD, JS, ST) replaces its rows: repeat as often as needed. DT writes a group once; a group that is already exported is not touched.
  • The A series (SF, WL, GB, TH, PP, E/R, OP) appends a new block in J:L at the first free spot and runs the macro on it. The old block stays in the work zone; the A:H rows with a formula like =K37 point to their own block.

To be confirmed

How to cleanly remove the previous J:L block before repeating WL or SF (by hand or with a macro) will be checked on the next delivery.

docs.title: How to change what an XL button does: Settings > Excel Actions
docs.text:
The Action list (XL strip button), its fields, the ALL sequence order and the floor, framing and walls extras blocks.

Why: a different workbook, different tree folders or a different ALL set without changing the app. By default the TemplateCom.xlsm rules described above are in place.

  1. Open Settings > Excel Actions and pick the button in the Action list.
  2. Edit the fields (table below) and the step order in ALL sequence (ids separated by commas).
  3. Press Apply / Run selected (or Apply / Run ALL) to test on the open workbook.
  4. Press Save as this job (this job only) or Save global default (all jobs).

Result: the XL strip buttons work by the new rules. Use global for this job removes the job rules; Reset built-in loads the built-in rules as a draft (saved with the buttons in step 4).

The section has four blocks: Excel macro actions, Floor folder matching, Framing folders - Excel blocks, Walls extras: sheathing, shear walls, shaft, units, balconies.

Fields of all four blocks Block What is in it Excel macro actions for the selected button: Workbook, Worksheet, Takeoffs folder aliases (which tree folders it reads), VBA macro, the columns Scan start column, Scan end column, Write start column, First scan row, Blank rows between blocks, Output units, Per-floor VBA first, Row order, the cleanup macro After VBA with the range After range (for example B_DeleteZeroRowsOnlyIn_AtoH), Always keep rows (rows the cleanup does not touch), Cleanup stops at, the checkbox Insert numeric floor group rows (0-5) before the takeoff rows Floor folder matching floor folder words for Floor 0 ... Floor 5: by default 0, basement, bsmt, 1, 1st, first, 2, 2nd, second and so on up to 5, 5th, fifth Framing folders - Excel blocks (in the app the words are separated by an arrow) Include framing export in ALL, Framing root aliases, Pair joists up to (ft) (default 7, 0 turns doubled stock off), Add Extra joists of the same size and length to the regular joist row, Add a framing list the workbook lacks (6th floor, balcony) from the nearest floor list, the floor and category rule tables, the checkbox for running the details macro Walls extras: sheathing, shear walls, shaft, units, balconies checkboxes Units in ALL, Sheathing in ALL, Shear walls in ALL, Shaft block in ALL, Balconies in ALL; fields Sheathing VBA, Units table at (the units table cell, default AM3), Shear root folders, Holdown folders, Balcony area names, Porch area names

Overview of all Settings sections: Settings.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
The first rows of the table are XL strip messages (full version), then come the Link to Excel and Auto Link messages, which Lite has too.

Message or symptom Cause and what to do Select one Takeoffs folder or item for Walls, then press the button again nothing is selected in the tree Excel ALL found more than one building/root in the selection folders of two buildings are selected; keep one Configured workbook 'TemplateCom.xlsm' is not open ... no open macro-enabled workbook with a Detailed Frame List worksheet Workbook ... is not macro-enabled the workbook is saved as .xlsx; .xlsm is needed No configured export folders with measured rows were found the selected building has no sqfts, walls... folders with numbers The workbook has the code H5 instead of a size the LG legend is not filled An opening is skipped with a warning the name does not start with WxH (4.3x7.8 d) Skipped ...: floor folder ... the floor folder was not recognized: openings/1, 1st, first are valid Headers landed on the wrong floor that is normal: the headers of a framing floor go to the wall block one floor down The workbook did not change macros are disabled in Excel; check the Trust Center Select one takeoff before pressing Link to Excel. nothing or several takeoffs are selected in Takeoffs Link to Excel takes one takeoff, not a folder: one number goes to one cell. a folder is selected; select one takeoff Open Excel, open a workbook, click the destination cell, then press Link to Excel again. Excel not found; open the workbook, click a cell Save the workbook first: a link needs its file path. the workbook is new and has no file; save it Excel is busy or a cell is being edited. Finish it and try again. Excel is busy or a cell is being edited in it; finish and press again An annotation takeoff has no quantity to link. the annotation takeoff has no quantity The workbook is open read-only., The cell is protected. remove read-only or the worksheet protection Auto Link works only with a DFL... the active workbook is not a DFL: no Detailed Frame List worksheet, no word Description in column A, or the workbook has no macros. Link to Excel works on any workbook

All workbook mistakes: Common mistakes, Excel DFL and notes.

docs.title: Other: bookmarks, calculator, sheet windows, templates, import
docs.text: Here: small features that are on by default but almost never used in E-Wood measuring: Bookmarks, Quick Calculator, detached sheet windows and Tile M2, the Templates tab, PlanSwift and PDF Takeoffs import. Each is described briefly: what it does, where the button is, when it may come in handy.

docs.title: Bookmarks
docs.text:
The Bookmarks module (on). A bookmark remembers the sheet and the view position, so you can come back to a spot on a large plan.

Action How Add a bookmark for the current view B, then K (a sequence, up to 0.9 s between presses) List the Bookmarks sub-tab in the Pages panel (Bkm): columns Name, Page, View Open Enter or double-click the row Delete Delete Dock under Pages the button in the tab header; back - Return Bookmarks to the tab list

Bookmarks are stored in the job (bookmarks.json). Crop bookmarks with a PNG are created by the AI module (Save AI crop here, AI Crop + in the AI console), and the selected bookmark goes into the AI terminal context (console); this is full version only. In everyday work, the tabs of open sheets and F (fit the sheet) play the role of bookmarks.

docs.title: Quick Calculator
docs.text: The Quick Calculator module (on). The calculator button on the right command strip (palette command Quick Calculator) slides out a Calculator panel to the left of the strip: regular operations and a Feet + inches + fraction line with the result in decimal feet (= 9.09 ft). Handy for turning 9'-1 1/8" into 9.09 for a wall name without leaving the app. It closes with the same button or the panel X.

docs.title: Detached sheet windows and Tile M2
docs.text:
The Detached Sheets module (on). A sheet can be opened not as a tab but as a separate window and moved to a second monitor.

Button Where What it does Open > Open as Tabs / Detach to windows Pages header open the selected sheets as tabs or as separate windows Tile M2 (the dot next to it - vertical layout) Pages header open the selected sheets as windows and tile them on the second monitor close button with a menu Pages header Close every other sheet tab and all detached windows..., Close all detached sheet windows on monitor 2 Detach, Tile M2 Sheet Manager the same from the sheet table

All tools work in a detached window, including Beam and Openings, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copying between windows and Ctrl+Z. Clicking a detached window makes it the Pages navigation target: selecting a takeoff in the tree opens the sheet in it. Legend groups and the mask show the same in the main window, a detached window and the PDF.

docs.title: Similar across all sheets
docs.text: The Similar tool finds identical symbols from a sample; the checkbox Search all sheets in this job extends the search to the whole job (up to 80 sheets per run). Steps, thresholds and traps: Editing and snapping.

docs.title: Templates: tree and takeoff presets
docs.text:
The Takeoff Templates module (on). The Templates tab next to Takeoffs and Estimating (it can also dock under Pages with the button Pop Templates out into a panel docked below Takeoffs) shows a tree of presets: folders and Line, Area, Count takeoff presets with name, type and color.

Action How Create a takeoff from a preset right-click the preset > Create New Takeoff: the takeoff is created in the selected Takeoffs folder with the preset's name and properties Edit presets expand Edit: Folder, Line, Area, Count add nodes; Edit, Dup, Del; Reset restores the built-in set Save for the job Job writes a copy of the tree into the job, Clear returns to the global one Settings Settings > Takeoff Templates: the same editor with Auto / COM / EWP modes

In E-Wood work the tree is built by More > Auto Tree from the COM template, and takeoff names carry numbers from the drawing (ext 2x6 9.09), so presets with a fixed name are rarely needed: perhaps for repeating Count items like hardware marks.

docs.title: PlanSwift and PDF Takeoffs import
docs.text:
Both imports are for old jobs; a new E-Wood job starts from a PDF (jobs).

Route What is added Where Main > PlanSwift a separate converter: an old PlanSwift job folder becomes a new OurPlanCore job new job Main > Open / Import > Import into the current job > PlanSwift project... sheets and takeoffs of the old job into the open job; the source folder is only read the 01. planswift group in Pages and Takeoffs, an import report Main > Open / Import > Import PDF Takeoffs... or Main > PDF Takeoffs (Page > ADD > PDF Takeoffs) a PDF with someone else's measurement annotations: the app scans the files (with subfolders), shows the lines, areas, points and rulers found, asks whether to use a new or the current job the from pdf group; a report import_reports/pdf_takeoff_import_<date>.md inside the job

PlanSwift Item and Note formulas are not carried over (known limitation); takeoff names are brought to the canon by hand after import. Any import is rolled back with Open / Import > Undo Last Page Operation.

docs.title: Extra features
docs.text: This section collects what OurPlanCore 3.0 has but everyday E-Wood measuring almost never needs: snapping and tracing, manager tabs, bookmarks, the calculator, importing old jobs. 3D and AI are in the full version only and are described in its block. The "Every day" and "Advanced" level pages give these features one line with a link here, so they do not distract from walls, areas and framing. If you need one of these features, everything is described on the pages of this level.

docs.title: What is here and why
docs.text:
Selection criteria (owner's decision, 10/17/2026):

  1. The module is off by default in Settings > Modules: Sheet Manager, Takeoff Manager, Report Builder, Materials, AI, 3D, Job Tracker. Without turning the module on, there are no buttons or tabs. Materials, AI and 3D are in the full version only, Lite does not have them at all (Lite vs full version).
  2. The feature is not in the measuring work rules. None of the skills for walls, openings, framing, roofing, shear walls and units mentions Snap, Ortho, Box, Layer Trace, Wall Trace, bookmarks, the calculator, detached windows, tree templates or PlanSwift import. The measuring canon rests on Line, Area, Count, J Area, Beam, Openings, Record, sheet dots, the export to Excel (in the full version, the XL strip) and Export PDF.
  3. A newer path replaced the feature. Report Builder gave way to the XL strip and the Excel and Link to Excel buttons, AI 3D Massing was replaced by the deterministic roof from edges, inserting PDF Takeoffs and PlanSwift is needed only for old jobs.

What stays on its own levels: the Line, Area, Count, J Area, Beam, Openings, Pitch, Ruler, Record tools and copying; W/F/S/U dots; export to Excel; Export PDF and Preview; editing and snapping as one set (Cut, Merge, Split, Break, Ends, Combine, Similar, P Line, Snap, Ortho, Box) on the Editing and snapping page; Crop to Sheet, the Hide mask, Overlay, legend groups; Settings. The 3D roof, the AI console, Agent Bridge and Workspace are described in the full version block, starting with AI in the app.

docs.title: How to turn a module on
docs.text:
1. Settings > Modules: check the module, Apply (until restart) or Save global default; Save as this job turns the module on only in the open job.
  2. The presets Current default, All modules on, Takeoff Only, Minimal set the whole set at once; Reset restores the built-in one.
  3. A module that is on adds its tab to the mode bar (Sheet Manager, Takeoff Manager, Report Builder; in the full version also Materials, AI Manager, 3D) or buttons to the ribbon (Name, Scale, Name+Scale, In Progress).
  4. A disabled module hides its buttons and tab; a key for a hidden command does not fire.
Demo in the full version: Settings, the routing and color sections, then Modules: the AI and 3D checkboxes, Apply and Save global default; the AI Manager and 3D tabs appeared in the mode bar. Lite does not have these checkboxes.

The full module list with groups: Settings, Modules.

docs.title: Ideas and roadmap

This page lists what OurPlanCore already has in part, what is planned, what is only an idea so far and what went to the archive. docs.title: OurPlanCore Lite vs full version
docs.text:
OurPlanCore comes in two versions built from the same code. Estimators run Lite: it has no AI models and no terminal, it is a bit simpler and almost three times smaller. This knowledge base describes Lite. What exists only in the full version is collected in the menu block "AI, terminal and 3D (full version)" or marked on the page with the words "full version only".

The full version does everything Lite does, plus the terminal, the AI module, 3D, the XL strip, Workspace and Materials. The app file size is at the bottom.

docs.title: Which version for whom
docs.text: Version For whom What it gives Lite estimators who do not use AI models everything for takeoff and delivery: sheets, tools, the Takeoffs tree, PDF, Excel and Link to Excel Full those who work with AI the same plus the Claude, Codex and DeepSeek terminal in the window, the AI module, the 3D roof, the XL strip, Workspace for two computers

docs.title: Where to get Lite and how it updates
docs.text:
What Where The app a single ourplancore.exe file in the shared Dropbox folder Office Folder\programs. It is usually copied to your own computer and run from there; running it straight from the Dropbox folder works too Excel templates in the same place, the templates folder: TemplateCom.xlsm, TemplateResidential.xlsm What changed in the same place, the changes folder: files Изменения программ <date>.txt ("program changes") Update the new file arrives in the same folder through Dropbox and replaces the old one; the previous version is not kept next to it. If you keep your own copy, copy the new file over it after the update Version in the window title, with a -lite tail: OurPlanCore 3.0.x-lite - <job>; the full version has no such tail

Lite is built from the same code as the full version, but separately and not with every release. So the Lite number can lag behind, and a new feature from What's new reaches Lite with the next Lite build (except what is cut out, see below).

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
ourplancore.exe file Size Lite (build of 11/11/2026) about 92 MB Full version (build of 11/14/2026) about 254 MB

Lite is smaller because its file leaves out the DeepSeek and OpenCode engine, the copy of the knowledge base for the assistant, voice input, Tesseract OCR, the Python libraries for parsing PDFs and images, the TemplateCom.xlsm template, window snapshots for the sample job cards and the .NET language files other than English.

docs.title: What Lite does not have
docs.text:
Missing What it is Where it is described The >_ terminal the panel with Claude, Codex and DeepSeek to the right of the sheet: the >_ button on the right strip, a palette command, Settings > Terminals AI console The AI module AI Inbox, AI Manager, AI crop and markers, AI Fill and Crop Hints, title block reading by the model, tracing requests through the AI Inbox, Settings > AI Crop Notes, palette commands in the AI category AI in the app Workspace shared server, second computer, archive of assistant conversations, Settings > Workspace Workspace Voice input Settings > Voice Input - The 3D module the 3D tab, 3D roof, Roof Base, 3D walls 3D roof, 3D and Massing The Materials module the Materials tab: materials from the PDF text Managers The XL strip the ALL, LG, SF, WL ... ST strip to the right of the sheet that writes into the workbook and runs its macros; the Settings > Excel Actions and Excel Rules sections; the Excel buttons on the side command strips Export to Excel, XL strip Create Project Excel Workbook the command that copies the built-in TemplateCom.xlsm into the job folder take the template from the templates folder in Dropbox OCR of scans reading the sheet number without a text layer Sheets

This cannot be turned on: the AI, 3D and Materials modules are not in Settings > Modules, and neither a saved preset nor the job settings will turn them on.

docs.title: What Lite has and what works the same
docs.text:
• Sheets, scale, W/F/S/U dots, all measuring tools, the Takeoffs tree, editing and snaps, crops, the Hide mask, overlays, the legend.
  • Detailed sheet rendering, PDF layers, Layer Trace, Count Similar, sheet names and scales from the PDF text: Python and PyMuPDF are kept in Lite for these.
  • PDF export, including the PDF for editing in Adobe (PDF and delivery).
  • Excel: Export > Export Excel to an .xlsx file, the Excel and Value buttons at the bottom (they write from the active cell of the open workbook), Link to Excel, Auto Link, Settings > Excel Links (Export to Excel, Lite).
  • The .ourplan job format is the same: it is one app built with a different switch.
  • Settings > Agent Bridge stayed, but without the terminal the bridge is needed only by an external agent; an estimator does not need it in Lite.

docs.title: How Lite differs in daily work
docs.text: What In Lite Settings its own profile %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite: settings start from the built-in ones and do not mix with the full version's settings. Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\roaming\logs .ourplan files Lite does not become the app for .ourplan, a double click on the file does not start it. Open the job from the app (Ctrl+O, the Open project file... link) or drag the file into the window Scans no OCR: the name and scale are read only from the PDF text, name a scanned sheet by hand (F2) Both versions on one computer they can be installed side by side: their profiles and settings are separate

docs.title: How to tell which version is open
docs.text:
1. Look at the window title: OurPlanCore 3.0.x-lite - <job> means Lite.
  2. Look at the right strip next to the sheet: Lite has no >_ button and no XL strip with the ALL, LG, SF buttons.

If you need AI models, the terminal or 3D: that is the full version, everything about it is in the menu block "AI, terminal and 3D (full version)", starting with AI in the app.

docs.title: Managers: Sheet Manager, Takeoff Manager, Report Builder, Materials, AI Manager, Job Tracker
docs.text:
Here: the mode bar tabs that are off by default in Settings > Modules, and the Job Tracker button. You need them when there are dozens of sheets and editing them in a table is easier, when you need a material list or prices, when AI works through AI Inbox, and when you want to switch the job card in the tracker from the app. Everyday measuring does without these tabs. Materials, AI Manager and 3D are in the full version only; Lite does not have them (Lite vs full version).

Turning on: Settings > Modules, check the module, Apply or Save global default (how to turn on). The tab appears in the mode bar next to Main View and Settings. From the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) the tabs open with the commands Show Sheet Manager, Show Takeoff Manager, Show Report Builder, and in the full version also Show Materials, Show AI Manager and Show 3D Viewer (3D); for a disabled module the command does not fire.

docs.title: Sheet Manager
docs.text:
The sheet table with proposed names, scale, source and confidence. The Rename and Scale Action checkboxes pick what to apply.

A table of all sheets for bulk operations. Turning the module on also adds the Name, Scale, Name+Scale buttons to the Main ribbon, and in the full version, together with the AI module, AI Fill and Crop Hints (Lite does not have these two buttons).

Group Buttons PDF Import PDF(s), PDF Takeoffs, Export PDF Raster source PDF / Auto, DPI presets, Options..., format Auto / WebP / PNG, Prepare, First On, First Off, Clean, Cancel Metadata Refresh, Analyze, Auto Name, Auto Scale, Name+Scale, AI Fill, Crop Hints, Apply Checked Open Open Sheet, Open Tabs, Detach, Tile M2, Open JSON Organize Sort A/S, D/Sec/WT, Repair Links, Auto Folders

Columns: Rename, Scale Action, Current Page, Current Scale, Proposed Name, Scale, Label, Suffix, Title, Name Source / Name Conf., Suffix Source / Suffix Conf., Scale Source / Scale Conf., Raster, Why, Warnings. The checkboxes in Rename and Scale Action pick what the Apply Checked button applies.

docs.title: How to prepare a raster for heavy sheets
docs.text:
What for: large sheets open faster from a ready raster, Ctrl+F3 snaps to black lines.

  1. Select the sheets in the table.
  2. In the Raster group, pick the PNG format and the DPI.
  3. Press Prepare and wait for it to finish.
  4. Press First On.

Result: the Raster column is filled, the sheet opens from the raster.

docs.title: How to set title block regions: Crop Hints
docs.text:
What for: a plan set with an unreadable title block gets names and scale from regions drawn once. Needed: the Sheet Manager and AI modules, that is, the full version.

  1. Press Crop Hints (Main ribbon or the Metadata group): the app opens a typical sheet of the plan set with the status show Sheet title / number, then Scale on the middle <profile> sheet.
  2. Draw three regions with the left button: Sheet #, Sheet Title, Scale; the right or middle button moves the sheet, Clear Current and Clear All erase.
  3. Press Save.
  4. Press Analyze: the metadata is re-read using the hints; AI Fill hands unrecognized title blocks to the model (online, needs a key).
  5. Check the Why, Warnings and Name Source columns (text, OCR, model or a learned rule) and press Apply Checked.

Result: the sheets are named and scaled from the title block regions; the app looks for the same regions on the other sheets of the plan set.

The same actions without the tab: the Name, Scale, Name+Scale buttons in the Pages panel and a preview before applying (sheets).

docs.title: Takeoff Manager
docs.text:
The takeoff table: type, sections, total, unit, price, folder.

The Takeoffs tree as a table: Item, Type, Sections, Total, Unit, Price, Cost, Notes, Folder. Buttons: Save, Refresh, Set Active, Properties, Open Estimating, New Folder, New Item, Auto Tree, From Pages, export CSV / TXT / Excel / Current Excel. Handy for checking totals and prices across a whole building; drawing is still done in Main View. To check totals before Excel, the Estimating tab in the Takeoffs panel is usually enough (tree).

docs.title: Report Builder
docs.text:
Report Builder reads TemplateCom.xlsm and shows the wall table.

Reload reads the TemplateCom.xlsm template, Refresh updates the table, Apply Walls writes the walls into the workbook. This is the old path into Excel; today, in the full version, walls, areas and framing are written by the XL strip with per-section buttons and ALL; in Lite the numbers go through the Excel, Value and Link to Excel buttons (Excel export). The tab stays for checking how old workbooks got their wall block.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Full version only: Lite has no Materials module. The tab reads materials from the drawings themselves, not from the Takeoffs tree: material mentions and schedule tables in the text of the job's source PDFs.

docs.title: How to collect materials from the job PDFs
docs.text:
What for: quickly see which materials, sections and schedules (sheathing, beams, hardware) are named in the plan set, with a link to the sheet. Needed: the Materials module is on, the job has sheets from a PDF.

  1. Open the Materials tab (or the palette command Show Materials).
  2. Press Extract; the palette command Extract Materials opens the tab and runs the same thing right away. The built-in helper reads the text of all source PDFs (with OCR on sheets without text, if it is installed) and the tables titled SCHEDULE, TABLE, LEGEND.
  3. Wait for the status Materials: N row(s), M schedule(s).
  4. Open the result: Rows CSV (a row for each mention: category, thickness, section, grade, quantity, sheet), Summary CSV (a summary by material), JSON (the full result), Folder (the result folder in the job).
  5. Press Report Sheet if you need a Materials Report sheet in Pages with this summary for copying.

Result: a material table on the tab and files in the job folder; Refresh re-reads the last result.

This is a reference from the drawings, not quantities: the E-Wood delivery is the DFL workbook. An assembly library (wall = studs + plates + OSB) is still an idea (plans).

docs.title: AI Inbox and AI Manager
docs.text: Full version only, together with the AI module. The AI Manager tab buttons, what goes into AI Inbox and how to review AI drafts are in the AI block: AI in the app, AI Inbox and AI Manager.

docs.title: Job Tracker: the In Progress button
docs.text: The Job Tracker module (Integrations group) is off by default. Once it is on, an In Progress button appears on the Main ribbon in the JOB group.

docs.title: How to switch the job card to In Progress
docs.text:
What for: the tracker sees that work has started, without switching the card by hand. Needed: the job name starts with a number NN. Name; the module is on.

  1. Open the job and press Main > JOB > In Progress.
  2. Read the status: Setting Job Tracker card NN to In Progress..., then Job Tracker: project NN set to In Progress.

Result: the card with the job number in the tracker is moved to In Progress by an external pipeline command. If the name has no number, the status says '<name>' has no leading project number (expected 'NN. Name'); Job Tracker was not updated.

The command is edited in Settings > Modules: Executable, Arguments (one per line), Save, Reset (restores the default pipeline command). The {number} placeholder is the job number. The pipeline moves the card to done on delivery, not the app (workflow).
