docs.title: How to sort sheets into folders
docs.text:
Why: a set of a hundred sheets turns into Arch, Struct, sections, details ..., and what is not needed goes to --------others. You need: sheets imported into 00. imported and named (names). Folder canon: Takeoff tree and sheet names.

  1. Pick a template in the Folder template list (COM for commercial, EWP).
  2. Press + New > Auto Folders: the standard folders are created.
  3. Press Setup > Sort: A > Arch / S > Struct: sheets are split by the letter of their number.
  4. Press Setup > Sort: D / Sec / WT suffix: details, sections, wall types and rcp go to their folders by the last tag of the name (d, sec, wt, rcp, u). Only non-empty folders are created.
  5. Drag the rest by hand or use right-click Move to Folder..., Cut and Paste Into Folder.

Result: 00. imported has the subfolders Arch, Struct, sections, details arch, details struct, rcp, units, demolition; extras in --------others; each building has its own folder with the same name as in Takeoffs; a revision has 01. old/ and 02. NEW SET <date>/.

Tips

  • A sheet whose name ends with - goes to --------others when sorting (the rule is in Settings > Sort A/S).
  • Only one folder (a building, 02. NEW SET <date>): right-click it, Organize > Auto Create Folders, then Sort A/S in This Folder and Sort D/Sec/WT in This Folder. The folders Arch, Struct, --------others, sections and others are created inside this folder, the rest of the set is not touched.
  • Made a mistake: Open / Import > Undo Last Page Sort.
  • Sorting rules are edited in Settings > Sort A/S and Sort D/Sec/WT (Settings).

docs.title: How to sort sheets and takeoffs
docs.text:
Why: to restore the order a101, a102, a201 after import and manual moves, and to group details in Takeoffs by sheet. You need: the job open, not read-only.

  1. Select a folder in Pages; if nothing is selected, the root is sorted.
  2. On the left icon strip press A-Z (Sort Pages A-Z) or Z-A (Sort Pages Z-A). Right-click on a folder, Organize > Sort Children A-Z or Sort Children Z-A does the same.
  3. In Takeoffs, select a building or floor folder and press the sort you need from the table on the right icon strip.

Result: the order in the tree is updated, the status shows Sorted ... with the folder name and the kind of sort.

Command Where What it does Sort Pages A-Z, Sort Pages Z-A left strip, command palette children of the selected Pages folder or the root, one level; numbers by value (a2 before a10) Sort Children A-Z, Sort Children Z-A right-click on a folder in Pages or Takeoffs, Organize the same for this folder Sort Takeoffs A-Z, Sort Takeoffs Z-A right strip, command palette children of the selected Takeoffs folder or the root, one level; detail references 1/A501 go by sheet, then by detail number Sort Root A-Z, Sort Root Z-A right-click on the Takeoffs root top level of the tree (buildings) Sort Takeoffs: Walls right strip walls in the folder and all subfolders: ext, corr, dem, then 2x6 and 2x4 Sort Takeoffs: Details by Sheet right strip, command palette details 1/A501, 2_A501 in the folder and all subfolders are grouped by the sheet after / or _ (sheets in number order, as in Pages), within a sheet by detail number; names without a separator go after the details

Tips

  • A-Z and Z-A are not covered by Undo Last Page Sort: only Sort A/S and Sort D/Sec/WT can be undone. Made a mistake: run the reverse sort or rearrange with Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down.
  • The order of takeoffs in the sheet legend is set separately: right-click the sheet, Organize > Sort Sheet Legend Auto, Sort Sheet Legend A-Z or Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space) (legend).

docs.title: How to name sheets across the whole set
docs.text:
Right-click a sheet, the PDF Metadata submenu (visible with the Sheet Manager module on). Before applying, the app shows a preview: the proposed name, the scale action, confidence and the reason. Uncheck anything unclear.

Why: names like a101 1st, s201 2nd instead of Page 7; together with the name, the sheet gets a W/F/S/U dot and a scale. You need: sheets in 00. imported; for scans without text, a raster at import (raster).

  1. Select the 00. imported folder (or the sheets you need) and press Name+Scale (Name and Scale work separately; the same buttons are on the Main ribbon with the Sheet Manager module).
  2. Read the Proposed Name, Scale Action, confidence and Why columns in the dialog; uncheck doubtful rows. Rename All and Scale All check all rows, Clear unchecks them.
  3. Press Apply.
  4. Name by hand whatever was not recognized: F2 on the sheet, Page > Batch Rename for a series, or Setup > Name / Scale....

Result: names in the <number> <tag> format, lowercase: a101 1st, s201 2nd, a105 rf, a8.01 1st rcp, ad101 demo, a3011 u; plans have a dot under the Scale header; the status shows Route: W 1st.

What the app reads: the sheet number based on the profile of the whole set (title block location, the SHEET NO. label, the sheet index); text repeated on every sheet (firm, phone) is not taken as a number. In Lite the number comes only from the PDF text: name a scan without a text layer by hand (F2). In the full version such scans are read by the built-in OCR, and a sheet that the text did not name can be read by an AI model from an image of the title block: the Read title blocks the PDF text cannot name with AI checkbox in Settings > Auto Rename / Scale (needs the AI module and a key, works online). Names you kept when opening the job are remembered by the app as final: in the suffix rules table this is the Kept column. For a set with an unreadable title block the full version has Crop Hints (Managers, Sheet Manager).

Tips

  • The tag always goes last: overall 1st, stair d. f only for the foundation, do not add it to floor plans.
  • Name on a folder is faster than on single sheets: the title block profile is built from the whole set.

docs.title: How to set and check the scale
docs.text:
Why: without a scale, Line and Area are not recorded; the scale belongs to the sheet, not to the takeoff. You need: a labeled dimension or a dimension string on the sheet.

  1. Press S (Scale) and click both ends of a dimension string or an overall dimension with a labeled size.
  2. Type the length in the dialog: 1/8" = 1'0", 1:96 and a segment length (24') are accepted. Press Enter.
  3. Press R (Ruler) and check against a second dimension: the tape shows the length without writing anything to the tree.
  4. For several sheets at once, select them in Pages, press F4 and enter the scale once. At the bottom of the window: the Scale: 1:N field, Set and Presets for typical values.
  5. If the scale of the open sheet is checked and other floors need the same, select them in Pages and choose right-click Apply Current Sheet Scale: the open sheet's scale is copied to the selected ones.

Result: the status shows Scale: 1/8" = 1'0", the tape matches the labeled dimension.

The app reads the scale from the label on the sheet by itself: the Scale button in the Pages panel or right-click PDF Metadata > Auto Scale from PDF... shows a preview (Scale Action, confidence), only checked rows are applied. The sheet name does not change.

Sheet Usual scale Floor plans 1/8" = 1'0" (1:96), 1/4" for small houses Unit plans 1/4" = 1'0" (1:48) Sections 3/8" = 1'0" Details NTS, no scale needed: measure from the dimensions in the text

The sheet label is not proof

Structural sheets are sometimes labeled 1/8" and printed at 3/16". Auto-scale and a manual choice are checked against a dimension string on the sheet itself. A sheet with several scales is calibrated for the zone you measure; enlarged plans are better moved to Arch/unlarged as a sheet copy. All sheet mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.title: W/F/S/U dots
docs.text:
Rows W, F, S by floor B, 1-5, L, R and one U dot. The selected dot is named in the status bar: Route: W 1st.

Under the Scale header each sheet has a grid of dots. One selected dot decides which building folder every new measurement from this sheet goes into, with any tool.

Row For which sheets Where new takeoffs go W (walls) architectural plans a101 1st walls/<floor> floor walls; Area and J Area into sqfts F (framing) structural plans s201 2nd framing/<floor> floor framing/... by tool S (shear) plan copies for shear walls shear walls/<floor>/shear, Count into .../holdowns U (units) unit plans a3011 u units, with any tool

docs.title: How to set a sheet's dot
docs.text:
Why: new takeoffs from the sheet land on the right floor and branch by themselves. You need: the sheet open; the dot grid is visible with the Viewport > Sheet routing checkbox (off by default; turning it off does not reset the dots, routing still works).

  1. Name the sheet per the canon (F2, Name, Batch Rename or Page Setup): the letter a plus a floor tag gives W, s plus a floor gives F, a last tag u gives U (a3011 u, S0-4A U, a copy ... U (2); a301 u el does not get the U dot). Sheets with the tags rcp, el, sec, d, demo, sch, n, wt, ft, fin and similar are skipped.
  2. If the dot did not appear or you need a different one, click the right dot by hand; clicking again clears it. A plan copy for shear walls gets S by hand. A dot set by hand is not replaced.
  3. For the whole job open Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing and press Route sheets without a dot now.

Result: the status shows Route: W 1st (or F 2nd, S 1st, U all floors); in the New Item dialog the destination line shows the folder.

Tips

  • A blank sheet from Blank Sheet with a name like a3011 u is left without a dot: press F2 and Enter with the same text, or click the dot.
  • A sheet copy (Ctrl+D) inherits the original's dot: on copies for shear walls switch it to S (sheet copy, dot).
  • Record continues the selected takeoff and ignores the dot.

The full destination table by tool, name rules and what to do with a wrong route: Names and auto-routing; row and floor settings: Routing: settings.

docs.title: How to hide a sheet's measurements
docs.text:
Why: to get finished or unrelated work out of sight before a check and the PDF.

What How Hide all measurements on a sheet click the dot to the left of the sheet in Pages (tooltip Hide all current takeoffs on ...); new measurements stay visible Hide one takeoff on a sheet select a segment on the sheet or a row in Takeoffs and press H (tree) Bring back the visibility dot next to the takeoff under the sheet in Pages (Visible on <sheet>: <takeoff>) or the dot at the sheet Toggle from a menu right-click a takeoff under the sheet in Pages, or a measurement in a separate sheet window: Hide on This Sheet / Show on This Sheet (the item name changes with the state) Bookmark a spot on the sheet B, then K; the Bookmarks tab (bookmarks) PDF layers the PDF Layers tab: visibility of vector PDF layers and Layer Trace (snaps and tracing) Sheet overlay the Overlay tab: an S plan over an A plan; for all floors Page > Batch Overlay (overlays) Blank sheet, crops, mask Page > Blank Sheet, Crop to Sheet, Annotation > Hide (sheets: advanced)

Result: what is hidden does not print in the PDF; this is how a separate PDF per building is made (PDF and delivery).

docs.title: How to pick a takeoff already measured on the sheet
docs.text:
Why: to continue a takeoff that is already on the open sheet without scrolling through the Takeoffs tree. You need: the sheet open, with measurements on it.

  1. In the Takeoffs panel, on the active takeoff row press More > Sheet Targets....
  2. Read the list: this sheet's takeoffs in legend order, each with its quantity on this sheet, an asterisk * on the active one.
  3. Click the takeoff you need: it becomes active, Space (Record) continues it.
  4. To cycle through them, choose the top menu item Next Sheet Target or the palette command Next Sheet Takeoff Target.

Result: the status shows Sheet takeoff target 2/5: <takeoff>.

docs.title: How to open a sheet in a tab or a separate window
docs.text:
Why: to keep a plan and a detail side by side, to move sheets to the second monitor. You need: for separate windows, the Detached Sheets module (on by default).

  1. Click a sheet in Pages: it opens in the current tab instead of the previous one.
  2. To keep the previous sheet open, right-click the sheet and choose Open in New Tab. For several sheets, select them with Ctrl or Shift and choose Open Selected in New Tabs.
  3. For a separate window choose Detach Sheet to Window; to tile the selected sheets on the second monitor, Tile Sheet on Monitor 2 (up to 64 sheets at a time).
  4. Move an open tab with right-click on the tab: Detach Tab to Window or Tile Tab on Monitor 2; all tabs at once: Detach All ... Tabs to Windows and Tile All ... Tabs on Monitor 2 (the number of tabs replaces the dots).
  5. Close what is not needed: the cross or right-click Close Tab on the tab, Page > Close Page for the active tab, the x button in the Pages header for all others at once.

Result: sheet tabs above the sheet window, separate windows on the second monitor; all tools work in a separate window.

Right-click on a measurement in a separate window gives Takeoff Properties... (takeoff properties), Section Properties... or Count Properties... (properties of this measurement; for a measurement with no takeoff the item is grayed out and called Measurement Properties...), Hide on This Sheet / Show on This Sheet, copying and pasting measurements. More about windows: detached windows.

docs.title: How to rotate, flip or level a sheet
docs.text:
The Page ribbon: groups ADD, ROTATE (Left, Right, 180, Level, Batch Rotate), FLIP, IMAGE and PAGE.

Why: a scan came in sideways, upside down or skewed. You need: the sheet open, the job not read-only.

  1. Open the sheet and go to the Page ribbon.
  2. In the ROTATE group press Left, Right or 180: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise, clockwise, or 180.
  3. For several sheets, select them in Pages, press Batch Rotate and choose Rotate Selected Left, Rotate Selected Right or Rotate Selected 180.
  4. If the plan is skewed by a few degrees, press Level, type a clockwise angle from -45 to 45 and press Enter (0 only fits the sheet to the window).
  5. Flip a mirrored scan with the Vertical or Horizontal button in the FLIP group.

Result: the status shows Rotate Right: updated <sheet>.; the sheet's measurements and markup are rotated with it, the scale is kept.

The sheet turns into an image

Rotate, flip, Level, Invert and Crop New Page rebuild the sheet as an image of about 108 DPI. Vector lines (PDF Snap, Black vector), the text layer (auto-name and auto-scale from text) and PDF layers are lost, small text gets blurry. There is no undo: rotating back restores the orientation but not the vectors. Rotate scans; a vector plan is better left as it is.

Button Group What it does Invert IMAGE inverts the sheet colors (light lines on dark); the sheet is replaced, and the inversion also goes into the PDF export Copy IMAGE puts a PNG of the sheet on the clipboard as a file: it can be pasted into File Explorer or a messenger Crop New Page IMAGE a new sheet <sheet> Crop from the currently visible area, with the same scale (steps) Crop to Sheet IMAGE details from different sheets on one sheet at true scale (steps) Batch Rename PAGE names of the selected sheets as a list, one per line (names) Batch Overlay PAGE overlays of S plans on A plans across the whole job (steps) Set Origin PAGE remembers the center of the visible area as the sheet's coordinate origin Offset Origin PAGE shifts that origin by X, Y in PDF points (input 12, -6) Close Page PAGE closes the active sheet tab

The origin from Set Origin is stored in the sheet and rotates with it; it does not affect measurements, Total or export, and is not needed in E-Wood work.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• f added to a floor plan (a101 1st f): f only for the foundation.
  • The tag is not last (a3011 u el): the U dot is not set, suffix sorting gets confused.
  • The scale taken from the sheet label without checking against a dimension.
  • A sheet copy for each takeoff type: copies are needed only for shear walls, a second level on the same sheet, another building and a new sheet set.
  • A vector plan rotated or inverted with the Page ribbon buttons: the sheet became an image, PDF Snap and auto-name no longer work on it (rotation).

All sheet and tree mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.text:
• Takeoff tree and sheet names: table of tags and folders
  • Split by sheets and routing, Names and auto-routing, Routing: settings
  • Jobs and saving, Sheets: advanced

docs.title: PDF and delivery
docs.text:
This page covers exporting sheets with measurements to PDF, a separate file per building, editing the finished PDF in Adobe Acrobat, the PDF Output ribbon and the live Preview, the sheet legend, and what else goes into the delivery. You need it at the end of a job and on a revision.

Sheets in the same folder structure as in Pages. A checkbox on a folder ticks all its sheets; open now marks the sheets that are open right now.

docs.title: What gets delivered
docs.text:
• The PDF gets only sheets with visible measurements; the client does not need the blank sheets of the plan set.
  • Different buildings get different PDFs. Measurements of other buildings on a shared sheet are hidden before export.
  • Measurements always on, Legend usually on, Markups only if the client needs the markup (the Hide mask and crops print without it).
  • A "new only" revision: by the branches of the new plan set, hide the rest.
  • By default the lines, areas and labels in the PDF can be moved in Adobe Acrobat, by the client too. If you need a PDF without that: turn off Editable.

The full delivery package (processed xlsx, Changes.txt, the .Finished folder): Workflow, export and delivery.

docs.title: How to export a PDF
docs.text:
Demo: Main > Export, tick the sheets you need, Export; status Exported PDF (2 sheet(s)).

Why: a file for the client with only the sheets that have measurements. You need: measurements checked, extras hidden.

  1. Press Ctrl+S: the saved state is what gets exported.
  2. Hide the extras: H on takeoffs, the visibility dot on the sheet in Pages, the Annotation > Hide mask over a neighboring plan (tree).
  3. Press PDF Output > Preview and look at the current sheet: line weight, labels, legend (below).
  4. Press Main > PDF > Export (the PDF Output module is required). For one or several sheets, select them in Pages and right-click Export Sheet to PDF... or Export N Selected to PDF....
  5. In the Export PDF dialog tick the sheets or folders (All, None), check the Measurements, Markups, Legend checkboxes and the Stroke field (line weight multiplier 0.25-10, default 1.5; saved on export).
  6. Press Export: the save window offers the job export folder and the name <job>_sheets.pdf (for one sheet, the sheet name). Name it by building: <job> Bldg A.pdf.
  7. Open the finished PDF and page through all of it.

Result: measurements in place, the legend is readable, no extra sheets.

docs.title: How to make a separate PDF per building
docs.text:
Why: the client gets a file for each building. You need: each building has its own sheet folder in Pages (multiple buildings).

  1. In Export PDF tick the building folder with one checkbox.
  2. If a sheet has measurements of another building (a shared plan), open the sheet, select the other building's folder in Takeoffs and press H: all its takeoffs on this sheet are hidden. Repeat on every shared sheet.
  3. Export and name the file by building.
  4. Restore visibility with the dots on the takeoffs under the sheet in Pages, and repeat for the next building.

Result: a file per building; the pipeline does the same automatically by the green dot (CLI).

docs.title: How to edit a finished PDF in Adobe Acrobat
docs.text:
Since version 3.0.27 the export by default puts measurements into the PDF as separate objects (annotations) instead of drawing them into the page. They look the same: OurPlanCore colors, weights and labels. In Adobe Acrobat these objects can be moved, edited and deleted. OurPlanCore Lite does the same.

Checked with the mouse in Acrobat on test files: lines, areas and labels move, points and joist areas do not. Object In Acrobat What matters Lines (Line) move Areas (Area) move Labels move a label is not tied to its line: if you moved the line, move the label separately Points (Count, Beam) do not move Joist areas (J Area) do not move the outline, joists and labels are one object here Legend should not move the same object type as Count; not tested on its own. It sits on top of all measurements and labels Sheet header, Annotation markup do not move they are in the page itself, not objects

Why: a small fix right in the PDF, without a new export. You need: a PDF exported with the Editable checkbox on, and Adobe Acrobat.

  1. Export the PDF as usual (above). The PDF Output > ADOBE > Editable checkbox is on by default.
  2. Open the PDF in Adobe Acrobat.
  3. Click a line, area or label and drag it with the mouse.
  4. Save the PDF in Acrobat.

Result: the object is moved in this PDF, and only in it.

Editing in Adobe does not recalculate labels and the legend

The numbers on the labels and in the legend stay the same. The edit lives only in this PDF: the OurPlanCore job does not change, and a new export will not repeat it. If the quantity changed, fix the measurement in the app and export again.

After an edit Acrobat draws the object itself, so the look changes a little:

  • a line keeps its color, weight and transparency; the dots at its vertices disappear;
  • an area fill keeps its transparency, and the same transparency goes onto the outline; an area with cutouts has no outline.

docs.title: How to turn it off
docs.text:
Where What to do Applies PDF Output > ADOBE > Editable uncheck it until another job is opened Settings > PDF Editable Export uncheck Export measurements as annotations, press Save global default or Save as this job for all jobs or for one; Clear job override removes the job setting, Reset loads the defaults

With the checkbox off: every measurement and the legend are drawn into the page, as in the old export, with the legend under the measurements.

Section header PDF editable export (Adobe). Captured on a generated job in 3.0.27: the Excel Links section was not yet in the list on the left at that time. Field Default What it does Export measurements as annotations on the same switch as Editable Lines (PolyLine: move, drag vertices) on lines as separate objects Areas (Polygon: move, drag vertices) on areas as separate objects Counts (one object per point) on points as separate objects, one object per point Joist areas (one object with contour, joists, labels) on a joist area as one object Labels as separate text boxes on unchecked: labels are drawn into the page Legend (one object on top of everything) on unchecked: the legend is drawn into the page, under the measurements Adobe measurement data (value updates when a vertex moves) on adds the sheet scale to lines and areas so Acrobat calculates its own value; this does not change the OurPlanCore labels and legend Line ends in Adobe None Circle - round line ends after an edit in Acrobat, about three times larger than the export dots Counts, joists, legend as Stamp object type. No need to change it: other types are untested and may lose their look when moved

The type settings change neither the sheet on screen nor the measurements themselves, only how they sit in the PDF.

Lite has the same ribbon and section; Lite stores its settings separately from the full version.

docs.title: PDF Output ribbon: reference
docs.text:
Print settings live separately from the screen settings (Viewport, Display): thick on screen, thin in the PDF. This capture is older: it does not have the ADOBE group yet. Group Buttons What they set LINES & AREA Line, Point, Edge, Fill, Opac line weight, Count point size, area border weight, area fill, transparency of Line and of the Draw line and Arrow markups (0-100 %, default 100) LABELS All, Line, Area, Joist, Count, Size which labels to print and their size OVERLAYS Legend, Header size of the legend and the sheet header ADOBE Editable measurements in the PDF as separate objects that move in Adobe Acrobat (details); on by default INCLUDE Meas, Markups, Legend, Extra glow what to include by default; Extra joists highlight PREVIEW Preview live window of the current sheet

Opac at 60-70 % keeps the drawing readable under heavy wall lines. The settings are saved globally and used on every export.

docs.title: How to check a sheet before export: Preview
docs.text:
Demo: PDF Output > Preview; the sheet preview redraws when you change the transparency and legend size on the ribbon. A non-modal window: change a setting on the ribbon and the preview redraws.

Why: see the sheet as it will print and tune the line weight and legend without test exports.

  1. Open the sheet and press PDF Output > Preview.
  2. Change Line, Opac, Legend on the ribbon: the preview redraws by itself.
  3. Zoom with the wheel toward the cursor, pan with the right button; buttons Fit, -, +, 100%.
  4. Switch sheets in Pages: the window follows the current sheet.
  5. Press Save PDF... if you need a PDF of just the current sheet straight from the preview.

Result: the settings are tuned; the window can stay open while you work. In the preview the legend is one list, Legend (N): the sheet legend groups are not taken into account here yet. With a large Legend on an 11x8.5 sheet the legend can cover half the plan; check the size.

docs.title: Sheet legend
docs.text:
Demo: two takeoffs under the sheet in Pages, right-click Legend Group > New Group; the legend on the sheet splits into walls and openings blocks. The legend lists the sheet takeoffs with color and symbol. Groups put shear walls or framing in a separate block.

The legend lists only the takeoffs measured on this sheet (split by sheets).

What Where Show, size, position on screen Display > Legend Show / Size / Pos Size in the PDF PDF Output > OVERLAYS > Legend Order Pages > sheet > Organize > Sort Sheet Legend Auto / A-Z / by Key (before space), Reset Sheet Legend Order (legend order) Groups under the sheet in Pages select takeoffs, Legend Group > New Group...; manage them in Organize > Legend Groups... (groups)

The legend is the same on screen, in the preview and in the PDF. Legend groups, the Hide mask, Crop to Sheet crops and sheet overlays: Sheets: advanced.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The PDF got sheets without measurements or another building's measurements.
  • Export before Ctrl+S: the latest edits did not make it in.
  • The legend covers the drawing: move Pos or reduce Legend in PDF Output.
  • Wall lines cover the dimensions: reduce Line or set Opac.
  • Neighboring takeoffs with the same color: the legend is unreadable (colors).
  • A line was moved or stretched in Acrobat, and the label and legend kept the old number. That is expected: Adobe does not recalculate them; fix the measurement in the app (details).

All delivery mistakes: Common mistakes, delivery.

docs.text:

  • Export to Excel, DFL: how the workbook works
  • Sheets: advanced, Multiple buildings

docs.title: Takeoff Routing in Settings
docs.text:
This page covers how OurPlanCore 3.0 sorts new takeoffs into building folders by itself and where to edit those rules. You need it when a new takeoff landed in the wrong place, when a job has non-standard folders, or when you prepare a job for a different tree template. How a plan set is split up in practice (which sheet carries walls, framing, shear walls, units) is on Split by sheets and routing.

Decision order: U sheet, then a rule by name or tool, then the W/F/S sheet dot, then the building. Record ignores all of this.

docs.title: How the app decides where to put a new takeoff
docs.text:
Checked from top to bottom, the first rule that fires wins:

  1. Sheet with the U dot. Any tool puts the takeoff into <building>/units. Name rules do not apply on a U sheet.
  2. Takeoff Name Routing. The takeoff name contains a word from the rules table (eve, rake, gable, prpt, trussheel), or the tool matches a rule (Openings). This rule beats the sheet dot: eve 24 main from a W sheet still goes to eves rakes/eves.
  3. W/F/S sheet dot plus the tool: see the Tool destinations table below.
  4. Building. The folder with the green dot in the Takeoffs header; if there is none, the Building root field from the settings; if that is empty too, the Takeoffs root.
  5. Sheet with no dot and no rule. The old word-based name parsing (sqfts, walls) kicks in: a fallback with no editor.

Record (Space) continues the takeoff that is already selected and does not compute a route. Existing takeoffs do not move when the dot or the rules change.

docs.title: Sheet Takeoff Routing: sheet dots
docs.text:
The dot matrix under the scale label: rows W, F, S, U; columns B, 1-5, L, R. W/1 is selected, the status bar shows Route: W 1st. Element Where What it does Dot matrix under the Scale label on the sheet one click sets a dot, a second click removes it; one dot per sheet Route: W 2nd status bar, after Takeoff: shows the row and floor; for U it is Route: U all floors Sheet routing checkbox Viewport ribbon shows or hides the matrix Routing settings Viewport ribbon opens Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing Destination preview New Item dialog the path where the takeoff will go is visible before it is created

The dot is stored in the sheet folder (takeoff_routing.json) and survives closing the job.

docs.title: Where new takeoffs go (defaults, 2nd floor example)
docs.text:
Tool W (Walls) F (Framing) S (Shear walls) U (Units) Line, P Line walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing/details shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Count walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns units Area, J Area sqfts framing/2nd floor framing/joists shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Beam walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing/beams shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Openings name rule: openings name rule: openings name rule: openings units

For Openings the tool rule in Takeoff Name Routing fires before the sheet dot, so openings from any sheet except U go into openings. If you turn that rule off, Openings on an F sheet land in framing/<floor> framing/headers.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Dot Level Walls folder Framing folder Shear folder Tags in the sheet name B Base / Basement basement foor walls basement framing basement base, b, bsmt, basement 1-5 1st-5th floor 1st floor walls 1st floor framing 1st floor 1st ... 5th L loft loft walls loft framing loft loft R roof roof walls roof framing roof roof, rf Typo in the basement folder

In build 3.0 the W row folder for the B dot is named basement foor walls by default (that is how the app spells it). If you need the correct spelling, change the Walls floor folder column for level B and click Save global default.

docs.title: Automatic dot from the sheet name
docs.text:
The dot is set automatically when a sheet gets a name: the Name button, F2 in Pages, Batch Rename, Page Setup, job intake by the pipeline and the Route sheets without a dot now button.

  1. The name ends in u or U (a3011 u, S0-4A U, a copy ... U (2)): U dot. a301 u el does not get the U dot: u is not the last word.
  2. Otherwise the letter of the sheet number picks the row: a... is W, s... is F. The rule is edited in the Route sheets from their names table.
  3. A level tag picks the column: 1st, 2nd, base, rf, loft. There must be exactly one tag: a1.7 1st 2nd gets no dot.
  4. A sheet with a tag from the Skip tags list is skipped: rcp; el; sec; d; det; demo; sch; sc; n; wt; ft; u; un; unit; units; fin; in; shw; sw; v; t.
  5. A dot set by hand is never replaced.

docs.title: Settings fields
docs.text:
The Levels, Rows and Tool destinations tables; at the bottom the Apply, Reset, Save global default, Save as this job, Clear job override buttons. Field What it sets Enable sheet routing turns off the whole dot matrix Create missing destination folders create destination folders that do not exist yet (with confirmation) Copies keep their source folders when pasting New takeoffs, the copy keeps the source subfolders, only the floor changes Building root default building when no green dot is selected Dot radius size of the dots on the sheet, 0.7-3 px Levels up to 16 levels: dot label, name, three floor folders, sheet name tags (Name tags) Rows four rows W, F, S, U: name, One dot flag, all floors, name-ending tags (Name ends with) Tool destinations for each row an All tools folder and a per-tool override: Count, Line / P Line, Area, J Area, Beam, Openings Route sheets from their names the letter rule (a is W, s is F) and the Skip tags list Route sheets without a dot now a pass over the whole job: sets dots on sheets that have none Preview current sheet destinations shows where takeoffs from the open sheet will go

A folder template is written with placeholders: framing/{framingFloor}/beams, walls/{wallsFloor}, shear walls/{shearFloor}/holdowns. The U row does not accept placeholders: it has no floor.

docs.title: Takeoff Name Routing: rules by name and tool
docs.text:
An ordered rules table and the Preview name field: type the name of a future takeoff and see the folder.

Default rules (top to bottom, the first match wins; the match mode is in the Match column):

Name text Match Tool Sheet row Destination (empty) Contains Openings Any openings gable stick Contains Any Any gables/gable stick gable Contains Any Any gables/gable trusses eve Contains Any Any eves rakes/eves rake Contains Any Any eves rakes/rakes prpt Contains Any Any parapets trussheel Contains Any Any trussheel post EndsWithWord Count F framing/{framingFloor}/posts stair EndsWithWord Any F framing/{framingFloor}/stairs

Order matters: gable stick sits above gable, otherwise every gable stick would go to trusses. EndsWithWord for post and stair requires a space before the word at the end of the name, case-insensitive. These two rules apply only on an F sheet; {framingFloor} comes from the selected floor. The path is counted from the building (green dot, Building root or the Takeoffs root).

docs.title: How to add or change a rule
docs.text:
Why: takeoffs with a given word in the name land in their own folder by themselves on the right sheet.

  1. Open Settings > Takeoff Name Routing and check that Enable name and tool rules is ticked.
  2. Add a row: Name text is the name text (for example siding), Match is Contains or EndsWithWord, Tool is Any or a specific tool, Sheet row is Any or F, Destination is the folder (roof misc/siding). The Enabled checkbox in the row turns the rule off temporarily without deleting it.
  3. Put the rule above the more general ones with the Move up / Move down buttons.
  4. Check it in the Preview name field: type 6" vertical siding and read the path.
  5. Click Apply (works until restart), Save global default (for all jobs) or Save as this job (only for the open one). Reset brings back the table above, Clear job override removes the job copy.

Result: in the New Item dialog a name with this word shows the new destination folder. No more than 100 rules; a rule with an empty Name contains is allowed only for a specific Tool.

docs.title: Takeoff Colors: fixed color
docs.text:
One rule: a Line or P Line with an exact name gets the set color. Field Default What it does Enable fixed line color on the rule works on create, rename, copy and Random Colors Exact name bft the name is compared as a whole, case-insensitive, ignoring outer spaces Fixed color #D3D3D3 (light gray) color for a Line and P Line with this name

Why: bracing for trusses (bft) is always gray and is not confused with walls. In the New Item dialog such a name shows the label Fixed by Takeoff Colors settings instead of a color picker. The app hands out all other colors at random, avoiding gray, black and white; Split gives the split-off takeoff a new color.

docs.title: How to check that the route is right
docs.text:
Why: make sure before drawing that the takeoff will land in the right folder.

  1. Open the sheet and read the status bar: Route: F 2nd means the F row, 2nd floor. No Route: means the sheet has no dot.
  2. Click the tool and read the destination path in the New Item dialog before clicking OK.
  3. After drawing, find the takeoff in the Takeoffs tree: the path must match the table above.
  4. For the whole sheet click Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Preview current sheet destinations.
  5. When pasting with Paste > New takeoffs, read the line Root: Takeoffs/B.: that is the destination building.

Result: the path in the dialog, the status bar and the tree all say the same thing.

A takeoff landed in the wrong place: check the sheet dot and the green dot first, then the name rules table. Common cases are walked through in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Settings examples
docs.text:
A six-story job

Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Levels: add a level with the label 6, name 6th floor, folders 6th floor walls, 6th floor framing, 6th floor, tag 6th. Save as this job, so the other jobs do not get an extra column.

Holdowns needed in a separate folder per floor

This is already set up: a Count on an S sheet goes to shear walls/<floor>/holdowns. If holdowns are placed on the architectural plan (W sheet), add a name rule: hdu to shear walls/holdowns, or temporarily switch the sheet dot to S.

Turn routing off for one job

Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing: untick Enable sheet routing, click Save as this job. The global rules do not change; Clear job override brings them back.

docs.title: Settings: all categories
docs.text:
Here: what is in each category of the OurPlanCore 3.0 Settings tab and when to go there. You need it when an app rule (folder, name, color, sheet size, key) does not match how you work: almost everything that used to be hard-coded is now edited here.

Resolution order: the job setting beats the global one, the global one beats the built-in one. Reset puts the built-in values back into the draft, Save writes the draft where you choose.

docs.title: The principle: draft, global, per job
docs.text:
Almost every category has five buttons at the bottom:

Button What it does Apply apply the draft now, until the app restarts; nothing is written to disk Reset put the built-in values back into the draft (how the app behaved before any edits) Save global default write it for all jobs Save as this job write it only for the open job (override) Clear job override remove the job copy, the global one applies again

Job copies live inside the job in AI_Context/settings/*.json, global ones in the app profile (for Lite %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\local\presets, for the full version %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore\presets). The profiles are separate: global settings of the full version are not visible in Lite. The rule: changing it for one job - Save as this job; changing it for good - Save global default; broke something - Reset and Save.

docs.title: How to change a rule for one job only
docs.text:
What for: a non-standard job (a sixth floor, different folders) does not break the rules of other jobs.

  1. Open the Settings tab and the category you need in the list on the left.
  2. Edit the fields or table rows in the draft.
  3. Press Apply and check the behavior in Main View.
  4. Press Save as this job.

Result: the category status says Using this job's override; other jobs follow the global rule. Clear job override returns the job to the global rule, Reset and Save global default change the built-in for everyone.

docs.text:
Auto Tree: the Mode switch and the folder tree with takeoffs for More > Auto Tree. Page Folders, From Pages and Takeoff Templates work the same way.

Four template editors with a Mode switch (Auto / COM / EWP). Page Folders - the folders Auto Folders creates; Auto Tree - folders and takeoffs for More > Auto Tree (in the COM template, units now has 1st-5th subfolders); From Pages - the top folders of the tree built from sheets; Takeoff Templates - presets that dock as the Templates tab under Takeoffs or Pages. Default size and the paper preset table.

docs.text: The first two categories set the folder of a new takeoff; Takeoff Colors sets its color. Details: Takeoff routing. Sheet Legend sets the automatic blocks by the current Takeoffs folders and their order on the sheet. It has Apply, Reset, a global setting and a job-only option. On a single sheet the automatic blocks can be turned off with a button by the legend, while manual groups stay available: Sheet legend.

docs.text: Full version only. Formats the AI answer for a schedule table crop into lines like HP1 (2) 2x8. Fields Tag/size separator, a preview (paste the recognized text on the left), a checkbox for the original tables. The raw answer stays in AI Inbox.

docs.title: Sort A/S and Sort D/Sec/WT
docs.text:
"Sheet name suffix, then folder" rules. The neighboring category Sort A/S holds the prefix rules.

Sort A/S: a table Match (sheet prefix / filename keyword) and Target plus the rule Page name ends with "-" into --------others. Sort D/Sec/WT: a table Suffix and Target folder; the suffix is taken from the last known word of the name (a1.20 rcp pr5 gives rcp); synonyms un/unit, det, sch/sc, sw. Only folders that receive something are created.

The Display ribbon: value labels, legend and header, sheet rendering, units, background around and under the sheet, zoom step.

Protection against a corrupted settings file

If the key assignment file cannot be read, the editor offers Recover settings...: Retry reading, Restore / import... or a confirmed Reset to original keys. The old bytes are kept, a regular Save does not overwrite the damaged file. For job data the equivalent is Open / Import > Project Data Recovery....

docs.title: Sheets: Crop to Sheet, blank sheets, Overlay, legend, Hide
docs.text: This page covers advanced sheet work in OurPlanCore 3.0: collect details from several sheets onto one, overlay one plan on another, tidy up the legend, add notes with markup and hide clutter before the PDF goes out. You need it when preparing a PDF delivery, when checking Arch plans against Struct plans, and on jobs with dozens of details.

docs.title: Crop to Sheet: details from different sheets on one
docs.text: Source: two corners around a detail. Target: the crop at 100 % scale, placed in reading order. The crop keeps a link to the source sheet and prints in the PDF. Target dialog: an existing sheet or a new blank one with a name and a size from the presets.

docs.title: How to collect details onto one sheet
docs.text:
Demo: Page > Crop to Sheet, target Details, two crops from different sheets land side by side on one sheet.

Why: all the job's details on one clean sheet at true scale for the client PDF. You need: the sheets with details open; a blank target sheet can be created in the dialog itself.

  1. Open the sheet with details and click Page > IMAGE > Crop to Sheet.
  2. Pick the target in the dialog: Existing sheet (the list shows blank sheets and sheets that already have crops) or New blank sheet with a name and a size from the Blank Sheet presets. The Open the target sheet after each crop checkbox opens the target after each crop. Click Start Cropping.
  3. Click two opposite corners around a detail (Snap and PDF snap work). The piece is copied to the target at 100 % scale. The first crop goes to the top left with a margin, the next ones go to the right with a gap; at the right edge a new row starts below. Occupied spots are skipped. Status bar: Crop to Sheet > <target>: click two opposite corners of each detail. Esc stops.
  4. Switch to other source sheets and keep going: the target stays the same until you start the tool again.
  5. Press Esc to drop a half-drawn box, a second Esc exits to Select.

Result: the crops run across the sheet left to right, then below, without overlapping each other. Default edge margin 36 pt, gap 18 pt. If there is no free space for a whole crop, it is not added: the status suggests a larger sheet or a new sheet. Each crop keeps a link to its source sheet. An unscaled target takes the scale of the first source; a crop whose source has a different scale is flagged in the status bar.

docs.title: On the target sheet
docs.text:
The Details sheet with crops, the 75% - not true scale badge on a reduced crop and the round lock button under the Scale label. Action How Select, move Select, click the crop, drag Rotate orange handle; Shift gives 15° steps; right-click Rotate Crop 90° Clockwise / Rotate Crop 90° Counterclockwise Size corner and side handles, proportional only Mirror right-click Mirror Crop Horizontal / Mirror Crop Vertical Restore scale right-click Reset Crop to 100% (true scale); a crop not at 100 % shows a red 75% - not true scale badge (on screen only) Opacity right-click Opacity...: slider 0-100 with live preview, one Undo step Order right-click Bring to Front, Send to Back, Bring Forward, Send Backward Where it came from right-click Open Source Sheet (<name>) Lock round button under the Scale label (only on sheets with crops): Lock crops on this sheet / Crops locked - click to unlock. Locked crops cannot be selected, clicks go to the takeoffs under them

Undo works on the target sheet (move, rotate, size, Reset, delete). Placing a crop from the source sheet is not undone: delete an extra crop on the target.

How a crop is stored and printed

A crop is an entry in the target sheet's annotations.json with a link to the source sheet and a rectangle. Only that rectangle is drawn, with the source's PDF layer visibility: at 3x on screen, at 4x in the PDF. It is always exported when the Annotations module is on, even if Markups are not output. When the source is renamed or moved, the link is rebased; a deleted source gives a red cross and the line Crop skipped on '<sheet>' on export. Rotating or mirroring the source sheet does not move the crop. An old EXE (a rollback to a .bak older than 2.2.34) reads the crop as line markup and loses its fields on save.

docs.title: How to cut the visible part of a sheet into a new sheet: Crop New Page
docs.text:
Why: a separate standalone sheet from a piece of a big sheet (one building, one plan out of several on a sheet), with its own measurements and its own PDF. You need: the sheet open; the sheet has a scale if there will be measurements on the new sheet.

  1. Open the sheet and set the zoom and pan so that only the part you need is on screen.
  2. Click Page > IMAGE > Crop New Page.

Result: a sheet <name> Crop made from the visible area appears in the same Pages folder with the source sheet's scale, and it opens right away; status Crop New Page: created <name> Crop. Measurements from the source sheet are not carried over to the new sheet.

The difference from Crop to Sheet: Crop to Sheet puts crops with a link to the source onto a target sheet, Crop New Page makes a new PDF sheet that you measure on like any other.

docs.title: Blank sheets
docs.text: Blank Sheet: name, width and height, in or mm units, presets, Swap width / height.

docs.title: How to create a blank sheet
docs.text:
Demo: Page > Blank Sheet, name Details, size Tabloid (17 x 11), Create.

Why: a clean sheet for detail crops or for a diagram.

  1. Click Page > ADD > Blank Sheet (or + New > Blank Sheet in Pages, right-click a folder New Blank Sheet).
  2. Type the Sheet name, pick a paper preset or type a size, use Swap width / height if needed.
  3. Click Create.

Result: a sheet next to the open one, with the scale from the first crop or set with S.

Field What it does Sheet name sheet name in Pages Paper size width and height, in / mm toggle Presets ARCH D (36 x 24), ARCH E (48 x 36), Letter (11 x 8.5), Tabloid (17 x 11), A4, A3 Swap width / height portrait instead of landscape Reset size from Settings > Blank Sheets Create creates the sheet next to the open one

Default 36 x 24 in. The size and the preset list are edited in Settings > Blank Sheets (Apply, Save global default, Save as this job, Clear job override).

Change Sheet Size...: right-click a blank sheet in Pages. The sheet gets a new blank PDF, the scale, legend and overlays are kept; takeoffs, markup and crops keep their coordinates from the top left corner; points that fall outside the new size are listed in a warning.

Large blank sheets (for example 11520 x 3600 pt for a whole building) zoom smoothly in 3.0: these are the 2.2.39-2.2.42 fixes.

docs.title: Overlay: one sheet over another
docs.text:
The S plan in red over the A plan of the same floor; on the left the Overlay tab with the Source, Alignment, Transform groups, under the sheet in Pages the overlay layer node.

The Overlay sub-tab in the Pages panel works with the open sheet:

Group Buttons Source Add..., Open Source, Choose / Replace..., Next Match, Remove; the up and down arrows change the layer order; Show overlay Alignment Auto Fit, Find Best, Edit by Points, Reset Transform X (pt), Y (pt), Scale (0.05-20), Rotation; the sliders give a live preview, Esc restores the saved values Color, Opacity tint color (Red, Blue, Green, Orange, Magenta, Gray, custom) and opacity

docs.title: How to overlay one sheet on another and align them
docs.text:
Why: check whether the walls and framing of the A plan and the S plan of the same floor line up. You need: both sheets in the job; the Sheet Overlay module (on by default).

  1. Open the sheet you are overlaying onto (for example the architectural floor plan).
  2. Right-click the overlay sheet in Pages (the structural plan of the same floor) and pick Sheet Overlay > Use This Sheet as Current Overlay.
  3. Right-click an empty spot on the sheet and pick Auto Fit Overlay: the app fits the overlay by the plan geometry (status Overlay auto fit: ...). If there is no overlay yet, it looks for a suitable sheet in the job by itself.
  4. If the fit is off, pick Fit by 2 Points in the same menu and click a point on the overlay (a wall corner), then the spot on the sheet where it should go: the overlay shifts.
  5. Click a second overlay point far from the first one and its spot on the sheet: the overlay scales and rotates by the two pairs. Esc after the first pair keeps only the shift.
  6. Set the color and opacity in the Overlay tab (right-click Overlay Properties... opens it on the right sheet).

Result: the S plan in color over the A plan, an overlay layer node appeared under the sheet in Pages; status Overlay fit by two points: <scale>x, rotation <angle> deg.

Demo: right-click the S sheet in Pages, Sheet Overlay > Use This Sheet as Current Overlay, right-click the sheet Auto Fit Overlay, then the Overlay tab and the Show overlay checkbox.

Tips

  • Point alignment is started by three identical commands: Fit by 2 Points in the sheet menu, the Edit by Points button in the Overlay tab and Move Overlay by Points (command palette and the icon on the left strip).
  • A click snaps to the nearest PDF point within 14 px (snapped to ... in the status bar), so click on wall corners and grid line intersections.
All overlay menu items Where Item What it does Right-click a sheet in Pages, Sheet Overlay submenu Use This Sheet as Current Overlay replaces the open sheet's active overlay layer with this sheet Add This Sheet as New Overlay adds the sheet as one more layer, the previous layers stay Overlay Properties... opens the Overlay tab for the sheet Clear Current Sheet Overlay removes the active overlay layer from the open sheet Right-click an overlay layer under a sheet in Pages Overlay Properties... the Overlay tab with this layer Hide Overlay / Show Overlay hide or show the layer without deleting it Open Overlay Sheet open the sheet that is overlaid Move Layer Up, Move Layer Down layer order: the top one is drawn on top Remove Overlay Layer delete this overlay layer Right-click the sheet in the window when there is an overlay Overlay Properties..., Auto Fit Overlay, Fit by 2 Points as in the steps above Overlay keys Keys (there must be an overlay on the sheet) Command What it does Ctrl+Alt and drag Move the overlay moves the overlay with the mouse Ctrl+Alt+Left and the other arrows Nudge the overlay shift by one step Ctrl+Alt++ / Ctrl+Alt+- Scale the overlay scale Ctrl+Alt+[ / ] Rotate the overlay rotate Ctrl+Alt+0 Reset overlay transform resets shift, scale and rotation the same keys with Shift Fine nudge the overlay left and others, Fine rotate the overlay left / Fine rotate the overlay right (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+[ / ]) fine step

The keys are remapped in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts (hotkeys).

docs.title: How to overlay S plans on A plans for all floors: Batch Overlay
docs.text:
Demo: Page > Batch Overlay, an S sheet as an overlay on an A sheet at opacity 60, Apply overlays; an Overlay node appeared in Pages. Three columns: all sheets, target sheets, the overlay sheet for each row.

Why: check walls and framing floor by floor without setting up the overlay on each sheet. You need: architectural and structural plans named by floor.

  1. Click Page > PAGE > Batch Overlay or right-click a Pages folder Batch Overlay....
  2. Select the target sheets (architectural plans) on the left and click Add as targets.
  3. For each row on the right pick the overlay sheet (the structural plan of the same floor) and click Use as overlay. The filter by name or folder is at the top.
  4. Set the color and opacity, shared by the whole batch, and click Apply overlays.

Result: an overlay sits on each target sheet at its original position and scale; existing pairs are skipped. Align afterwards with the regular Overlay tools. Undoing the last batch is a button in the same window (Last batch restored.).

docs.title: Sheet legend
docs.text:
An example of manual groups in the legend; automatic blocks take their names from the rules for Takeoffs folders.

The legend is the list of takeoffs measured on the sheet; in Pages these are the nodes under the sheet. Where to set it up:

By default the takeoffs on each sheet are automatically collected into blocks by Takeoffs folder: walls goes into Walls, openings into Openings, sqfts into SQFTs; framing has separate blocks Posts, Beams, Details, Stairs. The block order is set in Settings > Sheet Legend: on framing Posts comes first, then Beams, Details and the rest; SQFTs comes after the other measurements. A takeoff with no matching rule goes into Other. When a takeoff moves to another folder, its automatic block changes too.

What Where Display, size, position Display ribbon, Legend group: Show, Size, Pos, w/page Automatic blocks of this sheet the round button with three lines next to the crop lock under Scale, or right-click the sheet: Disable Automatic Legend Blocks on This Sheet / Enable Automatic Legend Blocks on This Sheet Order right-click the sheet (Organize submenu) or a takeoff node under the sheet: Sort Sheet Legend Auto, Sort Sheet Legend A-Z, Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space), Reset Sheet Legend Order; with several sheets selected the command applies to all (Sort N Selected Sheet Legends A-Z) Order for a folder right-click a Pages folder, Organize: Sort Sheet Legends Auto in Folder, Sort Sheet Legends A-Z in Folder, Sort Sheet Legends by Key (before space) in Folder, Reset Sheet Legend Orders in Folder: for all sheets in the folder at once Groups right-click a takeoff node under the sheet: Legend Group > New Group..., a group name or Main Legend (multi-select) Managing groups right-click the sheet, Organize > Legend Groups...: rename, Move Up, Move Down, Delete (the takeoffs return to the main legend), copy the set to other selected sheets The same groups on other sheets in Pages select the sheet with groups and the target sheets, right-click the sheet with groups, Organize > Copy Legend Groups to Selected Sheets (in the menu Copy Legend Groups to N Selected Sheets)

Automatic blocks are on for a sheet by default. The button turns them off only on this sheet: the takeoffs go back to one common legend, as before. After that you can create manual groups with Legend Group > New Group... or keep one common legend. Manual groups are kept when the mode is switched.

Auto is a live order by the configured blocks; inside a block the previous takeoff sorting applies. When automatic blocks are off, the old order goes by type: Line, then Area, then Count. A-Z, by Key and the manual Move Up in Legend / Move Down in Legend write the sheet's own order; Sort Sheet Legend Auto and Reset Sheet Legend Order remove it and bring back the live order.

Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space) sorts by the part of the name before the first space, numbers by value: A1 2x4, A1 2x6, A2 2x4, A10 2x4, B1 2x4, B1A 2x4. Handy for units and marks.

Manual groups are stored in the sheet's source.json (legend_groups), are not undone by Undo, and look the same on screen, in a detached window and in the PDF. Automatic blocks are built from the current Takeoffs folders; their names and order are edited globally or per job in Settings > Sheet Legend.

docs.title: Takeoff menu under a sheet in Pages
docs.text:
Right-click a takeoff node under the sheet; with several nodes selected the item shows the number, for example Hide 3 Selected on This Sheet. Hiding a takeoff from a sheet is faster with the H key: Takeoffs tree.

All items of the takeoff menu under a sheet Item What it does Select Linked Takeoff opens the sheet, selects the takeoff in Takeoffs and its measurements on the sheet Rename Linked Takeoff... renames the takeoff in the Takeoffs tree: the name changes on all sheets Hide on This Sheet / Show on This Sheet hides or shows the takeoff only on this sheet; a hidden one is not drawn and not printed in the PDF Hide Selected on This Sheet, Show Selected on This Sheet the same for all selected nodes under the sheet Move Backward, Move Forward drawing order on the sheet: which takeoff lies on top of its neighbor; does not change the legend Move Up in Legend, Move Down in Legend row up or down in the sheet legend Legend Group > ... legend groups, table above Sort Sheet Legend Auto, Sort Sheet Legend A-Z, Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space), Reset Sheet Legend Order legend order of the whole sheet

docs.title: On-screen size of the legend, header and labels
docs.text:
Right-clicking the legend or the scale header on the sheet opens a view menu:

Item What it does Legend show or hide the legend (same as Display > Legend Show) Legend Position corner or edge of the sheet, 8 positions Legend Size, Scale / Sheet Size Label Size presets Tiny (0.25), XS (0.5), Small (0.75), Normal (1), Large (1.35), XL (1.75), XXL (2.25); Custom... is your own multiplier from 0.25 to 3.0 Scale Legend With Sheet the legend grows and shrinks with the sheet zoom (like the w/page checkbox on the Display ribbon) Scale Measurement Labels With Sheet the number labels on measurements grow with the zoom; off by default, labels are screen-sized Scale Sheet Header With Sheet the scale and sheet size header at the top grows with the zoom; off by default

This is the on-screen view; the legend size in the PDF is set in PDF Output > OVERLAYS (PDF). The Fast pan/zoom checkbox on the Display ribbon (OVERLAYS / RENDER group) draws measurements and labels simplified while panning and zooming, and the full frame after you stop: motion is smoother on heavy sheets. Off by default.

docs.title: Markup: the Annotation ribbon
docs.text:
The MARKUP TOOLS group (markup tools) and the STYLE group: the Width slider and color swatches for the next marks.

Markup is notes on the sheet with no quantity: it does not go into Takeoffs or Excel, and it prints in the PDF if Markups is on in the export dialog (PDF). The Annotations module is on by default.

Button What it draws How Highlighter (Shift+H) a semi-transparent highlighter rectangle two corners Draw Line (D) a markup line clicks on points; C, Esc or a double click finish Arrow an arrow click the tail, click the tip Box (Draw Box Tool in the palette) a rectangular frame two corners Cloud a revision cloud two corners Area fill a polygon with a semi-transparent fill in the markup color clicks on the corners, C or a double click; with Box (F9) two corners Hide a white mask below Note (N) a text note click on the sheet, type the text

The color and width of the next marks are set by the STYLE group: the Width slider (tooltip Annotation line thickness, 1-12 px) and color swatches. They do not change marks that are already drawn.

Right-click a mark: copy, paste, edit, delete Item What it does Copy Markup (in the menu with the type: Copy Box Markup, Copy Arrow Markup; with several selected Copy N Selected Markups) copies the mark; same as Ctrl+C on the selection Paste Markups Here (Paste N Markup(s) Here) pastes what was copied: the top left corner of the copy lands at the click point; works on another sheet too Edit Note... only for a Note: the Edit Sheet Note window with the note text Delete Markup (Delete Box Markup, Delete N Selected Markups) deletes the mark; locked crops are not deleted this way

docs.title: How to cover part of a sheet with a mask: Hide
docs.text:
Demo: Annotation > Hide, four clicks around a label and C give a white mask; Ctrl+Z removes it. A white rectangle covers the neighboring plan; a thin dashed outline is visible on screen so the mask can be selected.

Why: remove a neighboring plan or clutter from the sheet before the PDF, without touching the measurements.

  1. Click Annotation > MARKUP TOOLS > Hide (Hide Area in the status bar).
  2. Outline the area with clicks and press C (or double-click), or press F9 and click two corners of a box.
  3. To move or delete the mask, select it with the Select tool on its dashed outline.

Result: part of the sheet is painted white; the mask sits above the sheet and the overlays but below the takeoffs and the other markup, so it does not hide measurements. It always prints in the PDF when the Annotations module is on, even without Markups.

Next to it, Annotation > Area now follows Box: two corners give a rectangular fill.

If a whole PDF layer is in the way

Furniture, dimensions or text of a vector PDF are easier to turn off as a layer than to cover with a mask: the PDF Layers tab, right-click the layer Hide Layer. Highlight Layer in the same menu highlights the layer in color so you can see what is on it; Clear Highlight or the Clear Hi button removes the highlight (PDF layers).

docs.title: Line opacity in the PDF
docs.text: PDF Output > LINES & AREA > Opac (0-100 %, default 100) is the opacity of Line takeoffs and Draw line / Arrow markup in the exported PDF and in the live Preview. A line with all its joints fades as one group. The export pipeline uses the same setting. It does not change the on-screen view: that is on the Viewport ribbon.

docs.title: Detached sheet windows
docs.text: Sheets can be opened as separate windows and laid out on a second monitor (Open > Detach to windows, Tile M2): Other, detached windows.

docs.title: Scenario: a Details sheet for the PDF delivery
docs.text:
1. Page > Blank Sheet, name Details, ARCH D.
  2. Open the sheet with details, Crop to Sheet, target Details, Start Cropping, two corners around each detail; go to the next sheets and continue; Esc.
  3. On Details arrange the crops, rotate, Reset Crop to 100% where they were shrunk, lock.
  4. On the plans use Hide to cover neighboring plans and clutter, PDF Output > Opac 60 % if the lines cover the drawing.
  5. Organize > Legend Groups... on plans with SW: a Shear group.
  6. PDF Output > Preview, then export per the PDF instructions.

docs.title: OurPlanCore hotkeys
docs.text:
This is the only OurPlanCore 3.0 key table on the site: default bindings by group, what to do with a Russian keyboard layout, and how to remap. You need it when your hand reaches for a key instead of a button. The in-app cheat sheet is F1.

F1 shows the current bindings, including remapped ones. A second F1 or Esc closes it.

Below are the default bindings. If the profile was changed, F1 and the key editor show the current values. A key fires only where the command applies: tools and editing in the viewport, tree commands in Pages or Takeoffs. When the focus is in a text field, the letter is typed instead of running a command.

docs.title: File, help, view
docs.text:
Key Action Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Shift+O Open / Import, pick a job / recent list Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S Save / Save As F1 key cheat sheet Ctrl+Shift+P Command Palette: any command by name F Fit: the whole sheet Ctrl++ / Ctrl+- zoom; mouse wheel with the step from Settings > Defaults B then K Add Bookmark (a sequence, up to 0.9 s between presses) - collapse the Pages and Takeoffs trees H Hide Selected Takeoffs Only: hide on the sheet the takeoff of the selected segment or row

The right mouse button always pans, in any tool.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Key Tool What it does E Select select and edit; Ctrl add to the selection, Ctrl+Shift remove, Alt vertices V Pan move the view S Scale scale from a known dimension R Ruler a dimension with no quantity P Count marks, pieces L Line polyline, linear feet A Area area; F9 box J J Area Joist Area B Beam a beam by two points O Openings an opening by box X Cut cutout in an Area, erasing a Line Space Record continue the active takeoff / stop Shift+H Highlight highlighter (markup) D Draw Line / Extra Joists markup line; in a selected Joist Area, extra joists N Note a text note on the sheet F3 / Ctrl+F3 Snap / PDF Snap snap to your own points / to PDF vectors F8 Ortho 90° and 45°; Shift while drawing turns it on temporarily F9 Box two-corner mode for Area, Cut, Hide

In 3.0 H is no longer the Highlighter: H hides a takeoff, the highlighter is on Shift+H. In Roof guide mode H stays Hip.

docs.title: Drawing and editing in the viewport
docs.text:
Key Action C finish drawing (a double click works too) Esc cancel drawing, exit the tool Backspace / Ctrl+Z remove the last point / undo an action Tab cycle Layer Trace options, toggle edge-snap Enter next Layer Trace step Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy measurements / Paste Measurements (Same or New takeoffs) Ctrl+A / Del select everything on the sheet / delete the selection F2 rename the takeoff of the selected object Ctrl+M / Ctrl+Shift+M Merge / Split: whole takeoffs from the tree or segments from the sheet Ctrl+Shift+B Break: a Line into separate segments Ctrl+Shift+V Break H/V: segments into - Horizontal and - Vertical takeoffs Shift while rotating 15° step (rotate handle of markup and crops)

More on Merge, Split, Break: Editing takeoffs.

The app has no redo of an undone action (Redo, Ctrl+Y): Ctrl+Z undoes a step for good, so before a series of undos check what you are rolling back.

docs.text:
Key Pages Takeoffs Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V copy, cut, paste a sheet the same for takeoffs and folders Ctrl+D Duplicate Page duplicate a takeoff Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down move the node move the node Ctrl+Z bring back what was deleted bring back what was deleted; undo Merge / Split F2 / Del Rename Page / delete Rename / delete Esc clear the selection Ctrl+Enter select the section's measurements on the sheet H hide the takeoffs of the selected rows on the current sheet F4 Set Scale on the selected sheets F5 Name / Scale Setup T New takeoff item (in the work window) Ctrl+Shift+V Break H/V (not Paste)

docs.title: Russian keyboard layout
docs.text: Keys work by the physical key: L draws a Line in both the EN and the RU layout, and the labels stay English. There is no need to switch layouts for the keys: you can type notes in Russian and press P right away.

docs.title: Assign or change a key
docs.text:
Search, the command table, the New shortcut field and the save buttons.
  1. Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts > Open Keyboard Shortcuts....
  2. Find the command: search by name, category, key or button name (Search command, category, key or control name); the Changed only checkbox shows only changed ones.
  3. Click the New shortcut: field, press the combination, Assign. For a sequence of up to three presses turn on Sequence.
  4. The editor shows a conflict in the same context and offers to move the binding; check which command loses its binding.
  5. Save global default for all jobs or Save for this job for the open one. The job copy wins; Use global for this job removes it.
Button What it does Remove keys remove the bindings of the selected command Reset command / Reset all to original bring back the defaults into the draft; then Save Import preset... / Export preset... load or save a set as JSON Choose command in app... the editor hides: Ctrl and click moves through tabs and menus, a plain click picks the command, Esc finishes Recover settings... if the bindings file cannot be read: Retry reading, Restore / import..., Reset to original keys

Until Save the old keys keep working. A binding on an input field moves the focus into it, on a list it opens the choice; it is not a macro. A disabled module and a read-only job still limit what the key can do, even when it is bound.
