docs.title: Snap and tracing
docs.text: This page covers the toggles on the bottom strip (Snap, PDF, Ortho, Box), the PDF Layers tab and Layer Trace, wall tracing inside an area, and tracing requests through the AI Inbox (full version only). In everyday measuring an outline is traced with clicks using Ortho and Snap; tracing is needed rarely, when the drawing is vector and there are many walls. How these techniques combine with editing: Editing measurements and snaps.

docs.title: Snaps on the tool strip
docs.text:
Right end of row 1: four toggles Snap, PDF, Ortho, Box. An active toggle is highlighted and applies to all drawing tools and to dragging vertices. Button Key What it does When to turn it on Snap F3 the cursor catches on points of your own measurements and markup on the sheet: ends and corners (end), segment midpoints (mid), intersections (intersection), Count marks, points of the drawing in progress; radius 14 screen px continue a wall exactly from the end of the neighboring one, close an outline at the same vertex, bring two lines together at a corner PDF Ctrl+F3 snap to corners and lines of a vector PDF; see the warning almost never Ortho F8 the next point only horizontal or vertical from the previous one; Shift while drawing or dragging turns it on temporarily rectangular plans, so the line does not drift by a fraction of a degree Box F9 Line and Area by two opposite corners instead of point by point; works for Cut, the Area annotation and the Hide mask rectangular room, shaft cutout, mask box

Snaps do not change finished measurements and do not affect quantities: a wall traced with clicks along the centerline without Snap gives the same length. Turn them on for clean geometry and a clean PDF, turn them off when the cursor starts sticking to the wrong things.

docs.title: How to trace an outline with Snap and Ortho
docs.text:
Why: a polyline with clean corners, closed exactly at the starting point. You need: a sheet with a scale.

  1. Turn on Ortho (F8) and Snap (F3).
  2. Click Line (L) or Area (A), give it a name, OK.
  3. Zoom in on the first corner and click.
  4. Move to the next corner: Ortho holds the axis. On a skewed run release Ortho with one F8 and turn it back on afterwards.
  5. To continue from someone else's end, hover over the end of another line: the Snap highlight shows end, click.
  6. Close it: bring the cursor to the first point (end highlight) and click; for an Area a click near the first point closes it by itself. Finish with C or a double click.

Result: an outline with no gaps at the corners; Total shows the length or area.

Demo: F3 (Snap) and F8 (Ortho) run a line from the ends of the neighboring one; F9 (Box) draws a rectangular area with two clicks.

Tips

  • Shift holds the axis also when dragging a handle or a whole measurement (Shift = ortho in the status bar).
  • Snap also works when dragging a vertex: the corner of one wall sticks to the end of another.
  • An extra point while drawing is removed with Backspace.

docs.title: How to draw a rectangle with two clicks
docs.text:
Why: a rectangular room, shaft or mask box without four clicks. You need: a sheet with a scale.

  1. Turn on Box (F9).
  2. Pick Area, Line or Cut.
  3. Click one corner, then the opposite one.

Result: a finished rectangle; for a Line, a closed outline of four sides. The status Cut: box is too small or cancelled: the box has no size means the corners are too close.

docs.title: Why PDF Snap is almost never used
docs.text:
Works unreliably

The owner's words: "PDF snap works very badly, I almost never use it." PDF (Ctrl+F3) catches on corners and lines of the PDF vector and on black lines of a raster; on real plans it sticks to borders, leaders and dimension lines just as readily as to walls, and needs a black-line index for scans. The recipes in this knowledge base do not use it: accuracy comes from Ortho, Box, Snap to your own points, zoom and editing vertices afterwards.

If you do turn it on: the status reads PDF Snap on: current sheet and sheet overlay vector points/lines; Tab cycles the modes for continuing along the drawing (vertices / edge / edges / contour / polyline), Viewport > PDF SNAP > Bridge sets the continuation radius (slider PDF Snap Tab continuation radius, 4-96 screen px, default 36). It is turned off with the same Ctrl+F3.

docs.title: PDF Layers
docs.text:
The sheet's layer list with visibility checkboxes and the Load, All On, All Off, Clear Hi, Layer Trace, Full, Apply buttons.

The PDF Layers sub-tab in the Pages panel (PDF Layers module, on by default) works with a vector PDF in which the drafter left layers: walls, dimensions, furniture, text. A scan has no layers.

docs.title: How to hide unneeded drawing layers
docs.text:
Why: remove dimensions and furniture so you see only the walls while tracing. You need: a vector PDF; the PDF layers checkbox on the Display ribbon turned on (by default the sheet is shown as one Static image picture).

  1. Open the PDF Layers tab under Pages and click Load: layers are read on demand.
  2. Untick the layers you do not need: the sheet redraws right away, status Layer off: <layer>. All Off and All On toggle all of them.
  3. To find a layer on the sheet, tick Hi on its row: the layer is highlighted; Clear Hi removes the highlight.

Result: the sheet shows only the layers that are on. The Apply button in this panel belongs to Layer Trace, it is not needed for visibility. Hidden layers also stay out of Crop to Sheet crops: a crop takes the visibility of the source sheet (crops).

docs.title: Layer Trace
docs.text: Tracing by layer: the app takes the geometry of one PDF layer (for example the walls layer) and turns it into a measurement without clicking it out. Vector PDFs only.

docs.title: How to take a takeoff from a PDF layer
docs.text:
Why: the outline or walls are on a separate layer, and it can be taken as a whole. You need: layers loaded (Load), a sheet with a scale, an active takeoff of the type the mode produces (table below): Area for Full, Line for Edge and All Edges, Count for Point.

  1. Make the right takeoff active: select it in Takeoffs and press Space, or create a new one with a tool button.
  2. Click Layer Trace in the PDF Layers panel. A trace bar appears above the sheet; its toggle shows Layer Trace instead of Manual.
  3. Pick the layer: click its row in the list, or hover over the drawing geometry (status Layer Trace hover: <layer>. Click/Enter locks layer; Tab cycles candidates) and click or press Enter to lock the layer.
  4. Pick the mode: Tab or the button with the mode name (on the bar above the sheet and in the panel) cycles Full, Edge, Point, All Edges; the status shows the current one.
  5. Hover over the line of the layer you need and click or press Enter (the Apply button in the panel does the same): status Layer Trace added <type> from '<layer>'.
  6. Check the result in the tree and on the sheet: delete extra segments (dimension lines, borders) with the Select tool; Ctrl+Z undoes the creation.
Mode What it creates Full one Area: a rectangle around the extents of the whole layer geometry, not along its outline Edge one Line: the layer segment nearest to the cursor Point one Count mark at the cursor point All Edges up to 48 of the longest layer segments, each as a separate Line

Result: the measurement goes into the active takeoff. If there is no active takeoff of the right type, the app removes what it created with the status No Line takeoff item is active... (or Area, Count). If there is nothing under the cursor: Layer Trace: no PDF layer found under this point.

docs.title: Layer menu in the PDF Layers list
docs.text:
A right-click on a layer row opens a menu with the layer name in the header. The Trace ... to Takeoff items turn on Layer Trace right away, set the mode and create a measurement in the active takeoff; they take the point where the cursor last was on the sheet. So first hover over the line you need, then move the cursor into the list and open the menu.

Item What it does Use for Layer Trace makes the layer the trace layer without hovering over the drawing; with Layer Trace on it is ready to create a measurement right away Trace Full Layer to Takeoff Full mode: an Area around the layer extents Trace Nearest Edge to Takeoff Edge mode: the segment at the last cursor point Trace Point to Takeoff Point mode: a Count mark at the last cursor point Trace All Edges to Takeoff All Edges mode: up to 48 of the longest segments Show Layer / Hide Layer turn the layer on or off, like the checkbox in the row Highlight Layer / Clear Highlight highlight the layer on the sheet or remove the highlight, like the Hi checkbox

In the full version, with the AI module on, there are two more items at the top, Save Layer Info for AI and Queue AI Request for This Layer: they write the layer details into the AI Inbox (AI in the app).

docs.title: Trace Walls Inside Area
docs.text: Deterministic wall tracing inside an area that is already drawn: from the PDF vector lines the app builds wall centerlines and puts them into a new Line takeoff. Requires the Advanced Takeoff Tools module (on).

docs.title: How to take off the walls inside an area
docs.text:
Why: dozens of partitions of a unit or a floor in one action, then just a check. You need: a vector PDF, a sheet with a scale, an Area along the zone outline (a finished 1st works).

  1. Right-click the area on the sheet or its row in Takeoffs: Trace Walls Inside Area....
  2. In the Trace Walls Inside Area dialog set New Line takeoff (name per the canon, for example int 2x4 9.09).
  3. Check Wall thickness (distance between the two face lines): 3 and 13 inches by default; Ignore walls shorter than 1 ft.
  4. On sheets with dark fill on bearing and rated walls, tick Only solid (dark) filled walls - demising / corridor / rated: the light gray unit partitions are dropped. Leave Dark cutoff at auto.
  5. The Include perimeter walls on the area edge checkbox adds lines along the area boundary (off by default: exterior walls are measured separately); Edge offset 1 ft sets the width of that zone.
  6. Click Trace. Status Tracing walls: reading sheet vector/raster lines....
  7. Check the length against a hand-traced run on at least one segment, delete extra lines, draw the missing ones with Record.

Result: a Line takeoff with centerlines. Short fragments, text and leaders are filtered out, collinear pieces are joined. If the vector did not work, the status reads PDF lines did not match; trying raster image; the Allow rough image-only trace (may catch text) checkbox allows a rough trace from the image.

Tips

  • Without a sheet scale the trace does not start: Set the sheet scale first: wall thickness is measured in real inches.
  • The trace does not tell ext from int and does not know the height: sorting into takeoffs stays with the estimator.
  • Where walls are drawn with a single line and no fill, the fill filter turns itself off; check the result more carefully.

docs.title: Tracing requests through the AI Inbox
docs.text: Full version only: Lite has no AI module, while Layer Trace and Trace Walls Inside Area above do work. With the AI module on, the sheet context menu has the items Trace wall from this point, Trace closed area and Check missed takeoffs on this page. They do not draw right away: they create an AI Inbox entry with the text Pending SmartTrace request or Pending SmartCheck request, which is then run and checked through AI Manager or the AI terminal (AI console, AI Manager). The result reaches the tree only after confirmation.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text:
• Snap on a dense drawing catches on a neighboring measurement or markup: turn off F3 or zoom in.
  • Ortho gets in the way on plans with diagonal walls: hold Shift only on the run that needs it.
  • Box stays on for all tools: after a rectangle turn off F9, otherwise the next polyline closes after the second click.
  • PDF is silent on a scan without a black-line index; on a vector it catches on borders as readily as on walls.
  • Layer Trace and Trace Walls give candidates, not a finished measurement: check the total length against a hand trace.

docs.title: Split by sheets and routing
docs.text:
Here: how a drawing set is split into working sheets for each kind of work, which sheet carries which W/F/S/U dot, what is drawn on it, and why a new takeoff goes into the right branch of the tree by itself. Needed at the start of every job and when the tree "sorted itself" the wrong way. How the rules work: Names and auto-routing, settings: Routing: settings, folder and name canon: Takeoff tree and sheet names.

Demo on a real job: a wall on a W sheet goes to walls/3rd floor walls, a beam on an F sheet to framing/3rd floor framing/beams, a shear wall on a sheet copy with the S dot to shear walls.

One floor gives several working sheets: an architectural plan with the W dot, a structural plan with the F dot, a plan copy for shear walls with the S dot, a unit plan with the U dot. Each dot leads to its own branch of one building's tree.

docs.title: Why split
docs.text:
The demo job shows all takeoffs on one sheet: area, walls, beam, joists, openings, roof together. That is handy for seeing what the app can do, but it is not how real work is done:

  • The sheet legend lists only the takeoffs measured on that sheet. A sheet with everything on it gives a legend half a sheet long that the client will not read.
  • The PDF sent to the client has one kind of work per sheet: walls read on the architectural plan, framing on the structural plan, shear walls on their own copy.
  • The sheet dot sorts new takeoffs by itself: on a W sheet a Line goes to walls, on an F sheet to framing, on an S sheet to shear walls. Without splitting, every takeoff would have to be moved by hand.
  • Checking is easier: open s201 2nd and you see only the 2nd floor framing and its legend.

docs.title: Which sheet carries what
docs.text:
Rule: one dot per sheet, one kind of work per sheet. Example for the 2nd floor, paths from the building root.

Sheet Dot What we draw Tool Where it goes by itself a201 2nd, architectural plan W 2 walls ext 2x6 9.09, corr 2x6 11.7, 2x4 9.09; floor area 2nd Line; Area walls/2nd floor walls; sqfts s201 2nd, structural plan F 2 joists, beams, posts, headers, details by number, stairs J Area; Beam; Count; Line framing/2nd floor framing/joists, .../beams, the floor root for Count (posts and headers later go to posts and headers/ext or int), .../details plan copy in Struct/Shear S 2 shear walls per schedule SW1-1; holdowns HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2 Line; Count shear walls/2nd floor/shear; shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns a3011 u, unit plan U partitions of a typical unit A 2x4 Line units with any tool a105 rf, roof plan W R roof planes rf 6; eaves eve 24 main, rake 12 main; trussheel 0.66 Area; Line sqfts; eves rakes/eves and rakes; trussheel (by name, the dot does not matter) a201 el elevations, s501 d details no dot openings 4.3x7.8; gables gable; parapets prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5; detail items Openings; Area; Line openings, gables/..., parapets by tool and name; a detail item without a rule word stays in the selected folder

What matters here:

  • Elevations and details get no dot (the tags el, d, sec, rcp are on the skip list), and that is fine: openings are routed by the Openings tool, and gable, prpt, eve, rake, trussheel by the name. For anything else on a sheet without a dot, first select the right folder in Takeoffs (for example framing/2nd floor framing/details), then draw, or continue an existing takeoff with Record.
  • Posts and headers on an F sheet go into the floor root framing/2nd floor framing; they are moved into posts and headers/ext|int after the takeoff, or created right in the right folder (New Item with the folder selected). A post is counted on the framing floor it supports.
  • Holdowns are counted on the S sheet together with the shear walls, not on the framing plan: a Count on an S sheet goes to holdowns by itself.
  • Sheet copies are needed only for shear walls, for a second level on one sheet, for another building and for a new sheet set. Do not make a copy for each takeoff type: walls and areas are drawn on one W sheet and split by tool.

docs.title: The sheet legend shows only its own takeoffs
docs.text: The legend is built from takeoffs that have measurements on this sheet; the same takeoffs are visible in Pages under the sheet. So on a201 2nd the legend has only the 2nd floor walls and area, and on the shear copy only the SW marks and holdowns. A takeoff drawn on two sheets appears in both legends. Legend order, groups and size: PDF and delivery, legend, legend groups.

docs.title: Example: one building after splitting
docs.text:
2nd floor sheets of a three-story building, folders per the canon:

00. imported/
  Arch/
    a201 2nd          W 2   walls, floor area
    a105 rf           W R   roof, eaves, truss heel
    a3011 u           U     unit A
  Struct/
    s201 2nd          F 2   framing: joists, beams, posts, headers, details
    Shear/
      s201 2nd sw     S 2   copy for shear walls and holdowns
  sections/  details arch/  details struct/  units/

The Takeoffs tree of the same building after the takeoff:

sqfts/                        2nd, rf 6
walls/2nd floor walls/        ext 2x6 9.09, corr 2x6 11.7, 2x4 9.09
units/                        A 2x4, B1A 2x4
openings/2/                   4.3x7.8, 3.3x6.5 d
framing/2nd floor framing/
  joists/                     2x10 16"
  beams/                      FB1 8, (2) 1 3/4 x 18 LVL 22
  headers/ext/                ext H228 4
  posts/                      C4 20
  details/                    12/S401, ribbon
shear walls/2nd floor/
  shear/                      SW1-1, WSW-C 7-16 OSB DTT2Z
  holdowns/                   HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2
eves rakes/eves/  rakes/      eve 24 main, rake 12 main
trussheel/                    trussheel 0.66

Several buildings: the same picture inside the building folder (Main/..., Grge/...); the building for new takeoffs is set by the green dot (building root).

docs.title: How to make a sheet copy for shear walls
docs.text:
Demo: Ctrl+D makes a copy of the sheet, F2 names it a101 1st sw, a click on the S/1 dot under Scale sets the route S 1st floor.

Why: 2nd floor shear walls and holdowns on a separate copy of the structural plan, with their own legend and their own place in the tree. You need: the structural plan s201 2nd named and scaled; a Struct/Shear folder in Pages.

  1. In Pages, right-click s201 2nd > Duplicate Page (Ctrl+D). The copy appears next to it with the same name and inherits the original's dot (F 2).
  2. F2, name s201 2nd sw; right-click Move to Folder... into Struct/Shear. The sw tag is on the auto-dot skip list, so renaming will not move the dot; the app never replaces a dot set by hand.
  3. Open the copy, click the S dot in column 2 under the Scale header. Status: Route: S 2nd.
  4. L, name SW1-1, trace the shear wall run, C. In the New Item dialog the destination line shows shear walls/2nd floor/shear; after creation the takeoff is there.
  5. P, name HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2, a point at the end of the wall: the takeoff went to shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns.
  6. The next run of the same mark: select the takeoff, Space (Record), keep drawing; Record continues the takeoff and ignores the dot.

Result: in Pages the copy s201 2nd sw in Struct/Shear with the status Route: S 2nd; in Takeoffs shear walls/2nd floor/shear/SW1-1 and shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns/HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2; the copy's legend shows only those.

Tips

  • A plan copy for a second building on a shared sheet is made the same way (rename, check the dot, green dot on the building): Multiple buildings.
  • The unit sheet a3011 u gets the U dot by itself on renaming; copies for each takeoff type are not needed.

docs.title: How to fix a takeoff that went to the wrong place
docs.text:
1. Read the status after creation: Route: and Auto routed to ... tell you which sheet and which row worked; the green dot in Takeoffs shows the building.
  2. Move the takeoff by dragging or with Ctrl+X and Paste Into Folder: measurements, color and legend order are kept.
  3. Remove the cause: set the copy's dot, clear the wrong green dot, rename the takeoff without a trap word (level 2 gets caught by the eve rule).
  4. If it repeats in every job, change the rule in Settings (Sheet Takeoff Routing or Takeoff Name Routing) instead of moving by hand.

Full breakdown: Names and auto-routing, a takeoff landed in the wrong place, Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Everything drawn on one sheet: the legend is unreadable, the client PDF cannot be assembled by kind of work.
  • The shear copy kept the F dot: shear walls landed in framing/.../details.
  • Sheet copies for each takeoff type: duplicate sheets, empty legends.
  • The tag is not last (a3011 u el) or two floor tags (a1.7 1st 2nd): the dot is not set, takeoffs go into the selected folder.
  • Record on the wrong takeoff: the measurement goes into it regardless of the sheet.

All sheet and tree mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Here: where the app is and how it updates, what you see on first launch, how to open the demo job and what to try in it, where to find commands (F1, palette) and where settings live. Needed on day one and after every update. To learn step by step: First steps: 10 lessons.

docs.title: Where the app is and how it updates
docs.text:
Estimators run OurPlanCore Lite: no AI models and no terminal, lighter than the full version. How they differ: Lite vs full version.

What Where The app itself a single file ourplancore.exe in the shared Dropbox folder Office Folder\programs Launch this file or a desktop shortcut to it Update a new file arrives in the same folder through Dropbox and replaces the old one; no previous version is kept next to it. What changed: the changes folder in the same place and What's new Excel templates the templates folder in the same place: TemplateCom.xlsm, TemplateResidential.xlsm Version in the window title: OurPlanCore 3.0.x-lite - <job>; the same in the first Version ... line of the log %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\roaming\logs\app-<date>.log

Jobs, settings and templates do not depend on the update: they are stored separately (see Where settings live).

The full version is installed separately: the file ourplancore.exe in the Desktop\updates\OurPlanCore folder, with the Excel templates next to it; the window title shows the number without -lite, the log is in %APPDATA%\OurPlanCore\logs. When it is updated, the previous file stays next to it as .bak for rollback.

Rolling back to .bak (full version)

An older build reads crops (Crop to Sheet) and Hide masks as regular markup and loses their fields on save. If you rolled back, do not save a job with crops until you are back on a fresh build.

docs.title: First launch and the start screen
docs.text:
Four tiles. Open / Import on the Main ribbon is always available, F1 shows the shortcuts. Tile What it does Open a recent job list of recent jobs and job folders New blank job an empty job, sheets are added later New job from PDFs a job from a folder of PDF drawings Open sample job a demo job to get acquainted

After that, work happens in Main View: Pages on the left, the sheet in the center, Takeoffs on the right, the tool strip at the bottom. Window map: on the section hub.

docs.title: Demo job: a tour
docs.text:
Demo: Open sample job on the start card creates the demo job; then the W, F, S and U sheets with their legends and the 3D tab (it exists only in the full version).

The demo job is a training job with no client data. Try every button on it without worrying about breaking anything: it can be created again at any time. The First steps: 10 lessons course uses it too.

docs.title: How to open the demo job
docs.text:
Why: to get a job with sheets, dots and a canonical tree where you can learn. You need: the app running; no job has to be open.

  1. Press the Open sample job tile on the start screen or open Main > Open / Import > Sample job (demo to explore); the same item is available as the Sample link at the bottom of the Open project... dialog.
  2. Wait for the status Sample project created: OurPlanCore Guide Sample.: the app creates the job in the jobs folder and opens it right away.
  3. In Pages, expand the 00. Guide folder and click a plan sheet.

Result: the window title shows OurPlanCore 3.0.x - OurPlanCore Guide Sample, sheets on the left, the Takeoffs tree with ready-made takeoffs on the right, Scale: and Route: in the status bar.

docs.title: What is inside
docs.text:
What Where to look Why 00. Guide hint cards image sheets at the top of the Pages folder a map of the window, ribbons and panels right in the app A plan with the W dot, a structural plan with the F dot, a copy for shear walls with the S dot, a unit plan with the U dot sheets in 00. Guide, dots under the Scale header how a sheet set is split up (split by sheets) A canonical tree: sqfts, walls/1st floor walls, framing/1st floor framing/..., openings, shear walls, eves rakes Takeoffs panel takeoff names with numbers for Excel, folders by floor Roof outline rf 6 with eaves roof plan and sqfts, eves rakes roof area with the pitch in the name; in the full version, a starting point for the 3D roof A Start here... note and observations in the AI Inbox plan sheet; Inbox panel with the AI module (full version only) an example of markup and AI entries

The exact contents of the demo after the 3.0.1 release should be checked against the job itself: takeoff and sheet names in the table are approximate.

docs.title: What to try, step by step
docs.text:
1. Sheets and dots. Open a plan, read Route: W 1st in the status bar; press F2 and enter the same name again: the dot does not change. Make a copy of the sheet (Ctrl+D), rename it to ... sw, click the S dot. Split by sheets
  2. Routing. Press L, type the name ext 2x6 9.09, look at the destination line in the New Item dialog, make two clicks and C: the takeoff sits in walls/1st floor walls. Names and auto-routing
  3. Tools. On the same plan O on a door, A on a room, X to cut an area; on a structural sheet J for a joist area and B for a beam from support to support. Tools
  4. Legend. Display > Legend Show, then right-click the sheet, Organize > Sort Sheet Legend by Key; H on a takeoff hides it from the sheet, the dot next to the takeoff under the sheet in Pages brings it back. Takeoffs tree
  5. Crops and mask. Page > Blank Sheet, then Page > Crop to Sheet from the plan onto the blank sheet; Annotation > Hide with a box over what is not needed. Sheets: advanced
  6. 3D (full version only). Turn on the 3D module, select rf 6, the 3D tab, Roof Base, Auto, Iso. In Lite, skip this step. 3D roof
  7. Export. PDF Output > Preview, Main > Export of one sheet; in an open copy of TemplateCom.xlsm click a cell, select a takeoff and press Excel at the bottom (in the full version also the XL strip, the WL button). PDF and delivery, Export to Excel

docs.title: Broke the demo, what next
docs.text: Anything goes: delete takeoffs, move sheets, change dots, clean the tree with Delete Empty. To start fresh, press Open sample job again: the app creates a new copy with a unique name (OurPlanCore Guide Sample (2)), the old one stays in the jobs folder; you can delete it in File Explorer via Open in Explorer or keep it as your sandbox. The demo does not touch the app settings (Settings); your global rules stay yours.

docs.title: F1 and the command palette
docs.text:
Ctrl+Shift+P: any command by name, with its current shortcut next to it. Key What it opens F1 a shortcut cheat sheet over the window; closes with Esc Ctrl+Shift+P command palette: categories File, View, Workspace, Tools, Edit, Pages, Sheets, Takeoffs and, in the full version, AI; type part of the name and Enter Ctrl+O Open / Import; Ctrl+Shift+O - recent jobs

A command without a shortcut (for example Ends, Toggle Dark Theme, Hide / Show All Takeoffs) is run from the palette or gets a shortcut in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts. Shortcuts work by physical keys in both the English and the Russian keyboard layout. Full list: Keyboard shortcuts.

Demo: Ctrl+Shift+P, type show all, Enter: the Hide / Show All Takeoffs command hides all measurements on the sheet, running it again shows them.

docs.title: Theme and sheet look
docs.text:
The Display ribbon:

Button What it does Dark dark window theme Paper sheet paper tone: White, Soft gray, Medium gray, Dark gray, Warm, Soft green, Black Edge background around the sheet: White, Gray, Dark Static image, DPI the sheet as a single raster (on by default, 150 DPI); Black vector draws vectors in black Legend Show / Size / Pos measurement legend on the sheet Zoom mouse wheel step

The dark theme is easier on the eyes in long sessions, but check takeoff colors before the PDF on white paper: the PDF prints on white.

docs.title: How to make your first measurement
docs.text:
Why: to go from an open job to a saved takeoff in five minutes. You need: a job with named sheets (from intake or the demo).

  1. Press Ctrl+O and choose Open project... (jobs).
  2. In Pages expand 00. imported/Arch, open a floor plan, read Scale: in the status bar and the dot under the Scale header (sheets).
  3. Press L, name the takeoff ext 2x6 9.09, trace the exterior walls, press C (tools).
  4. Find in Takeoffs where the takeoff went: walls/1st floor walls with the W 1 dot (names and auto-routing).
  5. Select the takeoff, press Space, draw another run: Record continues the takeoff instead of creating a new one (tree).
  6. Press Ctrl+S and wait for Save: Saved hh:mm:ss.

Result: a takeoff with two sections in walls/1st floor walls, Total in LFT, the job saved. Next, step by step: First steps: 10 lessons.

docs.title: What the entities mean
docs.text: The sheet sets the drawing and scale, the takeoff (takeoff item) is what we count, the measurement connects them. This is a data diagram, not a screenshot of the window. Entity Role Project / Job the whole job: sheets, Takeoffs tree, job settings, source PDFs; one .ourplan file Page / Sheet a sheet with a scale, a W/F/S/U dot, a legend and overlays Takeoff item a named container for measurements of one type: Line, Area, Count, Joist Area Measurement geometry on a specific sheet; one takeoff can collect measurements from several sheets Annotation (markup) marks with no quantity: Highlight, Draw Line, Arrow, Box, Cloud, Note, Hide

docs.title: Where settings live
docs.text:
What Where General settings, shortcuts, logs Lite: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\roaming (settings.json, logs folder); full version: %APPDATA%\OurPlanCore Rule presets (routing, shortcuts), caches Lite: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite\local; full version: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore, terminal files there too Settings of a specific job inside the job in AI_Context/settings Jobs the jobs folder shown by Open project... (Manage job folders... adds folders)

Lite has its own profile: its settings start from the built-in defaults and do not mix with the full version's settings. Each Settings section has Reset, Save global default and Save as this job: a rule can be overridden for one job without touching the global one. Which sections exist: Settings and modules. Some tabs (Sheet Manager, Takeoff Manager, Report Builder, Job Tracker) are off by default and are turned on in Settings > Modules; Materials, AI and 3D exist only in the full version. What they do and when they are needed: Extra features.

docs.title: Takeoffs tree
docs.text:
This page covers the Takeoffs panel, a new takeoff and Record, copying between sheets and buildings, hiding, search, Estimating. You need it every day; the canonical folders and names are on Takeoff tree and sheet names, several buildings and the green dot on Multiple buildings.

At the top, the green and red root dots, the active takeoff line with Record, Total; below, the buttons and the tree. Tabs Takeoffs, Estimating, Templates.

docs.title: Panel: reference
docs.text:
Element What it does Green and red dots root for new takeoffs: the selected building or all of Takeoffs (multiple buildings) Record (Space), More, Props, Find, Sheet, >, < the active takeoff line: continue recording, properties, show in the tree, pick a takeoff from this sheet, next and previous > (Switch to next takeoff item), < (Switch to previous takeoff item) make the next or previous takeoff from the list of all job takeoffs active, wrapping around; status Active takeoff target 3/12: <name>. They do not switch during Record More on the active takeoff line Properties..., Find in Tree, Sheet Targets... (same as Sheet), Previous Target, Next Target (same as < and >) Sheet list of takeoffs measured on the open sheet, with quantities; the active one is marked *; at the top Next Sheet Target - the next takeoff of this sheet Total total of the active takeoff in its units New Folder, New Item (T) folder and takeoff under the selected folder Delete Empty delete takeoffs with no measurements; Ctrl+Z brings them back as a batch More Roof Base from area (3D module, full version only), Auto Tree (COM template roots), From Pages (folders by sheet structure) Export Save, Save As..., Export CSV, Export TXT, Export Excel, Export to Current Excel Icons in the panel header Refresh Takeoffs tree - reread the tree from the job folder, status Takeoffs tree refreshed.; Collapse all Takeoffs nodes and Expand all Takeoffs nodes - collapse or expand all folders. The same commands are on the right icon strip: Collapse Takeoffs Tree, Expand Takeoffs Tree Search left field by folder name, right field by takeoff or measurement name; the button in the left field Match takeoff folder case exactly (on) tells A from a, off searches case-insensitive Tabs on the right Takeoffs, Estimating, 3D (module, full version only), Templates

Under each takeoff in the tree you see sections: measurements by sheet; Ctrl+Enter selects the section's measurements on the sheet.

Key What it does F2 rename a takeoff or folder (Rename...) Delete delete; Ctrl+Z with focus in the tree brings it back Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down order in the folder Ctrl+Enter select the section's measurements on the sheet Ctrl+M / Ctrl+Shift+M Merge and Split the selected takeoffs (editing) Shift / Ctrl + click select a range of rows or add one row drag the mouse from an empty spot in the tree row selection box; with Ctrl adds to the selection Alt + drag from a row a box started right from a row (in F1: Start marquee selection from a row); without Alt, dragging a row moves it Right-click on a takeoff Rename..., Properties..., Set Unit Price, Cut, Copy, Paste Into Parent Folder, Delete; on an Area Create Line Grid...; on a Joist Area Set / Reset Joist Direction; all items: tree menus

docs.title: Building and root
docs.text: One building: the roots walls, sqfts, framing... sit right in Takeoffs; do not create a Main folder. Several buildings: a folder for each (A, B, Grge); the green dot (Use selected folder as root) makes the selected folder the root for new takeoffs, the red dot (Use Takeoffs root) returns to the shared root. How to run a job with several buildings, copy identical buildings and deliver them as separate workbooks and PDFs: Multiple buildings.

docs.title: How to build the job tree
docs.text:
Why: the COM template roots with the right names in one click. You need: the job open; for several buildings, the building folders created.

  1. Select the Takeoffs root (or a building folder).
  2. Press More > Auto Tree: units, sqfts, walls, gables, parapets, trussheel, openings, eves rakes, roof misc, framing, shear walls, trims, siding appear with floor subfolders.
  3. Add whatever is missing with the New Folder button under the selected folder (for example BW/1st).

Result: a canonical tree; the template content is edited in Settings > Auto Tree (Settings).

docs.title: How to create a takeoff: New Item
docs.text:
Demo: T, name C4 20, type Count, marker style Diamond, routed to framing/1st floor framing. Name, measurement type, point symbol, color and a preview of the target folder before creation.

Why: a takeoff with the right name, type and color before the first click on the sheet.

  1. Press T or the New Item button (any measuring tool opens the same dialog).
  2. Type the Name: Excel reads the numbers in the name (formats).
  3. Pick the Measurement type: Count, Line, Area, Joist Area; for Count, the symbol in Count display (circle, cross, square, star, triangle, diamond, ring).
  4. Leave Color random or pick your own; the name bft gets a fixed gray (Fixed by Takeoff Colors settings).
  5. Read the target line at the bottom: where the takeoff will land by sheet dot and name. If needed, tick Review similar on this sheet (search for similar symbols right away) or set up Beam annotation line and Offset lines (up to two parallel companion lines).
  6. Press OK.

Result: the takeoff sits in the target folder, status Takeoff: <name> (Route: ...), drawing goes into it. New Folder creates a folder under the selected one; right-click on a folder gives Rename Folder..., Folder Properties..., Organize > Auto Create Tree / Create Folders From Pages / Sort Children A-Z.

docs.title: How to continue a takeoff: Record
docs.text:
Demo: select a takeoff, Space (Record), draw one more partition and C; Total grows in the same takeoff.

Why: add a run to an existing takeoff without creating a duplicate.

  1. Select the takeoff in the tree (or press Sheet to pick from those measured on this sheet; > and < step through the neighbors).
  2. Press Space: the status shows Mode: Record <name>.
  3. Draw with the tool you need: all measurements go into this takeoff; the sheet dot does not apply.
  4. Press Space again to stop. A tool button instead of Record creates a new takeoff.

Result: a new section under the takeoff in the tree, Total went up. Props opens the properties of the active takeoff (name, color, symbol; for a Joist Area, spacing and direction), Find shows it in the tree.

Tips

  • Right-click on a takeoff > Set Active Target makes it active without starting a recording: the color and symbol for drawing, Total, and its measurements are highlighted on the sheet. On a takeoff that is already active the item is called Active Target. While another takeoff is in Record you cannot switch: status Record stays on <name>.
  • Right-click on a measurement on the sheet > Takeoff Properties... opens the properties of its takeoff without hunting for it in the tree; the next item, Section Properties... (Count Properties... for a Count), edits the name and note of just this section.

docs.title: How to copy measurements to another sheet or building
docs.text:
Demo: Ctrl+C on one sheet, Ctrl+V on another, New takeoffs picked in the Paste Measurements window. Same takeoffs adds the measurements to the same takeoffs, New takeoffs creates copies of the takeoffs. The Root: line shows the target building.

Why: do not draw identical floors or buildings a second time.

  1. Press E, select the measurements on the sheet (with a box or Ctrl+A), Ctrl+C.
  2. Open the target sheet (another floor or another building) and press Ctrl+V.
  3. In the Paste Measurements dialog pick: Same takeoffs - the measurements are added to the source takeoffs (usually not what you want for another building); New takeoffs - copies of the takeoffs are created with the same names and properties.
  4. Read the Root: line (green dot or root) and check the tree.

Result: with New takeoffs the copies sit in the same folder as the source, but in the target building (A/sqfts to B/sqfts, A/framing/2nd floor framing/details to B/framing/2nd floor framing/details). On a sheet with a different dot of the same row only the floor changes: framing/2nd floor framing/posts becomes framing/3rd floor framing/posts. The target building is taken in this order: the green dot, otherwise the root, otherwise the sheet's building by its dot. Folder mirroring is turned off with the Copies keep their source folders checkbox in Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing. Copying a whole building: Multiple buildings.

Tips

  • In the tree Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V copy and move takeoffs and folders, Ctrl+D duplicates, dragging moves. A move keeps the measurements, color, symbol and legend order; deleting and creating again loses them.

docs.title: How to hide a takeoff on a sheet
docs.text:
Demo: H hides the selected takeoff on the sheet, the visibility dot under the sheet in Pages brings it back.

Why: get finished work out of the way while checking, hide another building before the PDF.

  1. Select a segment on the sheet or a row (rows, a folder) in Takeoffs.
  2. Press H: status Hidden N whole takeoff(s); the takeoff is hidden only on the current sheet, a folder hides all its takeoffs on it.
  3. To bring it back, click the visibility dot on the takeoff under the sheet in the Pages tree (Visible on <sheet>: <takeoff>): H only hides, it does not toggle.

Result: hidden items are not drawn and not printed in the PDF: this is how a separate PDF per building is prepared (PDF and delivery).

Key What it does H hide on the current sheet the takeoffs of the selected segments or tree rows Shift+H Highlighter tool (marker markup) Dot on the sheet in Pages hide or show all measurements on the sheet Hide / Show All Takeoffs a palette command with no default key

docs.title: How to check totals: Total, Estimating, search
docs.text:
All takeoffs in one table: checking totals before Excel.

Why: make sure the numbers and names are ready for Excel.

  1. Select a takeoff: Total in the active takeoff line and Takeoff: in the status show the quantity.
  2. Open the Estimating tab: a table of all takeoffs with totals, units and price (Set Unit Price in the takeoff right-click menu); the Open button pops it out into a separate window.
  3. Press Delete Empty: takeoffs with no measurements are deleted (Ctrl+Z brings them back as a batch).
  4. Find a building or branch with the folder search, a takeoff or measurement with the takeoff search: what is found expands in the tree.

Result: no empty rows in Estimating, totals match what you expect; you can move on to export to Excel. The Templates tab (tree and takeoff presets) is hardly needed in E-Wood work: Other.

In the Estimating header: a filter field (by takeoff, section, sheet, note), the Sheet checkbox (only measurements of the open sheet), Open (table in a separate window), Select, Page, Props (same as the menu items below). Rows come in two kinds: the whole takeoff and its section.

Right-click on an Estimating row What it does Go to Page (Go to First Page with several rows) open the measurement's sheet and select the rows' measurements Select on Canvas (Select N on Canvas) select the measurements of the chosen rows on the sheet; the sheet of the first row opens by itself Section Properties... (Count Properties... for a Count) on a section row, the section name and note; on a takeoff row, the takeoff properties window; with several rows the item is called Measurement Properties... and is disabled Rename Section, Delete Section rename or delete a section, only on a section row; with several rows Rename Measurement and Delete Measurement are disabled

docs.title: Merge, Split, Break in brief
docs.text: Merge (Ctrl+M) combines several takeoffs into one with all their sections, Split (Ctrl+Shift+M) divides a takeoff by sections or by sheets, Break (Ctrl+Shift+B) cuts a Line into segments, Ends places a Count at the ends. Undo: Ctrl+Z in the tree or right-click Undo Takeoff Merge / Split. Details: Editing and snaps.

docs.title: How to change color, price or note for many takeoffs at once
docs.text:
Why: one color per branch (for example all BW) or a shared note without editing each takeoff.

  1. Select takeoffs in the tree (Shift or Ctrl + click, a box) and right-click > Bulk Properties (N Items).... For a whole folder with subfolders: right-click on the folder > Bulk Item Properties....
  2. Tick what you are changing: Apply color (palette swatch or color code), Apply unit price per <unit> (only if all takeoffs are of one type and the Estimating module is on), Replace notes.
  3. Press OK: fields without a tick do not change.

Result: status Updated bulk properties for N takeoff item(s); all measurements of these takeoffs get the new color too.

docs.title: Folder properties: defaults for new takeoffs
docs.text:
Right-click on a folder > Folder Properties... opens the Takeoff Folder Properties window:

Field What it does Display name folder name (rename) Notes folder note, shown in the tooltip over the folder Default measurement type the type preselected in New Item for a takeoff in this folder Default name prefix default prefix for a new takeoff name Default unit price price of a new takeoff (only with the Estimating module) Default notes for new items the note a new takeoff gets Default color remembered and shown in the folder tooltip; the new takeoff color is still random

The values apply in subfolders too: the nearest folder up the tree with the field filled in wins. The tooltip over the folder shows them as a Default: ... line.

docs.title: Takeoff colors
docs.text:
A new takeoff gets a random color without gray, black and white; Split gives the split-off part a new color; the name bft is always gray (Settings > Takeoff Colors). Identical colors on neighboring takeoffs make the legend unreadable: change them in Props or right-click Properties..., many at once through Bulk Properties. Right-click on a folder > Random Colors for Items gives all takeoffs of the folder and subfolders different palette colors in one click.

The size of Count symbols and the line weight on screen are set on the Viewport ribbon, LINES & AREA group: Point (tooltip Count marker size, 0.25-4, default 1) and Line (0.25-4); you can type a number in the field next to it and press Enter. This is only the look on screen and in separate sheet windows; the PDF has its own values: PDF Output > LINES & AREA (PDF).

docs.title: Tree menus: reference
docs.text:
Right-click on a takeoff: at the top Set Active Target and recording, below that editing, properties, Clipboard and Organize. Some items are visible only with the Advanced Takeoff Tools module.

Items marked "module" are visible while Advanced Takeoff Tools (or the named module) is on in Settings > Modules; Advanced Takeoff Tools, Takeoff Automation and Estimating are on by default (Settings). With several rows selected the labels show the count: Delete selected takeoffs, Move 3 Up.

Takeoff menu Item What it does Set Active Target (Active Target) make the takeoff active without recording (Record) New Section, for a Count Add Count start recording a new section into this takeoff on the open sheet Create Line Grid..., Trace Walls Inside Area... on an Area, module: a line grid over the area; walls along PDF lines inside the area (tracing) Joist > Use Area As Joists... (Joist Properties...), Refresh Regular Joists in All Area Segments, Start Extra Joists Mode (D), Set / Reset Joist Direction, Set Direction for All Areas on an Area, module: make the area a joist zone and its properties, recalculate regular joists in all sections, add extra joists, set the direction for one zone or for all zones of the takeoff at once (J Area) Create Count Points Along Lines..., Break Lines Into Segments, Count Points At Line Ends... on a Line, module (editing) Find Similar... on a Count, module: find the same symbols on the sheet Count Display Count point symbol 3D > Wall, Roof Base from Area 3D module, full version only (3D) Merge Selected Takeoffs..., Split Selected Takeoffs..., Undo Takeoff Merge / Split module (Merge and Split) Rename..., Delete item + measurements, Duplicate Item rename, delete with measurements (Ctrl+Z brings it back), a copy next to it with the same name Properties..., Bulk Properties..., Set Unit Price properties of one takeoff, of several at once (above), price (Estimating module) Clipboard > Copy Item, Cut Item, Paste Into Parent Folder copy, cut, paste into this takeoff's folder Organize > Move Up, Move Down order in the folder (Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down) Folder menu Item What it does New Folder, New Item new folder or takeoff inside Rename Folder..., Delete folder + children rename; delete with all contents (Ctrl+Z brings it back) Folder Properties... the Takeoff Folder Properties window (above) Bulk Item Properties..., Random Colors for Items properties or different colors for all takeoffs of the folder and subfolders Count Display, 3D Count symbol and 3D for the folder's takeoffs (3D in the full version only) Clipboard > Copy Folder, Cut Folder, Paste Into Folder, Duplicate Folder copying and moving a branch Organize > Auto Create Tree, Create Folders From Pages Takeoff Automation module: template roots and folders by sheets (tree) Organize > Move Up, Move Down, Sort Children A-Z, Sort Children Z-A folder order and sorting its contents Open in Explorer the folder on disk Section menu (a measurement under a takeoff) Item What it does Section Properties... (Count Properties... for a Count) section name and note Set Notes... (Set Notes for N Rows...) one note for several sections at once Count Display, Rename Section the section's Count symbol; section name Go to Page, Select on Canvas open the section's sheet; select its measurements on the sheet (Ctrl+Enter) Merge Segment..., Split Segment... (Split Count Section...) module: move the section to another takeoff or a new one Create Count Points Along Line..., Break Line Into Segments, Count Points At Line Ends... on a Line, module Create Line Grid..., Refresh Regular Joists in All Area Segments, Start Extra Joists Mode (D), Set / Reset Joist Direction, Set Direction for All Areas on an Area, module; Set Direction for All Areas takes this zone as the sample, you draw two points along the joists, and all zones of the takeoff get the direction Move Up, Move Down, Delete Section section order; delete the section Takeoffs root menu (empty spot in the tree)

Auto Create Tree and Create Folders From Pages (Takeoff Automation module), Paste Into Root, Sort Root A-Z, Sort Root Z-A, Open Takeoffs in Explorer.

docs.title: Palette commands for the tree
docs.text:
The Ctrl+Shift+P palette finds commands with no default key by name:

Command What it does Show Takeoffs Tab, Show Estimating Tab open the Takeoffs or Estimating tab on the right Show Takeoff Manager the Takeoff Manager tab in the mode bar (Managers) Refresh Takeoffs Tree reread the tree from the job folder Previous Takeoff Target, Next Takeoff Target like < and > (at least two takeoffs needed) Next Sheet Takeoff Target the next takeoff measured on the open sheet

docs.title: Measuring tools
docs.text:
Here: the bottom strip tools in order of how often they are used, their keys, step-by-step tasks, and what appears in the tree. Needed every day; topic rules (what exactly to trace) live on the pages of the "Work" section. Editing finished measurements, Cut, Merge, Split, Similar and the Snap, Ortho, Box snaps: Editing and snaps.

Row 1: tools and snap toggles. Row 2: Transform, sheet scale, Fit and zoom. On the right, the Value and Excel buttons.

docs.title: General rules
docs.text:
• A tool button (L, A, P, J, B, O) creates a new takeoff: the New Takeoff Item dialog opens with the name, color and a preview of the destination folder. To continue an existing takeoff: select it and press Space (Record).
  • Drawing: a click places a point, C finishes, Esc cancels an unfinished shape, Ctrl+Z or Backspace removes the last point. Snaps to the drawing and to the axes (F3, Ctrl+F3, F8, F9) are off in a regular measurement: Editing and snaps.
  • The status bar shows Mode: Record <takeoff> and Takeoff: <takeoff> (Route: W 1st): what you are drawing and where it will go.
  • Without a sheet scale, Line and Area are not created (scale).
  • The right mouse button always pans the sheet, the wheel zooms, F fits the sheet to the window.

docs.title: Tool table
docs.text:
Button Key What it does What appears in the tree Line L a polyline along a wall or detail centerline, linear feet a Line takeoff, LFT Area A a closed outline, square feet; F9 box by two corners an Area takeoff, SF Count P a point per symbol, pieces a Count takeoff, ea J Area J a joist area with direction and spacing a Joist Area takeoff: pieces and LFT Beam B beam length between supports, one point per beam a Count takeoff with the length in the name Open O a box around an opening, a point in the center a Count takeoff WxH Scale S sheet scale from a known dimension - Ruler R a tape dimension on the sheet with no quantity; the dot on the button (Ruler Sheet Visibility) hides the sheet's rulers markup Pitch - roof pitch rise:12 from two points; in the palette, the Pitch Tool command markup Select E select and edit measurements; Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V - Pan V pan the sheet - Cut, P Line, Similar, Repeat, Merge, Split, Break, Ends, Combine, Transform X, Ctrl+M, Ctrl+Shift+M, Ctrl+Shift+B editing finished measurements and takeoffs, finding similar symbols, segment series Editing and snaps Snap, PDF, Ortho, Box F3, Ctrl+F3, F8, F9 snaps: to your own points, to the drawing, to the axes, by two corners Editing and snaps

The Value and Excel buttons on the right write the selected takeoff into the open Excel workbook: Export to Excel. The Link to Excel button next to them keeps the takeoff's number in a cell and updates it by itself: Link to Excel. The Auto Link button on the DFL links all takeoffs at once whose numbers are already in the J:L list: Auto Link.

docs.title: How to draw a wall: Line
docs.text:
Demo: L, name ext 2x6 9.09, route line walls/1st floor walls, clicks along the exterior wall centerline and C. The takeoff ext 2x6 9.09: purpose, size, height in feet. Disconnected runs are separate measurements of one takeoff.

Why: linear feet of everything counted by length: walls, BW, shear walls, eve and rake, truss heel, parapets, ledger and rim in details. You need: a sheet with a scale and a W, F or S dot.

  1. Press L (the Line button).
  2. Type the name following the pattern <purpose> <size> <height>: ext 2x6 9.09, corr 2x6 11.7, eve 24 main, prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 par. Read the destination line and press OK.
  3. Click along the wall centerline corner by corner.
  4. Press C: the run is closed, Record is on.
  5. Draw the next run of the same takeoff; Space stops Record.
  6. For a new height or size press L again: that is a new takeoff, not a continuation.

Result: with the W dot the takeoff is in walls/<floor> floor walls, with F in framing/<floor> framing/details, with S in shear walls/<floor>/shear; names with eve, rake, prpt, trussheel, gable go to their own roots from any sheet. Total shows LFT.

Rules: Exterior, Bearing Walls, Shear Wall, Eve, Parapet, Truss Heel.

docs.title: How to take off an area: Area
docs.text:
Demo: A, the 1st floor outline and C; then X (Cut) with F9 (Box) cuts a bathroom out of the area. The outline follows the real floor boundary. Shafts are cut out with Cut, not with a second outline.

Why: SQFT of floors, balconies and porches, roof planes, gables, facade sheathing. You need: a sheet with a scale.

  1. Press A (the Area button), type the name 1st, blcny, rf 6, gable or siding/6" vertical, OK.
  2. Trace the outline corner by corner; C closes it. For a rectangle press F9 and click two corners.
  3. For a hole inside (shaft, open to below) press X and trace the cutout inside the area.
  4. For two overlapping areas, select both with the Select tool and choose Combine > Remove Overlap (editing).

Result: with the W dot the takeoff is in sqfts, with F in framing/<floor> framing/joists (for joists use J Area, not Area), with S in shear; Total in SF.

Rules: SQFT 1st, 2nd, Roof, Gable, Wall Sheathing.

docs.title: How to count pieces: Count
docs.text:
Demo: P, name HDU5 SB5x24, four points at the ends of shear walls; total 4 ea. One point per physical symbol. The takeoff's icon and color set it apart from its neighbors in the legend.

Why: posts, holdowns, hardware, anything counted in pieces.

  1. Press P (the Count button), type a name by mark or model: C4 20, HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2, MPB88Z S2.1, int H228 4.
  2. Pick the point icon in the Count display field (circle, cross, square, star, triangle, diamond, ring) and press OK. The app remembers the chosen icon and offers it for the next new Count.
  3. Click the center of each symbol; for a holdown, at the end of the shear wall.
  4. Missed: press E, drag the point, or Delete.
  5. To add points to a finished takeoff later, right-click it in Takeoffs and choose Add Count (for Line and Area this item is called New Section), or select it and press Space.

Result: with the W dot the takeoff is in walls/<floor> floor walls, with F in the root of framing/<floor> framing (posts and headers are later moved into posts and headers/ext|int), with S in shear walls/<floor>/holdowns; Total in pieces. In the Templates panel the same Add Count item creates not a takeoff but a Count preset in the template tree (Templates).

Rules: Post, Holdowns, Headers.

docs.title: How to count joists: J Area
docs.text:
Demo: J, name 2x10 16", floor framing outline and the joist direction line; the app counts pieces and linear feet. Joist area: outline, direction, spacing. The app counts pieces and lengths by itself.

Why: joist or rafter pieces and lengths by area without counting by hand. You need: a structural plan with the F dot and a scale.

  1. Press J (the J Area button), type the name <size or series> <spacing>: 2x8 16", 11 7/8 TJI 16", OK.
  2. Trace the area, C.
  3. Draw the direction line along the joists when the app asks; Shift keeps the direction orthogonal.
  4. Open Props and check the spacing, end joists, doubled joists. A hole in the area: X.
  5. For extra joists under walls, select the area and press D (Extra Joists).
  6. If needed, turn on the Detailed area label checkbox in Props (order and net lengths in a table on the sheet) and Move joist note (the table can be dragged with the Select tool, Ctrl+Z undoes the move; the position is saved and printed in the PDF).

Result: with the F dot the takeoff is in framing/<floor> framing/joists; Total shows pieces and LFT. A change of direction, spacing or material means a new area. A plain Area named 2x8 16" will not give joists in Excel.

docs.title: J Area right-click menu
docs.text:
These items are in the menu of the area on the sheet (some of them also in a separate sheet window), in the menu of a section under the takeoff, and in the Joist submenu of the takeoff in Takeoffs. Needs the Advanced Takeoff Tools module (on).

Item What it does When you need it Use Area As Joists... on a plain Area opens Takeoff Item Properties: the Joist layout checkbox turns the takeoff into a J Area (Joist type, O.C. spacing (in), pitch, length rounding). On a J Area the same item is called Joist Properties... the area was drawn with a plain Area, but joists need to be counted Set / Reset Joist Direction sets the direction of one area again: draw a two-point line along the joists the direction came out crosswise Set Direction for All Areas one direction line on the selected area sets the same direction for all areas of the takeoff on all sheets; status Joist direction ... applied to N areas all areas of the takeoff run the same way Refresh Regular Joists in All Area Segments carries the takeoff's common properties (type, spacing, Default far-edge joist) over to all areas and recalculates the regular joists; for areas without their own direction the app asks you to draw a line, one by one. End joists set on the sheet are kept after changing the spacing or type in Props Start Extra Joists Mode (D) the same as D: clicks inside the area place Extra Joists, D or Esc exits; available when the area's direction is set extra joists under walls Delete Nearest Extra Joist deletes the extra joist under the cursor (right-click exactly on its line); a miss gives the status Right-click directly on an Extra Joist to delete it., Ctrl+Z brings it back an unneeded Extra Joist

Rules: Joist.

docs.title: How to measure a beam: Beam
docs.text:
Demo: B, two beam ends, name FB1; the app adds the length to the name: FB1 52. Drawn from support to support, mark entered: the length was added to the name, already rounded.

Why: beams and headers with the order length in the name, which Excel reads.

  1. Press B (the Beam button) and draw from support to support.
  2. Type the mark or size in the dialog: FB1, (2) 1 3/4 x 18 LVL, ext H228; the app adds the order length in feet. Press OK.
  3. For a second identical beam, select the takeoff, press Space and place another point.
  4. For a series of beams in a row, press the Repeat arrow next to the Beam button: each beam is drawn with two points until Esc.

Result: a Count takeoff with a point on the beam and the length in the name (FB1 14), with the F dot in framing/<floor> framing/beams. The tool does the rounding: up to 8' it rounds up to a whole foot, over 8' up to an even number (8.3 gives 10, 13.2 gives 14). Do not add feet by hand, and do not put (n) together with n points.

Rules: Beam, Headers.

docs.title: How to count openings: Openings
docs.text:
Demo: O, a box around a window, name 4.0x4.0, the other windows with one click each; total 4 ea. A box around an opening on an elevation, a point in the center, the size name 4.3x7.8.

Why: windows, doors, garage doors with the size in the name, one point per opening.

  1. Press O (the Open button) and click two corners of a box around the opening.
  2. Type the name <width>x<height> in decimal feet with one decimal place: 4.3x7.8; suffix d door, gd garage door, lv louver. Different marks of the same size = one takeoff. Press OK.
  3. Repeat for each opening; showing up on both the plan and the elevation does not double it: one point per opening.

Result: a Count takeoff in openings from any sheet except U; the floor is the folder openings/<0|1|2|roof>, takeoffs are moved into it by hand.

Rules: Windows and Doors.

docs.title: Other tools and buttons
docs.text: Tool When and how Pitch roof pitch from a section: two points along the roof plane, the result rise:12 for the name rf 6. The Pitch button is in row 1 next to Ruler; in the Ctrl+Shift+P palette the same command is called Pitch Tool, it has no shortcut Ruler (R) checking the scale and dimensions; gives no quantity Ruler Sheet Visibility the small dot on the Ruler button: hides the rulers already on this sheet (new rulers stay visible); pressing again shows them all. Handy when rulers were placed only to check the scale and get in the way of reading the sheet Ruler screen thickness the Ruler slider on the Viewport ribbon, RULER / EXTRA group: on-screen thickness of ruler and Pitch lines, 0.5-6 px (default 1); a field next to it for an exact number Scale: and Set the scale field in row 2 of the strip: type 1/8" = 1'0" or 1:96 and press Set (or Enter). The scale is written to the current sheet, its measurements are recalculated; Presets gives typical values (scale) Reset Rotate Selection the button with a circular arrow to the right of the Rot slider: returns the slider to zero, the selection stays rotated; the next rotation counts from the new position (Transform) Expand all Pages nodes, Expand all Takeoffs nodes icons above the Pages and Takeoffs trees expand all folders, the icon next to them collapses. The same commands are on the icon strips at the edges of the sheet: Expand Pages Tree on the left, Expand Takeoffs Tree on the right Record (Space) continue the selected takeoff; Space again stops it (Record) Cut, P Line, Similar, Repeat, Combine, snaps Snap / PDF / Ortho / Box cutouts, points along a line, similar symbols, segment series, overlapping areas, snaps to the drawing: Editing and snaps

docs.title: OurPlanCore troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom, cause and what to do, for OurPlanCore 3.0. You need it when the app does not behave as expected: something disappeared, landed in the wrong place, is slow, does not save. Start with the table for your symptom.

docs.title: Sheets or takeoffs disappeared
docs.text: Symptom Cause What to do No measurements on the sheet, but they are in the tree the takeoff is hidden with the H key or with the sheet visibility dot the visibility toggle on the takeoff in Takeoffs or the visibility dot on the sheet in Pages (Show all takeoffs on <sheet>) A whole takeoff is gone after Merge it was merged into the surviving one Ctrl+Z with focus in Takeoffs or right-click Undo Takeoff Merge / Split; a copy is in AI_Context/takeoff-merge-trash A folder disappeared after an agent edit deleted through the Agent Bridge agent_bridge.py undo or the AI_Context/agent-trash folder A sheet vanished after sorting Sort A/S or D/Sec/WT moved it Open / Import > Undo Last Page Sort; search the sheets in Pages A sheet or takeoff deleted by accident Ctrl+Z in the same tree brings back the last deletion; Delete Empty is undone too Measurements are there, the legend is empty or wrong a different legend order or groups right-click the sheet: Reset Sheet Legend Order, Organize > Legend Groups... After a rollback to a .bak, crops and masks are gone an EXE older than 2.2.34 reads them as line markup and loses them on save do not save the job with the old EXE; go back to 3.0 and open a copy made before the save

docs.title: A takeoff landed in the wrong folder
docs.text:
Symptom Cause What to do No Route: in the status bar the sheet has no W/F/S/U dot set a dot under the Scale label or Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Route sheets without a dot now Route sheets without a dot now did not set a dot the sheet name has a tag from Skip tags (sec, el, d, rcp...), two level tags (1st 2nd), or u is not the last word set the dot by hand or rename the sheet The takeoff went into another building the green dot is on a different folder in the Takeoffs header click the red dot (root), or select the right building and the green dot eve or gable did not follow the sheet dot name rules beat the dot this is by design; change it in Settings > Takeoff Name Routing A Count on a W sheet landed in walls/... that is the default place holdowns on an S sheet or add a name rule A new takeoff is not created, a message about root the green dot points to a deleted folder click the red dot and pick the building again A pasted copy landed in a different subfolder the Copies keep their source folders checkbox turn it on or off in Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing, check the Root: line in the paste dialog

The rules explained: Takeoff routing; which sheet carries which kind of work and copies for shear: Split by sheets; several buildings: Multiple buildings.

docs.title: Slow
docs.text: Symptom Cause What to do Zoom stutters on a large blank sheet fixed in 2.2.39-2.2.42 update to 3.0; check the version in the window title A heavy PDF sheet takes long to open the raster is not prepared Sheet Manager: select, PNG and DPI, Prepare, then First On; or Display > Static image Slow after opening a job background page warm-up turn off Settings > Defaults > Warm all job pages in background (off by default) Switching sheets, the tree or Save lags various causes note exactly which operation and the version; the app log has Viewport slow frame lines with timings for slow frames Name over a whole set takes long one sheet in a 127-page set takes about 12 s to read this is normal; run it on a folder, not sheet by sheet

docs.title: Saving, opening, version
docs.text: Message or situation Cause What to do Saved in local recovery the .ourplan package is not updated yet click Save and wait for Save: Saved hh:mm:ss before copying the file Job Is Already Open / This job is owned by another OurPlanCore instance the job is open in a second window or on another computer (Workspace, full version) close the second window; in Workspace wait for the sync, do not open it at the same time Save failed after a sheet was moved to another folder fixed in 2.2.16 update The job sits in a cloud sync folder, Save or opening fights with it the sync client swaps or locks the file keep the working job in Desktop\OurPlanCore Jobs, copy it to the cloud after Save; on a message about an external change, save your version with Save As Corrupted metadata JSON Open / Import > Project Data Recovery...: an entry from the list, Retry reading or Restore from copy... The .ourplan itself cannot be read open the offered local recovery; Recovery does not repair a ZIP or PDF An interrupted sheet operation the .undo/operations log: Undo Last Page Operation Not enough space the unpacked job is bigger than the free space free up space outside jobs and recovery

docs.title: Which version is running
docs.text: The version is in the window title and in the Version ... line of the app log. Lite has a -lite tail on the number: OurPlanCore 3.0.x-lite - <job>; Lite sits in the shared Dropbox folder Office Folder\programs, with no previous version kept there. The full version is installed in the updates folder Desktop\updates\OurPlanCore, and its rollback is the .bak file next to the EXE (the file name carries the version, for example ourplancore.exe.2.2.42-....bak). The old separate Preview is no longer used. If a feature from What's new does not work, check the version in the title first: Lite is built separately, and its number can lag behind the full version.

docs.title: Lite: what is missing
docs.text: Symptom Cause What to do No >_ button, no XL strip, no AI Manager, 3D, Materials tabs Lite is open: it does not have these this is by design; the list: Lite and the full version A double click on an .ourplan does not open Lite Lite does not register itself as the app for .ourplan Ctrl+O and Open project... or Open project file..., or drag the file into the window After switching to Lite the settings look brand new Lite has its own profile %LOCALAPPDATA%\OurPlanCore Lite set up what you need again in Settings and click Save global default Name does not name a scanned sheet Lite has no OCR: the name is read only from the PDF text name the sheet by hand (F2)

docs.text:
The terminal and Workspace exist only in the full version; Agent Bridge is in Lite too (Lite and the full version).

Symptom Cause What to do The assistant writes context_unavailable fixed in 2.2.36 for sheets with crops and markup update; the Context button opens the file, it should contain state: open Run does not start the terminal no Git Bash or assistant shortcut install Git Bash, sign in to the CLI once; with Workspace no shortcut is needed The agent does not see the job the bridge is off or the job is read-only Settings > Agent Bridge > Enable local assistant access; agent_bridge.py sessions The agent answered with a timeout the outcome is unknown do not repeat the request with a new ID; inspect and check the tree Synchronization is running a sync is in progress wait and repeat Sync now or Share current saved project Job version conflict edited on two computers Settings > Workspace > Review conflicts: Keep this computer, Use server version or Open preserved files

Close it first. the pipeline changes the package only when the app is closed: close the window and repeat '<name>' has no leading project number (expected 'NN. Name') rename the job to NN. docs.title: Workspace: second computer
docs.text:
Full version only

OurPlanCore Lite has no Workspace: no Settings > Workspace section and no background sync. In Lite, a job is passed on as a copy of the saved .ourplan file (Jobs and saving). How the versions differ: Lite vs full version.

Here: the shared workspace of the full version: a private server, a second computer, shared jobs, presets and assistant conversations. You need it when working from a laptop. Importing one job into another is described in Jobs and saving, the pipeline console OurPlanCoreCli on the same page, the module list in Settings, Modules, the Job Tracker button in Managers.

docs.title: Workspace: a shared workspace
docs.text:
There is no screenshot of this section on purpose: it always shows the server address, the computer name and the names of current jobs.

What it is. A private server keeps shared rules and notes, agent skills, settings presets, selected saved jobs and archives of Claude and Codex conversations. The app works locally and syncs in the background; plan editing and the terminal do not wait for the server. The local folder by default is Documents\OurPlanCore Workspace; inside are knowledge, skills, profile, projects, conversations and runtime (a working projection for the assistants).

Group in Settings > Workspace Buttons and fields This computer Use shared workspace, device name, Local workspace folder, Automatic synchronization with an interval, categories (Claude / Codex skills and supporting scripts, Shared conversation archives), Save, Sync now, Import this setup, Open local folder, Server status Workspace server server address (stored on each device separately) Connect another computer Create code for another computer (a one-time code valid for 10 minutes), Connect this computer Projects Share current saved project, Open selected, Review conflicts, Apply shared presets Conversations Continue selected, Setup on this computer, Import a Claude / Codex conversation

docs.title: How to connect a second computer
docs.text:
What for: continue the same job from a laptop with the same rules and assistant conversations. Needed: the app is installed on both computers; the server address is known.

  1. On the main one, open Settings > Workspace, check Use shared workspace, connect the device and press Import this setup (the source folders do not change).
  2. Press Share current saved project for the .ourplan you need: the package goes to the server, later saves sync by themselves.
  3. On the second one, enter the server address and the code from Create code for another computer in Settings > Workspace, press Connect this computer. Rules and skills download; jobs and conversations on request.
  4. Press Projects > Open selected: the shared job is open. The terminals on the new computer need Git Bash and a one-time login to the assistant CLI (AI console).
  5. Before switching computers, press Ctrl+S, then Sync now and wait for the Synced status.

Result: both computers see one job, presets and conversations; status Synced in Settings > Workspace.

docs.title: Conflicts and limits
docs.text:
• A conflict keeps both versions: Review conflicts, then Keep this computer, Use server version or Open preserved files.
  • An open job is not replaced by the server version; a modified local file is not overwritten on download.
  • Deletion does not spread between devices. Cached jobs and knowledge are available offline.
  • Shared presets are applied only with the Apply shared presets button; job copies of settings still win; local presets are backed up first.
  • A conversation over 256 MB is skipped with a warning, the rest sync (3.0).
  • Keys, assistant logins and personal folders are not imported or synced.

OurPlanCore is an app for taking off quantities from PDF drawings: sheet, scale, measurement, Takeoffs tree, then export to the Excel DFL and PDF. Here: the window map, how this section is organized, and the path from an open job to delivery.

This section describes OurPlanCore Lite, the build estimators have: no AI models and no terminal, simpler and lighter. AI models, the terminal, 3D and the XL strip exist only in the full version; they are grouped in a separate menu block "AI, terminal and 3D (full version)" or marked on the page. Item-by-item differences: Lite vs full version.

  • Start with the course

  • Try it on the demo job

docs.title: Path: open a job, deliver the work
docs.text:
1. Open the job. Main > Open / Import > Open project... or the Open a recent job tile on the start screen. The job already comes with sheet names and W/F/S/U dots. Jobs
  2. Check the sheets. Expand 00. imported/Arch, open a floor plan, check Scale: in the status bar and the dot under the Scale header (Route: W 1st). Name unnamed sheets (Page N) by hand and set the scale with S. Copies for shear walls get the S dot by hand. Sheets, Split by sheets
  3. Takeoffs tree. More > Auto Tree creates the COM template roots; several buildings: a folder for each, the green dot on the current one. Tree, Multiple buildings, tree canon
  4. Measurements by scope. One scope per pass over the sheet: walls L, openings O, areas A, joists J, beams B, posts and holdowns P. Space continues the selected takeoff. Tools, takeoff order in the workflow
  5. Takeoff names. The name carries the numbers for Excel: ext 2x6 9.09, 4.3x7.8 d, rf 6, eve 24 main. A new takeoff goes into a folder by itself, based on the sheet dot and the name. Names and auto-routing, name formats
  6. Check. The Estimating tab, Total on a takeoff, the sheet legend (Organize > Sort Sheet Legend by Key), H hides finished work, Delete Empty removes empty takeoffs. Tree
  7. Excel. Open the building's workbook made from TemplateCom.xlsm (the templates folder in Dropbox), click a cell, select a takeoff or folder in Takeoffs and press Excel or Value at the bottom; a number that should follow the measurement goes in with the Link to Excel button; run the calculation from the J:L list with the E-Wood tab buttons in Excel. In the full version the XL strip does the same section by section (ALL, the LG legend). Export to Excel, DFL workbook, E-Wood tab
  8. PDF and delivery. Ctrl+S, hide what is not needed (H, Hide mask), PDF Output > Preview, then Main > Export: only sheets with measurements, a separate PDF per building. Then the processed xlsx and Changes.txt for a revision. PDF and delivery, delivery

docs.text: Here: typical values from delivered jobs, so you notice a number of the wrong order of magnitude. This is a sanity check, not a standard: a deviation means "open the detail, units and scope", not "adjust to the average".

docs.title: How to use it

1. Counted an item - compare it with what is typical for a similar building and scope.
  2. Out of range - check the units (LFT or pcs), spacing, unit multiplier, floor, double waste.
  3. Found the reason and it is a feature of the project - keep it, with a note if needed.
