docs.title: Notes in the DFL
docs.text:
Here: what kinds of notes the workbook has, where they go, how to write the text and when a note is not needed. A note = a row in column A with the prefix Important:, Note: or Comment: on a yellow fill, explaining a decision or an assumption that is not visible from the row itself.

Without a prefix or without yellow, the note gets lost

The worksheet is read by a program. A row without one of the three prefixes or without the yellow fill will not make it into the final file as a note, and a note above a header goes into the previous block. Full rule with diagrams: File format, notes.

Three note levels on a yellow fill and a continuation on a second row. At the bottom: rows that will not reach the final file.

docs.title: Where a note goes
docs.text:
Main note (header) Section or block note Where in the block between Detailed Material List and Description; a new one goes first under the header of its section (Roof Frame list, 1st Floor Walls), after the notes already there. A note about one group of rows inside a section: right above those rows Look Important: red bold on yellow A:F. A regular Note: red bold, no fill yellow fill A:F. Note: and Comment: black, bold in the reference books. Important: red bold, allowed here too About decisions for the whole building: construction type and FRT, sheathing and discrepancies between sheets, what is by others, preliminary set everything about this block: wall type per schedule, floor elevations and height, how the stud height is split, spacing and source sheet, limits of where it applies, assumptions with the word verify Order template ones first (Walls are panels by others, Roof and Floor Trusses are by others), then project ones as found

Choose the level by the cost of a mistake: Important: for global decisions with a big price difference, Note: for medium importance, Comment: for a small thing about one element. Table and examples.

  • A note about a specific block lives in that block, not in the header. The text must read on its own without the block: when the file is assembled, notes go into a common list, duplicates are removed, similar ones are merged. Not Note: No changes in this area, but Note: No changes for the 1st floor walls.
  • Text in A, columns B-F and G:H empty, only the A:H range. Do not make a separate worksheet for notes, and do not use Excel cell comments.
  • A reference in a local note points to the detail of its own wall type. A similar picture on a neighboring detail (for example, a shaft wall instead of an exterior wall) does not count: check the detail title.

docs.title: How to write the text
docs.text:
1. A natural phrase with a verb, in full words: joists use, roof uses, clips counted at. Abbreviations live in B and D, not in the note.
  2. One fact = one note. Two thoughts = two Note: rows. A long thought can continue on the next row without a prefix, with the same yellow fill.
  3. Length: target 80 characters, ceiling 100 (the note must fit in A:F). If it does not fit, use a second row, not telegraph style; do not merge cells, shrink the font or widen columns.
  4. The source is always a sheet or detail number: per S201, per 8/S3.0, ; see 4/A703. Not per page, not a PDF page number. No source: assumed; verify.
  5. Separator inside is ;, a period at the end. No =, arrows, dashes as separators, or parentheses with opinions. Ranges in words: levels 2 thru 6, S203 thru S206. A hyphen only inside a dimension 9'-1 1/8".
  6. Discrepancy between sheets: lead with the value that was counted, cite one authoritative sheet; the other side's sheet can be omitted: Note: Roof sheathing differ, 19/32" per struct S612, 15/32" per arch; counted 19/32"; verify.
  7. Optional only with a reason: a note with the condition above the rows, and the rows themselves in the option color (Options).
Abbreviation Written in the note as shtg, ply sheathing, plywood btm pl, o/, pre-eng Btm plate, over, pre-engineered @16", - S-203 at 16" o.c., per S203 A-351..A-355, 2-6 one sheet per A351, levels 2 thru 6

docs.title: Before and after
docs.text:
Pairs from a delivered job (anonymized). Left column: the draft; right column: what went to the client.

Do not write it like this Write it like this Floor joists 11 7/8" TJI @16" o.c. S-201/S-202, not 16" TGI on A-352 Note: Floor joists use 11-7/8" TJI at 16" o.c. per S201/S202. plus Note: Architectural sections show 16" joists; structural depth used. Roof pre-eng trusses @24" o.c. 19/32" ply, PSCL clips @16" - S-203 Note: Roof uses 19/32" exterior-rated plywood per S203; PSCL size matches. plus Note: PSCL clips counted at 16" max per S203; 6 per 4x8 sheet allowed. Ext shtg 15/32" exp 1 ply S-101 vs 5/8" on A-351..A-355 - took struct Note: Wall ply counted as 15/32" per S101; arch calls 5/8"; verify. Stairs are metal and concrete by others - see 4/A-703 Note: Metal and concrete stairs are by others; see 4/A703. Btm pl anchor Powers wedge 7" emb @32" o.c., BPS5/8-3 - 6,10/S-301 no note: the spec is in the row, B = 5/8" Ø x 7" emb., purpose E = for Ext Walls Note: Assumed all walls shall have (2) btm plates per page A5; verify Note: All walls assumed to have (2) btm plates per A5; verify.

docs.title: Fact in the row = no note
docs.text:
A note is needed for a decision or an assumption. If the fact is already visible in the row, the note duplicates it and goes stale at the first edit.

Fact Where it lives Anchor size and embedment B: 5/8" Ø x 7" emb.; E: for Ext Walls Stud height E of the stud row: 11' 8 3/8" SW mark, detail sheet E: SW-2, 8/S3.0 A floor repeats another section header: 4th Floor Framing List is the same as 3rd Floor Partial count E: partial count, no waste

A note must not argue with its row: by others in the note with a quantity filled in, or assumed 6" with 3-5/8" material in B, is a mistake.

docs.title: Spec cells and a reference without "per"
docs.text:
The spec cells to the right of the table are filled in from the PDF when each job is created, not before delivery (DFL: work areas).

Cells What Where on the drawings O3, O5 wall sheathing (ply/OSB), Zip wall types, typ. wall elevation, SW schedule on the S sheet O4, O6 WRB, Zip Tape wall types on A O8 subfloor section, floor types R3 ... R7 main roof, overframes, metal, flat, shingles typ. roof sheathing on the S sheet, section P, S next to them source sheet bare reference: S3.0, 8/S3.0, A3.0 S2.5, 2/S9
  • P and S hold only the reference, without per, without not shown; assumed and without a thickness.
  • The item does not exist in the building (no flat roof): leave per page, do not make anything up.
  • A discrepancy between arch and S goes into a main note right away: Note: Roof Sheathing differ, 15/32" Ply per 3/S3.0 and 1/2" OSB per A4-03; counted 1/2" CDX Ply. No spec: Note: Roof sheathing thickness is not specified; assumed 1/2" Ply; verify. The structural sheet wins.
  • 7/16" Zip on S and Zip R-3 in the wall type are one product, not a discrepancy: Note: Wall Sheathing 7/16" Zip R3 per 8/S3.0 A2-00.
  • E callout row by row in the detail/sheet format: 15/S311, 9/13/S311.

docs.title: Optional only with a reason
docs.text:
The client reviewer's comment: an item may be called optional only when it is entirely an assumption, and the reason is written next to it.

An option is defined by the row fill color, not by the word: without color the row goes into the main list as required. How to color it: Options and color.

  • Note: Optional framing for unspecified roof corridor frame; assumed 2x10; verify if truss.
  • Note: Verify spacing of 2x10 corridor joists; not indicated; assumed 16" o.c.
  • Panel building, stick variant of the walls: under the local note Note: Optional stick frame, if walls are not panels; verify.
  • Furring or rainscreen as an option: with a note on why it is there and which detail it comes from.

docs.title: Template notes and preliminary set
docs.text:
• Walls are panels by others is deleted if there is no panel in scope; do not touch Roof and Floor Trusses are by others without checking. Floor trusses are by others; verify goes in every Floor Framing List where the floor is framed with trusses.
  • Progress set without structural: a detailed main note that beams, posts, balcony, shear walls and heights are assumed; verify; windows as drawn; walls under concrete as optional stick with a note.
  • A library of ready-made wording. If the decision changes the price significantly, use the Important: prefix instead of Note::
Wording library (Standarts worksheet, put in your own sheet)

Headers

  • Note: Headers assumed (2)2x10 for short spans and (3)2x10 for long spans unless noted otherwise; verify.
  • Note: All headers at 2x6 walls are (3)2x10 and at 2x4 walls (2)2x10 per S0.2.
  • Note: Header sizes assumed per schedule S0.2; sizes may vary; verify.

Plates, studs, walls

  • Note: All walls assumed to have (2) btm plates per A5; verify.
  • Note: 3rd floor exterior walls have a single bottom plate per S5.2; differs from A5.
  • Note: Exterior walls assumed 2x6 and interior walls 2x4; verify.
  • Note: All posts assumed built-up studs; verify if solid.

Sheathing

  • Note: Roof sheathing differ, 5/8" CDX per arch A4.1, 1/2" per struct S0.1; counted 5/8"; verify.
  • Note: 7/16" Zip indicated on one sheet only; wall sheathing assumed 1/2" Ply; verify.
  • Note: 5/8" DensGlass over Zip sheathing at wall types A1 and A2 per A4.1.

By others

  • Important: All EWP products are by others.
  • Important: Floor trusses are by others; verify.
  • Note: Metal studs are by others.
  • Note: Aluminum railing materials are by others; verify components.
  • Note: Anchor bolts are Hilti by others.
  • Note: Pavers deck system is by others.

Framing assumed, budget only

  • Note: Framing plans are not provided; all framing assumed for budget only.
  • Note: Plans are preliminary; no sections, details or framing plans; budget only.
  • Note: Plans are not to scale; verify all lengths.
  • Important: Existing structure to remain; products listed for new construction only.

Decks, balcony, stairs

  • Note: Balcony joists assumed 2x10 P.T. per S2.1; A5.1 shows 2x8 P.T.; verify.
  • Note: Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify.
  • Note: Stairs assumed to have (4) 2x12 stringers; verify.
  • Note: Railing material assumed to match rear deck; verify.

Trims

  • Note: All exterior trim assumed primed vertical grain cedar per A6.1.
  • Note: No details provided; all trims assumed per elevations.
  • Note: Interior doors height assumed 6'8"; verify.

A note is needed only for an assumption: Note: Anchor bolt spacing is not indicated; assumed 36" o.c.; verify. (36" o.c. and 1/2" Ø are the template default, see Anchor Bolts)

docs.text:
Column Rule Example A label from the dictionary below; spacing, plies and purpose go in the label Studs Ext 16" o.c., Plates Ext (2) dbl top, Beam (3) Flush B size or model; P.T., FRT, grade after the size 2x6 P.T., 2x10 FRT, (2) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, 11-7/8" TJI 210, LUS210 Zmax C formula from G and H of its own block =EVEN(G33*H33*1.1) D LFT (not FT), SQ FT, 4x8, pcs, 50' rolls LFT E sheet or detail, SW mark, stud height, purpose; inches with the " sign 8/S3.0, SW-2, 9' 1 1/8", for Ext Walls G takeoff: SF for panels, LF for lumber, number of points for hardware 3760 H spacing in inches, plies, height 16, 2

docs.title: Names and auto-routing
docs.text:
This page covers how the app decides which folder a new takeoff goes into, by the sheet dot and by the name; how to read the Route: status; what to do when a takeoff lands in the wrong place. You need it when the tree "sorted itself" in an unexpected way. Which sheet carries which scope and how a plan set is laid out: Split by sheets and routing; name formats and the canonical folders: Takeoff tree and sheet names; rule settings: Routing: settings.

The building comes from the green dot, the floor and row come from the sheet dot, a word in the name can override the row. Example: sheet s201 2nd with the F dot, Beam tool, name FB1 8: framing/2nd floor framing/beams.

docs.title: Rule order
docs.text:
A new takeoff is created by a tool, New Item, or by pasting New takeoffs. The folder is picked as follows; the first matching rule wins:

  1. Building. The folder with the green dot; without one, the Takeoffs root (building root).
  2. U sheet. If the sheet has the U dot, the takeoff goes to <building>/units with any tool; the name is ignored.
  3. Rule by name or tool (Takeoff Name Routing): the Openings tool or a word in the name from the table below.
  4. W/F/S sheet dot: the sheet row and floor plus the tool give the folder (table).
  5. Sheet without a dot: the old classifier by name words and the floor from the sheet name (fallback).
  6. Nothing matched: the takeoff stays in the folder selected in the tree.

Record continues the selected takeoff and does not touch the rules. Renaming a finished takeoff does not move it; a manual move always wins.

docs.title: W/F/S/U sheet dot
docs.text:
The selected dot is shown in the status: Route: W 2nd, Route: F 1st, Route: U all floors.

Where a new takeoff from a 2nd floor sheet goes, paths from the building root:

Tool W dot F dot S dot U dot Line, P Line walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing/details shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Area, J Area sqfts framing/2nd floor framing/joists shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Count walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns units Beam walls/2nd floor walls framing/2nd floor framing/beams shear walls/2nd floor/shear units Openings openings (rule by tool) openings openings units

Floors: B (basement), 1-5, L (loft), R (roof); the folders basement foor walls, loft walls, roof framing and so on are set in the settings. A Count on an F sheet usually lands in the floor root framing/2nd floor framing. If a Count/Points name ends with a space and Post, the takeoff goes to framing/2nd floor framing/posts. A name ending in Stair on an F sheet goes to framing/2nd floor framing/stairs with any tool. Letter case does not matter; posts or stairs on another floor go to the matching folder of their own floor. Missing folders are created when you confirm in the dialog.

How dots are set and removed: Sheets, W/F/S/U dots. In short: a plus a floor gives W, s plus a floor gives F, a trailing u tag gives U; by hand, click the dot; for the whole job, Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Route sheets without a dot now.

When you paste New takeoffs, the copy goes into the same folder as the source, but in the target building; on a sheet with a different dot of the same row only the floor changes (copying).

docs.title: Rules by name and tool
docs.text:
These rules rank above the sheet dot (except on a U sheet): eve 24 main on a W sheet still goes to eves rakes/eves. Regular rules look for a substring, case-insensitive; Post and Stair need the word at the end of the name and an F sheet. The first match from the top wins.

Match Folder Openings tool openings gable stick gables/gable stick gable gables/gable trusses eve eves rakes/eves rake eves rakes/rakes prpt parapets trussheel trussheel Count/Points with Post at the end on an F sheet framing/<floor> framing/posts Stair at the end on an F sheet, any tool framing/<floor> framing/stairs

gable stick sits above gable, otherwise it would also go to trusses. The folder is spelled eves, not eaves. The rules are edited in Settings > Takeoff Name Routing (order, Preview name, global and per job): Routing: settings.

A substring catches extra names

The eve rule also fires on the name level 2, the rake rule on brake. Check the target line in the New Item dialog; if it caught one, rename before creating or move it afterwards.

docs.title: Fallback: sheet without a dot
docs.text:
When the sheet has no dot and the name does not hit any rule, the old classifier works. It splits the name into words (case-insensitive, 2x6 and 1st are whole words) and looks at the measurement type:

Type Words in the name Where Area base, basement, sqft, sf, sft, deck, porch, blcny, balcony, cant, cantilevered, flat, rf, roof or a floor 1st...8th sqfts Line wall, walls, corner, corners, ext, cor, corr, dem, demo, 2x4, 2x6, 2x8, half walls/<floor> floor walls; the floor comes from the sheet name or its folders (base, 1st...8th, floor 2, level 2); no floor found - the walls root with the status no sheet floor was detected Count - not routed, stays in the selected folder

Status after creation: Auto routed to Takeoffs/sqfts. or Auto routed to Takeoffs/walls/2nd floor walls.

dem and demo are the same thing to the app: demising

In takeoff names dem and demo count as wall words (demising) and are sorted as one group; in sheet names demo is the demolition tag (ad101 demo), and such sheets get no dot. Demolition takeoffs in a reconstruction job will not land in a separate folder through the word demo: make your own folder for them and select it before measuring (Reconstruction).

docs.title: How to fix a takeoff that landed in the wrong place
docs.text:
Why: put the takeoff back in the right folder without losing the measurements and color.

  1. Read the status after creation (Route:, Auto routed to ...) and look at the green dot: most often another building is active or the sheet has the wrong dot.
  2. Drag the takeoff to the right folder, or press Ctrl+X on it and right-click Paste Into Folder on the folder: the move keeps the measurements, color and legend order. No need to delete and redraw.
  3. Remove the cause: set the sheet dot, clear the green dot, rename the takeoff without the trap word.
  4. If the error repeats on every job, fix the rule in Settings (Sheet Takeoff Routing or Takeoff Name Routing) instead of moving takeoffs by hand every time.

Result: the takeoff is in place, Total did not change. A sheet copy for shear walls and other typical cases: Split by sheets.

docs.title: What the Excel macros read from the name
docs.text: The takeoff name is the input for the DFL workbook: a wall ext 2x6 9.09 gives the size and height, an opening 4.3x7.8 d the size and type, eve 24 main the overhang in inches, rf 6 the pitch, prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 three heights, details rim, ledger, bft the column M flags. Numbers in their own unit and in their own place: unit table and examples in Takeoff tree, numbers in the name; how the XL buttons read the tree: Export to Excel.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: A name that is exactly bft is always light gray: on creation, rename, random colors and copy (Settings > Takeoff Colors, Exact name, Fixed color). Other takeoffs get a random color without gray, black and white; Split gives the new part a new color.

docs.title: Sheet legend order
docs.text: By default the sheet legend is split into blocks by Takeoffs folders, in the order from Settings > Sheet Legend. For example, walls goes to Walls, framing/<floor>/posts to Posts, sqfts to SQFTs. Pages > sheet > Organize: Sort Sheet Legend Auto, A-Z, by Key (before space) (by the part of the name before the first space, numbers by value: A1 2x4, A1 2x6, A2 2x4, A10 2x4, B1 2x4), Reset Sheet Legend Order. To turn off the automatic blocks on just one sheet and keep manual groups, use the button next to the crop lock: Sheets: legend.

docs.title: Building types that come in
docs.text:
Type What to look at Hotel Porte cochere, storage and other buildings as separate branches and workbooks; PTAC openings; a multi-layer facade (ZIP-R by facade type): read through all layers Podium, Type III Everything in the plane of the exterior wall is FRT: studs, plates, headers, blocking, sheathing; wood walls below the podium are FRT too. No LVL/PSL/LSL in the plane of the exterior wall, do not write "LVL FRT". Walls under the podium are stick, not panels Residential over parking Parking: exterior-type gypsum and insulation per the assembly; above it, regular COM Condominiums, villas, several buildings Each building gets its own folder in Takeoffs and its own workbook; identical structure in twin buildings is not a mistake, but each workbook is complete Residential (single house, garage) Garage, porch, porte cochere have their own outlines and roof pitches; EWP per the specification, not out of habit

The construction type (Type III, Type V-A, V-B) comes from the Code Compliance Summary on the cover sheet; it is not a conditional note. Type V has no general FRT. FRT and FRTW are different designations, write them as in the project. More about FRT: Tips: FRT.

Client Metal studs WM Count and show Timberline Count and show Littleton Count and show EBS By others Probuild By others Triangle By others Interstate By others Bliffert By others

docs.title: What the client's reviewer asked for (October 2026)
docs.text:
Comments on delivered jobs, adopted as rules:

  • Wall panels. The only walls that are not panels: walls under a concrete slab, in an existing frame, short and irregular sloped walls, possibly exterior build-up. A wall next to CMU can easily be a panel; do not add optional stick because it is next to CMU. Do not automatically exclude exterior build-ups from panels: check the assembly.
  • Optional. "Be careful calling anything option, unless it totally assumed." Option rows get their own color (Options and color). An optional block must have a note with the reason: what is not specified, what was assumed, what to verify. Example: Optional framing for unspecified roof corridor frame (assumed 2x10 - verify if truss).
  • H-clips only for square edge, not for T&G.
  • New subfloor over an existing floor per detail: include it in full: old building, old floor, the whole floor gets covered.

docs.title: Common mistakes and how to avoid them
docs.text: Collected from reviews of delivered jobs over the last few months. No names or project numbers. Each mistake has three columns: what it looks like in the takeoff or the DFL, why it is bad, and how to do it right and where to read the rule. Before delivery, go through the checklist: it follows the same sections.

docs.title: Walls
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Wall type assigned as a group: a corridor recorded as demising, 2x6 interior as exterior. Different walls pull different plates, sheathing, bracing and FRT; quantities drift by hundreds of LF. Each wall run per the wall schedule of its own floor, not "looks like the one next to it". Split at a change of size, height or sheathed side. Exterior, Corridor, Demising Stud height taken as floor-to-floor or the ceiling elevation. Studs are longer than real by the depth of the floor framing and plates; the whole floor is overstated. Stud height = floor-to-floor minus subfloor minus floor framing depth minus plates; check against the section of each building. The wall name carries the height in decimal feet (ext 2x6 9.09). Exterior, Wall Sizing section, Tips: Studs P.T. bottom plate on a wood floor. Extra material and a wrong specification. P.T. only on concrete and masonry. A double bottom plate only where a detail shows it. Sill Plates Metal studs not counted and no note. The client cannot see that metal walls were excluded on purpose. If metal is by others, there is no row, but the Metal Studs by others note is required. If we count them, write the gauge (6" 18ga mtl). Client rules, Metal Tracks Shaft walls dropped as "panels by others"; a CMU elevator shaft recorded as shaftliner; trash chute missed. Shafts are almost never part of the panels, and shaft materials vary. Capture every shaft in the takeoff and determine the material from the plan and the wall type. Shaft, Wall Panels

docs.title: Openings
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Openings not deducted from sheathing, WRB, insulation and the anchor line; or deducted twice (from the plan and from the elevation). Sheathing and WRB overstated by dozens of sheets, or understated. Deduct once, on its own floor, from every row that needs it. Windows under 4' are not deducted. Windows and Doors, Wall Sheathing Window height taken as the head height, not the product height. The opening size in the name (5.8x5.9) and the deductions are wrong. Height = product size from the schedule; the head elevation on the elevation is not a size. Check whether it is the R.O. or the unit size. Windows and Doors A full storefront counted, and its door counted again as a separate opening. Double count. Storefront once; a door inside a composite opening is not a second opening. Windows and Doors

docs.title: Floor framing and beams
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way A beam mark missed on one of the floors where it is shown; PSL under beam ends not per schedule. Beams and supports in the DFL do not match the framing plan. Every mark on every floor where it is shown; posts and PSL per schedule. Beam, Post Hangers not at both ends of a joist, or counted from the purchased boards after cutting; no Zmax outside; Zmax bases but no hangers. Hardware does not match the number of connections. Hangers by assembly, both ends of each joist, model per detail, whole pieces only. Outside and on P.T. use Zmax; ties to trusses under sheathing without Zmax. Hangers Rim recorded as 1-3/4 LVL Rim with no such callout on the drawing; rim broken into 16' pieces. Made-up product, wrong length. By default 11-7/8" Rim or LSL Rim per the specification, in LF with a factor. LVL rim only when a deck or a corridor attaches to it. Rim Board, Tips: Rim A stair counted once when there are eight stairs; stringers from the (4) LVL template when there are two 2x12 flights. Quantity and material do not follow the project. Multiply by the number of stairs; stringers and their material per detail; assign a flight to one confirmed level. Stair Ledger and its fasteners taken from another floor, or no fastener row. Wrong length and screw count. Ledger on its own floor, fasteners as a separate row per detail. Framing details

docs.title: Roof
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Roof pitch not taken from the sheet (6:12 instead of 4:12), or pitch correction applied twice. Dozens of extra sheathing panels and clips. The number in the name rf 6 = pitch from the sheet; the correction sqrt(1+(rise/12)^2) exactly once. Garage, porch and porte cochere have their own outlines and pitches. Roof SQFT, Roof Sheathing Roof-to-wall ties not along all bearing lines; tie spacing not equal to truss spacing. Ties understated by half. Ties along each bearing line, spacing = truss spacing, on both sides if the detail says so. Roof Sheathing, Hangers Canopy counted again in eve/rake; not all eaves counted. Eaves and soffit doubled or understated. Canopy is not part of eve/rake; all eave runs with the overhang in inches in the name (eve 24 main). Eave, Canopy Attic draft stop missed or copied from the shear wall total. The most common miss; the area has nothing to do with shear. Draftstops Plan sheet or roof plan, attic profile from the section, an Area triangle for each line, a separate row. Gable, Demising

docs.title: Sheathing
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way H-clips with T&G or with decking thicker than the spec threshold; clips "4 per sheet" instead of by support spacing. Thousands of extra clips, or a shortage. Clips only for square edge, by support spacing and the model from the detail (PSCL at 16" = 6 per 4x8 sheet); each building has its own spacing. H-clips "Vapor Barrier" in the DFL instead of WRB; Tyvek with a fluid-applied barrier. Wrong product and wrong purpose of the layer. Call the exterior barrier WRB / Weather Barrier, product from the specification. Wall Sheathing, Exterior Wall Materials Sheathing name replaced with a template one: "LP FlameBlock 2-sided" became "7/16 OSB FRT", "5/8 EXT. SHEATHING" became Ply with no basis. The client gets the wrong product. Product name as in the project; resolve an arch vs S discrepancy with a note citing both sources and the value used. Wall Sheathing On a panel job both sides of a shear wall counted separately, although the exterior side is already in ext walls; P in the mark read as "two sides". Sheets doubled. On a panel job one side is in the panel; the SW needs only the required second side. P = perforated. Shear Wall

docs.title: SQFT areas
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Porch SQFT on the Front Page not filled in; balconies and porch not in their own rows. The building total is wrong. Balconies and porches as separate Front Page rows. Porch, Balcony Area drawn as a rectangle "to hit a known number", or balconies joined by a bridge into one polygon. The area cannot be checked, extra feet. Area along the real outline; one type can be built from several polygons in one takeoff. 1st-5th Floors

docs.title: Deck, porch, balconies
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way A balcony block without its own unit multiplier (900 SF instead of 60); a formula references the header of another block. Area and material are multiplied by the wrong thing. Each block has its own header with the number of instances, formulas from it. Count balcony types separately from the plan. Deck / Porch / Balcony frame Porches "mirrored" from balconies instead of counted separately; the porch has no ceiling joists, ledger and hangers. A porch is a different structure. Count the porch independently; framing not shown - note Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify. Deck / Porch / Balcony frame

docs.title: Shear walls and holdowns
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Holdown model not from the table of its own building and floor; straps mixed with anchors; one holdown through a wood floor instead of two. Wrong hardware in the wrong quantity. Model per the SW schedule of its own floor; to concrete one holdown as drawn, through a wood floor two (below and above); a holdown over a beam does not need a transfer below (client instruction). Shear Wall Anchors at one spacing for the whole building; wedge anchor replaced with Titen HD with no basis. Anchor spacing and type depend on the SW. Split by spacing and by SW, type from the detail; a double-sided SW gets double anchorage; plate washers per the table. Anchor Bolts G of a double-sided SW multiplied by 2 again. Sheets doubled. G = sum of the two faces, no extra x2; label double-sided SWs "both sides". Shear Wall

docs.title: Excel DFL and notes
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Notes in telegraph style (shtg, ply, o/), longer than the A:F width, "optional" with no reason, a note contradicts its row ("by others" with a quantity next to it). The client does not understand what was assumed and why. A natural phrase with a verb, up to 80 characters, per <sheet>, one fact = one note; an optional must have a reason. Standard notes A note without yellow fill or without the Important:, Note:, Comment: prefix; a note above the block header. The note does not make it into the final file or ends up in the previous block. Prefix, yellow fill, under the header of its own section. File format, notes A material row colored for personal use or in a revision; an option without color. A colored row counts as an option and drops out of the main list; an option without color counts as required material. Color only for options; orange for review; in a revision, color the changed cell or F. Options and color Section header without color or with text in B-F; deck without the word Frame; decking and railing directly under the framing. The app mixes materials or loses the block. Bold, colored, B-F empty. Headers, Groups A whole floor copied: formulas reference the header of another floor or block; detail labels left over from the old place. Quantities are calculated from someone else's inputs. Formulas only from the block's own inputs; after copying, check the first row of each section and the labels. Formulas, Checklist An area measured in OurPlanCore did not make it to Excel or was not updated after an edit. The DFL does not match the takeoff. After every takeoff change, update the number in the DFL; before delivery, check the key G values against the tree. Checklist Unit FT instead of LFT; the label does not match the calculation (Plate (2) for a single plate, Posts (3) for two). Format not per template, the client reads it wrong. In D: LFT for lumber, pcs for hardware, SF for panels; the label = what the formula calculates. Takeoff item labels

docs.title: Sheets and tree in OurPlanCore
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way Scale taken from the sheet label (1/8") while the sheet is printed at 3/16"; a sheet with several scales left with one. All lengths and areas on the sheet are wrong. Check the scale against a known dimension and grid lines; calibrate a sheet with several scales by zone. Takeoff tree, OurPlanCore: getting started Joists drawn as a plain Area named 2x8 16"; a beam or an opening entered as a plain Count. The export cannot see direction, spacing and lengths. Joists only with J Area, beams with Beam, openings with Openings. Joist, Beam All takeoffs in one color and one icon; the f tag added to a takeoff plan; the sheet tag not last (1st overall). The legend is unreadable, the W/F/S/U point is not set. Each new takeoff gets its own Color, point takeoffs their own CountSymbol. Sheet name a101 1st, tag at the end, f only for the foundation. Takeoff tree

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text: What it looks like Why it is bad The right way The PDF has every sheet of the set (hundreds of pages), or several buildings in one file. The client hunts for takeoffs among empty sheets. Export only sheets with takeoffs; each building gets its own PDF. Workflow Processed xlsx older than the working xlsm; notes or rows missing in the xlsx. The client gets the wrong version. Make the processed file after the last edit and check it against the xlsm. Workflow A revision has no Changes.txt, or an open comment is recorded as fixed. The client does not know what changed. Changes and Open items sections, in English, per <sheet>; anything unresolved only in Open items. Workflow The project dragged on, and the owner learned about it on the delivery day. The deadline slips without warning. As soon as you see the deadline slipping, report it right away, not at the end.

docs.title: What is NOT a mistake
docs.text:
Do not flag in a review:

  • checked in column G.
  • An empty G for a single porch.
  • A cut list where there are fewer boards than pieces.
  • The same structure in twin buildings.
  • Template defaults on a panel job with no structural info.

docs.title: How to use the KB
docs.text:
This knowledge base is the estimator's working memory: open a page, check the rule, apply it in OurPlanCore or in the Excel DFL. This page explains briefly how the KB is organized and how to read its pages.

Everything described in the KB is done in this window: sheets (Pages) on the left, the drawing in the center, the takeoff tree (Takeoffs) on the right. Panel names in the KB text match the labels on screen.

docs.title: Site sections
docs.text:
Tab What is there When to open it Start Workflow, takeoff tree and sheet names, pre-delivery check, client rules, common mistakes On day one and before every delivery OurPlanCore The app: getting started, interface and tools, takeoff names and sheet dots, shortcuts, troubleshooting, what's new When you are not sure which button or key does something Work Topic pages for each framing element, in the order you take them off: job types, walls, openings, floor framing, roof, sheathing, areas, deck, trim During takeoff: open the element, check how to count it and how to name it Reference Tips and key rules, hangers, hardware, formulas and factors, standard notes, DFL row names When filling the Excel workbook and when you are unsure about a rule

The "Work" menu follows the takeoff order: go down the list top to bottom and you skip nothing. It is a checklist, not a classification.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Ctrl+K opens search. Search by the English term from the drawing: rim, truss heel, holdown, prpt, draft stop. Russian words are found too, but drawing terms in the KB are always English, so they give more precise results.

docs.title: How to read a topic page
docs.text:
Pages in the "Work" section follow one template. If you need just one answer, go straight to the right section:

Page section Question it answers Picture at the top What it looks like on the drawing or in the structure What it is How the element differs from its neighbor (Sill Plate is not Btm Plate) Where to find it in the drawings Which sheet gives the dimension, mark, specification How to measure in OurPlanCore Tool (Line, Area, Count, J Area, Beam, Openings), unit, what to trace, on a sheet with which point W/F/S/U How to name it in the tree and the DFL row Takeoff name in Takeoffs, row in Excel, unit, formula or factor Common mistakes What has already been found in reviews, plus a link to the general list Example A piece of the tree or the DFL, 3-6 rows See also Related pages

Drawing terms in the text are English (Joist, Rim Board, FRT). Copy takeoff names and DFL row names exactly as written: Excel macros read them.

docs.title: Source priority
docs.text:
1. Drawings and specifications of the current project.
  2. Structural details and schedules.
  3. Arch plans, wall types, assemblies, RCP, energy notes.
  4. Client and job type rules from this KB: Client rules.
  5. Tips and key rules and topic pages.

If a KB rule contradicts the drawing, the drawing wins. Do not hide the discrepancy: write a note in the DFL with both sources and the value you used (how to format it).

docs.title: If there is no rule
docs.text:
1. Make sure it really is missing: search by the English term and by a synonym (eave and eve, holdown and HDU, WRB and Tyvek).
  2. Check Tips and key rules and Common mistakes: many decisions are written there as "mistake and the right way".
  3. Not there either: decide from the drawing, record it with an assumed; verify note with the sheet number, and flag the question for the owner. A decision the owner confirms later goes onto the topic page.

How to make changes to the KB itself is described on the editor page: Updating the KB.

docs.title: Images and diagrams
docs.text: Templates for inserting images and diagrams consistently. This is an estimator's cheat sheet - there will be a lot of visuals, so we keep all inserts in one style.

docs.title: Where to put files
docs.text:
docs/
└── assets/
    └── images/
        ├── walls/
        │   ├── exterior-2x6-section.png
        │   └── ...
        ├── framing/
        ├── roof/
        └── hangers/
  • Folder layout = wiki section, so it does not turn into a dump.
  • File names: Latin letters, lowercase, hyphens (exterior-2x6-section.png).
  • PNG/SVG for diagrams, JPG/WEBP for photos. Over 500 KB - compress if possible.

docs.title: One image with a caption
docs.text:
<figure markdown>
  ![Wall section, exterior 2×6](../assets/images/walls/exterior-2x6-section.png)
  <figcaption markdown="span">Exterior 2×6 wall - typical section</figcaption>
</figure>
This is what figure + figcaption looks like.

Text part: rules, bullets, tables.

</figure>

</div>

docs.title: Formatting rules
docs.text:
• Every diagram gets a short caption (what it is, where to look, which project).
  • If the diagram is from a specific project, add the project number to the caption and do not publish private parts (client names, prices, personal data).
  • Do not insert screenshots with an "Email/UID/Password" field - crop to the content.
  • Do not insert large PDFs as an image - a separate page with pdf.js or a link to the raw file is better.

docs.title: Maintaining the knowledge base
docs.text: This page describes how the KB site is maintained. Checked October 17, 2026 (OurPlanCore 3.0.0). The order of checking and delivering a project is in the QA checklist.

docs.title: Corrections from readers
docs.text: Readers send corrections through the suggestion page, no sign-up needed. The form sends them to a server; the receiver and the update procedure are described in tools/feedback-server/README.md. Corrections are visible only to the owner on a private page; its address is in the same file. Only the owner puts them on the site.

docs.title: Where to update the app description
docs.text:
• Overview, window map and the path to delivery: OurPlanCore 3.0.
  • The section describes OurPlanCore Lite, the build estimators have. What Lite lacks (AI models, terminal, 3D, Workspace) lives in the menu block "AI, terminal and 3D (full version)"; small things inside regular pages are marked with the words "full version only". List of differences: Lite vs full version; check it against docs/LITE_BUILD.md and Models/AppEdition.cs in the app source.
  • Each feature is described on one page of its level: "Every day" (jobs, sheets, tools, tree, Excel, PDF) or "Advanced".
  • Shortcuts: one canon.
  • Version changes: what's new.
  • 3.0 screenshots: docs/assets/images/ourplancore/v3/, taken on the demo job (Open sample job) in a separate app profile, with no client data.
  • Symbols that are not on the keyboard (long dash, arrows, guillemets) are caught by python tools/check_symbols.py; run it before committing.

One feature should have one detailed description. On other pages leave a short route to it. Do not copy the shortcut table into several places.

docs.title: What to check when updating
docs.text:
1. State the version and the date of the check.
  2. Check the command name, module availability, scope of action and how the result is saved against the current app.
  3. Separate finished features from plans and experimental modules.
  4. Check links and images. Keep the URLs of existing pages and useful anchors when reworking text.
  5. Check that the image matches its caption. Mark a screenshot of an old version as such; do not present it as a check of the new EXE.
  6. Check the final page on a wide and a narrow screen, the search and expandable instructions. Keep the previous version for rollback.

docs.title: Checking the local build
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs Material. From the root of its repository:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mkdocs build --strict
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8000

A successful local build does not yet mean the public site is updated. Publishing is a separate step, after checking the result and with the owner's permission. The exact publishing route and configuration are in the repository; an old record about stopped Actions should not be taken as the current state of CI.

docs.title: Working with sources
docs.text:
An estimating rule must have a context where it applies and a source. Statistics from past jobs help find an unusual value, but they do not replace the drawings and scope of the current project. A conflict between sources must be shown, not silently resolved.

The public KB includes anonymized rules, instructions and examples. The user's working paths, correspondence, access credentials, personal data and project materials stay internal unless permission is given.

docs.title: Pre-delivery check
docs.text: Checklists by section, in the order of the "Work" menu. Go through all of them before every delivery; plan 30-60 minutes for a full check, especially for items that come in large numbers. What exactly has been found in reviews and what it looks like: Common mistakes.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
• Scale checked against a dimension on every takeoff sheet, not against the label.
  • Arch, Structural, specs, schedules, wall types, RCP read before the bulk of the takeoff.
  • Project scope (Frame, Wall panels, EWP by others, NO metal, EXT) understood and reflected in the DFL header.
  • Each floor recorded separately; identical floors marked with a note, but materials still listed.
  • Each takeoff in the tree has its own color; names follow the tree canon.
  • Nothing doubled: no item ended up in two branches (a wall in both units and walls, a canopy in both eve and canopy).

docs.title: Walls
docs.text:
• The type of each wall run (ext, corridor, demising, unit, furring) taken from the wall schedule, not assigned as a group.
  • Stud height calculated from the section: floor-to-floor minus subfloor, floor framing, plates. Exact heights recorded (9'-1 1/8").
  • P.T. plate only on concrete and masonry; double bottom plate only where a detail shows it.
  • Bearing walls: plies and spacing from the stud schedule of their own floor; extra plies on a separate Extra row.
  • Corridor 2x4 staggered = two rows at 16", 2x6 plates.
  • Shaft walls recorded, material determined (CMU, shaftliner, wood); trash chute not missed.
  • Metal studs: counted with gauge, or a by others note per the client rule.
  • Wall panels: walls under concrete, inside an existing frame, short and sloped walls counted as stick; exterior build-up walls checked against the assembly and scope, not automatically excluded from panels; being next to CMU is no reason for optional stick.
  • FRT by construction type: Type III - everything in the plane of the exterior wall is FRT, no LVL/PSL there; if the exterior wall is FRT, then blocking and parapets are too.

docs.title: Openings
docs.text:
• One point per physical opening, size = the product from the schedule (not the head elevation).
  • Storefront once; a window and a door under one header = one opening.
  • Openings deducted from sheathing, WRB, insulation and the anchor line once, on their own floor; windows under 4' are not deducted.
  • Doors wider than 4' recorded as double; material and fire label stated.
  • Jamb blocking at windows and interior doors; blocking around windows with Zip R or insulation.

docs.title: Sheathing
docs.text:
• Every assembly read through all layers (ZIP-R by facade type, second gypsum layer, cover board, Z-girt).
  • Exterior sheathing per Arch and energy notes, interior per Structural; a discrepancy recorded with a note citing both sources.
  • Product name as in the project; the exterior barrier is called WRB, product from the specification.
  • Shear walls: number of sides per schedule; on a panel job one side is in the panel; P = perforated.
  • Floor-height FRT strips 2' or 4' around the perimeter of their own floor; box sheathing, truss heel, gables, parapet (inside = outside minus insulation board) counted.
  • Underlayment, sound membrane, 3/4 ply under bathrooms, new subfloor over existing (if the detail requires it).
  • Roof sheathing by pitch from the sheet, correction applied once; H-clips only for square edge, by support spacing and clip model.
  • The measured area made it to Excel and was updated after edits.

docs.title: Floor framing and roof
docs.text:
• Every beam mark on every floor; posts and PSL under beams per schedule; a post counted once, on the top floor it supports.
  • Joists only with J Area: direction, spacing, end joists, openings; lengths split in N / L pairs.
  • Rim: product per specification (11-7/8" Rim, LSL Rim), in LFT with a factor; rim at roof TJI too.
  • Hangers at both ends, by assembly, model per detail; Zmax outside and on P.T.; DHU only over stair, elevator and shaft walls.
  • Ties along all bearing lines, spacing = truss spacing; truss bracing over the whole area under the roof.
  • Ledger and fasteners on their own floor as separate rows; bolts, washers, nuts separately.
  • Blocking: two rows for walls 10' and taller; drywall ledger; kitchen 2x6 4 per 14', bath 1 per 14'.
  • Stairs multiplied by the number of stairs; stringers per detail.
  • Attic draft stop as a separate row; piggyback sleepers; flat roof curb blocking (2) 2x6 P.T. if nothing is specified; densdeck or cover board on a flat roof.
  • Eaves: all runs; canopy and porch not in eve/rake; dropped soffits per RCP.

docs.title: Areas, deck and porch
docs.text:
• Areas follow the real outline; balconies and porch as separate Front Page rows.
  • Each balcony and porch block has its own multiplier, formulas from its own header; porch counted independently of balconies.
  • Railing: as a system (composite) or by component (wood painted), not mixed; exterior posts P.T.
  • Porch: ceiling joists, ledger, hangers; framing not shown - note assumed; verify.

docs.title: Shear walls and holdowns
docs.text:
• Holdown model per the SW schedule of its own building and floor; one to concrete, two through a wood floor.
  • Anchors by spacing and by SW, type from the detail; washers per the table; double-sided SW = double anchorage.
  • A35 and other SW hardware only where notes or details require it.

docs.title: Excel DFL and notes
docs.text:
• Formulas from the block's own inputs; the first row of every new formula checked; 1.1 not applied twice.
  • Copied blocks: references point to their own floor, detail labels corrected.
  • Units: LFT for lumber, pcs for hardware, SF for panels; the label matches the calculation.
  • File formatting per the format checklist: headers, prefixes and yellow fill of notes, color-coded options, groups, types in F.
  • Notes: main ones in the header, local ones in their block; natural phrase, up to 80 characters, per <sheet>; every optional has a reason; a note does not contradict its row.
  • Template notes checked against scope (Walls are panels by others only with panel scope); zero and unused rows deleted.
  • Front Page: Customer, Date, Total pages, areas by floor, porch and balcony.
  • A different grade or material on a separate row (MSR, P.T., FRT).

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
• OurPlanCore job saved; PDF only of sheets with takeoffs, one per building.
  • Processed xlsx made after the last edit, notes and rows in place.
  • If Auto Link was used: Probable rows reviewed right away, wrong ones removed.
  • If the workbook has Link to Excel: no links in Pending, Conflict or Broken; before delivery to the client, links removed with Remove All Links from This Workbook....
  • Revision: Changes.txt filled in (Changes and Open items), every item confirmed by a sheet of the new set; nothing open presented as fixed.
  • Revision: "before / after" comparison with the previous delivery in Excel and PDF: what was added, what was removed, note wording.
  • The delivery folder is named like the client folder at intake; source drawing PDFs not sent.

docs.title: AI-assisted check
docs.text: A finished DFL can be given to an assistant for an extra cross-check: sections by scope, missing rows, quantities with questionable units. Accept only a specific report with sheet references and check it by hand; the manual checklist is still required.

docs.title: Page preview
docs.text: This page is a quick visual check: open it locally and look at readability, image cards, tables and links between rules. It does not replace the working sections of the wiki; it shows what a good topic page should look like.

docs.title: Quick route
docs.text:
• Joist

    Product family, spacing, hangers and EWP naming should be visible next to the images, not hidden in long text.

    Open Joist

  • Interior Trims

    Base, Crown, Casing and Door/Window Trim are best checked with rule cards: image + rule + what to do in the takeoff.

    Open Interior Trims

  • Exterior Wall

    Wall height, bottom plate, shear/draft-stop notes and material variants should read like a checklist.

    Open Exterior

  • QA

    Before output, check scope, drawings, formulas, waste, FRT, hangers and client-specific rules.

    Open QA checklist

docs.title: How a topic page should read
docs.text:
Block What it should contain What it is for What to count Specific takeoff items So there is no argument over whether an item is in scope Rules Short estimating rules To apply the rule quickly in PlanSwift/Excel Where to look Plan, schedule, notes, details So the estimator does not search for the source at random Visual check Image + rule + action note So the image is not a separate gallery with no purpose Check Final QA list To catch mistakes before output

Main rule

An image must be tied to an action: what to check on the drawings and how it changes the takeoff/output.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
Where Keys What it does Wiki search Ctrl+K / Cmd+K Quickly find a rule by a Russian or English term.

Where the full table is

The app's shortcuts and the key binding editor are described in one place: OurPlanCore keyboard shortcuts. On a topic page, leave a link to the right scenario, so that an old copy of the table does not show up in search as a current instruction.

docs.title: Visual check
docs.text: Hide 4 illustrated rules Joist product family Keep the exact series: TJI 230, RED, LPI, BCI. The output should show which product family was specified in the schedule. O.C. spacing Spacing is measured center-to-center, not from the edge of the lumber. Before the formula, check that the plan really shows 12 / 16 / 19.2 / 24 o.c. Interior Trim perimeter Base and Crown are counted by room perimeter, but exceptions have to be checked separately. Kitchen cabinets, closets, garage and the room schedule can change the count. Feedback rules Corrections from the boss should go into the exact topic page, and into reference if it is a general rule. That way the rule can be found later through search and does not get lost in the source map.

docs.title: Mini checklist before delivery
docs.text:
• The rule is short and usable.
  • Technical terms kept in English: Joist, Rim Board, FRT, Sheathing, Hangers.
  • Explanations in the page language (Russian on Russian pages).
  • The image has an action note: what to check and what to do.
  • There is a link to related pages.
  • No private data: emails, UID, salary, credentials, private links.

docs.title: Suggest a correction
docs.text:
Found a mistake, an outdated rule, or something missing? Write it here. No account needed. Only the site owner reads the corrections and decides what goes in.

You can attach up to 3 screenshots: with the button, by dragging a file onto the form, or by pasting a screen capture with Ctrl+V. The form shrinks large pictures before sending.

What is wrong How it should be (if you know) Your name (optional)

Screenshots (up to 3, optional)

Choose a file, drag it here, or press Ctrl+V Do not fill in Send

docs.title: Takeoff tree and sheet names
docs.text:
The canon: how the Takeoffs tree in OurPlanCore 3.0 is organized and how takeoffs and sheets are named. Names are read by Excel macros and by the app's routing, so the format matters down to the letter.

Four levels: building, work type, floor, takeoff. A single building has no building folder. Next to each branch: the tool and a sample name.

docs.title: Tree shape
docs.text:
• Takeoff path: <building>/<type>/<floor>/<takeoff>.
  • One building: the roots walls, sqfts, framing... sit directly in Takeoffs, do not create a Main folder. Several buildings: one folder per building (Main, Grge, Storage, CFS, BldngA); the active building is marked with a green dot, an inactive one with a red dot.
  • COM template roots (More > Auto Tree): units, sqfts, walls, gables, parapets, trussheel, openings, eves rakes, roof misc, framing, shear walls, trims, siding; plus BW for bearing walls. There is no separate sheathing root: sheathing is calculated from walls, areas, gables, parapets.
  • The old and archive folders are history only; do not measure from them.
  • Move a takeoff only with the move operation: it keeps the measurements, color, icon and legend order.
Green dot = active building: new takeoffs go into its folders. To switch, click the dot next to another building. The second half of the tree: framing by floor (beams, headers, posts, joists, details, stairs) and shear walls with holdowns. Sample names on the right.

docs.title: Branches and name formats
docs.text:
Branch Path Tool Takeoff name Examples Walls walls/<floor> floor walls/ Line <category> <size> <height in feet> ext 2x6 9.09, corr 2x6 11.7, dem 2x6 9.09, 2x4 9.09 (partition, no prefix), furr 2x4 9.0 Bearing walls BW/<floor>/ Line BW mark or type BW4-4-24, BW typical - The folder eves rakes/eves is spelled exactly like this, not eaves: routing works by this name. Put the mark (W1), the sheet and the R.O. of openings in the takeoff's Notes, not in the name.

docs.title: Numbers in the name
docs.text:
The name is the input for Excel. Each number is always in its own unit:

Takeoff Number Unit Wall, truss heel height decimal feet (9.09 = 9'-1 1/8") Opening product width x height feet, one decimal place Eve, rake overhang inches Roof rf 6 pitch, rise per 12 number Parapet prpt A B C outside height, inside height, top width; then the detail number feet Beam, header order length; the Beam tool rounds it itself: up to 8' rounds up to a whole foot, longer rounds to an even number feet Joists 16" spacing inches

docs.title: Colors and icons
docs.text: Each new takeoff gets its own Color; point takeoffs (Count) also get their own CountSymbol. Identical colors in neighboring takeoffs make the legend and the PDF unreadable. Split assigns a new color itself; gray is reserved for bft.

docs.title: Where a new takeoff goes
docs.text:
Under the Scale header each sheet has a grid of points: rows W (walls), F (framing), S (shear walls) by floor, and a U row (units). A new takeoff from a W 2nd sheet goes into walls/2nd floor walls (Line, Count) or into sqfts (Area); from an F 2nd sheet into framing/2nd floor framing/... by tool; from an S sheet into shear walls; from a U sheet into units with any tool. Names with eve, rake, gable, prpt, trussheel and the Openings tool go to their own roots from any sheet except U. Record continues the selected takeoff and ignores the point.

The point is set automatically from the sheet name. The status Route: W 2nd shows where a new takeoff will go.

How points work, name rules and settings: Takeoff names and sheet dots.

docs.title: Sheet names (Pages)
docs.text:
Format: lowercase, <sheet number> <tag>, the number without spaces or hyphens (S-101 = s101). The tag always goes last: overall 1st, north base, stair d.

What is on the sheet Tag Examples Floor plan 1st ... 8th, base (not bsmt), rf (not roof) a101 1st, s201 2nd, a105 rf, a1.7 1st 2nd (two floors) Foundation f (foundation only; do not add it to floor plans) s101 f Unit plan u (as the last tag; gives the U point) a3011 u, a301 common terrace u Unit finishes fin a302 fin Details; a section together with details d s501 d, stair d Sections sec, d sec, str sec, elev sec a3.01 sec Elevations; bathroom and kitchen elevations el, in el a201 el, a601 in el RCP rcp a8.01 1st rcp Notes, cover sheet, code/egress/loading plan n g001 n Schedules sch, dr sch, win sch a901 win sch Wall and floor types (WALL SCHEDULE on A = wt, FLOOR/ROOF SCHEDULE = ft) wt, ft a501 wt Demolition demo ad101 demo Title sheet t g000 t Revision duplicate (PR/ASI on top of the main set) package suffix a1.20 rcp pr5 Panel plans panel supplier number + wp + floor w1 wp ground

A legend or "SHEET NOTES" in the plan's title block does not make it n. A sheet from a separate PDF takes its number from the file name. Names within one folder are unique.

docs.title: Pages folders
docs.text:
--------others/        unused sheets under their own names: title, civil, landscape, MEP, notes
00. imported/          wt, ft and unclassified sheets go right here
  Arch/                A plans, elevations, roof (Arch/unlarged - enlarged plans)
  Struct/              S plans and notes (Struct/Shear - copies for shear walls)

  rcp/

Several buildings: a building folder with the same name as in Takeoffs. Revision: 01. old/ and 02. NEW SET <date>/ with the same layout inside.

docs.title: Sheet copies and scale
docs.text:
• A sheet copy is needed only for shear walls (S point one floor below), for a second level on the same sheet, for another building and for a new sheet set. Do not make copy folders for each takeoff type.
  • Check the scale against a dimension string and grid lines, not the sheet label: S sheets are sometimes labeled 1/8" when they are actually 3/16". A sheet with several scales is calibrated for the zone you need.
Detail codes for Excel (M flags)

A detail name in framing/.../details gives a flag in column M of the export, and the C_RimBoardBlockingHangers macro expands the flag into rows. How to write them: a doubled letter = x2 (rr, bb, hh16), a number = o.c. spacing (b48, h16, blt24), a space and a digit = group number (b 1, r 1).

Code What Default r / rr Rim board rb Ribbon board l / ll Ledger b / bb, b48 Blocking, blocking at spacing 48" o.c. bd Blocking for Drywall bft Bracing for Trusses h16 / hh16 Hangers 16" o.c. s / ss / s16 Screws 16" o.c. t / tt / t16 Ties 16" o.c. blt / blt24 Anchor Bolts + Washers + Nuts (three rows) spacing and size per detail

Material override at the end of the selection: r = 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, r 1 = 1 3/4 x 18 LVL, b = 11 7/8 TJI 230, b48 = 2x10, h16 = ITS2.56/9.5, l = 2x12 P.T., l 1 = 2x10. More: Rim Board, Blocking, Anchor Bolts, Hangers.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The path of a project from the client folder to delivery. This is the general route; how to measure each element is on the topic pages of the "Work" section, how to fill Excel is in the Reference.

Eight steps. Gray steps are done by automation at intake, green ones by the estimator, blue is delivery. A revision adds Changes.txt.

Golden rule of takeoff

Do not jump around the drawing. Take one scope (for example, exterior walls) and scan the whole sheet left to right, top to bottom, before moving on to the next one. That way you do not lose corners, dead-end areas and small wall pieces at stairs and shafts.

One pass = one strip across the full width of the sheet, then the next one below. One scope per pass.

docs.title: 1. The project arrives
docs.text:
1. The project sits in the client folder (Dropbox) under the client's name: <queue number>. <Project>_<Client>_<tags>. You will need this name at delivery: the folder in .Finished has the same name.
  2. The project gets an internal running number and a folder <N>. <name> with the drawings, Excel and the OurPlanCore job. The number is not made up: it is the next one in the job log.
  3. Scope is read from the tags on the client folder: Frame, Frame. Wall panels, Frame. EWP by others, Revision, NO metal, EXT. What each tag changes: Client rules.
  4. Revision: the folder has Revision, rev, review or an email with the changes. The Excel base is a copy of the previous delivery; the new and old sheet sets are kept separately.

docs.title: 2. PDF analysis
docs.text:
1. Cover sheet and sheet index: how many buildings, which sheet series (A, S, G), which sheets are takeoff sheets (floor plans, roof plan, framing plans).
  2. Wall sheathing and insulation come from the wall types sheet; roofing from the structural roof framing and the section; subfloor from the section. A conflict between arch and S is resolved right away: structural wins, the discrepancy is recorded with a note ... per <sheet>; verify.
  3. Scales: plans are usually 1/8", unit plans 1/4", sections 3/8", details NTS. The scale label on the sheet is not proof; check the scale against a dimension on the sheet.
  4. Raster set (scan): auto-names and auto-scale will not work, sheets are named by hand from the title block.

docs.title: 3. The job in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Sheets are sorted into folders 00. imported/Arch, Struct, sections, details ...; unused ones go to --------others. Sheet name a101 1st.
  1. Sheets. Name is <sheet number> <tag> in lowercase: a101 1st, s201 2nd, s101 f, a105 rf, a3.01 sec. The tag goes at the end, f only for the foundation. Full table of tags and folders: Takeoff tree and sheet names.
  2. Scale. Set Scale from a known dimension, check with Ruler against a second dimension. A sheet with several scales is calibrated by zone.
  3. W/F/S/U points. Under the Scale header each sheet has a point: W (walls) on architectural plans, F (framing) on structural, S (shear) on copies for shear, U on unit plans. The point decides which building folder a new takeoff goes into. It is set automatically from the sheet name; for an older job use Settings > Sheet Takeoff Routing > Route sheets without a dot now. How it works: Takeoff names and sheet dots.
  4. Takeoffs tree. More > Auto Tree creates the COM template roots (walls, sqfts, framing, openings, shear walls, units...). Several buildings: one folder per building (Main, Grge); the active building is marked with a green dot.
  5. Excel per building. Each building gets its own workbook from TemplateCom. Right away fill in the main header notes (template ones first, then project ones) and the spec cells for wall, floor and roof sheathing with a reference to the sheet. How to format them: Standard notes.

docs.title: 4. Takeoffs in the order of the "Work" menu
docs.text:
COM template roots. Each takeoff goes into <building>/<type>/<floor>/<takeoff>; the name carries the numbers for Excel.

Go down the "Work" menu top to bottom, one scope per pass over the sheet:

Step What Tool Where it goes 1 Walls: ext, corridor, demising, unit, basement, BW Line walls/<floor> floor walls, BW/<floor>, units 2 Openings Openings openings/<floor> 3 Sheathing, gables, truss heel, parapets, box Area, Line gables, trussheel, parapets (walls are calculated from walls x height) 4 Floor and roof areas Area sqfts (1st, blcny, rf 6) 5 Floor framing: posts, beams, headers, joists, details, stairs Count, Beam, J Area, Line framing/<floor> framing/... 6 Shear walls and holdowns Line, Count shear walls/<floor>/shear, .../holdowns 7 Eaves, roofing, eve/rake Line eves rakes/eves, eves rakes/rakes 8 Deck, porch, balconies Count by block type Balcony blocks, Porch blocks 9 Siding, trims (if in scope) Area, Line, Count siding, trims

Rules: each new takeoff gets its own color and its own point icon; Record continues an existing takeoff, pressing the tool again creates a new one; joists only with J Area, beams only with Beam, openings only with Openings. Name formats: Takeoff tree.

docs.title: 5. Excel DFL and notes
docs.text:
Full version of OurPlanCore: the XL strip buttons send tree branches into the open TemplateCom workbook section by section; ALL does everything in order. Lite does not have this strip.
  1. The building workbook is open, the DFL worksheet is active. In OurPlanCore Lite numbers go over with the Excel, Value, Link to Excel and Auto Link buttons, and the calculation from the J:L list is run with the E-Wood tab buttons in Excel. In the full version the XL strip sends takeoffs section by section (walls, sheathing, areas, openings, framing...) and runs the macros itself. Details: Export to Excel, Lite vs full version.
  2. Wall height lives in column E of the stud row (to 1/8"), units in D: LFT for lumber, pcs for hardware, SF for panels. Row names: DFL row names.
  3. Formulas only from the block's own inputs; check a new formula on the first row right away. Do not multiply by 1.1 a second time: Formulas.
  4. Notes: prefix Important:, Note: or Comment:, yellow fill, always under the header of their block. A natural phrase, up to 80 characters, per <sheet>, no =. Samples: Standard notes. Headers, color-coded options, groups and revision marks: File format.
  5. Balconies, porches, holdowns go in blocks, following delivered jobs: Deck / Porch / Balcony, Shear Wall.

docs.title: 6. Check
docs.text: A full check before delivery, especially for items that come in large numbers: nothing is doubled, every measured area made it to Excel, notes do not contradict the rows. Checklist by section: Pre-delivery check, list of known mistakes: Common mistakes. In OurPlanCore: Estimating, Total, sheet legend (Organize > Sort Sheet Legend by Key).

docs.title: 7. Export
docs.text:
PDF Output: Preview, then Export. Only sheets with visible takeoffs go into the file.
  1. PDF. Save the job (Ctrl+S). Hide what is not needed (H), collect details with Crop to Sheet. PDF Output > Preview, then Export. The PDF has only sheets with takeoffs; each building gets its own PDF (hide the branches of other buildings). Revision "new only": by the branches of the new sheet set.
  2. Processed xlsx. The working .xlsm is turned into an .xlsx with formulas converted to values and no links between workbooks. Excel must be closed for this. Check that notes and rows are in place and that the xlsx is not older than the working xlsm.
  3. Changes.txt - only for a revision, review or rework. In English, one line = one change, past tense, source per <sheet> or per <detail>/<sheet>. Anything unresolved goes only under Open items (the section is required, even with one line). No Russian text, no cells, no internal details. Small things are grouped into one line. The file name is exactly Changes.txt.
Changes.txt sample 
<Excel name without extension>

Changes
- Stair and trash shaft walls above the podium were changed from CMU to wood framing. The corresponding framing quantities were added.
- Ceiling blocking was added per A7.01.
Open items

- Revised structural drawings were not provided.

docs.title: 8. Delivery
docs.text:
1. The client folder .Finished\<name as at intake> gets: PDFs per building, the processed xlsx, and Changes.txt for a revision. Source drawing PDFs and internal files are not delivered.
  2. The folder must be named exactly like the Dropbox folder at intake.
  3. The job status is marked in the tracker; if the deadline slipped, say so in advance, not on the delivery day.

docs.title: Anchor Bolts
docs.text: Foundation corner: P.T. sill plate on sill seal, anchors through the board with a washer and nut. Three DFL rows: Anchor Bolts at the spacing from the anchorage schedule, Washers and Nuts by the number of bolts. Photo: hunker.com, source, found via Pinterest. An anchor bolt with washer and nut fastens the P.T. plate to concrete. Size, embedment and spacing come from the anchorage schedule and the SW schedule; if they are blank, use the template default (below).

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Anchors for the bottom plate on concrete or masonry, ledger fasteners for balconies and porches to the house, through bolts at beam-to-post connections. Each group is its own row: Anchor Bolts, Washers, Nuts. General rules for bolts and screws are on the Bolts page; holdown anchors are on Shear Wall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text:
Sheet What to take Sill and sole plate anchorage schedule (S0.x, S5xx) Diameter, length, embedment (emb), spacing, product (Titen HD, wedge anchor, cast-in J-bolt) by wall type Shear Wall Schedule Its own anchor spacing under each SW mark, often tighter than typical Balcony and porch ledger details (S3xx) Through bolts or screws, spacing, washers S general notes Hilti or another product by others, minimum embedment

Size, embedment and spacing come from the anchorage schedule. Schedule not found: use the template default (1/2" Ø emb., 36" o.c.), put assumed in E and the note Note: Anchor Bolts 1/2" Ø @ 36" o.c. assumed; verify.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: The anchor line length equals the LFT of walls on concrete on the same floor (walls/<floor>, F point for the foundation). Openings in this line (overhead doors, doors) are deducted once. Ledger: the ledger length from the balcony or porch block. Spacing and anchor type are not needed in the name; they live in the DFL.

docs.title: Default when the plans have no anchorage schedule
docs.text:
DFL template row (Foundation walls block):

DFL row B (spec) H (spacing) Formula C Anchor Bolts 36" o.c. 1/2" Ø emb. 36 =CEILING((G*12/36)*1.1, 2) Washer 36" o.c. per detail, usually 3x3 Square 36 same formula, one washer per bolt

G - length of walls on concrete. Shear walls get their own rows with their own spacing from the SW schedule; the default does not apply to them. If the sheets have an anchorage schedule or notes with a size, they win over the default.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
DFL row B (spec) Unit Formula Anchor Bolts 48" o.c. 1/2" Ø x 4" emb Titen HD pcs =CEILING(G*12/48,2), E = for Ext Walls Anchor Bolts 32" o.c. per SW schedule, same format pcs a separate row for each spacing Washers 3x3 or plain per detail pcs equal to anchors Nuts pcs equal to anchors Through Bolts (ledger, beam-to-post) 1/2" Ø per detail pcs spacing per detail, washers and nuts in their own rows

B format: diameter, length or embedment, product, in that order (5/8" Ø x 7" emb, 1/2" Ø x 4" emb Titen HD); general rules for writing hardware are in Hangers: how to write hardware in the DFL. The block of four rows (Blocking, Anchor Bolts, Washers, Nuts) is inserted by the B_BoltsAdd macro, see Excel macro hotkeys. Small hardware under 50 pieces is rounded up to an even number. Holdown anchors are counted in the holdowns block: DFL blocks.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• One anchor spacing for the whole building without the SW schedule.
  • Wedge anchor replaced with Titen HD with no basis in the detail.
  • Openings not deducted from the anchor line, or deducted twice.
  • Washers copied with the old spacing and not recalculated.
  • Hilti by others counted as ours; the note must stay.
  • All mistakes for the section: Deck, porch, balconies, Shear walls and holdowns.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Anchor Bolts 48" o.c.   1/2" Ø x 4" emb Titen HD   42  pcs   =CEILING(G*12/48,2)   for Ext Walls  S0.2
Anchor Bolts 32" o.c.   1/2" Ø x 4" emb Titen HD   18  pcs   SW1 per schedule       S502
Washers                 3x3                60  pcs   =C<bolts>
Nuts                                        60  pcs   =C<bolts>

docs.title: Balcony Trims
docs.text: Fascia and edge trim along the open sides of the balcony, soffit underneath, flashing at the wall. Counted only when trim is in scope.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The finish rows of a balcony block: fascia and edge trim around the perimeter, soffit underneath, post wrap, flashing at the wall. The full map of layers from frame to finish is on the canonical page Balcony build-up; the frame is on Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Balcony section A4xx, details A5xx Fascia, soffit (beadboard), flashing, post wrap: material and size Elevations Visible trims, color and profile, what is hidden by the railing Job scope Frame only: do not insert trim at all

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Lengths and areas come from the block size W x D and the multiplier G, as for railing. The soffit under the balcony is an Area along the real outline only when the outline is not a rectangle; W x D is usually enough.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
DFL row Material Unit Rule Balcony Trims / Fascia 1x10, 5/4x8 LFT open sides: =(W+2*D)*G Soffits at Balcony Beadboard SQ FT =W*D*G Post Wrap 1x8 LFT by post height x 4 sides Flashings at Wall Copper / drip edge LFT along the wall, =W*G

Size not specified: TBD in the material and the note Note: All trims to be verified. Scaled per elevations.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Balcony trims dissolved into the general Exterior Trims without their own row.
  • Frame rows (sleepers, joists) written into the trims block.
  • Trim inserted when the scope is Frame only.
  • All mistakes for the section: Deck, porch, balconies.
