docs.title: Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame
docs.text: Porch deck framing: P.T. ledger at the house wall, joists with hangers, rim around the perimeter, posts. Each element is its own row in the DFL. Photo: NPS Photo, public domain, source Framing plan: ledger to the building, joists and hangers, beam on posts, rim and blocking. Units: posts pcs, beam and joists LFT, hangers pcs.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The structural frame of open platforms: posts with base and cap, beams, ledger, box or rim, joists with hangers, blocking, sleepers, structural subfloor, stringers. A balcony sits at an upper-floor wall on posts or cantilevered; a porch is a covered entry with a roof and ceiling (ceiling joists); a deck is a platform near grade on posts. Finish (decking as a finish, soffit, trims, railing by type) lives on the Balcony build-up and Rails & Decking pages; this page covers only the structure.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text:
Sheet What to take Floor plans A1xx Balcony doors (tag), W x D size of each type, how many and on which floors S floor framing plans Deck joist callout (size, spacing), beam marks B1..B5, posts Sections A4xx and details S3xx/S6xx Ledger and its fasteners, post cap and base, hangers, End Joists, flush or dropped beam Post and hardware schedule (S6xx) Cap model by number of plies, base, through bolts Roof plan and porch section Porch roof, ceiling joists, ceiling (gypsum), whether there is framing at all

A door with no wood joist callout on the S plan usually means concrete or trusses under the balcony (a terrace over the garage). That is a separate block, not a copy of the wood one.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area: sqfts/blcny and sqfts/porch, Area tool along the real outline on the sheet with the W point. Do not join different balconies with a bridge; do not draw a rectangle to hit a known number.
  2. Blocks: one Count item per balcony type in the Balcony blocks folder (porch in Porch blocks), a point for every instance. Item name #4 Balcony 12.9x7.83 (2GZO x7), where x7 equals the number of points; the point Notes hold the unit tag, side and floor (2GZO S 2nd fl). The points go on copies of the plan sheets (a120 balcony), the working plans stay clean. The number of points equals the multiplier G in the block header in Excel.
  3. Counting instances: balcony doors on the plans multiplied by floors, checked against the deck joist callout on the S plans.
  4. Count porches separately from the plans, do not mirror them from the balconies: the number of blocks, sizes and porch count usually do not match the balconies.
  5. Connections with a detail number (5/S311) are counted as a Line item in framing/<floor>/details, one item per detail; see Framing details.
Count with points: one point for every balcony instance; the item name carries the type, size and number of instances. Balcony at the wall: ledger with screws, P.T. joists on Zmax hangers, end joist, beam on a post with a cap, decking and railing. Every callout is a block row in the DFL.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Block header: #N Upper Balcony List W' x D' <G> unit; porch #N Porch Framing List W' x D', A:B fill green 99CC00; a ground deck frame must have the words Deck and Frame or Framing. The group sits inside Framing; decking, railing and trims follow the frame under their own headers, notes go under the header: File format, groups. Zero rows and empty template rows are deleted. Full block content with formulas: DFL blocks.

Tree name DFL row Unit Formula or rule Balcony blocks/#1 Balcony 12x8 (x6) Posts 6x6 P.T. pcs 2 per balcony, =2*G; a corner balcony against two walls may carry 1 Post Bases ABA66Z pcs model from the schedule, not a default Post Caps pcs by number of beam plies: 3-ply BCS2-3/6 Zmax, 2-ply BC46 Zmax; read the schedule Beam (3) 2x12 P.T. B4 front, (2) 2x12 P.T. B3 sides LFT plies as the leading multiplier: =3*W*G Ledger 2x12 P.T. + Screws SDWS22400DB LFT, pcs screws =CEILING(...,3), 3 per point Box or Rim of the same size LFT only if the beam is not flush Joists 2x12 P.T. 16" o.c. LFT count W*12/16+1; long 14' board and /2 in the formula Hangers LUS210 Zmax, End Joists + LUC210 Zmax, HUC212-2 Zmax pcs hangers on both ends; outdoors always Zmax Decking 2x6 DuxxBak SQ FT W*D*G; 5/4x6 only on a terrace over the garage Porch blocks/#1 Porch 12x7 (x5) Ceiling Joists 2x8 16" o.c. + Ledger + Hangers LFT, pcs separate from rafters, required Beam (2) 2x10 B1 / (3) 2x10 B2 LFT porch codes differ from balcony codes 5/8" Gyp ceiling SQ FT two layers inside the formula: =CEILING(G*2*1.1,10)*G

Terrace over the garage (trusses and LW concrete): Subfloor 3/4" Ply in 4x8 sheets, Sleepers 2x4 P.T., Decking 5/4x6; bases on such stacks are 0.

docs.title: Rules that break the block
docs.text:
• Outdoor posts (porch, balcony, railing) are always P.T.. An enclosed porch or a balcony under a roof gets regular framing, not P.T.
  • Porch framing not shown: right under the block header Note: Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify.
  • Every connection from the S sheet gets its own row with the detail in E: beam to post (ML210Z, HL33Z, through bolts with washers and nuts, SDS), beam to beam (HUC...-2), end joists of a different size (End Joists). Hardware format: Hangers: how to write hardware in the DFL.
  • Railing: 2 posts per balcony, as a system or by components depending on the type, see Rails & Decking and Railing.
  • Flashings, Trims, Soffits, Post Wrap only when they are in scope; with Frame only do not insert them.
  • Porch and balcony stacked: the Porches row on the Front Page is filled separately; the balcony does not replace it.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A balcony block without its own units multiplier (900 SF instead of 60).
  • Porches mirrored from balconies instead of counted separately from the plans.
  • Post cap BCS2-3/6 Zmax by default instead of the model by plies from the schedule.
  • Hangers on one end only, or without Zmax outdoors.
  • Posts not P.T. outdoors, or P.T. under a roof.
  • Porch SQFT empty on the Front Page; canopy and porch counted again in eve and rake.
  • All mistakes for the section: Deck, porch, balconies.

docs.title: Railing
docs.text: Composite railing corner: a 4x4 post covered with a sleeve and cap, cap rail on top, balusters between the rails. In the balcony block: posts in pieces by corners and spacing, railing in LFT along the perimeter without the stair opening. Photo: timbertech.com, source, found via Pinterest. Railing assembly: posts, top and bottom rails, balusters, cap rail. Every element is a separate DFL row; the railing type sets the method (system or by components).

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Railing for a balcony, porch or deck. This page covers what goes into the balcony block in the DFL: posts, row formulas and choosing the counting method. System types (composite, Azek, wood, cable, metal), decking and post hardware are fully covered on the canonical page Rails & Decking.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Elevations Railing type (composite, wood, cable, aluminum), height 36" or 42" Details A5xx Components: post sleeve, cap, rail sections, or balusters and rails Plans and block size Railing length: front W plus open sides D Spec notes Aluminum railing by others and the like: do not count the railing, the note stays

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
A separate railing takeoff is usually not needed: the length comes from the balcony block size (front W and open sides D) and is multiplied by the number of instances G. A complex outline (a terrace, a porch all around) is traced with a Line on the plan. Block area and points: Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame.

Composite is counted as a system, painted wood by components. Detailed rows are on the Rails and Decking page.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
One method per run: a factory system or by components. Composite is always a system; by components only for painted wood. Do not mix.

Type DFL row Unit Formula Any Note: Railing is composite; verify product a note about the system right under the railing rows Any Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T. pcs 2 per balcony, =2*G; height 4' in E Composite (system) Post Sleeve Sleeve for 4x4, Post Cap Cap for 4x4 pcs by posts Composite (system) Rail sections 6' Rail section unit front and sides as separate rows Wood painted (by components) Balustrades 2x2 pcs =EVEN(G*2.2), G = railing LFT x units Wood painted (by components) Rails (top & bottom) 2x4 LFT =EVEN(G*2.2) (two runs) Wood painted (by components) Cap Rail 2x6 LFT =EVEN(G*1.1) Aluminum / metal only the note Note: Aluminum railing materials are by others; verify components material not counted

Outdoor railing posts are always P.T.. Blocking and bolts for the posts, if the detail shows them, go in the frame rows with the detail in E.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Three posts per balcony instead of two; a corner balcony against two walls carries one.
  • System and component counting mixed on one run.
  • Aluminum or vinyl railing counted as material instead of a note.
  • Posts at Rails without P.T..
  • All mistakes for the section: Deck, porch, balconies.

docs.title: Balcony build-up
docs.text: Bottom to top: frame, sleepers, EPDM, decking. Rows 1-6 are counted on the frame page, rows 7-12 here. Pavers and membrane are often by others.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The map of all balcony layers and the canonical page for the finish layers: post wrap, EPDM, decking as a finish, soffit underneath, fascia and edge trim, flashing at the wall, an assembly with pavers. The frame (posts, beam, ledger, joists, hangers, sleepers, subfloor) is counted on Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame, the railing on Rails & Decking. The Balcony Trims page is a short pointer here.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Balcony section A4xx Layer order: subfloor, sleepers, membrane, decking or pavers Details A5xx (balcony edge, wall flashing) Fascia, edge trim, soffit, flashing, post wrap Spec and notes Pavers Deck System by others, decking product (DuxxBak, composite) Job scope Frame only: do not insert rows 7-12

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Areas and lengths come from the block size W x D and the multiplier G (see frame). The soffit underneath and the decking equal the balcony area; trims and flashing go along the perimeter: the front and sides are open, the wall side gives flashing.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
# DFL row Material Unit Who counts it 1 Posts + Post Bases + Post Caps 6x6 P.T., per schedule pcs frame 2 Beam (3) front, Beam (2) sides 2x12 P.T. LFT frame 3 Ledger + screws, Box if the beam is not flush 2x12 P.T. LFT frame 4 Joists + Hangers Zmax + End Joists 2x12 P.T. 16" o.c. LFT, pcs frame 5 Sleepers (Terrace, often 2 layers) 2x4 P.T. LFT frame 6 Subfloor (Terrace) 3/4" Ply 4x8 frame 7 Post Wrap 1x8 / 5/4x LFT here 8 EPDM membrane SQ FT here, if ours per spec 9 Decking 2x6 DuxxBak (balcony), 5/4x6 (Terrace) SQ FT here, =W*D*G 10 Soffits at Balcony Beadboard SQ FT here, =W*D*G 11 Balcony Trims / Fascia 1x10, 5/4x8 LFT here, =(W+2*D)*G 12 Flashings at Wall Copper / drip edge LFT here, =W*G

Rows 7-12 are inserted only when trim is in scope. Size not specified: TBD and the note Note: All trims to be verified. Scaled per elevations.

docs.title: Assembly with pavers
docs.text:
A balcony on a slab or over a garage instead of decking on sleepers:

Layer, top to bottom Scope Porcelain Pavers + Thinset Mortar usually by others, note Note: Pavers Deck System are by others Roofing Membrane, Tapered Rigid Insulation check the scope Conc. Deck, Structural Steel structural, not trim

Over a garage with trusses and LW concrete the block is counted as a Terrace: 3/4" Ply subfloor, 2x4 P.T. sleepers, 5/4x6 decking.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Frame rows duplicated in the finish block (sleepers twice).
  • 5/4x6 decking on a regular balcony instead of 2x6 DuxxBak per the detail.
  • Pavers and membrane by others counted as material.
  • Trim inserted when the scope is Frame only.
  • Decking area without the units multiplier.
  • All mistakes for the section: Deck, porch, balconies.

docs.title: Casing, Corner & Band
docs.text: Top corner of a window: flat PVC casing on the sides and head, a head crown with a cap above it. Casing sides and head are counted in LFT from the opening size; crown and cap are separate rows by the head width. Photo: elitetrimworks.com, source, found via Pinterest. A corner board covers the cut edge of the siding at the corner. Counted in LFT by the corner height times the number of corners of that type.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Trim around openings and across the face of the elevation: ext. casing (sides, heads, apron, mulls), corner boards, band and watertable, head crowns with cap and flashing, window sills, shutters, louvers, brackets. All of it is wood, PVC or composite linear stock; siding and cladding are not part of it.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Elevations Where there is casing, corner, band; how many corners; shutters and louvers by window Window and door details (A5xx, A6xx) Casing profile (5/4x4), head crown, cap, drip cap, sill, 3-sides or 4-sides Wall sections Band and watertable, flashing above them, build-up under the corner Spec and notes Material (PVC, Azek, Hardi trim, vinyl), All trims to be verified

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Casing, corner and band are Lines in the trims root, one item per profile: 2" casing, 8" horizontal trim, corner 5/4x6. Elevations have no sheet dot, so check that the item landed in trims. Casing is easier to count with a formula from the opening list (perimeter of one window x quantity); use a Line only where the profile follows a complex outline. Shutters, louvers and brackets are Count points, with their own color and symbol for each takeoff.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Tree name DFL row Size Unit Rule trims/casing sides Ext. Casing sides 5/4x4 LFT vertical sides of openings trims/casing heads Ext. Casing heads 5/4x4 / 5/4x6 LFT head, often wider; (at crowns) as a separate row Ext. Casing (apron & sides) 5/4x3 LFT sides plus apron under the window Mull trims 5/4x6 LFT between ganged windows Casing garage doors (sides), Head casing garage dr 5/4x8, 5/4x12 LFT overhead doors separately Ext. Casing Vinyl J-channel / 3-1/2" Vinyl casing LFT with vinyl siding, do not duplicate with 5/4 Head crowns, Crown cap, Head flashing 3-1/2" crown, 1x4, Drip edge LFT stack over the head: crown, cap, flashing Window Sills 1" Sill / 2" Sill LFT when a sill is shown trims/corner 5/4x6 CornerBoards 5/4x6 / 5/4x8 LFT corner height x number of corners; bays as a separate row trims/band 5/4x10 Band Trims, Watertable Trim 5/4x10 / 5/4x12 LFT plus Flashing at band drip edge on top trims/shutters Shutters - paneled 20"x60" pairs a pair per window, size in the row Louver vent, Brackets 24" Dia, 5-1/2"x7"x? pcs the ? in the size stays as verify
  • 4-sides casing runs around the whole perimeter, 3-sides has no bottom (sill or siding). Write this in the row; it changes the LFT.
  • Vinyl corner (4" Vinyl corner) is a different product, not 5/4.
  • Size not specified: TBD in size, scaled or assumed in E, the note Note: All trims to be verified. Scaled per elevations.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Casing in one row without splitting sides, heads, mulls, garage.
  • With vinyl siding both J-channel and wood casing counted.
  • Head crown without cap and drip edge, though the detail shows them.
  • Band and watertable without flashing on top.
  • Shutters in pcs instead of pairs; shutter size lost.
  • Trim around stone or EIFS missed (see Exclusions).
  • All Excel and row mistakes: Excel DFL and notes.

docs.title: Exclusions and J-Channel
docs.text: EIFS, stucco, stone and brick veneer are by others. WRB, sheathing, furring and wood/PVC trim around them are ours; J-channel is ours only with vinyl siding.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The exclusion rule for the trim scope and the canonical page for J-Channel. What EIFS, stucco, stone and brick veneer are, how to recognize them on the plans and which accessories come with them is covered on the canonical page Siding - EIFS / Stucco / Veneer.

docs.title: What we do not count in Exterior Trims
docs.text:
System Count it? Why EIFS (synthetic stucco, Dryvit, Sto) no finish system by others Stucco (cement, 3-coat) no plaster trade, by others Stone veneer, brick veneer no masonry by others Siding (Hardi, vinyl, cedar) not here its own scope Siding

What stays ours next to them: wood/PVC casing, corner board, band, watertable, soffit, fascia, frieze, columns, porch and balcony trim, WRB and sheathing under the cladding, furring. If the whole elevation is EIFS or stone, trim can be close to zero: do not pad the quantity, add the note Note: Stone Veneer by others.

docs.title: J-Channel
docs.text:
J-Channel is a J-shaped profile that takes the cut edge of the siding. It covers the end and gives a clean termination line.

Condition Where J-channel goes Whose Vinyl siding around windows and doors, under soffit and frieze, at corner posts, inside corners, along the rake ours, LFT Siding meets another material joint with stone, brick, EIFS, decking, porch ceiling ours, if the siding is ours EIFS / stucco casing bead, stop bead, track at the bottom, at dissimilar material usually by others with the system

With vinyl siding Ext. Casing is often the Vinyl J-channel itself: the row Ext. Casing | Vinyl J-channel | LFT. Then do not duplicate it with 5/4 wood casing. Quantity: perimeter of all openings plus terminations. The word J-channel stays in the row; do not reduce it to a generic casing.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: J-channel with vinyl siding: a Line around the openings on the elevation, or a formula from the opening list (perimeter x quantity), plus a Line along the rake and the joints. No separate takeoff is needed for EIFS, stucco and veneer: they are by others; siding area 0 and a note.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Stone or brick veneer counted as siding.
  • With vinyl siding both J-channel and 5/4 casing counted on the same openings.
  • J-channel with EIFS written as ours.
  • Trim around veneer missed because "the wall is by others".
  • All sheathing and WRB mistakes: Sheathing.

docs.text:

docs.title: Furring & Window Jambs
docs.text: Horizontal section through a window: stud wall, sheathing, furring under the siding, window frame, jamb for the wall depth, casing outside. Jambs and furring live in the sections, not on the elevation.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Two things that are easy to miss because they are not on the elevations. Furring is the strip between the WRB and the siding: a vent gap (rainscreen) or a flat plane for the cladding. A window jamb is the board that builds out the opening depth from the window frame to the siding plane. Z-furring on CMU and basement furring are covered on Furring (walls); this page covers furring under siding and jambs as part of the exterior scope.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall sections (A3xx, A4xx) Whether there is furring under the siding, size 1x4 / 2x4, spacing, P.T. or not Window and door details (head, jamb, sill) Jamb 2x4 / 2x8 / 2x10 by wall thickness, P.T. at the bottom Wall types (wt) Rainscreen in the wall assembly, continuous insulation (the jamb gets deeper) Flare and bump details 2x blocking, rip as req'd

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Furring under siding: from the siding area (from siding or the elevations) converted to LFT by spacing; no separate Line is needed; solid furring is written in SQ FT. Jambs: with a formula from the opening list (perimeter x quantity); the opening sizes come from openings. Basement wall area under treated furring: an Area or Line along the section on the sheet with the W point.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
DFL row Size Unit Rule Furring 1x4 @ 16" o.c. 1x4 or 1x4 P.T. LFT =CEILING(SF*12/16*1.1,10); spacing in the row Furring (solid) 1x4 SQ FT when the detail calls for a solid plane Furring 2x4 2x4 / 2x4 P.T. LFT thicker per structural Window jamb 2x4 / 2x8 / 2x10 LFT perimeter of 3 sides (2 jambs + head) or 4 with the sill, x number of windows Jambs (in older workbooks Blocking around all openings) 5/4x4 P.T. LFT nailer for casing and flashing; inserted by B_JambsAllBlock 2x blocking, rip as req'd 2x LFT flare and bump per the detail
  • P.T. and non-P.T. are different products: P.T. at the foundation and in wet areas, usually not higher up. Do not write one size for the whole wall if the detail distinguishes them.
  • Window jamb and Blocking around all openings are two different rows, not a choice: the jamb builds out the depth, the blocking gives a nailer.
  • Do not offer furring at CMU as optional; if the detail shows it, it is required. Treated basement furring is a separate P.T. assembly.
  • Metal stud walls: the wood jamb in the openings is ours even if the framing is by others. If jambs are not needed, the note Assumed window jambs 2x4 are not used per A8.53; verify.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Furring missed because only the elevations were checked.
  • One size and one P.T. for the whole wall height.
  • 2x4 jamb on a thick wall with continuous insulation (2x8 is needed).
  • Furring written as optional for no reason.
  • Structural jamb confused with interior casing.
  • All wall mistakes: Walls.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Furring 1x4 @ 16" o.c.         1x4 P.T.   1290  LFT   =CEILING(1560*12/16*1.1,10)   7/A401
Window jamb                    2x8        612   LFT   =(2*5.5+3.3)*42 windows        4/A601
Jambs                          5/4x4 P.T. 650   LFT   B_JambsAllBlock                A601

docs.title: Trim macros
docs.text:
Excel macros that calculate and insert trim blocks: C_TrimsCalc (a block for one element multiplied by the quantity), collapsing identical rows, inserting ready-made jambs, pavers, balcony and bolts blocks. The general map of hotkeys and all the workbook macros: Excel macro hotkeys.

C_TrimsCalc: the trim rows of one window are multiplied by the number of such windows; the total is written as a formula, not a number.

docs.title: If the macro "does nothing"
docs.text:
1. The active workbook is the one with macros (TemplateCom or the trims workbook), not an xlsx copy.
  2. Macros are enabled: Excel asks when opening; otherwise File > Options > Trust Center > Macro Settings.
  3. Run it: the assigned key, a ribbon button, or Alt+F8 and the macro name.

docs.title: Three columns: Label, Value, Unit
docs.text:
The trim calculation macros expect exactly three adjacent columns: Label, Value, Unit. Select three columns with the trim rows:

Label Value Unit Ext. Casing sides 380 LFT Head casing 204 LFT Soffits at Porch 120 SQ FT (quantity row) 2 EA

If the selection is not three columns, the macro shows an error and exits.

docs.title: C_TrimsCalc: block x quantity
docs.text:
Calculates the trim for one element multiplied by the number of such elements (trim of one window x number of windows, trim of one balcony x number of balconies).

  1. Write out the trim rows of one element (unit FT or SQ FT).
  2. Right below them, a row where Value equals the quantity, Unit EA.
  3. Several blocks in a row are fine: each one is closed by its own EA row.
  4. Select the three columns across all blocks, run C_TrimsCalc.
  5. Two rows below the selection a Label | Sum * EA table appears with formulas =B12*3. Check the Labels and multipliers.

The macro writes formulas, not numbers: the checker sees what the quantity is made of. Do not replace the formula with a number.

docs.title: C_SumTheSameValues: collapse identical rows
docs.text: Key Label + Unit, values are summed. Useful when CornerBoards 5/4x6 | LFT appears on every elevation and floor. Select the three columns, run it (default Ctrl+Shift+F). The selection is cleared and replaced with unique rows with sums: work on a copy if you need the source rows.

docs.title: Y_MultiplySelectedCells: multiply everything
docs.text: Multiplies every selected cell by a multiplier address (it asks for the address, for example G208): appends *G208 to a formula, turns a number into =<number>*G208. For a waste factor and a block-wide multiplier. Default Ctrl+M.

docs.title: Inserting ready-made blocks
docs.text:
Insertion goes from the selected row down, shifting A:H. First put the cursor on the right row, then run it: one row off will shift someone else's data.

Macro What it inserts What to fix afterwards B_JambsAllBlock Jambs 5/4x4 P.T. with a formula by openings, the Wall Materials header only if it is missing size (5/4x4, 2x4, 2x8) and P.T. per the detail B_PaversBlock Pavers with the note Note: Pavers Deck System are by others area in G, scope by others. Railing: Decking + ... Railing in the Insert Block menu B_Balcony_Insert_Template_FromText a balcony block from the command b 12x30 or b 1.3x1.9 u2 (posts, beam, ledger, joists, decking, trims) structure per S: cap by plies, Zmax hangers, decking per the detail; see DFL blocks B_BoltsAdd Blocking, Anchor Bolts, Washers, Nuts (4 rows), G empty lengths in G, size and spacing per the detail B_ShaftWallsBlocks two shaft wall blocks, CH + J and H + C, G empty area in G, size and spacing; Delete Zeros removes the extra block

docs.title: Cleanup after inserting
docs.text: Macro Key Action X_DeleteRowsByColor Ctrl+Shift+D delete the gray placeholder rows of the template B_DeleteZeroRowsOnlyIn_AtoH Ctrl+E delete rows with Value 0 only in A:H X_DeleteCellsUp / Y_InsertCellsUp Ctrl+Q / Ctrl+W delete or insert cells with a shift Y_noValidation Ctrl+Shift+V remove validation dropdowns Y_CheckEnglish Ctrl+Shift+T spell check Y_InsertDate Ctrl+Shift+O insert the date

docs.title: Order for a trim block
docs.text:
1. Put the cursor on the row, run the right insert macro.
  2. Fix the size and P.T. per the specific detail.
  3. Fill Value with formulas with visible addends.
  4. The element repeats N times: an EA row and C_TrimsCalc.
  5. Collapse duplicates across elevations: C_SumTheSameValues.
  6. Waste or a block-wide multiplier: Y_MultiplySelectedCells.
  7. Cleanup: gray rows, zeros, validation. Finish: date and spell check.

docs.title: Exterior Trims
docs.text:
Exterior Trims are wood, PVC or composite linear stock and products on the outside of the building: casing around openings, corner boards, band and watertable, head crowns, soffit and fascia, frieze, columns, porch, deck and balcony trim. It is a separate scope: not siding, not EIFS, stucco or veneer, and not framing. We count only the trim material and only when trim is in the job.

What we do not count

EIFS, stucco, stone and brick veneer are finish systems by others. Canonical page: EIFS / Stucco / Veneer; the rule for the trim scope and J-channel: Exclusions and J-Channel.

docs.title: What is included and in what order
docs.text:
• Casing, Corner & Band

    Ext. casing (sides, heads, apron, mulls), corner boards, band and watertable, head crowns with cap and flashing, shutters, louvers, brackets.

    Casing, Corner & Band

  • Furring & Window Jambs

    Furring 1x4 / 2x4 under siding and jamb 2x4 / 2x8 / 2x10 in openings. They live in the sections, not on the elevations.

    Furring & Jambs

  • Soffit & Fascia

    Soffit and fascia along eaves and rakes, frieze, rake moulding, returns, columns.

    Soffit & Fascia

  • Porch / Deck / Balcony

    Porch trims, flare; hub for railing, balcony layers, pergola.

    Porch / Deck / Balcony

  • Rails & Decking

    Canonical page for railing: composite as a system, wood by components, metal by others; decking, post hardware, lattice.

    Rails & Decking

  • Balcony build-up

    All balcony layers: what the frame counts, what the trim counts; assembly with pavers.

    Balcony build-up

  • Outdoor Shower & Pergola

    IPE privacy screen, pergola, trellis, canopy.

    Shower & Pergola

  • Trim macros

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Read the siding material note on the elevations: Hardi, vinyl, cedar, EIFS, stone. It decides which trim is possible at all (vinyl often means J-channel instead of casing).
  2. Open the window and door details, wall sections, eave details: profiles, furring, jambs, head crown with cap and flashing.
  3. Count by groups: openings (casing), corners and bands, overhangs, porch and balcony, products (shutters, louvers, columns).
  4. Size not specified: TBD and the note Note: All trims to be verified. Scaled per elevations. Do not make up a product.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: The trims root in the building tree. The physical object sets the takeoff type: casing, band, corner and fascia are Lines, one item per profile (2" casing, 8" horizontal trim); soffit and the porch ceiling are Areas along the real outline; shutters, columns, brackets are Counts. Each takeoff has its own color and its own point symbol. Elevations and RCPs have no sheet dot, so check where the item landed. Eave and rake lengths come from eves rakes, the siding area from siding.

docs.title: DFL row
docs.text:
A Description B Size C Qty D Unit E Ext. Casing sides 5/4x4 =2*5.5*34 LFT A601 Head crowns 3-1/2" crown =3.3*34 LFT scaled CornerBoards 5/4x6 =8*28 LFT A201 Soffits at Porch Beadboard =12*8*G SQ FT 6/A550 Columns 12" Dia Fbg Non-taper w/c&b 4 pcs 8' Shutters - paneled 20"x60" 12 pairs A201
  • LFT for linear stock, SQ FT for panels and beadboard, pcs and pairs for products. Column and post height separately, not inside the description.
  • Size and profile always visible (5/4x4, 3-1/2" crown, 4" Vinyl corner); never write a generic trim.
  • In the trims workbook for macros a row is three columns: Label, Value, Unit, see Trim macros.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Trim counted when the scope is Frame only.
  • Vinyl siding: J-channel and wood casing on the same openings.
  • Canopy and porch counted again in eave and rake; porch SQFT empty on the Front Page.
  • A product guessed instead of TBD and a note.
  • All mistakes: Excel DFL and notes, Deck, porch, balconies.

docs.title: Porch / Deck / Balcony
docs.text:
The hub for trim on open platforms. The frame is counted on Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame; this page covers what goes on top and outside: porch trims, railing and decking, balcony layers, shower screen and pergola.

Always include

These elements are not visible on the main elevations and are easy to forget. Go through every porch, deck and balcony separately, by its own sections and details. Insert trim only when it is in scope; with Frame only do not insert it.

  • Rails & Decking - railing by type (composite as a system, wood by components, metal by others), decking, post hardware, lattice, skirt. open

  • Balcony build-up - all balcony layers, finish rows 7-12, assembly with pavers. open

  • Shower & Pergola - privacy screen, pergola, trellis, canopy. open

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. On the plans and elevations find every porch, deck and balcony, determine the type and the number of instances (see the blocks on the frame page).
  2. Open the section and details of each: what is shown (fascia, soffit, columns, railing), what material.
  3. For each block, after the frame rows add the trim rows with the block multiplier G. Size not specified: TBD and a note.

docs.text:
Porch ceiling from below: board soffit (row Soffits at Porch, SQ FT), fascia along the edge (Fascia Trim at Hdr outside), decorative brackets and wrapped columns. Each element is counted as a separate row with the block multiplier. Photo: hbelementsinc.com, source, found via Pinterest. Section through the porch header: fascia trim outside and inside, soffit trim, frieze, crown, beadboard soffit (SQ FT), column wrap.

docs.text:
A wall that flares out at the bottom under shingles: its own set of blocking and trim.

Flare: 2x blocking (rip as req'd), crown, 5/4x10 trim with drip edge, cedar shingles. Flare sheathing and WRB go in their own rows. DFL row Size Unit Blocking (plates double) / (studs double) 2x6 LFT Trims 5/4x10 LFT Crowns 2" Crowns LFT Flare Sheathing 1/2" CDX Ply 4x8 WRB per the wall spec SQ FT

docs.title: Rails & Decking
docs.text: Posts, cap rail, balusters, decking: each has its own row. Composite railing is counted as a system, painted wood railing by components. Composite railing on a deck: the post is covered with a white sleeve and cap, a wood-look cap rail on top, balusters between the top and bottom rail, composite decking. Such a system is counted as railing LFT plus posts in pieces; decking separately in SQ FT. Photo: timbertech.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Railing and decking of balconies, porches and decks: railing systems (composite, Azek, wood, cable, metal), decking, post hardware, balusters, cap rail, deck fascia, skirt, risers, lattice. This is neither trim nor framing: the frame is on Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame, the balcony layers on Balcony build-up. This page is the canonical page for railing types; the short version for the balcony block is on Railing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Elevations Railing type (composite, wood, cable, aluminum), height 36" or 42", whether the decking is visible Details A5xx (railing detail, deck edge) Post, sleeve, cap, rail sections or balusters, cap rail, fascia, skirt Spec and notes Railing by others, product (Trex, Azek, DuxxBak), verify Plans Railing length by side, number of balconies and porches of each type

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Decking and railing come from the block size: area W x D, railing front W plus open sides D, multiplied by the number of instances G. The area of balconies and porches as an Area sits in sqfts/blcny and sqfts/porch; a deck near grade with a complex outline is traced as an Area in sqfts with a clear name, railing along a broken outline as a Line. Do not put the product and height in the name; they live in the DFL.

Left: composite as a system (posts with sleeve and cap, 6' sections); right: painted wood by components (posts, balusters, rails, cap rail). Two posts per balcony; do not mix methods in one block.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
One counting method per run: a system (factory sections) or by components. Composite and Azek are always a system; by components only for painted wood. Do not mix.

Outdoor posts are always P.T.; under a roof (enclosed porch) regular. Post base and anchor (ABU66 Zmax, DTT2Z) only when the detail shows them, as frame rows with the detail in E, format per Hangers. Full block content: DFL blocks.

docs.text:
• Three posts per balcony instead of two; a corner balcony against two walls carries one.
  • System and component counting mixed: Rail sections together with Balustrades.

  • Rails (top & bottom) taken as one run instead of two.
  • Balcony decking 5/4x6 instead of 2x6 DuxxBak per the detail.
  • A product guessed instead of TBD and the note Decking & Railing products to verify.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Open garden structures in the exterior scope: privacy and shower screens, pergolas and trellises, a canopy over the entry. There are usually few details, and many rows go in as assumed per the elevation.

docs.text: Screen: an Area for the screen area (slats) and a Count of posts. Pergola: a Count of beams and trellis members with the length in the row, a Line for the ledger. docs.title: Soffit & Fascia
docs.text: Eave corner from below: vented soffit panels between the wall and the fascia, fascia with a gutter along the edge. Soffit is counted by area (overhang length times width), fascia in LFT along the same line. Photo: brothersgutters.com, source, found via Pinterest. Gable corner: the eave with soffit and fascia runs along the wall, the rake follows the slope, a return in the corner. A proper cornice return is a separate set of rows.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Soffit (the underside of the overhang), fascia (the edge board), frieze (the board on the wall under the soffit), rake moulding, returns and porch columns. Usually a separate block Soffits and Fascias. Eave and rake lengths come from Eve and Rake; soffit sheathing (5/8" exterior gypsum, plywood) is Sheathing, not trim.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Eave and rake details (A5xx) Overhang width, soffit material (vinyl vented, beadboard, 1x), fascia, frieze, rake moulding Elevations Where the eaves are, where the rakes are, returns (cornice or pork-chop), columns and their type RCP and porch sections Porch and canopy ceiling: material, area, 5/8" exterior gypsum under the finish Spec Soffits assumed Vinyl; Fascias assumed PVC or 1x Alum wrapped; verify

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Overhang lengths are Lines in eves rakes/eves and eves rakes/rakes with the overhang in inches in the name (eve 24 main, rake 12 main, returns 12): one line feeds both the trim and the overhang sheathing. Soffit as an area (beadboard, panel) is an Area along the real underside outline in trims or in the job's agreed branch (rcp 1.6); the outline is not the roof deck. Do not feed one area twice: either length x width or an Area. A canopy is not part of eave and rake; it has its own rows. Columns are Count points.

docs.text:

docs.title: Ceiling / Soffit Framing
docs.text: Dropped soffit: a 2x box around the perimeter below the ceiling. The source is the RCP, it is not on the structural plan. We count the framing (plates, frame, screws), the finish goes in Interior Trims. Dropped soffit with the gypsum removed: a 2x box hung under the floor joists along the wall, with pipes and a duct running inside. On the RCP such a box shows as a line with a height mark; we count plates around the perimeter and frame by area. Photo: themakerista.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Interior ceiling and box framing: dropped soffits over kitchens and in corridors, ceiling boxes for ducts, the mechanical room ceiling (Ceiling Mech), the kitchen ceiling per unit. This is framing scope, not finish and not the exterior soffit. Ceiling finish (crown, gypsum) is Interior Trims; the roof soffit under the overhang is Eve / Eave; soffit plywood under roof trusses is Roof Sheathing; gypsum backing on a wall parallel to the joists is Bracing for Drywall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take RCP (a8.01 1st rcp) dropped soffits, boxes, ceiling heights, zones by unit Mech / MEP plans mech room ceiling, screens, equipment above the ceiling Sections, ceiling details (A454) box depth, construction, plate and frame size, spacing Kitchen and unit plans kitchen ceiling per unit

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
On the RCP sheet (sheet dot by floor): Line (L) around the perimeter of each box for plates, Area (A) over the ceiling area for frame at a spacing. Area and perimeter are measured by hand from the A sheets, not taken from the floor's overall sqft. There is no fixed branch for these takeoffs in the tree.

To be confirmed

Where to put soffit takeoffs in the tree (framing/<floor> framing/details/soffit or roof misc) is not confirmed by delivered jobs.

docs.text:
Sections are organized per floor or per area (1st, 2nd, Loft), like interior trims.

Ceiling Mech is typical for single-story jobs with a mech room; on a multifamily building it is replaced by a ceiling per floor in the truss heel zone: Truss Heel. G is the perimeter or area from the A plans, H the number of plates or the spacing, D the board length.

docs.title: Beam
docs.text: Beam tool: two points along the beam from bearing to bearing; the app rounds the length and creates a Count takeoff FB1 8 with the first mark. A second beam of the same mark and length goes into the same takeoff as a second point. Flush LVL beam at joist depth: joists on both sides hang on face-mount hangers. The beam is one Count takeoff with the length in the name; hangers are counted by the number of joist ends on it. Photo: plasticinehouse.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A beam is a floor or roof beam that carries joists, rafters or posts: (2) 2x10, (3) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, 5 1/4 x 11 7/8 PSL, 5 1/2 x 14 GL. A steel beam is by others, but the wood nailer on it is ours: Steel Beam Web Fillers. A header over an opening is Headers; a beam between doubled rafters in the roof is Roof Header. Flush (at joist depth, on hangers) and Dropped (below the joists) go into the Label.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take S framing plan of the floor marks (FB1, B2, H5), location, span, bearing at both ends Beam schedule (S5xx, S6xx) size, plies, material by mark. No schedule - build the legend yourself from the labels on the plan Sections, details flush or dropped, bearing, hangers, PSL and squash blocks under the ends General notes EWP by others, nailer on steel beams, lumber grade

docs.title: Size when there is no beam schedule
docs.text:
The mark and size from the S sheet always win. If there are none, use the E-Wood defaults by span for flush beams and the garage center beam:

Beam 6'-9' 9'-12' 12'-14' 14'-16' 16'-18' Flush under the floor (2) LVL at joist depth (2) LVL at joist depth (3) LVL at joist depth (3) LVL at joist depth (3) 14" LVL Flush under the floor and roof (under an exterior wall) (3) 9-1/2" LVL (3) 11-7/8" LVL (3) 14" LVL (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL Garage center beam 22' 24' 26' Floor above (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL (3) 24" LVL Ceiling only (3) 14" LVL (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL

Up to 6' and headers in walls: full table on the Headers page.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Beam tool (B), framing sheet with the F point. Draw a line along the beam centerline from bearing face to bearing face; the length appears in the name by itself.

  • The app does the rounding: up to 8' inclusive it rounds up to the whole foot, longer rounds up to the next even foot (9.2' gives 10, 12.1' gives 14). Do not add feet yourself.
  • One built-up beam = one point with (n) in the name. Do not place n points and (n) at the same time.
  • Draw every beam that is not part of the wall panels. Every mark on every floor where it is shown.
  • A mark with the letter H (H5) can be a beam by its role; do not move it to headers just because of the letter.
  • Ledger, rim, blocking, nailer are separate Lines in details, not beam points.
  • Repeat Beam (the button next to Beam) draws several separate beams in a row without picking the tool again.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Path: framing/<floor> framing/beams/<mark or size> <length>. The size for a mark comes from the LG legend (B2 - (3) 2x10) on export.

Tree name A (Label) B (material) C D E beams/FB1 8 Beam (2) Flush 2x10 points 8 FB1 per S601 beams/(3) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL 14 Beam (3) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL points 14 beams/B2 14 + LG B2 - (3) 2x10 Beam (3) Dropped 2x10 points 14 B2 beams/int 4x10 4 Beam 4x10 points 4 beams/H5 8 Beam (2) per schedule points 8 H5

Hangers for beams: by the built-up width and condition (face, top, concealed, skew), for every end that hangs on another beam or wall. Selection: Hangers; how to write it in B: hardware format in the DFL. Exterior and on P.T.: Zmax as a separate word.

Export: the BM button on the XL strip replaces only the beam rows on the floor worksheet; template rows stay. The C_BeamsSort macro sorts by mark and length.

Built-up LVL: actual width Written as Actual size (2) 1 3/4 x 9 1/2 LVL 3 1/2 x 9 1/2 (3) 1 3/4 x 9 1/2 LVL 5 1/4 x 9 1/2 (4) 1 3/4 x 9 1/2 LVL 7 x 9 1/2

The width of the pack sets the hanger (HU412 for 3 1/2 x 11 7/8, HGUS7.25/12 for 7 x 11 7/8). On EWP jobs (we count only LVL, PSL, GL, I-joists) regular 2x beams are not included: EWP / Capital.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A mark missed on one of the floors: the same FB7 is on both S102 and S103.
  • Feet "for bearing" added to the tool length - the rounding is already done.
  • A pack of three LVLs written as three points plus (3) in the name: triple count.
  • PSL or squash blocks under the beam ends per schedule not counted (2 became 4).
  • Hangers not on both ends, or counted by purchase boards after cutting; the model does not match the detail (U210-2, not LUS210-2).
  • A beam inside a wall panel drawn on a panel job.
  • Tri-Force beams and beams with steel plates keep inch fractions in B: write the nearest foot.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.text:

    beams/
      FB1 8                        6 points
      FB1 10                       2 points
      (3) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL 14    3 points
A B C D E Beam (2) Flush 2x10 6 8 FB1 per S601 Beam (2) Flush 2x10 2 10 FB1 Beam (3) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL 3 14 S102 Hangers HU412 6 pcs 9/S501

docs.title: Joist
docs.text: J Area tool: zone outline, direction arrow, spacing. The app gives the joist count and lengths for the zone by itself. A plain Area named 2x8 16" does not do that.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Joists are floor or flat roof members at a spacing: sawn 2x10, I-joists (11 7/8 TJI 230, LPI, BCI, RFPI, NI), LVL. Floor trusses and roof trusses are by others and we do not count them, but we do count the rim, blocking, hangers and ties around them. Rafters of a pitched roof are measured with the same tool, see Dbl / Trpl Rafters.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take S framing plan of the floor direction, spacing, size, zone boundaries, extra and double joists, openings Joist schedule, general notes I-joist series and depth, rim, web stiffeners, squash blocks, blocking rows Beam schedule, details bearing: on top of a beam, on hangers, top chord bearing Firewall and stair details DHU/DGU instead of ITS over stairs, elevators, shafts

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
J Area tool (J), framing sheet with the F point. Outline the zone, set the direction (with Shift, strictly along the axes), spacing, end joists; extra joists are added to the selected zone with the D key.

  1. Split the zone where the direction, spacing, material or bearing line changes. One arrow for the whole floor does not describe the floor framing.
  2. In every zone check: direction, start and end boundary, include end joists, openings, extra and double joists.
  3. Check the count and lengths on one simple zone first, then do the rest.
  4. Do not draw rafters by others or trusses by others as joists.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Path: framing/<floor> framing/joists/<size series spacing use>: 2x8 16", 11 7/8 TJI 230 16", flat roof 11 7/8 TJI 16", porch 16 TJI 560 24", cant.

Export: the JS button on the XL strip writes joists as "count / length" pairs into the floor worksheet. Layout follows the C_JoistsSort macro rule:

  • a length over 8' that is odd gets +1 (11' becomes 12');
  • equal lengths are added into one row;
  • short ones (up to 7') go on a double-length board: 90 x 6' becomes 45 x 12', and E gets 90 pcs 6';
  • extra joists of the same length are added to the main row.
A (Label) B (material) C D E Joists 16" o.c. 11 7/8 TJI 230 36 20 S102 Joists 16" o.c. 11 7/8 TJI 230 45 12 90 pcs 6' Dbl Joists 11 7/8 TJI 230 4 20 under wall per S102 Hangers ITS2.37/11.88 =EVEN(G*12/16) pcs Rim Board 11-7/8" LSL Rim LFT x 1.05 LFT

Hangers: on both ends of every joist that hangs; count by assemblies, not by purchase boards after cutting. Model per the detail (U210-2, not LUS210-2). ITS is top-flange only up to 16" depth and with no skew; deeper - HIT. Exterior and on P.T.: Zmax as a separate word; H2.5A ties to trusses under the sheathing go without Zmax. Selection: Hangers; how to write it in B: hardware format in the DFL.

A face-mount hanger holds the joist end on a beam: one such connection for every end that hangs. Photo: ArmchairBuilder.com, CC BY 2.0, source.

Spacing factor if you count by hand: pcs = zone width LFT x 12 / spacing plus the end joist; 16" gives 0.75, 19.2" gives 0.625, 24" gives 0.5. This is geometry, not the 1.1 stud factor: Formulas.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A plain Area named 2x8 16": there is no count, the area goes to Excel.
  • Spacing restarted from an interior beam, or a joist removed though it does not land on the beam (tolerance about 2").
  • Hangers not on both ends; ITS on joists 18" and deeper; DHU where the drywall stops under the floor (ITS is needed).
  • Rim split into 16' and called 1-3/4 LVL though not specified: Rim Board.
  • Rim at roof TJI forgotten.
  • Series lost: TJI instead of 11 7/8 TJI 230; RED rewritten as TJI; there is no TJI 9 1/2 in the 360/560 series.
  • Top chord bearing missed: there it is blocking instead of a ribbon, see Ribbon Board.
  • Long 2x ceiling joists spliced over a support counted as one board.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
framing/
  2nd floor framing/
    joists/
      11 7/8 TJI 230 16"      J Area, 3 zones
      2x10 16"                J Area, porch
      cant                    J Area, cantilever
A B C D E Joists 16" o.c. 11 7/8 TJI 230 3 12 S102 Joists 16" o.c. 11 7/8 TJI 230 36 20 Hangers ITS2.37/11.88 42 pcs 9/S501

docs.title: I-joist profiles (manufacturer reference)
docs.text:
Write the series and depth as in the schedule. The images are archived, for checking the family name.

Show TJI, RED, LP, RFPI, BCI, Nordic profiles TJI Series 110, 210, 230, 360, 560. In the row 11 7/8 TJI 230, not a generic TJI. RED / Red-I Do not rewrite as TJI; mark, depth and series as in the schedule. LP / LPI SolidStart LPI 20Plus, 32Plus, 36, 42Plus, 52Plus, 56. The flange affects the hanger (ITS2.56 vs ITS2.37). RFPI LVL-flange and solid-sawn-flange versions; keep the series and depth visible. BCI / Boise BCI is not TJI; keep the + s suffix in the mark. Nordic NI NI-20, NI-40x, NI-60, NI-80, NI-90; Nordic has its own hanger notes. Spacing o.c. Spacing is measured center to center; 12 / 16 / 19.2 / 24 only from the plan or notes.

Official guides for checking names: TJI, LP SolidStart, BCI, RFPI, Nordic, APA I-joist.

docs.title: Post
docs.text: Archived 3D view of the frame: posts highlighted in blue, ridge in red, roof beams in yellow. A post is counted on the floor it supports, with the full height from the base to the bottom of the beam. 6x6 post under a deck beam: a post cap on top holds the beam, the post runs down to the post base. In the DFL the post is one row with the full height, Post Cap and Post Base are separate rows by the number of posts. Photo: plasticinehouse.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A post is a stand-alone column under a beam, not a wall stud: solid 6x6, 4x4, 5 1/4 x 5 1/4 PSL, steel pipe, or a built-up (2) 2x6, (4) 2x4. A post comes with a Post Base at the bottom (to concrete or a beam) and a Post Cap at the top (to the beam). Studs inside a wall (jack, king, a pack under a header) belong to Walls, not here. Posts under the Ridge and a Roof Header are counted here too, in roof framing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take S framing plan of every floor post marks (C4, P1, WP2), location, which beam it sits under Post / column schedule (S5xx, S6xx) size, material, plies, cap and base by mark Sections, elevations, datums how many floors the post runs through, height from the base to the bottom of the beam Post-to-beam, post-to-foundation details cap and base model, anchor, blocking under the post Roof framing plan posts under the ridge and roof header

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Count tool (P), one point at the center of the post, on the framing sheet with the F point. Every mark and height is its own takeoff, with its own Color and CountSymbol.

  1. A continuous post is counted once: on the top floor it supports. Remove duplicates on the lower floors. Height = sum of the floors it runs through.
  2. Do not merge separate story posts on one axis into one without a continuity detail. A doubtful splice goes into the takeoff Notes as "verify".
  3. Height is from the actual base to the bottom of the supported beam, by the section datums. Floor-to-floor is not the post height: under an 11 7/8" beam the post is taller than under an 18" beam.
  4. Cap and base per the detail: a separate Count takeoff CCQ66 S2.1 in details, or the model in the post Notes. One cap and one base per post.

Post Count takeoff: one point at the center of each post, the name has the mark, size and height.

A post that runs through several floors is counted once on the top floor it supports. Height is from the base to the bottom of the beam, not floor-to-floor.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Path: framing/<supported floor> framing/posts/<mark size height>. Height in the name in feet.

Tree name A (Label) B (material) C (qty) D E posts/C53 - 5 1/4 x 7 PSL + 2x6 Posts 5 1/4 x 7 PSL points order length, ft C53, schedule sheet posts/6x6 SYP#1 P.T. 8.2 Posts 6x6 SYP#1 P.T. points 10 detail posts/C4 20 Posts per schedule points 20 C4 posts/(3) 2x6 9.1 Posts (3) 2x6 points x 3 10 details/ABU66 Zmax S2.1 Post Bases ABU66 Zmax points pcs 5/S501 in the post Notes Post Caps CCQ66, BC46 Zmax = posts pcs 6/S501

Export to Excel: the PS button on the XL strip puts the posts into the worksheet of their floor. The size for a code (C4 - 6x6) comes from the LG legend: without a legend row, B gets the code instead of the size. The C_PostsSort macro lays out the rows. The order length in D is a standard board (8, 10, 12, 14, 16...).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A post drawn on every floor it runs through and counted twice.
  • Height taken as floor-to-floor, without the beam depth.
  • Cap and base not on every post: 8 posts give 8 caps and 8 bases; 4 P1 posts are 4 sets, not 3.
  • Posts and Post Caps created under every built-up beam. End studs are part of the wall; a post is counted when an explicit material is named: 4x4, 6x6, PSL, steel.
  • Exterior posts (porch, balcony, railing) without P.T. Under a porch roof P.T. is not needed.
  • An exterior base without Zmax. It is written as a separate word after the model: ABU66 Zmax, not ABU66Z (hardware format in the DFL).
  • The post is not specified on the plan and the DFL has a made-up size. A note is needed: "post size not specified, assumed 6x6; verify".
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
framing/
  2nd floor framing/
    posts/
      C4 - 6x6 10                 4 points
      C53 - 5 1/4 x 7 PSL + 2x6   2 points
  roof framing/
    posts/
      P1 4x4 8.2                  6 points
A B C D E Posts 6x6 4 10 C4 per S601 Post Bases ABU66 Zmax 4 pcs 5/S501 Post Caps CCQ66 4 pcs 6/S501

docs.title: Stair
docs.text: Stair block: stringers carry treads and risers, the flight bears on the landing (platform beam, joists, ledger). Stair hangers go in the same block. A flight on site: four notched 2x12 stringers, temporary treads from offcuts, the bottom of the flight sits on the landing. In the DFL stringers are counted in pieces by flight length, treads and risers by the number of steps. Photo: finehomebuilding.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Stair is the wood stair framing: stringers, treads, risers, landing (platform beam, platform joists, ledger, box), hangers and hardware. A metal lobby stair or a prefab stair by others is one note row, with no material. Stair railing and finish are not here.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take A stair plans and sections (A4xx, A5xx) number of stairs and flights, flight width, number of risers, run and rise S stair detail (for example, 2/S603) stringer table by run: size, LVL or 2x12, stringer spacing S floor framing plan platform beam, platform joists, landing ledger, marks Str FB5 Hanger schedule, details hangers at stringer ends (LSC), platform joists, balloon detail of the stair walls

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Path framing/<floor> framing/stairs/<element>. The tool type follows the physical object, not one tool for everything:

Element Tool Name example Box, landing ledger Line (L) box str, ledger str Platform joists J Area (J) Stair 2x10 16" Platform beam, stringers by mark Beam (B) or Count (P) Str FB5 10, Stair HP5 5
  1. Assign the flight to a confirmed level: the stair is visible on two plans but is counted once.
  2. Stringer order length = sloped length plus bearing, rounded up to a standard board: run 8'-3" and rise 5'-8" give 10.0' along the slope, we order 12'.
  3. Step sizes from the stair plan, not scaled off a neighboring sheet.
  4. Identical stairs - one block with a multiplier; different ones - separate blocks.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Export: the ST button on the XL strip puts the stair takeoffs before Subfloor. The block in the DFL starts with a Note: 2 Stairs row, where G = number of stairs, and all quantities are multiplied by G.

A (Label) B (material) C D Rule Stringers (4) 2x12, per table 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL, 1 3/4 x 14 LVL =4*G per flight 10, 12, 14 4 stringers per flight; 2x12 by default, LVL per the detail table Treads 2x12 Treads number of treads / 3 per 12' board 12 treads = risers minus number of flights Risers 1x8 Risers number of risers / 3 12 risers from the A plan Platform Beam (2) 2x12, (2) 1 3/4 x 11 1/4 LVL =2*G 10 size per the stringer end detail Platform Joists 2x10 =9*G 10 from the landing J Area Platform Ledger 2x10, at CMU 2x10 P.T. =4*G 14 Hangers LSC, LUS210, HUCQ210-3 by connections x G pcs one LSC per stringer top end Screws SDWS 1/4 x 4 1/4 =4*4*G pcs attachment of the stringer bottom board

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The stair not multiplied by the number of stairs: 8 identical stairs, one counted.
  • Stringers from the template (4) 1 3/4 x 16 LVL for a two-flight stair. Two flights - 8 pcs 2x12 at 10-12'; LVL only when the detail table calls for it.
  • Stringer length taken off the plan (horizontal projection), not along the slope.
  • A flight counted on both plans where it is visible.
  • Stair hangers mixed with demising hangers. DHU/DGU at the stair firewall is a separate row, see Tips.
  • LSC count taken from order boards after cutting, not from the physical stringers.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
framing/
  2nd floor framing/
    stairs/
      box str            Line, 24 LF
      ledger str         Line, 12 LF
      Stair 2x10 16"     landing J Area
      Str FB5 10         2 points
A B C D E Note: 2 Stairs 2/S603 Stringers (4) 2x12 =4*G 12 2/S603 Treads 2x12 Treads =6*G 12 Risers 1x8 Risers =6*G 12 Platform Beam (2) 2x12 =2*G 10 Str FB5 Hangers LSC =8*G pcs 2/S603

docs.title: Subfloor Sheathing
docs.text: Subfloor by default is 3/4" T&G glued to the joists. The FRT strip at the exterior wall, underlayment, and subfloor over an existing floor are separate rows.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Subfloor is the panel decking over the joists: 3/4" T&G OSB or AdvanTech, on panel adhesive. Counted separately: the FRT strip around the perimeter, underlayment under the finish, decking under tubs, and decking over an existing floor. The vertical sheathing strip at floor level is the Floor-height Sheathing page, not subfloor.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor assembly (A5xx, A6xx), general notes thickness and product, T&G, adhesive, layers on top S general notes, FRT note FRT strip 2' or 4' from the exterior wall; blocking under its edge Finish schedule, bath details 1/2" underlayment, 3/4" ply under tubs Reconstruction details new subfloor over the existing floor, if the detail calls for it Deck and balcony sections structural subfloor of balconies, separate material

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
The area comes from sqfts/<floor> (the floor Area); no separate measurement is needed. For the FRT strip you need the exterior perimeter of that floor: a Line along the exterior walls or the sum of the ext walls of the floor.

  • Sheets = SQ FT / 32 x 1.1, rounded up to a whole sheet (4x8).
  • FRT strip: floor perimeter x strip width (2' or 4'), on its own floor. A 4' strip written as 10 sheets instead of 54 is a typical undercount.
  • Panel adhesive: the Panel Adheasive 29OZ row per the template rate; this row is often forgotten.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
There are usually no takeoffs in framing: the rows take the area from the SQFT worksheet. The SF button on the XL strip moves the areas to A2_SQFT_calc; the subfloor is calculated in each Floor Framing List.

A (Label) B (material) C D E Subfloor 3/4" T&G OSB =CEILING(G/32*1.1,1) 4x8 assembly sheet Subfloor FRT 4' 3/4" T&G FRT perimeter x 4 / 32 x 1.1 4x8 FRT note Panel Adheasive 29OZ per template rate pcs Underlayment 1/2" Ply area / 32 x 1.1 4x8 finish schedule Plywood at Tubs 3/4" Ply by number of tubs 4x8 Addendum A Blocking 2x FRT strip perimeter LFT under the FRT edge

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The FRT strip not counted from the perimeter of its own floor, or missed entirely.
  • Underlayment over the whole area, though the detail gives 3/4" ply only under tubs, not under showers.
  • New subfloor over the existing floor not included, though the reconstruction detail calls for it.
  • No panel adhesive row.
  • Balcony and terrace decking counted as house subfloor: they have their own material per the section.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A B C D E Subfloor 3/4" T&G OSB 60 4x8 A501 Subfloor FRT 4' 3/4" T&G FRT 24 4x8 S001 note 12 Panel Adheasive 29OZ 84 pcs Archived photo: an AdvanTech sheet being nailed to the joists. Write the product as in the spec (AdvanTech, 3/4" T&G OSB), not generically.

docs.text:

  • Blocking, Reconstruction

docs.title: Blocking
docs.text: Blocking - short boards between joists or trusses. A solid row is counted in LFT by the row length; rows at 48" o.c. are counted with the formula from the Blocking o.c. page. 2x2 cross bridging between two joists under the subfloor. It is the same takeoff as blocking: one row across the span is counted in LFT by the row length; take the material and row spacing from the framing plan or details. Photo: gotknowhow.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Blocking is short boards between joists, trusses or studs: stiffness, support for panel edges, drywall backing, fireblocking. Kinds: joist blocking, blocking for drywall, bracing for trusses, blocking at eves, parapet blocking, blocking under the FRT subfloor strip, kitchen and bath blocking. Blocking inside wall panels is not counted on a panel job. Rows at a fixed spacing: Blocking o.c.; drywall backing on a wall parallel to the joists: Bracing for Drywall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Framing details, general notes blocking rows between joists, size, spacing, FRT Truss bracing note (per 1/S5.00) bracing for trusses, 2x6 Wall sections blocking at eves, parapet blocking, blocking at the FRT subfloor strip Kitchen and bath elevations blocking for cabinets and grab bars Steel beam details LVL/LSL blocking at steel beams, even when EWP is by others

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line (L) along the blocking row on the framing sheet with the F point; line length = row length. Takeoff framing/<floor> framing/details/<name>: blocking for trusses, bd (drywall), bft, blocking 48, detail number 12/S401. A detail called out on several plans is traced on each one.

Line along where the detail applies: the line length goes to G of the DFL row, the detail name gives the M flag on export.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Export: the DT button puts details into J:L of the floor; the names bft and bd give flags in M (bd bd when doubled), the C_RimBoardBlockingHangers macro lays out the rows. All rows in LFT, D = board length 16.

Tree name A (Label) B (material) C D E details/blocking Blocking joist size (2x10), 11 7/8 TJI =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 detail details/bd Blocking for Drywall 2x4 =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 details details/bft Bracing for Trusses 2x6 by default; anything else only if the truss detail says so by default 1 row for every 10' over the area under the trusses 16 truss detail or assumed details/blocking eves Blocking at Eves 2x6 =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 details/2x6 kitchen Blocking 2x6 4 boards of 14' per kitchen, 1 per bath 14
  • One factor for all rows: blocking, ribbon, ledger, drywall blocking = LFT x 1.1 once in the formula; rim 1.05 only on EWP, otherwise 1.1. The canonical numbers: Formulas.
  • Bracing for trusses: by default 2x6 every 10' over the whole area under the roof, garage included. If the truss detail of this house gives another size or spacing, write it per the detail and add the sheet reference.
  • Walls 10' and taller: two rows of blocking.
  • Exterior blocking is FRT when the exterior wall is FRT. Parapet blocking FRT or P.T. per the detail.
  • Kickers and braces are counted only when they are on a detail: firewall (2) 2x6 @ 48, gable kickers @ 5'.
  • Cross bridging for I-joists TB27: length x 2 x 12 / 16 pcs.
  • EWP by others, but blocking at steel beams is shown: a LVL/LSL blocking row with a note and a measurement.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Bracing for trusses not counted over the whole area under the roof (garage forgotten).
  • Wall panel blocking counted separately on a panel job.
  • Blocking under the edge of the FRT subfloor strip missed.
  • 48" o.c. spacing counted as a solid row, or the other way around.
  • Kickers added "out of habit" though the detail has none; or the detail gives three boards and one is written.
  • Parapet blocking without FRT when the walls are FRT.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A B C D E Blocking 11 7/8 TJI 230 =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 12/S401 Blocking for Drywall 2x4 =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 6/8/9/S400 Bracing for Trusses 2x6 =CEILING(G*1.1/D,1) 16 1/S5.00, template default, verify

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Blocking o.c., Bracing for Drywall, Ribbon Board, Rim Board
  • Formulas: Blocking, COM: Blocking in panelized

docs.title: Blocking o.c.
docs.text: Blocking rows at 48" across the joists: the number of pieces is counted from the zone length and the spacing, not as a solid row.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Blocking o.c. is blocking laid out across the span at a fixed spacing, usually 48" o.c.: flat (laid flat between joists), diagonal (crossed, bridging) or vertical (between studs). It is counted from the zone length and the spacing, not in LFT of a solid row. Solid blocking and all its kinds: Blocking.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Framing notes, typical details row spacing (48" o.c.), type: flat, diagonal, vertical Framing plan zone length along the joists where the rows are needed Wall details (shear, fire) vertical blocking between studs at a spacing

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Line (L) along the joists through the zone (zone length across the rows) on the framing sheet with the F point. Takeoff framing/<floor> framing/details/blocking 48 or with the detail number. The LFT of the line goes to G of the row.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
A (Label) B C (formula, English Excel names) D H Blocking Flat 48" o.c. joist size =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1/D,1) 16 48 Blocking Diagonal 48" o.c. 2x =CEILING(G*12/H*2.5*1.1/D,1) 16 48 Vertical Blocking 16" o.c. 2x4 =CEILING(G*12/H*1.5/D,1) 16 16

What the letters mean: G - zone LFT (line length), H - spacing in inches, D - board length in feet (16), 1.1 - waste, the multiplier - blocking type.

Type Multiplier Flat 2 Diagonal 2.5 Vertical 1.5

The canonical multiplier table: Formulas, Blocking formulas.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• 1.1 added a second time though G already includes waste.
  • Spacing taken from the template, not from the job note.
  • The formula applied to in-panel blocking on a panel job.
  • Plates and wall blocking converted to pcs though the template expects LFT.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A B C D E G H Blocking Flat 48" o.c. 2x10 =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1/D,1) 16 note 7 per S001 240 48

With G = 240 LFT: 240 x 12 / 48 = 60 rows, x 2 = 120 pieces, x 1.1 = 132, / 16 = 9 boards of 16'.

docs.text: • Blocking, Ribbon Board, Formulas

docs.title: Bolts
docs.text: Bolt with washer and nut: three rows in the DFL. Spacing and diameter per the detail; one washer per bolt, two when there is wood on both sides.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Bolts are the bolts from connection details: beam-to-post through bolts, nailer bolts to a steel beam, ledger bolts, holdown bolts. Every bolt row comes with Washers and Nuts rows. We do not count nails: they are bought by the box. Anchors to the foundation (Titen HD, wedge anchor, J-bolt per the SW schedule) have their canonical page at Anchor Bolts; this page covers only connection bolts.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Connection details (post-to-beam, ledger, steel beam nailer) diameter, length, spacing, how many per connection, washer General framing notes typical nailer note: 3/8" bolts staggered @ 24" o.c. Holdown schedule holdown bolts, if not included with the product Scope, client notes ATS rod system by others - do not count

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: A separate measurement is rarely needed: the length comes from the detail Line (details/2x10 ledger + screws, details/nailer), the number of connections from the Count of posts or beams. Point bolts per details: Count (P) with the detail name.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
The blt macro (insert bolts) gives three rows at once. Formulas in pcs; a result under 50 is rounded up to an even number (significance 2).

A (Label) B C D E Anchor Bolts 24" o.c. (2) 3/8" Ø x 6" =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1,2) pcs detail Washers 24" o.c. (2) 3/8" Washers same formula pcs Nuts 24" o.c. (2) Nuts for 3/8" Ø same formula pcs Bolts 1/2" Ø x 8" through connections x bolts per connection pcs beam-to-post detail
  • One washer per bolt; two when there is wood on both sides (through bolt).
  • The washer matches the bolt diameter: a 5/8" bolt does not get a 1/2" washer. A 3x3 plate washer only when the detail or the SW schedule calls for it; otherwise a regular washer.
  • Bolts are written on their own floor, next to the beam or ledger they belong to.
  • Screws need no washers or nuts: Screws.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• One Label for a detail with bolts and a detail with screws.
  • Wrong washer diameter, or 3x3 Square everywhere by default.
  • The nuts or washers row missed.
  • Steel beam nailer bolts missed, nailer counted as single: Steel Beam Web Fillers.
  • ATS rod counted when the scope is by others.
  • Ledger bolts taken from another floor.
  • All floor framing mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A B C D E G H Anchor Bolts 24" o.c. (2) 3/8" Ø x 6" =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1,2) pcs note II.B per S101 86 24 Washers 24" o.c. (2) 3/8" Washers =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1,2) pcs 86 24 Nuts 24" o.c. (2) Nuts for 3/8" Ø =CEILING(G*12/H*2*1.1,2) pcs 86 24

docs.title: Bracing for Drywall
docs.text: The wall runs parallel to the joists: there is no joist above the top plate to hold the ceiling drywall. A 2x4 bracing or ledger along the top of the wall gives that backing. The board length depends on the wall height.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Bracing (drywall bracing, drywall ledger) is 2x4 boards that back the drywall edge where a wall runs parallel to the joists or trusses: on exterior walls on one side, on demising walls on both sides, on corridor walls. These are wall rows, not floor rows, but the board length is picked by the wall height. On a panel job it is always counted, because it is not part of the panel. Blocking between joists: Blocking; ribbon under the joists: Ribbon Board.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor framing plan which walls run parallel to the joists and trusses Wall schedule, sections wall heights by type: ext, corridor, demising Ceiling details, RCP drywall ledger, dropped soffit (a soffit is not bracing)

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: No separate measurement is needed: the length comes from the floor walls (walls/<floor> floor walls/ext ..., corr, dem). If bracing is shown only on part of the walls, draw a Line (L) along those runs in framing/<floor> framing/details/bracing.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Three rows per floor, by wall type. G = LFT of walls of that type, D = board length from the table, C = G / 8 x 1.1: one board for every 8 LFT of wall plus 10%.

A (Label) B C D G Bracing Ext Walls 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) by height LFT of ext walls on the floor Bracing Corridor 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) by height LFT of corridor walls Bracing Demising 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) by height LFT of demising, two sides per the detail

Board length by the tallest wall of the type on the floor (this is the canonical table; COM links here):

Wall height Bracing length up to 10' inclusive 14' over 10' up to 12' 16' over 12' up to 16' 18' over 16' 20'

Export: the WL button on the XL strip moves the walls to A3; the bracing rows are filled from the same LFT. If the detail gives a ledger instead of bracing, Label Blocking for Drywall and the bd flag.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Board length not by wall height: an 11' wall got 14' instead of 16'.
  • Demising counted on one side; the detail gives both.
  • A dropped soffit taken for bracing: soffits are counted on Ceiling / Soffit Framing.
  • On a panel job the bracing was thrown out with the panels, though it is not part of the panel.
  • All wall mistakes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A B C D E G Bracing Ext Walls 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) 16 6/S400 412 Bracing Corridor 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) 16 161 Bracing Demising 2x4 =CEILING(G/8*1.1,1) 16 both sides 648

docs.text:
