docs.text:
• Siding, Siding types, Underlayment, EIFS / Stucco / Veneer
  • Formulas and factors, Client rules, Trim macros

docs.title: Siding
docs.text:
Siding is the field of the exterior wall: lap and clapboard, shingle and shake, panel, board and batten, vinyl, Hardi (fiber cement), cedar, composite. It is counted by area in SQ FT per elevation. A separate scope: trim around the siding is Exterior Trims, and EIFS, stucco, stone and brick veneer are cladding by others.

One elevation, three rows: board and batten on the field, shingle accent in the gable, stone veneer at the bottom (by others). Porch columns and railing are separate takeoffs. Photo: Robert Neustadter, CC BY-SA 4.0, source

docs.title: What is included and in what order
docs.text:
• Siding types

    Lap, shingle, panel, board and batten, vinyl, Hardi, cedar, composite; exposure and material in the row.

    Siding types

  • Underlayment

    WRB per spec, Zip, furring and rainscreen, Cedar Breather, starter, J-channel, flashing.

    Underlayment

  • EIFS / Stucco / Veneer

    What it is, how to recognize it, why it is by others, what next to it stays ours.

    EIFS / Stucco / Veneer

  • Measuring

    Area by elevation in OurPlanCore, gables and accents separately, deductions, waste, by others.

    Measuring

docs.title: Count it or not
docs.text: Cladding Count it? Why Lap, shingle, panel, board and batten (wood, vinyl, Hardi, composite) yes wall field, SQ FT EIFS, stucco no, except the WRB, sheathing, furring and trim next to it finish system by others Stone, brick veneer no, except the WRB, sheathing, furring and trim next to it masonry by others Siding by others / TBD 0 plus a note client or another trade

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Read the notes on the elevations: siding material, exposure, where the accent is, where stone or EIFS is. Write the note into the DFL right away (Note: Siding is Hardi; verify if Trims are Hardi or PVC).
  2. Open the wall sections: WRB per spec, furring, Cedar Breather.
  3. Trace the areas by elevation, wall by wall; gables, dormers, bays and accents as separate items.
  4. Deductions by the rule: large openings once, windows under 4' are not deducted.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: The siding root in the building tree, an Area per item for each material and color: 6" vertical, panel grey, shingle gable. Elevation sheets (el) have no point, so check that the item landed in siding. Details: Measuring.

docs.title: DFL row
docs.text:
A Description B Size C Qty D Unit E Siding Hardi plank 6" exp =L+R+Front+Rear SQ FT A201 Siding Gable front Vinyl Shingles =... SQ FT A201 Siding 2 Boral TruExt 1x10 Shiplap =... SQ FT A202 Siding Per customer TBD 0 SQ FT note

Material and exposure always in the row; gable and accent separately; the unit is SQ FT, not LFT.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• WRB called Vapor Barrier, or Tyvek when the spec calls for fluid-applied.
  • Stone or EIFS counted as siding.
  • The gable accent merged with the field of another material.
  • The measured area not moved to Excel or not updated after edits.
  • All sheathing and WRB mistakes: Sheathing.

docs.text:

  • Wall Sheathing, Material catalog, Standard notes

docs.title: Siding types
docs.text: Material, profile and exposure (6" exp, 5-1/2" to weather) are part of the product: always in the DFL row. How to measure the area: Measuring.

docs.title: Lap / Clapboard
docs.text:
Lap siding: overlapping boards, the visible course width is the exposure. Count the SQ FT of the field, write the exposure in the row. Photo: Daniel Case, CC BY-SA 3.0, source Row example Note Hardi plank 6" exp fiber cement, 6" exposure 4" Ext Clapboard 4" exposure Vinyl clapboard Dutch lap, double 4", 4-1/2" Red Cedar clapboard cedar, verify grade Clapboard material not specified: verify material in the note

Vinyl lap comes with starter strip, J-channel and corner posts; these are accessories from Underlayment.

docs.title: Shingle / Shake
docs.text:
Cedar shake on the wall field. Waste is higher than for lap; on a solid substrate under the shakes Cedar Breather is needed. Photo: EgorovaSvetlana, CC BY-SA 4.0, source Row example Note Cedar shingles "Perfection" 5-1/2" to weather 5-1/2" exposure Vinyl Shingles vinyl shake panel Vinyl Shingles (gable) gable accent, separate row

A gable shingle accent is almost always a separate row from the field. A flare (the wall flaring out under shingles) has its own blocking and trim: Porch / Deck / Balcony.

docs.title: Panel / Board and batten / Shiplap
docs.text:
Fiber cement panel siding: large sheets on exposed fasteners, joints on a grid. Count the SQ FT of the field plus LFT of joints for Z-flashing or battens and trim at the edges. Photo: engineeredassemblies.com, source, found via Pinterest. Row example Note Hardipanel siding fiber cement panel; Z-flashing at horizontal joints Boral TruExt 1x10 Shiplap composite shiplap, product in the row 1/2" Panel panel at bays and gable Board & Batten board plus batten; battens in LFT if counted separately 1x6 Vert. Cedar BDS. vertical cedar board Wainscotting accent panel

Board and batten on the field, shingle in the gable and stone at the bottom on one elevation: three rows, see the photo on the overview page.

docs.title: By material
docs.text: Material What it changes in the takeoff Vinyl starter, J-channel, corners, undersill are accessories; Vinyl J-channel can be the casing Fiber cement (Hardi) plank, panel or shingle; note verify if Trims are Hardi or PVC Cedar clapboard, shingle, vertical; verify grade; Cedar Breather under shingle Composite (Boral TruExt, LP SmartSide) product in the row Wood clapboard grade and primed in the note (primed vertical grain cedar) Aluminum, steel rare; usually by others, check the scope

docs.title: Orientation and neighboring rows
docs.text: Keep Siding Horizontal (lap) and Siding Vertical (board and batten, 1x6 Vert. Cedar) separate if the template splits them. Next to the siding field there are often Post Wrap (1x10 / 1x12) and Fascia (1x8 / 1x12); that is trim: Exterior Trims.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Exposure and material dropped from the row.
  • Field and gable accent in one row.
  • Vinyl accessories not counted as trim.
  • Cedar shingle without Cedar Breather on a solid substrate.
  • Panel without Z-flashing at the joints.
  • All sheathing mistakes: Sheathing.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Siding, Underlayment, Measuring, EIFS / Stucco / Veneer
  • Casing, Corner & Band, Material catalog

docs.title: Underlayment
docs.text: House corner before siding: vertical furring strips (rainscreen) nailed over sheathing that doubles as the WRB, tape at the joint with the foundation at the bottom. Furring is counted in LFT by spacing over the wall area, WRB in SQ FT by the wall area. Photo: greenbuildingadvisor.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The layers between the siding and the frame that are not visible on the elevation: WRB (weather resistive barrier), sheathing, furring or rainscreen, Cedar Breather, starter, J-channel and corner posts, flashing. Look at the wall sections and wall types, not only the elevations. Sheathing is counted in Wall Sheathing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall types (wt) and wall sections Layer order: siding, furring, WRB, sheathing, studs Spec division 07 and notes WRB product: housewrap (Tyvek), fluid-applied, self-adhered, Zip Window and joint details Z-flashing, head flashing, kickout, step flashing Elevations Vinyl: where the starter, J-channel, corners go

docs.title: Wall layers, outside to inside
docs.text:
1. Siding (the field, SQ FT), see Siding types.
  2. Furring or rainscreen 1x4 / 2x4, P.T. or not (if shown).
  3. WRB per spec, or Zip (WRB built into the sheathing).
  4. Sheathing (CDX, OSB, Zip): its own scope.
  5. Stud wall.
Siding, furring, WRB, sheathing, stud. The WRB is named per the spec; with Zip the barrier is already built into the panel.

docs.title: WRB, not Vapor Barrier
docs.text:
DFL row Material Unit Rule WRB Tyvek or another housewrap SQ FT only if the spec names a housewrap WRB fluid-applied (product per spec) SQ FT do not write Tyvek Zip system 7/16" Zip + Zip Tape 4x8, rolls no separate WRB needed, do not duplicate
  • The exterior barrier is called WRB, weather barrier or air barrier. Vapor Barrier is a different layer in a different place in the wall; do not name the row that way.
  • WRB area equals the wall area with openings deducted once; windows under 4' are not deducted. Exterior gypsum porch and canopy soffits also go into the WRB.
  • The WRB spec cell in the DFL header (O4) is filled in when the job is created; the sheet reference goes without the word per (A3.0).

docs.title: Furring / Rainscreen
docs.text: The strip between the WRB and the siding, often missed. 1x4 or 2x4, P.T. or not per the section; LFT by spacing, or SQ FT if solid. The full rule and jambs: Furring & Window Jambs.

docs.title: Cedar Breather
docs.text: A ventilated mat under cedar shingles or shakes on a solid substrate. Counted in SQ FT of the shingle walls; check the details if the siding is cedar shingle on solid sheathing.

docs.title: Vinyl accessories
docs.text:
DFL row Where Unit Starter strip bottom of the first course LFT J-Channel around windows and doors, under the soffit, at corners, along the rake LFT Corner posts (outside, inside) corners LFT Undersill / finish trim under the window, at the top of the wall LFT

With vinyl, Ext. Casing is often the Vinyl J-channel itself: do not duplicate it with 5/4 wood casing. Canonical page: Exclusions and J-Channel.

docs.title: Flashing in siding
docs.text:
Flashing Where Unit Z-flashing horizontal joints of panel siding LFT Head flashing / drip cap over windows, doors, head trim LFT Kickout flashing where the roof meets the wall pcs Step flashing along the roof slope at the wall LFT Band / watertable flashing under the horizontal band LFT

Flashing as a visible row; do not dissolve it into the siding SQ FT. Window flashing in detail: Window flashing.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Vapor Barrier instead of WRB; Tyvek when the spec calls for fluid-applied.
  • Zip and a separate housewrap counted together.
  • Furring missed because it is not on the elevation.
  • Openings not deducted from the WRB, or deducted twice.
  • All sheathing mistakes: Sheathing.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
WRB            fluid-applied (per spec 07 27 26)   8 420  SQ FT   =C<walls SF>-C<openings>   A3.0
Furring        1x4 P.T. @ 16" o.c.                 6 950  LFT     =CEILING(8420*12/16*1.1,10) 7/A401
Cedar Breather                                     1 240  SQ FT   gable shingle areas          A201

docs.text:

  • Material catalog

docs.title: Floor SQFT
docs.text: Area along the outside outline of the floor on the sheet with the W point, name 1st. Shafts and open to below are holes inside the polygon. The area goes to the Front Page and to every "per SQFT" row.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Floor SQFT is the floor area of each level measured to the outside outline. It feeds the Front Page, subfloor and floor layers, blocking and other "per SQFT" rows. Keep the floors separate even if they are identical: 1st, 2nd, 3rd. The other pages of this section (basement, loft, roof, deck, porch, balcony, cantilevered) follow the same rules with the specifics of their type.

docs.title: General area rules
docs.text:
1. Area tool along the real outside outline on the plan sheet with the W point (a101 1st). Sheet scale checked against a known dimension.
  2. Shafts, stair openings and open to below are holes inside the polygon or a separate open to below deduction; not both.
  3. One type on one building can be built from several polygons in one takeoff. Do not join separate zones with a bridge.
  4. Do not draw a rectangle to hit a known SQFT number: the outline must match the plan.
  5. Name = a token the export understands: base, 1st...8th, blcny, porch, deck, cant, rf 6, flat, conc areas, open to below. An Area with such a name goes to sqfts by itself; there are no floor subfolders inside sqfts.
  6. The area must reach Excel and update when the takeoff is edited: compare the number in the workbook with the app before delivery.
  7. Linear exclusions (cat walk 4') are a length with a known width, not an Area.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans (a101 1st, a102 2nd) Floor outline, shafts, open to below Framing plans (s201 2nd) Joist direction and zones (that is already a J Area, not SQFT) Sections (sec) Which levels exist: basement, loft, mezzanine Floor assemblies (ft) What goes over the area: subfloor, underlayment, sound mat

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/1st Front Page, 1st Floor SQ FT as measured sqfts/1st Subfloor 3/4" T&G 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) sqfts/1st Panel Adheasive 29OZ pcs per template sqfts/1st Underlayment and layers per assembly per Floor Sheathing 4x8 same sqfts/open to below deduction SQ FT minus

Export: the XL strip, SF button, moves the sqfts branch to the Front Page and the template spec cells.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Floors merged into one area, or one floor copied to another with someone else's formulas.
  • A shaft deducted twice (hole plus separate deduction).
  • A rectangle "to hit the number" instead of the plan outline.
  • Area fixed in the app, the old one left in Excel.
  • Porch and balcony empty on the Front Page (they are counted separately, see Porch, Balcony).

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/sqfts/
  base             Area   1620 SF
  1st              Area   1741 SF   (2 polygons: house and addition)
  2nd              Area   1690 SF
  open to below    Area     84 SF
  blcny            Area    112 SF
  rf 6             Area   2210 SF
Floor SQFT gives sheets: SQFT / 32 x 1.1, rounded up to a whole sheet. Floors separate.

docs.text:

docs.title: Balcony SQFT
docs.text: Balcony: frame, sleepers, membrane, decking. The area is an Area blcny; typical balconies are marked as blocks with a point for every instance.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A balcony is a raised exterior platform, cantilevered or on its own frame, attached to the building. The area gives the decking and build-up; the frame and railing go in separate rows. Do not join balconies with a bridge into one polygon and do not mix them with a porch: they are different blocks with different multipliers. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans, unit plans (u) Outline, balcony type per unit, number of repeats Framing plans, details (S) Cantilever or frame, end joists, hangers, beam-to-post connections Details (d) Decking 2x6 DuxxBak, sleepers, membrane, railing system Elevations Side and floor of every balcony

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the decking outline of one balcony, name blcny. Identical balconies: polygons in one takeoff, or one polygon plus a multiplier in the block.
  2. Typical balconies: one Count takeoff per type (#4 Balcony 12.9x7.83), a point for every instance, unit, side and floor in the Notes; folder Balcony blocks. The number of instances comes from the points, not from the area.
  3. A cantilevered balcony changes the rim, blocking and holdowns: see Cantilevered.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row (Balcony block) Material Unit Formula sqfts/blcny Front Page, Balconies SQ FT as measured x units sqfts/blcny Decking 2x6 DuxxBak per spec SQ FT SQFT x 1.1 x units Line along the edge Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T. 2 per balcony pcs =2*G same line Rails (top & bottom), Balustrades, Cap Rail or a composite system per detail LFT, pcs Railing

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A balcony block without its own units multiplier (900 SF instead of 60).
  • Balconies joined with a bridge into one polygon.
  • Sheathing added where the detail gives decking with no sheathing.
  • Railing counted by components and as a system at the same time.
  • Balcony trims merged with the general exterior trims.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

  blcny               Area   58 SF
Takeoffs/Main/Balcony blocks/

Balcony #4
Decking        2x6 DuxxBak     447   SQ FT   58 x 7 x 1.1
Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T.         14   pcs

docs.title: Basement SQFT
docs.text: Basement Area along the slab outline, name base. The area is needed for the Front Page and for whatever goes on the slab: sleepers, underlayment, insulation per the assembly.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Basement SQFT is the area of the lowest level on the slab. Unlike the floors above, there is usually no subfloor on joists here: the area drives over-slab layers (sleepers, underlayment, rigid) only when the assembly shows them. Basement wall framing (studs, P.T. plates, box sheathing) is a separate page: Basement Walls. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Basement plan (a100 base) Slab outline, stair opening, mech areas Foundation plan (s101 f) What is concrete, what is wood; existing or podium Floor assemblies (ft), sections Over-slab: sleepers, underlayment, insulation Code / finish notes Finished basement or not

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the slab outline on the a100 base sheet (W point). Name base (not bsmt): the token goes to sqfts.
  2. A basement under part of the house: only that part; crawl space separately, if needed.
  3. Do not count existing or podium conditions as standard panels without details.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/base Front Page, Basement SQ FT as measured sqfts/base Sleepers 2x4 P.T. per detail LFT by spacing sqfts/base Plywood / Underlayment over slab per assembly 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) sqfts/base Rigid Insulation over slab per assembly SQ FT as measured

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Plywood and sleepers on the slab missed because "it is concrete there".
  • Name bsmt instead of base: the area did not go to sqfts.
  • Basement measured to the 1st floor outline, not to the slab.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

Basement
Sleepers        2x4 P.T. 16" o.c.    1340   LFT   8/A500
Plywood         3/4" T&G              56   4x8   over sleepers

docs.title: Cantilevered SQFT
docs.text: The joists run past the bearing to the outside. On the cantilever the rim, blocking and often holdowns change, and a soffit appears underneath. The cantilever area is a separate Area cant.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A cantilever is part of a floor, roof or deck that extends past the bearing with no post underneath. The cantilever area is counted separately because it has a different rim, extra blocking, FRT per the exterior wall rules, and a soffit underneath. In the deliverable keep a visible Cantilevered label so it is clear why the area is separated. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Framing plan (S) Where the joists run past the wall; direction, cantilever length Details (d) Rim on the cantilever, blocking over the bearing, straps or holdowns, soffit Sections (sec) Height and layers underneath (soffit, insulation) Floor plan (A) Cantilever outline (bay, bump-out)

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the cantilever outline on the floor framing plan (W point). Name cant.
  2. The cantilever joists are drawn with the J Area as part of the joist zone; the cant area is needed for the soffit, rim and blocking, not for counting the joists a second time.
  3. The soffit under the cantilever is Soffits at Floor Overhangs by length or area (Soffit and Fascia).

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/cant Cantilevered label in the floor block SQ FT as measured cantilever perimeter Rim Board per detail, FRT if the exterior wall is FRT LFT x 1.1 bearing line Blocking 2x between joists over the wall LFT per detail underneath Soffits at Floor Overhangs 1x12 / Vinyl / 5/8" Ext Gyp LFT / SQ FT details Holdowns / straps only if shown pcs

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The cantilever dissolved into the floor area, the rim and blocking on it not changed.
  • The soffit underneath forgotten.
  • Holdowns or straps added without a detail (or missed when there is one).
  • Cantilever joists counted a second time through the area.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

2nd Floor Framing List
Rim Board (Cantilevered)   11-7/8" LSL Rim   26   LFT   3/S401
Blocking                   2x12              22   LFT   over wall

docs.title: Deck SQFT
docs.text: Deck: ledger to the house, joists on hangers, beam on posts, decking, railing. The decking area is an Area deck; frame and railing are on their own pages.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A deck is an open exterior platform with no roof, on its own frame. The decking area gives the decking, sleepers and underlayment per the detail; the frame (ledger, joists, beams, posts) is counted on the Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame page. On many COM jobs the deck is not in scope: check, do not assume. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plan / site plan (A) Deck outline, stairs Deck framing plan, details (S) Ledger, joists, beams, posts, attachment (bolts, screws) Details (d) Decking material, sleepers, underlayment, railing Scope Whether the deck is in the job

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the decking outline on the plan (W point). Name deck; several decks of one type are polygons in one takeoff, different types are different takeoffs.
  2. Deck stairs are not part of the area: stringers and steps separately.
  3. Railing is a Line along the open perimeter, in trims or framing per the agreed tree.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/deck Front Page, Deck SQ FT as measured sqfts/deck Decking composite / 5/4x6 P.T. per spec SQ FT or LFT SQFT x 1.1 sqfts/deck Underlayment 1/2" per detail 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) Line along the edge Railing, Posts at Rails 4x4 P.T. per detail LFT, pcs Railing

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Deck counted though it is not in scope (or the other way around).
  • LVL rim used by default: only when a deck attaches to it.
  • Railing and stairs forgotten; guards as a separate row.
  • Deck area assigned to a house floor.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

Ground Decks Framing List

Posts at Rails  4x4 P.T.          8   pcs

docs.title: Loft SQFT
docs.text: Loft: the loft floor inside the volume of a story plus a guard along the open edge. The area is a separate Area, not part of the floor below.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A loft is a loft or mezzanine inside the volume of a story, often over part of the plan. Its area is counted separately from the floor below it: it drives its own subfloor, its own joists and the guard along the open edge. On the Front Page the level is called Loft, not the next floor number. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Loft / mezzanine plan (A) Floor outline, open edge, stair Sections (sec) Height, framing type: floor framing, roof framing or by others Framing plan (S) Loft joists, beams, bearing; depth and hangers Door / guard notes Guard along the open edge

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the loft floor outline on the loft plan sheet (W point). Name loft.
  2. The open edge (over the room below) is not part of the loft area, but it is needed as the guard length: a Line in trims or framing per the agreed tree.
  3. Confirm the framing type: floor joists, roof-type or by others; that decides where the joists go (Joist).

To be confirmed

The loft token in the name auto-routing is not confirmed: check that the takeoff landed in sqfts; otherwise move it, or add a rule in Settings > Takeoff Name Routing.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/loft Front Page, Loft SQ FT as measured sqfts/loft Subfloor in Loft Framing List 3/4" T&G 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) Line along the open edge Railing / guard per detail LFT

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Loft not found: it is on the architectural sheets, the framing is on the structural ones.
  • Guard along the open perimeter forgotten.
  • Loft written as 5th instead of Loft on the Front Page.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

Loft Framing List
Joists 16" o.c.    2x10     ...   LFT   S203
Subfloor           3/4" T&G  12   4x8

docs.title: Porch SQFT
docs.text: Porch: a floor on its own frame and a ceiling (soffit) under the roof. The floor area is an Area porch; the roof over the porch is its own Area in roof.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A porch is a covered platform at an entry, on its own frame. Its area gives the floor (decking or subfloor) and the ceiling (5/8" Gyp exterior, two surfaces in one row with x2). The roof over the porch is a separate area per Roof SQFT; the porch eave is a separate takeoff eve 12 porch. A porch is counted on its own, separately from balconies, even if it looks similar. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plan (a101 1st) Porch outline, posts Framing plan, details (S) Ceiling joists, ledger, hangers, beams, posts; framing not shown - Note RCP (rcp) Ceiling material: 5/8" Ext Gyp, DensGlass, beadboard Elevations, sections Porch roof, pitch, columns

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the porch floor outline on the plan (W point). Name porch. Several identical porches are polygons in one takeoff; different types are different takeoffs.
  2. Typical porches in a multifamily building are marked as blocks: one Count takeoff per type, a point for every instance (see Deck / Porch / Balcony Frame).
  3. Trace the porch roof in sqfts separately (rf 4 porch or rf mtl 4).

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text:
Tree name DFL row (Porch block) Material Unit Formula sqfts/porch Front Page, Porches SQ FT as measured sqfts/porch Decking or Subfloor per detail SQ FT / 4x8 SQFT x 1.1 or /32 sqfts/porch Ceiling 5/8" Gyp exterior SQ FT SQFT x 2 x 1.1 same area Ceiling Joists 16" o.c. + Ledger + Hangers per detail LFT, pcs separate from rafters posts Posts P.T. outdoors; under the roof no P.T. pcs

Framing not shown: Note: Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify right under the block header.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Porch SQFT empty on the Front Page (the house total did not add up).
  • Porch mirrored from the balconies instead of counted separately.
  • Porch ceiling counted as regular interior gypsum, not exterior.
  • Porch roof ended up in the main rf 6 with the wrong pitch.
  • Porch eave counted again inside eve 24 main.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/sqfts/
  porch       Area   96 SF
  rf 4        Area  118 SF   (porch roof)
Covered Front Porch Framing List
Note: Porch framing is not specified; all framing assumed; verify.

Ceiling                   5/8" Gyp     212   SQ FT   x2

docs.title: Roof SQFT
docs.text: The Area is drawn along the plan projection of the roof plane; the name carries the pitch: rf 6. The pitch factor is applied once in Excel.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Roof SQFT is the roof area in plan, split by pitch and type: main planes, overframe, metal, flat areas, garage, porch. It drives the roof sheathing, clips, flat roof layers and roofing materials in scope. General measuring rules: Floor SQFT, rules section.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Arch roof plan (a105 rf) Roof plane outlines, the 6:12 pitch on each, overframe, flat Elevations (el) Pitch, if the plan does not show it; separate porch and garage roofs Sections (sec) Flat vs pitched, canopy, stair lid Roof framing plan (S) Truss and rafter boundaries, sheathing product

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area along the plan projection of every roof plane on the roof plan (W point). One pitch and one material = one takeoff; planes of the same pitch can be collected as polygons in one takeoff.
  2. Name rf <pitch>: rf 6 = 6:12, rf mtl 4 (under metal), overframe 4, flat, ply flat, flat grge, elev rf flat. The number = rise per 12.
  3. Garage, porch, porte cochere, storage get their own outlines and pitches, even if the house next to them is 6:12. Do not carry a pitch over from the previous house.
  4. The pitch correction sqrt(1+(rise/12)^2) (4:12 = 1.054, 6:12 = 1.118, 8:12 = 1.202, 12:12 = 1.414) is applied once in the Excel formula. The name rf 6 does not change the geometry.
  5. Do not add overframe automatically; the lower sheathing under an overframe is per the detail.

docs.title: Tree name and DFL row
docs.text: Tree name DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/rf 6 Front Page, Roof SQ FT as measured sqfts/rf 6 Roof Sheathing 19/32" Ply or OSB 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT*1.118/32*1.1,1) sqfts/rf 6 Clips PSCL 19/32 pcs H-clips sqfts/flat Rigid Insulation, Densdeck, EPDM per assembly SQ FT same area sqfts/rf mtl 4 Roof Sheathing (metal) 1/2" Ply 4x8 with 1.054

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Pitch not from the sheet (6:12 instead of 4:12 on the garage: 53 sheets instead of 50, 212 clips instead of 200).
  • Pitch factor applied twice or not at all.
  • All roof planes in one polygon with no split by pitch and material.
  • Flat roof layers (Densdeck, XPS) missed, piggy sleepers forgotten.
  • The soffit underneath taken as the sheathing area.

All area mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/sqfts/
  rf 6            Area   2210 SF
  overframe 4     Area    180 SF
  rf mtl 4        Area    410 SF
  flat            Area    960 SF
Takeoffs/Grge/sqfts/
  rf 4            Area   1420 SF
Roof plan: every roof plane is its own polygon. Gable triangles are not part of the roof area. Archived render.

  • Truss Heel, Overframes

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: The header sits on jack studs, king studs hold the pack at the sides. (2) and (3) in the name are the number of plies. Exterior wall from the inside: over each window a doubled header sits on jack studs, king studs at the sides, a sill with cripples under the window. Each opening gives one header on the ext row at the size from the header schedule; cripples and jacks are not part of the header. Photo: thespruce.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A header is a beam over an opening in a wall; it carries the load down to the jack studs. Exterior (ext) and interior (int) headers are counted separately, the size and number of plies come from the header schedule, not from the window width. On a panel job headers inside panels are not counted, only flush and loose. A roof header is a different topic: Roof Framing: Header.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Header schedule (S), typical wall details Mark and size by span and floor: H228, HPA, (3) 2x10 Tagged plans (s102) Marks over openings, where the engineer showed them Window and door schedule, elevations Opening width, combined openings Panel drawings, scope What is inside the panel, what is flush or loose Code summary FRT on headers in the plane of the exterior wall on Type III

docs.title: Size when there is no header schedule
docs.text:
The size from the header schedule and from the plans always wins. When there is no schedule (usually residential), use the E-Wood defaults by span, that is, by opening width:

Where the header is up to 4' up to 6' 6'-9' 9'-12' 12'-14' 14'-16' 16'-18' Exterior bearing wall 2x6 (Exterior brg wall) (2) 2x10 (3) 2x10 (2) 9-1/2" LVL (2) 11-7/8" LVL (2) 14" LVL (2) 16" LVL (3) 16" LVL Interior bearing wall 2x4 (Interior brg wall) (2) 2x10 (2) 2x12 (2) 9-1/2" LVL (2) 11-7/8" LVL (2) 14" LVL (2) 14" LVL (2) 16" LVL Flush header or beam under floor framing (2) 2x at joist depth with 2x joists, (2) LVL with I-joists same as up to 4' (2) LVL at joist depth (2) LVL at joist depth (3) LVL at joist depth (3) LVL at joist depth (3) 14" LVL Flush header or beam under floor framing and roof (under an exterior wall) (3) 9-1/2" LVL (3) 11-7/8" LVL (3) 14" LVL (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL

Garage center beam, by span:

Load 22' 24' 26' Floor above (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL (3) 24" LVL Ceiling load only (3) 14" LVL (3) 16" LVL (3) 18" LVL

Write the size taken from the table as a note at the header or beam row (see DFL notes), so it is clear it did not come from a schedule.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Count tool (point), one per physical header, or Beam along the span between supports: Beam measures the length itself and rounds it in the name (up to 8', up to the next whole foot; longer, to an even number).

  1. Branch framing/<floor> framing/headers/ext/ and .../headers/int/. The F dot on an S sheet puts the Count into framing/<floor> framing; then move it into headers/ext or select the folder before New Item.
  2. Name: ext H228 4, int H228 4, HPA 4, ext (3) 2x10 8: side, mark or size with plies, order length in feet.
  3. The folder floor is the real bearing scope, not the number of the architectural elevation.
  4. One built-up header = one point with (n); do not place n points.
  5. A storefront of several windows does not necessarily give as many headers; a combined opening can have one common header.
  6. Keep a wood header separate from a steel member and its nailer.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
The HD button on the XL strip puts headers into the wall block of the floor below; the side ext / int is taken from the name. In the LG legend the row HP2 - (2) 2x10 gives the size by code, otherwise the code itself lands in B.

Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor ext H228 4 Ext. Headers (2) up to 48" 2x8 pcs count x plies, length from the name ext H228 7 Ext. Headers (2) up to 72" pcs ext (3) 2x10 8 Ext. Headers (3) over 72" 2x10 pcs three boards per header int H228 4 Int. Headers (2) pcs 9.0x6.8 gd garage door Garage headers (3) pcs per schedule not on the plan note The headers indicated on the plan... black bold text, no fill

If the exterior wall is FRT, the headers in its plane are FRT too; LVL/PSL are not used in the plane of the exterior wall on Type III. Note samples: DFL notes.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Header derived from the window width: different bearing conditions give different marks.
  • (3) entered as one board.
  • Headers inside panels counted on a panel job.
  • Floor taken from the elevation, not from the bearing scope; the upper floors have different sizes.
  • Exterior headers without FRT on Type III (on one check: the whole 4th floor).
  • One combined opening written as two headers.

Walkthrough with examples: all opening mistakes.

docs.text:
framing/2nd floor framing/headers/
  ext/
    ext H228 4        Count, 14 ea
    ext (3) 2x10 8    Count, 2 ea     Notes: 4/S501, FRT per A001
  int/
    int H228 4        Count, 9 ea

  • DFL row labels

docs.title: Window Flashing & Sill
docs.text: Window Flashing covers three sides (head and two jambs), Sill Flashing is the pan at the bottom. A door has only three sides: at the bottom there is a threshold, not a pan. Window rough opening before install: the tape on the two jambs and the head goes on the Window Flashing row, the pan tape along the bottom of the opening, turned up onto the wall, goes on Sill Flashing. Lengths come from the W and H of the opening. Photo: terrylove.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Flashing around windows and doors is our scope, even when the wall framing is by others. Two different rows: Window Flashing (tape on the head and both jambs) and Sill Flashing (the pan under the window). Doors have no sill flashing. Roof, wall and deck flashing are on another page: Flashing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Window and door schedule W and H for the flashing length Wall type schedule Wall type at the opening: wood, metal stud, CMU or concrete Window head, jamb, sill details Flashing tape, sill pan, wood jamb on CMU Specs, WRB notes Flashing tape product, compatibility with the WRB

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Flashing is not drawn separately. It is figured from Openings: the OP button on the XL strip moves the openings into the workbook, and the F_Openings macro outputs Window Flashing and Sill Flashing per the rules below. Your job on the sheet: the right type (window with no suffix, door d, garage door gd) and the size from the schedule. Do not type lengths in by hand.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
DFL row Material Unit Formula Window Flashing Flashing Tape LFT (2 x H + W) x qty Sill Flashing Sill Flashing LFT W x qty Door Flashing (3 sides) Flashing Tape LFT (2 x H + W) x qty; no sill Window Flashing at Mtl Walls, Sill Flashing at Mtl Walls same LFT separate rows for metal walls Window Flashing at CMU Walls, Sill Flashing at CMU Walls same LFT separate rows for CMU and concrete Window Jamb at CMU/Concrete 1x4 P.T. or 2x4 P.T. LFT per detail; flashing is counted even without a jamb
  • Wood walls: the base row is always there. Mtl and CMU walls are added on separate rows, even if the detail geometry is the same: for the client these are different subcontractors and different WRBs.
  • Sides + head = Window Flashing, bottom = Sill Flashing: two rows, do not combine them.
  • On CMU and concrete the flashing has no nailing plane: the detail often shows a wood jamb 1x4 P.T. or 2x4 P.T. around the perimeter, and the tape and casing attach to it. Jamb logic: Furring & Window Jambs.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A door got Sill Flashing: the d or gd tag is missing.
  • Wood, Mtl and CMU walls merged into one row.
  • Size taken from the elevation instead of the schedule.
  • P.T. wood jamb on CMU not checked.
  • Flashing on metal walls missed "because the wall is by others".

Walkthrough with examples: all opening mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Window Flashing            Flashing Tape     LFT   =(2*5.0+3.0)*12
Sill Flashing              Sill Flashing     LFT   =3.0*12
Window Flashing at Mtl Walls   Flashing Tape   LFT   =(2*7.8+4.3)*6
Window Jamb at CMU         2x4 P.T.          LFT   =(2*4.0+2.9)*4

docs.title: Windows and Doors
docs.text: The Openings tool on an elevation: a box around the opening, the app writes the size name 3.0x5.0 itself and places a point in the center. One point is one physical opening.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Openings are all the holes in the exterior wall: windows, exterior and patio doors, garage doors, storefront, exterior louvers. They give a header, jamb studs, flashing and a deduction from the sheathing. Interior doors are a separate scope (doors, jambs, casing), not openings. Headers are counted on their own page, Headers.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Elevations a201 el Window and door marks (diamonds), floor by the elevations on that view Window schedule, window types (win sch) Unit size; the general notes say whether it is the R.O. or the unit size Door schedule (dr sch) Size, material, fire label: 3070 HM C-lbl Floor plans Door tags, storefront, garage doors; windows with no marks on the elevation Sheets of another building A type width that is missing on your own sheet (write it in Notes)

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Openings tool (O key), the result is a Count/point with the size.

  1. Drag a box around the opening on the ... el elevation: the app measures WxH in feet and creates a takeoff named with the size. If the marks are on the plans, draw on the plans.
  2. Floor folders sit directly under openings: 0 (below the 1st), 1, 2, roof. No windows and doors subfolders. The point's floor is between the floor elevations of that view; stair windows half a level lower go to the lower floor.
  3. Name W.WxH.H in decimal feet, one digit after the point: 5.8x5.9. Doors d (3.3x6.5 d), garage doors gd (9.0x6.8 gd), louvers lv. Different marks of the same size are one takeoff. Write the mark, sheet and R.O. in Notes: Note: A601 type W1, RO 3'-0" x 5'-0".
  4. Size comes from the schedule, not from the line length on the elevation. Window height = unit height, not the top elevation (7'-2" on the drawing is often the head elevation).
  5. One point per opening, the point inside the opening. One color per size, the same on all floors.
  6. Do not count twice: a window on a matchline is taken in the view where it is whole; a faded background with no marks is not counted; a sash of a combined window is not a window.
  7. Storefront, multi-slide, garage doors, HM doors with no type: separately, each from its own size source. A full storefront once; its door is not a second hole.

The size name is needed by the OP button on the XL strip: it reads WxH from the name and moves the openings into the workbook, where the F_Openings macro figures the flashing.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor openings/1/3.0x5.0 Window Flashing + Sill Flashing LFT (2H + W) x qty, W x qty openings/1/3.3x6.5 d Ext. Doors 3070 1 unit MARK FIRE LABEL; flashing on 3 sides ea, LFT no sill flashing openings/1/9.0x6.8 gd Garage headers (3), flashing on 3 sides ea, LFT no sill openings/1/2.0x2.0 lv louver, deduction from the sheathing ea interior doors Int. Doors 2670 ..., jambs by the size of the adjacent wall ea a door wider than 4' is a double (2)2670
  • Door casing on 3 sides in LFT; interior door jambs are counted as points per unit and grouped by wall size (a point at 2x6 = 2x6 jamb).
  • Hardware numbers are not needed in the DFL; material and fire rating are.
  • Openings are subtracted from the sheathing, WRB, insulation and foundation line once and on their own floor. Windows smaller than 4' are not subtracted from the sheathing: Wall Sheathing.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Window height taken as the top elevation, not the unit height.
  • Opening counted twice: on the plan and the elevation, from two views, the storefront door separately.
  • The d tag missing: the door got Sill Flashing.
  • Openings not subtracted from the sheathing and WRB (garage doors) or subtracted twice.
  • A door wider than 4' written as a single leaf.
  • Size eyeballed from the elevation instead of taken from the schedule; R.O. confused with the unit size.

Walkthrough with examples: all opening mistakes.

  1/

  roof/

Grge/openings/

docs.title: Box Sheathing
docs.text: Box sheathing covers the floor framing "box" between the wall below and the wall above: rim, joist ends, subfloor. A narrow strip, not the whole wall.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Box sheathing is a narrow horizontal strip of sheathing around the exterior perimeter at the floor framing level: it covers the rim board, the joist ends and the subfloor between the top plate of the wall below and the bottom plate of the wall above. On a panel job the walls arrive sheathed, but this strip stays loose material, so it lives on its own row. Do not confuse it with Truss Heel (the strip at the roof) or with full wall sheathing (Wall Sheathing).

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall section (sec), floor framing detail Strip height: joist depth + subfloor + plates per section; material Floor type schedule (ft) Floor framing depth (TJI 11 7/8", 2x10, 14" open web) Panel notes, scope Whether the box is in the panel or stays loose Attic / roof sections Attic box: extra plate + box = subfloor on the top floor

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
There is no separate takeoff: length = the floor's exterior perimeter from the walls/<floor> floor walls/ext ... lines, strip height = floor framing depth with subfloor per the section of this building. Area = perimeter x height. The Excel export (XL strip) puts Box Sheathing at the end of each floor's wall section with its own Tape row.

  • Each floor has its own strip: 1st, 2nd, 3rd. For the top floor under a parapet the box is written into the parapet block with a Note.
  • The material is the same as the wall's ($O$3 OSB or $O$5 Zip) unless the detail calls for something else.
  • Openings are not subtracted from the strip.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text: Source in the tree DFL row Material Unit Formula perimeter walls/1st floor walls/ext ... Box Sheathing 7/16" Zip / 1/2" OSB 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) same area Tape Zip Tape (only with Zip) LFT =CEILING(SQFT*0.4*1.1,10) same area Vapor Barrier (WRB) per spec SQ FT as part of the wall

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Box called truss heel or the other way around; they have different geometry and different rows.
  • Strip height taken from the previous building, not from this one's section.
  • Box forgotten on the top floor under the parapet, or counted twice there.
  • On a panel job the box thrown out together with the panels, although it stayed loose.
  • Copied detail labels not corrected for this floor.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
2nd Floor Walls
...
Tape                Zip Tape        1980   LFT
Box Sheathing       7/16" Zip         18   4x8    4/A501
Tape                Zip Tape         230   LFT
Holdowns (2) btm top  HDU5           20   pcs    SW-3

docs.text:

  • Parapet, Rim Board
  • Wall Panels - what is in the panel, what is loose

docs.title: Exterior Wall Materials
docs.text: The wall layer by layer from outside in: veneer, WRB, exterior gypsum, structural sheathing, framing. Each exterior layer is a separate row; interior gypsum and insulation between the studs are not counted in the frame scope.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: The exterior envelope is everything that sits on the framing on the outside: structural sheathing (Wall Sheathing), exterior gypsum (Type X, Densglass), continuous insulation, WRB, opening flashing, bracing, window jambs and furring. These items hide in the wall sections and the wall type schedule, not on the elevations. The wall framing can be someone else's (metal studs, CMU), and the envelope still stays ours. Interior drywall, interior insulation and sound batts are not counted.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall type schedule (wt), UL assemblies Gypsum layers (1 or 2), over FRT, Densglass by zone Wall sections (sec), details Layer order by the arrows, Z furring, jambs at openings, furring under siding Energy / envelope sheets Continuous insulation, Zip R, WRB (product per spec) Elevations (el) Densglass zones and material changes, facade build-out Job scope and notes Metal studs by others, CMU by others, furring "not utilized"

docs.title: Exterior gypsum sheathing
docs.text:
• 5/8" Type X exterior grade is the standard exterior gypsum. 19/32" is not used for gypsum: that is a plywood/OSB designation.
  • (2) layers: when the wall type or UL assembly calls for two layers.
  • over FRT: gypsum over structural 1/2" Ply FRT, a separate row.
  • Split Densglass by level and elevation if the schedule splits it that way. 5/8" Densglass over Zip = two products, two rows.
  • Gypsum in SQ FT, structural ply in 4x8.
Wall type with a UL assembly: (2) layers of 5/8" exterior gypsum on the outside face. Two layers = two rows or one "(2) layers" row. 2HR wall behind brick: 5/8" Type X gypsum over 1/2" FRT sheathing. Both exterior layers are our rows; the batts between the studs and the gypsum inside are not.

docs.title: Insulation (continuous)
docs.text:
• Insulation: continuous insulation on the outside face of framed walls, only outside, over the sheathing.
  • Insulation at CMU: continuous insulation on CMU walls, a separate row, the area is usually larger. Z metal furring goes under it.
  • Zip R is written together with the insulation (Zip R-3 = sheathing plus insulation).
  • Unit SQ FT, opening deductions are the same as for the sheathing.
CMU: veneer, continuous insulation (the Insulation at CMU row), Z metal furring, air barrier, block. The block is someone else's; insulation, furring and flashing are ours.

docs.title: Metal stud and CMU walls: what stays ours
docs.text:
Row Material Unit When Wall Sheathing 5/8" Type X SQ FT Gypsum on metal walls, even if the studs are by others Bracing Ext Walls / Bracing Corridor / Bracing Demising 2x4 LFT Bracing on metal walls Window Flashing at Mtl Walls, Sill Flashing at Mtl Walls Flashing Tape / Sill Flashing LFT By wall type, see Window Flashing Window Flashing at CMU Walls Flashing Tape LFT The same for CMU Window jambs 2x4 / 2x8 by wall depth LFT If openings in metal walls are packed out with lumber; otherwise the Note Assumed window jambs 2x4 are not used per A8.53; verify Z furring metal Z LFT Under insulation on CMU Furring under siding 1x4 or 2x4 P.T. LFT Rainscreen per detail; P.T. and non-P.T. on different rows

Do not add furring at CMU as optional without a detail. Details: Furring, Furring and Window Jambs.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The whole wall block thrown out because of "metal by others": gypsum, insulation, flashing, bracing stayed ours.
  • Gypsum layers not split: 1 layer, (2) layers, over FRT.
  • Insulation and Insulation at CMU merged into one row.
  • Interior gypsum, insulation between the studs or sound batts counted.
  • "Vapor Barrier / Tyvek" written although the spec calls for a fluid-applied WRB.
  • Assembly not read to the end: a third 5/8" layer, Z-girt, overbuild missed.

All sheathing mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example (job A, FRT wood + CMU + metal openings)
docs.text:
Wall Sheathing               5/8" Type X            6670   SQ FT
Wall Sheathing (2) layers    5/8" Type X            2530   SQ FT
Wall Sheathing over FRT      5/8" Type X            4190   SQ FT
Wall Sheathing               1/2" Ply FRT            298   4x8
Box Sheathing                1/2" Ply FRT             75   4x8
Insulation                   1.5" Cont. Insulation  6670   SQ FT
Insulation at CMU            1.5" Cont. Insulation 13350   SQ FT
Bracing Ext Walls            2x4                     ...   LFT
Window Flashing at Mtl Walls Flashing Tape          1650   LFT
Sill Flashing at Mtl Walls   Sill Flashing           670   LFT
Note: Assumed window jambs 2x4 are not used per A8.53; verify.
Note: Furring strips under the siding are not utilized per A8.53; verify.

docs.title: Floor Sheathing
docs.text: Floor assembly by the arrows: 3/4" T&G subfloor, underlay, second 3/4" T&G layer, adhesive. Each sheet is its own row. Insulation between the joists and the ceiling gypsum are not counted in the frame scope. Archive illustration.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Floor sheathing is everything that lies on the joists over the floor area: subfloor, underlayment, a second layer under tile or tubs, FRT strips around the perimeter, sound mat. The base 3/4" T&G subfloor is covered in Subfloor; this page covers the extra layers from the floor assembly that get lost most often. The exterior strip at the floor framing level is Box Sheathing, not this page.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor type schedule (ft), assemblies All layers by the arrows: subfloor, underlayment, sound mat, gypcrete (by others) Structural notes, framing plan Subfloor thickness, FRT perimeter 2' or 4' at the exterior wall Details (tubs, tile, existing floor) 3/4" Ply under tubs (not under showers), new subfloor over the existing one Sections (sec) Underlayment and sleepers over a slab (over slab)

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
The area comes from sqfts/1st, sqfts/2nd (Floor SQFT); there is no separate takeoff for the sheathing. FRT strip: the floor's exterior wall perimeter (walls/<floor> floor walls/ext ...) x the strip width from the S sheet. Zones under tubs and tile, when needed, as separate polygons in sqfts with a clear name (tubs, tile).

  • Each layer is counted once and on its own floor.
  • 1/2" underlayment from the assembly can be a very large quantity: read the assembly, not just the framing plan.
  • Include new subfloor over an existing floor if the detail shows it.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text: Source DFL row Material Unit Formula sqfts/1st Subfloor 3/4" T&G 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) same area Panel Adheasive 29OZ pcs per template same area Underlayment 1/2" Ply per assembly 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) ext perimeter x 2' or 4' Subfloor FRT 3/4" T&G FRT 4x8 =CEILING(LFT*4/32*1.1,1) sqfts/tubs Plywood 3/4" Ply (under tubs) 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1)

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• FRT strip not figured from the full perimeter of its floor (10 sheets instead of 54).
  • Underlayment from the assembly missed because it is not on the framing plan.
  • 3/4" Ply put under showers although the detail says "at tub locations".
  • New subfloor over an existing floor left out on a reconstruction.
  • Ceiling gypsum and insulation between the joists ended up in the frame scope.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
2nd Floor Framing List
Subfloor            3/4" T&G            128   4x8    S201
Subfloor FRT        3/4" T&G FRT         54   4x8    4' perimeter per S001
Panel Adheasive     29OZ                 16   pcs
Underlayment        1/2" Ply            128   4x8    A6-01 floor type F2
T&G subfloor on joists. Sheets = SQFT / 32 x 1.1, rounded up to a whole number. Archive photo.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Subfloor, Floor SQFT, Box Sheathing
  • Reconstruction - new floor over an existing one

docs.title: Gable Sheathing
docs.text: Gable stick: the framed triangle above the wall's top plate. Gable sheathing is counted from the top of the top plate up to the slope; the wall below is already in walls. Photo: wheezinggirl, CC BY 2.0, source.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Gable sheathing covers the gable triangle under a gable roof, from the wall's top plate up to the slope. Two types: gable trusses (truss by others, we count only the sheathing and WRB) and gable stick (we count the framing and the sheathing, see Gable Wall). The heel strip on the eave sides is Truss Heel. The attic draft stop lives in the same branch, but it is an interior attic partition, not exterior sheathing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Roof plan notes Trusses = gable trusses; 2x10, TJI, stick = gable stick Elevations (el) Triangle outline, dormer gables, where the wall ends and the gable starts Sections (sec) Top plate height, pitch, heel Draftstops plan (for example A1-00) and section A4 Draft stop lines and the attic profile (span x rise) Wall notes / fire rating Draft stop thickness (1/2" Ply, 5/8" Type X), gable material

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Area tool along the real face of the gable on the elevation (a201 el), including steps and dormers. Bottom of the polygon = top of the top plate. Several gables of one type can be collected as polygons in one takeoff.
  2. For gable stick add a Line btm (bottom of the triangle) and top (both sloped edges): the export figures plates and studs from them.
  3. Draft stop: location from the Draftstops Plan sheet, attic profile from the section, one Area triangle per line (base = span across the building, apex under the ridge). Place it on the architectural roof plan, not on an S sheet. Its own color, source sheets in Notes. At hips the triangle is smaller: mark it "check".
  4. Do not collect one gable twice from two elevations, and do not put it both in gable and in the wall area. Existing gables go in a separate takeoff (existing gable).

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row (Gable Walls block) Material Unit Formula gables/gable trusses/gable (Area) Wall Sheathing 7/16" Zip / 1/2" OSB 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) same area Vapor Barrier (WRB), Tape with Zip per spec SQ FT / LFT as for the wall gables/gable stick/gable stick (Area) + btm, top (Line) Studs for Gables, Plates Ext (3), Blocking per Gable Wall gables/gable trusses/draft stop (Area) Draft Stop 1/2" Ply or 5/8" Type X per detail 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1)

The GB button on the XL strip moves the gables branch into the Gable Walls block.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Draft stop not counted or copied from the shear wall total (the most frequent miss).
  • Area measured, but the old number stayed in Excel.
  • Gable counted twice (two elevations, or gable plus wall).
  • Truss heel included both in gable and in trussheel.
  • Draft stop thickness not checked (7/16" vs 1/2").
  • Plates and studs counted for gable trusses although they are already in the truss.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/gables/gable trusses/
  gable            Area   412 SF   (4 polygons, north and south elevations)
  draft stop       Area   318 SF   (3 lines from A1-00, profile from A4-01)
Takeoffs/Main/gables/gable stick/
  gable stick      Area   96 SF
  btm              Line   24 LFT
  top              Line   27 LFT
Gable area is counted from the top of the wall's top plate; the truss heel on the eave sides is a separate trussheel strip.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Gable Wall - stick gable framing and the row table
  • Truss Heel, Wall Sheathing, Demising Walls (draft stop on walls)

docs.title: Holdowns
docs.text: Holdown at the end stud of a shear wall, anchored into concrete. One Count point per such connection; the model comes from the table for your building and floor. Photo: Thester11, CC BY-SA 3.0, source.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A holdown is the hardware at the end of a shear wall that keeps the stud from uplifting: HDU, HDUE (embedded, cast into concrete), HTT, DTT (light), plus MSTC, CS16, LSTA straps between floors. Holdowns sit at points, anchor bolts are spaced along the slab: these are different rows (Anchor Bolts). Post caps, bases and hangers do not belong here: they go in framing/.../details.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Shear wall schedule Holdown model by SW mark, straps, anchor Framing plans with SW marks Symbols at the SW ends, double symbols, the ? sign Details (S2.2, 4/S5.5) Connection configuration: to concrete, through the floor framing, over a beam Sections / elevations Connection level: the bottom of the wall may not be on the framing sheet's floor Detail: holdown with SDS on the chord studs, threaded rod anchor into concrete, an anchor with a plate washer next to it. Do not delete what the engineer shows explicitly. Archive excerpt.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Count tool: one point at the real connection (end stud), not on the callout text. One takeoff per model and configuration, its own color and CountSymbol.
  2. Take the model from the table for your building and your floor. Do not add rods, anchors or Zmax if they are not in the detail.
  3. (2) DTT2Z = two pieces at one connection: as many points as there are locations; show the number of pieces separately (in the name or in Excel), do not multiply twice.
  4. A shared end of two SW, a connection on the plan and on a detail, top and bottom on different sheets: check whether it is one location or two levels.
  5. Holdowns not marked on the plan: takeoff TBD HD and the Note Holdown locations are assumed; verify. Keep a ? sign as an undefined connection with its source.

docs.title: Counting rule (1 to concrete, 2 through the floor framing)
docs.text:
Connection How many pieces DFL row SW stud sits on concrete 1, as drawn Holdowns (1) btm, C =G SW over wood floor framing 2: below and above the floor framing Holdowns (2) btm top, C =G*2 Holdown sits over a beam do not add a transfer holdown under the beam (client instruction, 09/22) as shown Threaded rod only if shown its own row

Count straps (MSTC40, CS16) as separate takeoffs, do not mix them with anchors.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row B (model) Unit E shear walls/1st floor/holdowns/HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2 Holdowns (1) btm HDU11 pcs SW-2 shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns/HD1 (2) DTT2Z Holdowns (2) btm top DTT2Z pcs SW mark shear walls/1st floor/holdowns/DTT2Z at WSW-B Holdowns (1) btm DTT2Z pcs WSW-B shear walls/2nd floor/holdowns/MSTC40 type C S2.3 Straps MSTC40 pcs S2.3

Place in the DFL: the wall section of the floor whose SW the holdown restrains, a block at the end of the section after the last Tape (under Box Sheathing). G = number of points from OurPlanCore, one row per model.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Model taken from the table of another building or floor (HDUE13 instead of HDUE17).
  • One holdown through wood floor framing instead of two.
  • Straps mixed with anchors on one row.
  • A shared end of two SW counted twice, or top/bottom on two sheets counted as two locations.
  • A threaded rod or Zmax added that is not in the detail.
  • Anchor bolts at one spacing for the whole building instead of the spacing from the SW schedule.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/shear walls/1st floor/holdowns/
  HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2     Count 14     (to concrete)
  HD1 (2) DTT2Z         Count  6     (two pieces per connection)

docs.title: Shear Wall
docs.text: Interior shear wall: OSB on one side only, per the schedule. The run length is a Line in the shear walls branch; the sheathing follows the SW schedule, not the Arch sheets. Photo: bbaunach, CC BY 2.0, source.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A shear wall (SW) is a wall run that resists wind and seismic loads through structural sheathing, heavier nailing and holdowns at the ends. SW sheathing is counted strictly per the structural shear wall schedule: type, thickness, side, layers. A regular wall of the same length is already in walls: the SW is not added to it, it adds only what the regular wall does not have (a second side, a different material). Anchorage is a separate page: Holdowns.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Shear wall schedule (S) Mark, sheathing and thickness, one or two sides, blocking, nailing, holdown, anchor spacing Framing plan (s201 2nd) SW marks and their limits; a floor framing plan shows the walls below - take the floor from the "walls below/above" notes Holdown and SW details What is at the wall ends, what is between floors Wall sections (sec) Which level the wall is on, height Shear wall schedule: mark, sheathing, blocking, fasteners, anchor spacing. The same mark in another building does not mean the same spec. Archive excerpt.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Line tool along the actual SW segment between its limits, not along the room outline. LFT unit.
  2. A floor framing plan shows the SW of the floor below: a copy of the sheet in Struct/Shear with the S dot sends new takeoffs into shear walls/<floor below>.
  3. One takeoff per schedule row: do not merge SW4-1 and SW4-2 because their lengths match. One takeoff can contain several runs.
  4. Read the side: the outside face of an ext SW is already counted in ext walls, only the inside face is needed. Label a two-sided SW "both sides"; its G = the sum of the two faces, with no extra x2. P on the mark = perforated.
  5. On a panel job one sheathed side is already in the panel; count only the required second side.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Material Unit Formula shear walls/1st floor/shear/SW1-1 Wall Sheathing in the floor's wall block, E = SW1-1 per schedule, for example 15/32" Ply 4x8 =CEILING(LFT*H/32*1.1,1) shear walls/1st floor/shear/WSW-C 7-16 OSB DTT2Z same, E = mark 7/16" OSB 4x8 same shear walls/2nd floor/shear/ext W4B same per schedule 4x8 same separately Draft Stop per detail 4x8 not from the SW total, see Gable Sheathing

Name = mark plus confirmed differences (material, thickness, fasteners). The SW button on the XL strip puts the areas into the floor's wall block.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Two sides counted as x2 on top of the sum of two faces, or P read as two sides.
  • Schedule rows with different specs merged by length.
  • SW floor taken from the sheet instead of the "walls below" notes: the SW ended up one floor too high.
  • Attic draft stop copied from the shear wall total.
  • FRT applied to a demising SW automatically; FRT only per the exterior wall rules.
  • A35 and other clips added out of habit, not per detail.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/shear walls/1st floor/shear/
  SW1-1                      Line   86 LFT
  WSW-C 7-16 OSB DTT2Z       Line   42 LFT
  ext W4B                    Line  118 LFT
Takeoffs/Main/shear walls/1st floor/holdowns/
  HDU11 SB1x30 S2.2          Count  14

docs.title: Truss Heel
docs.text: Eave detail: 1'-7" truss heel height between the top of the wall and the underside of the deck, a vertical 1/2" OSB strip on the heel, the wall Zip below, 2x8 sub-fascia and 1x8 fascia outside. Take the height from a detail like this or from the truss package. Archive excerpt. Raised heel: the vertical heel member of the truss above the top plate, the truss tied down to the wall with straps. The truss heel sheathing strip covers exactly this end along the whole eave side: wall length times heel height. Photo: greenbuildingadvisor.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Truss heel is the vertical strip of sheathing at the truss ends along the eave sides of the building: between the wall's top plate and the underside of the roof deck. Its height is set by the truss heel (heel height), typically 0.66 to 3 feet. On the gable sides this strip is already part of the gable triangle (Gable Sheathing); on the eave sides it is easy to forget. It is not Box Sheathing and not soffit.

Raised heel truss on the top plate: a sheathing strip the height of the heel (the name carries the height in feet), the roof starts above it.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Truss profile / truss package Heel height, heel limits, bearing condition Roof section, soffit detail (sec, d) Strip height, material (often the same as the wall), deck offset Roof plan (rf) and wall plan (1st) Which walls the trusses bear on: that is where the strip goes Scope / notes Trusses by others do not cancel the loose heel sheathing; check the scope

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
1. Line tool along the walls the trusses bear on (eave sides), on the top floor plan or the roof plan. LFT unit.
  2. The name carries the heel height in decimal feet: trussheel 0.66, trussheel 1.25. Different heights = different takeoffs. The trussheel folder sits directly under the building; a name with trussheel goes there by itself.
  3. Do not mix up the numbers: in eve 24 the number is in inches (overhang), in prpt 3.4 3 2 they are parapet heights, in trussheel 1.25 it is the strip height in feet.
  4. Area = length x height; the export figures it (XL strip, TH button). The boundary with gable and wall sheathing must be explicit, with no double layer.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Material Unit Formula trussheel/trussheel 1.25 Truss Heel Sheathing (in the Gable Walls block or the template's roof block) same as the wall, for example 7/16" Zip 4x8 =CEILING(LFT*1.25/32*1.1,1) same area Vapor Barrier (WRB) per spec SQ FT =CEILING(SQFT*1.1,10) same length Blocking at Eves 2x6 LFT per detail, see Roof Sheathing

To be confirmed

Check the exact Label of the heel row in the current TemplateCom (block and name) against a delivered workbook; a descriptive name is given here.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• The strip on the eave sides not counted at all (gable sides are there, eave sides are not).
  • The same strip counted both in gable and in trussheel.
  • Height taken from another building or read as an overhang in inches.
  • "Vapor Barrier / Tyvek" written although the spec calls for a different barrier.
  • With top chord bearing, blocking between the trusses forgotten instead of a ribbon.

All mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/Main/trussheel/
  trussheel 1.25     Line  236 LFT   (eave sides of main)
Takeoffs/Grge/trussheel/
  trussheel 0.66     Line   84 LFT

docs.title: Wall Sheathing
docs.text: Structural sheathing on an exterior wall: OSB sheets over the studs. Area = wall length x wall height, minus openings wider than 4'. Archive photo.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Wall Sheathing is the structural panel on the outside face of a framed wall: OSB, plywood or Zip. It is not the same as Exterior Gypsum (Type X, Densglass) and not interior drywall: exterior gypsum goes on a separate row (Exterior Wall Materials); interior gypsum, interior insulation and sound batts are not counted in the frame scope. Narrow strips (box, truss heel, gable, parapet) have their own pages and their own rows.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall type schedule (wt) and wall sections (sec) Product, thickness, number of layers by the layer arrows; wall side Structural general notes, table WS-1 (for example S3.1) Structural thickness and nailing; the wall table and the roof table (WRS-1) are different Shear wall schedule Shear wall sheathing: side, thickness, layers; see Shear Wall Energy / envelope sheets Zip, Zip R, WRB, continuous insulation Elevations (el) Densglass zones, material changes, gables

docs.title: Source priority
docs.text:
Situation Decision Arch says Zip, structural says OSB/ply Take Zip, the main DFL Note cites both sources No Zip: Arch 1/2", Structural 5/8" Take 5/8" (the stronger one), Note with both sheets 19/32" This is 5/8" for plywood/OSB, not 1/2" 7/16" Zip on the S sheet and Zip R-3 in the wall type One product, a factual Note, no "differ" No thickness anywhere assumed 1/2" Ply; verify in the main Note

Take the product name from this plan set: LP FlameBlock 2-sided is not 7/16" OSB FRT, do not turn 5/8" EXT. SHEATHING into Ply without a reason, write CDX only if the set says so. Call the exterior barrier WRB / Weather Barrier per the spec (fluid-applied is not Tyvek), not "Vapor Barrier".

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
There is no separate sheathing branch in the tree. The wall area is collected from the wall lines: the wall name carries the height (ext 2x6 9.09), and the Excel export multiplies the length by the height.

  1. Walls are traced with Line in walls/<floor> floor walls/ on the sheet with the W dot (a101 1st). A change in height, size or sheathed side = a new takeoff.
  2. Before counting, build a table of surfaces: building, floor, side, product, thickness, layers, gross or net, deductions. Count the layers by the detail arrows.
  3. Deductions: openings are subtracted on their own floor and once (from the sheathing, WRB, insulation, Z-girt). Windows narrower than 4' are not subtracted. Garage doors are subtracted.
  4. Strips outside the walls come from their own branches: gables, trussheel, parapets, box from the floor framing depth. Each strip is counted once.
  5. How many sides: on a panel job one side is already in the panel, only the required second side is separate. The outside face of a shear wall is already in ext walls, add only the inside face. P on the mark = perforated, not two sides.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Material Unit Formula walls/1st floor walls/ext 2x6 9.09 Wall Sheathing 7/16" Zip or 1/2" OSB 4x8 =CEILING(SQFT/32*1.1,1) same takeoff Tape Zip Tape (only with Zip) LFT =CEILING(SQFT*0.4*1.1,10) same takeoff Vapor Barrier (in the template) WRB per spec SQ FT =CEILING(SQFT*1.1,10) same takeoff Insulation exterior 1" Insulation or Zip R SQ FT as WRB walls/1st floor walls/ext ... Wall Sheathing as a second row 5/8" Type X (exterior gypsum) SQ FT Exterior Wall Materials

The spec lives in the template cells: O3 sheathing, O4 WRB, O5 Zip, O6 Zip Tape, and P holds a bare sheet reference (S3.0, 8/S3.0, without the word "per"). It is filled in when the job is created. The Box Sheathing and Holdowns rows sit at the end of the floor's wall section.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Openings not subtracted (garage doors) or subtracted twice (doors on two floors).
  • Thickness and product inherited from the previous building instead of read from this set.
  • Vapor Barrier and Tyvek with a fluid-applied barrier in the spec.
  • Arch vs structural conflict resolved silently, without a Note citing both sheets.
  • Interior gypsum, interior insulation or sound batts counted.
  • Area measured in the app, but the old number stayed in Excel.
  • The same layer counted both in the wall and in the gable or parapet.

All sheathing mistakes: common-mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
1st Floor Walls
Wall Sheathing      7/16" Zip        214   4x8     8/S3.0
Tape                Zip Tape        2740   LFT
Insulation          Zip R-3         6850   SQ FT   A2-00
Note: Wall Sheathing 7/16" Zip R3 per 8/S3.0 A2-00.
Box Sheathing       7/16" Zip         21   4x8
Tape                Zip Tape         270   LFT
Zip System: panel and WRB in one product, the Tape row is required. The gable triangle is in the gables branch, the wall below is in walls. Archive photo.

docs.title: Basement Walls
docs.text: Wood basement wall on a slab: P.T. btm plate, studs, box sheathing and WRB over it. A concrete basement wall gives no framing.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Basement walls are the wood walls on the base level: exterior walls on the slab, walls under the podium, partitions and corridors in the basement. It is a full stick wall with its own plates, studs and sheathing, even when the building above goes in panels. The floor area is counted separately in Basement SQFT; this page covers only the framing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Basement plan a100 base Which walls are wood and which are concrete or CMU Foundation plan s101 f Slab, foundation walls, sill plates Wall section at the slab Stud height: the basement often has three different heights Wall type schedule Size, P.T., furring at concrete Code summary FRT below the podium on Type III

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, on the a100 base plan (W dot, level B). Branch walls/base floor walls, names as for regular walls: ext 2x6 9.24, corr 2x6 9.24, 2x4 9.24.

  1. A concrete or CMU wall gives no framing: do not draw it in walls. Furring in front of concrete is a separate takeoff furr 2x4 9.24 (Furring).
  2. Take the height from the section for each run: in the basement the floor framing and beams change the height more often than on the upper floors. One height for the whole basement is a mistake.
  3. Walls under a concrete slab or podium count as stick even on a panel job (Wall Panels).
  4. Basement metal walls: framing is by others, but box sheathing, WRB and flashing stay ours (Metal Tracks).

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text: Takeoff name DFL row Material Unit Formula / factor ext 2x6 9.24 Plates Ext (1) btm 2x6 P.T. (always on concrete) LFT LFT x 1.1 same Plates Ext (2) dbl top 2x6 LFT LFT x 2 x 1.1 same Studs Ext size by height pcs LFT x 1.1 (16") same Blocking 2x, Bracing 2x4 LFT by wall type same Box Sheathing OSB, Vapor Barrier (WRB per spec) 4x8, SQ FT Box Sheathing corr 2x6 9.24 Plates Corr btm 2x6 P.T. or LSL P.T. LFT per detail basement openings Window Flashing, Sill Flashing LFT Window Flashing 2x4 9.24 (under podium) Studs Interior FRT on Type III pcs note with the source

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• One stud height for the whole basement when the section shows three different heights.
  • Height taken as floor-to-floor without subtracting the subfloor and floor framing.
  • Walls below the podium thrown out as "panels by others".
  • A concrete wall traced as a wood wall.
  • Treated basement furring not split out as a separate P.T. assembly.
  • The Vapor Barrier row says Tyvek although the spec calls for a different WRB.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

  ext 2x6 10.3        Line, 21.1 LFT    Notes: W4A, 1/A701, FRT below podium
  ext 2x6 9.24        Line, 15.7 LFT
  furr 2x4 9.24       Line, 36.8 LFT    Notes: 8/A500, P.T. at concrete
