docs.title: Bearing Walls, BW
docs.text: Bearing wall on a structural plan: hatched band, callout with the mark. Read the mark from the stud schedule of your plan set: size, number of studs in the pack, spacing.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: BW (bearing wall) is a wall that carries floor framing or the roof. The engineer beefs it up: more plies per stud, different spacing, sometimes MSR. For the takeoff, BW is a separate branch of the tree: walls keeps only regular walls, shear walls keeps SW. One physical wall can be in walls, in BW and in shear walls at once: these are three different purposes, their lengths are not added together.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Structural plans s102 2nd Bearing wall bands (hatch or gray fill per the plan set legend), BW marks Stud schedule (TYPICAL WOOD STUD WALL DESIGNS, s104) Size, plies, spacing, grade for each mark, the interior unit bearing walls row General notes s001 Whether the framing plan shows the walls below or above the floor Floor plans a101 Which architectural wall sits under the band: ext, corridor, demising, unit Wall sections Stud height, double btm plate, FRT below the podium

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, along the physical bearing wall band.

  1. Set the floor first. A framing sheet often shows the walls below the floor (on job A sheet S003 confirmed it), but this is not universal: check the notes of your plan set. The folder is the physical floor of the wall, not the plan number.
  2. Select the BW/<floor> folder in Takeoffs and draw in it. The F sheet dot on a structural plan would put the Line into details, so set the folder yourself or move it afterwards.
  3. One takeoff per mark: BW4-4-24, BW6-2-24. With no mark, BW typical - per stud schedule with the source in Notes is acceptable.
  4. Different marks and both frames of a double wall are separate lines. Repeated callouts on one continuous run do not make a second line.
  5. Do not trace beams, leaders, CMU or deck hatching: the BW band is told apart by the legend of this particular plan set.
  6. Copy sheets into the BW folder only when asked.

A linear BW markup does not count studs by itself: it gives the length, to which Excel applies the plies and spacing from the schedule.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor BW/3rd/BW4-5-24 Studs Interior (base, 24" spacing) pcs LFT x 0.625 same Extra Dbl Studs Interior pcs LFT x 0.5 x (plies - 1) BW/3rd/BW6-3-24 Studs Demising (base) + Extra pcs base + extra by plies BW/4th/BW typical - per stud schedule the same rows, type from the interior unit bearing walls row pcs per the floor's schedule

This is how BW are written in delivered workbooks:

  • The main stud row uses the regular spacing factor (16" = 1.1, 24" = 0.625).
  • Extra plies go on a separate Extra or Double Extra row with the Extra factor (16" = 0.75, 24" = 0.5) times the number of additional studs.
  • Subtract the BW length from the regular studs of the same size: the base is not doubled.
  • B is the single size, D the order length, E the height, the mark and sheet go in F.
  • Plies and spacing come from the stud schedule of your floor: the same mark can have different values on the 3rd and 5th floors.

Full factor table: Formulas; extra and dbl studs on COM: COM Commercial.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• BW drawn in walls and added to the regular walls: the length is counted twice.
  • Floor taken from the sheet number although the plan shows the walls below the floor.
  • Plies and spacing made up: with no mark, write typical - per stud schedule and the source.
  • Extra24 factor set to 0.625 instead of 0.5.
  • Stair and small 2x4 runs declared corridor 2x6 without a confirmed mark.
  • Double btm plate added because of the floor name, not because of a detail.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
BW/
  3rd/
    BW4-5-24                         Line, 52.9 LFT
    BW6-3-24                         Line, 161.7 LFT
    BW6-4-24                         Line, 60.3 LFT
  4th/
    BW typical - per stud schedule   Line, 168.0 LFT   Notes: S104, S003 walls below

docs.title: Corners
docs.text: Wall corner in plan: 2-stud L, 3-stud, California corner with backing for gypsum. Stick: a separate row per floor. Panels: not counted.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A corner is the stud pack where two walls meet: 2 or 3 studs, or a California corner. The stud factor 1.1 (one stud per foot plus waste) covers cutoffs and studs at openings, but corners and T-intersections on stick framing are counted on a separate row. On a panel job the corners are already inside the panel.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans Number of exterior corners and T-intersections per floor Typical wall details, corner detail How many studs per corner, backing for gypsum Structural details Corner holdowns, extra studs, where called out Scope Stick or panels: on a panel job corners are not counted

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text: Count tool (points), one in each exterior corner and each T-intersection on the floor plan. Takeoff corners in walls/<floor> floor walls (the W dot puts the Count into walls; the word corners itself counts as a wall token). Give it its own CountSymbol so the points look different from holdowns.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor corners (Count, 1st floor) Corners 2x6 (wall size) pcs corners x studs per corner (2 or 3 per detail), length = stud height corners (Count, 2nd floor) Corners on a separate row pcs per floor, not one total

If no corner detail is shown, write a visible note: Corners assumed 3 studs; verify.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Corners counted on a panel job: they are already in the panel.
  • All floors added into one row.
  • T-intersections and backing forgotten although the detail shows them.
  • Corner counted as 2 studs when the detail shows 3.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.text:

  corners      Count, 14 ea     Notes: 3-stud per 5/A701
walls/2nd floor walls/

docs.title: Corridor Walls
docs.text: Staggered stud wall: 2x4 studs in two staggered rows on one 2x6 plate, insulation woven between them. In the DFL these are 2x6 plates and two rows of 2x4 studs.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A corridor wall separates a unit from a common area: corridor, stair, garage, lobby. It is fire-rated, often on 2x6 plates with staggered 2x4 studs, and it carries a ledger or drywall bracing on top where the floor framing runs parallel. A wall between two units is a Demising wall, and a shaft wall is a Shaft wall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans a101 1st Wall type marks along corridors, stairs, garage Wall type schedule (wt), UL assembly Plate and stud size, staggered or not, gypsum layers, rating Section at the corridor, S details Ledger, 2x10 corridor joists on a ledger, blocking, hangers Door schedule Fire-rated unit entry doors (3070 ... C-lbl) Stud schedule If the corridor wall is also bearing: mark in BW

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, on the floor plan (W dot).

  1. Category by run: a wall segment at a stair or at the garage is also corr, even if it continues a demising wall.
  2. Name corr 2x6 11.7: category, plate size, height. A double corridor wall (two frames on the plan) is corr (2) 2x6 11.7.
  3. A staggered wall is one line: plates by the name 2x6, the two stud rows are handled in the DFL.
  4. Start a new takeoff when the height or size changes. Height comes from the section of your building, not floor-to-floor (Exterior: stud height).
  5. If the wall type is bearing, trace the same wall again in BW/<floor>.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor corr 2x6 11.7 Plates Corr (1) btm 2x6 (P.T. only on concrete) LFT LFT x 1.1 same Plates Corr (2) dbl top 2x6 LFT LFT x 2 x 1.1 same Studs Corr 2x4 staggered pcs LFT x 1.1 x 2 (two rows at 16") same Bracing Corridor 2x4 LFT by wall height same Blocking LFT by wall type same Bracing for Drywall 2x4 LFT where the floor framing runs parallel to the wall corr (2) 2x6 11.7 the same rows for two frames x 2

Hangers over a corridor wall are regular ITS when the gypsum stops below the floor framing. DHU / DGU only where the joists bear over a true fire wall per detail (stair, elevator, shaft): Hangers. Corridor joists at the roof without a detail get a note with the reason, not Optional with no explanation (Standard notes).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Corridor and demising mixed up as a group: on one check 241 LF of corridor became 161, and demising grew from 577 to 648.
  • A piece of corridor wall at a stair written as ext.
  • DHU used only because the wall is a corridor wall.
  • A staggered wall counted with one row of studs.
  • 2x6 plates forgotten: studs are 2x4, and the plates were written as 2x4.
  • Ledger and corridor joist hardware not listed on separate rows per detail.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.text:
walls/
  2nd floor walls/
    corr 2x6 9.09        Line, 161.0 LFT
    corr (2) 2x6 9.09    Line, 24.5 LFT   (two walls at the stair)
    dem 2x6 9.09         Line, 648.2 LFT

docs.title: Demising Walls
docs.text: Double demising wall: two frames with an air gap, gypsum on both sides, 1/2" OSB draft stop in the floor framing. Each frame is its own line and its own DFL rows.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A demising (party) wall separates two units. It can be single or double: two independent frames with an air gap. It is rated, often carries double studs on the lower floors and needs a draft stop in the floor framing and in the attic. A unit-to-corridor wall is a Corridor wall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans a101 1st Wall type mark between units; one frame or two Wall type schedule (wt), UL assembly Size of each frame, gypsum layers, sound insulation Wall-to-floor details (a701) Draft stop (1/2" OSB), solid blocking, acoustic sealant Stud schedule, S plans Double studs, BW marks on demising SW schedule Shear sheathing on one side of the demising wall Draftstops plan, roof plan Attic draft stop: see Gable Dwelling unit separation wall detail: 1/2" OSB draft stop over the wall, solid blocking at the joist ends, fire-rated seal. The draft stop here is a separate row, not part of the sheathing.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, on the floor plan (W dot).

  1. Name dem 2x6 9.09: category, size, height.
  2. A double wall with identical frames is one line dem (2) 2x6 9.09.
  3. A double wall with different frames (2x4 and 2x6, different heights) is two lines, one per frame: dem 2x4 9.09 and dem 2x6 10.5.
  4. Make it double only if the plan shows two frames: do not double a wall because of its name.
  5. The draft stop in the floor framing is not drawn separately: its length equals the demising wall length, the area is figured in the DFL. The attic draft stop is a triangle Area in gables/gable trusses/draft stop on the architectural roof plan.
  6. A bearing demising wall is also traced in BW/<floor> by its mark.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor dem 2x6 9.09 Plates Demising (1) btm, (2) top LFT LFT x 1.1, x 2 x 1.1 same Studs Demising 2x6 pcs LFT x 1.1 (16") or x 0.625 (24") same Bracing Demising 2x4, Blocking LFT by wall height and type same Bracing for Drywall 2x4 on both sides LFT where joists run parallel to the wall same Draft Stop 1/2" OSB SQ FT LFT x floor depth, regular material, not P.T. dem (2) 2x6 9.09 the same rows for two frames x 2 BW mark on demising Extra Dbl Studs Demising pcs Bearing Walls

Shear sheathing on a demising wall can be on one side only or on part of the length: per the SW schedule, see Shear Wall. Hangers over a demising wall with gypsum below the floor framing are ITS; DHU only over a true fire wall per detail.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Draft stop missed or copied from the shear wall total.
  • Draft stop written as P.T., or its thickness not checked against the detail (7/16" vs 1/2").
  • Wall made double because of the word "demising" although the plan shows one frame.
  • Type assigned as a group: 10 LF of demising ended up in exterior, a corridor wall named dem.
  • Lower-floor double studs from the stud schedule not listed.
  • Floor-to-floor draft stop and attic draft stop mixed into one row.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.text:

  3rd floor walls/

    dem 2x4 9.09        Line, 36.0 LFT      (single at the stair)
gables/
  gable trusses/
    draft stop          Area, 3 triangles   Notes: A1-00, A4.1

docs.title: Exterior Walls
docs.text: Exterior wall in section: plates, studs, sheathing, WRB, insulation. Before counting, split the wall into layers and decide which of them are in scope.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: An exterior wall runs along the building perimeter and has sheathing on the outside. It differs from interior walls in its layers (sheathing, WRB, insulation), the FRT requirement and the fact that all facade openings are cut out of it. A wall on concrete brings along Sill Plates, and at the top Gable, Parapet and Truss Heel.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans a101 1st Wall outline and length, wall type marks Wall type schedule (wt) Stud size, spacing, layers, fire rating, FRT Sections a3.01 sec Stud height, floor framing makeup, where the wall ends and the gable starts Elevations el, energy sheets Densglass and Zip zones, continuous insulation, material changes Structural s101, SW schedule Shear walls, holdowns, blocking of tall walls Code summary (n) Construction type: on Type III everything in the plane of the exterior wall is FRT

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit. The W sheet dot on a floor plan puts a new line into walls/<floor> floor walls.

  1. Run the line along the wall centerline over the real runs. Do not trace callouts or dimension lines.
  2. Start a new takeoff when the height, size, construction or sheathed side changes. One run with several callouts stays one line.
  3. Decide the wall type run by run, not as a group: a piece of demising between two exterior walls does not become ext.
  4. A double wall is two frames only if the plan shows two frames.
  5. BW and shear walls are not drawn in walls: they have their own branches, BW and Shear Wall.
  6. Give each takeoff its own Color.

Line on the 1st floor walls. The name carries the category, size and height: ext 2x6 9.09.

docs.title: Stud height
docs.text:
The height in the name is the wall height including plates, in decimal feet. It is not floor-to-floor and not the ceiling elevation. Read the section of each building: from the floor-to-floor subtract the subfloor and the floor framing depth, then check whether the gypcrete is poured over the framing or between it. Example: 9'-6" floor-to-floor minus 11 7/8" TJI minus 3/4" subfloor = 8.45'. In the DFL the height lives in column E of the stud row (to 1/8"), in the wall name it is decimal feet.

Kitchen section: the 9'-0" stud height sits between the subfloor and the underside of the floor framing above. Red lines are the wall limits, not floor elevations.

docs.title: Which stud for the wall height
docs.text:
The wall height (with plates, as in the name) decides which stud to order:

Wall height Stud 7'-0" ... 8'-1 5/8" 8' precut (92-5/8) 8'-1 3/4" ... 8'-4 1/2" 8' full height stud 8'-4 3/4" ... 9'-1 5/8" 9' precut (104-5/8) 9'-1 3/4" ... 10'-1 5/8" 10' precut (116-5/8) 10'-1 3/4" ... 10'-4 1/2" 10' full height stud 10'-4 3/4" ... 12'-4 1/2" 12'
  • There is no 9' full height stud, and no 11' stud either.
  • 10' precut is the tallest precut.
  • Short studs are cut from long ones: count 4' as 8', 5' as 10', 6' as 12'.
  • Example: an 8'-4 1/2" wall takes an 8' full height stud, a 12'-2" wall takes a 12' stud. Gables are not always 12' studs: check the height of each stud.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Naming canon: <category> <size> <height>. Older examples with x (ext 2x6 x) mean the same thing: the x stands in place of the height.

Takeoff name What it is DFL row Unit ext 2x6 9.09 Exterior 2x6, 9.09' high Studs Ext, Plates Ext (1) btm P.T., Plates Ext (2) dbl top pcs, LFT corr 2x6 11.7 Corridor wall, see Corridor Studs Corr, Plates Corr pcs, LFT dem 2x6 9.09 Unit separation wall, see Demising Studs Demising, Plates Demising pcs, LFT dem (2) 2x6 9.09 Double demising, two identical frames two groups of rows pcs, LFT furr 2x4 9.09 Furring wall, see Furring Plates Furring, Furring LFT 2x4 9.09 Regular partition, no prefix Studs Interior, Plates Interior pcs, LFT 2x6 half Half wall height from the name pcs, LFT

Along with the wall the DFL gets Bracing Ext Walls 2x4, Blocking, Wall Sheathing, Vapor Barrier (the template label; the material is the WRB from the spec, not Tyvek by default), Insulation, Holdowns and Ext. Headers. Stud factors (16" = 1.1, 24" = 0.625) have one canon in Formulas. The WL button on the XL strip moves the walls into the floor block; a suffix after the height (ext 2x6 10.09 5/S400) is split off automatically.

Layer rules are on separate pages: Wall Sheathing, Exterior Wall Materials. FRT: if the exterior wall is FRT, then the blocking, the parapet and the headers in its plane are FRT too. Count a facade build-out separately for the vertical and the horizontal parts, FRT per detail. Metal stud and CMU walls: framing is by others, but exterior gypsum, insulation, flashing and window jambs stay ours (Metal Tracks).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Stud height taken as floor-to-floor or the ceiling elevation.
  • Wall type assigned as a group: corridor and demising mixed up, a piece of demising ended up in exterior.
  • P.T. plate on wood floor framing: P.T. only on concrete and masonry.
  • Double bottom plate everywhere although the detail shows it only on some floors.
  • The barrier row says Tyvek with a fluid-applied WRB: use the product from the spec.
  • Openings subtracted from the sheathing twice or not at all.
  • Missed rigid insulation, Densglass by facade zone, dropped soffit from the RCP.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

  1st floor walls/

    corr 2x6 9.09     Line, 161.0 LFT
    dem (2) 2x4 9.09  Line, 96.5 LFT
    2x4 9.09          Line, 540.8 LFT
  2nd floor walls/
    ext 2x6 8.45      Line, 410.9 LFT

docs.title: Furring
docs.text: Left: CMU, rigid insulation, Z-metal furring. Right: framing, sheathing, WRB, 1x4 P.T. strip, siding. Different products, both called furring.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Furring is a strip or profile that creates a gap and a nailing plane. Three cases: Z-metal furring on CMU under continuous insulation, a 1x4 / 2x4 P.T. strip under siding (rainscreen), and a furring wall, a light wood wall in front of concrete at elevators and the core. The canon of rules and formulas is Furring & Window Jambs; this page has only what you need to mark it up and name it correctly.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall sections, details at CMU and concrete Z-furring, insulation thickness, P.T. at concrete Siding details, wall types Strip under siding: size, spacing, P.T. Plans at the elevator and stairs Furring wall along concrete walls RCP, roof notes 1x3 strapping under trusses or panels, if specified

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
• Furring wall: Line in walls/<floor> floor walls, name furr 2x4 9.09, W dot. Height from the section, as for a regular wall.
  • Z-furring and the strip under siding: the wall length or facade area they cover; a separate Line with the product name (z furring, 1x4 furring) or figured from the siding area (Siding).
  • Do not add furring at CMU as optional: the client's reviewer strikes it. A wood wall next to CMU can be panelized (Wall Panels).

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor furr 2x4 9.09 Plates Furring, Studs Interior LFT, pcs as for a wall, btm P.T. on concrete z furring Furring Z furring (metal) LFT SQFT x 12 / spacing x 1.1 1x4 furring Furring 1x4 P.T. or 2x4 P.T. LFT spacing per detail; P.T. and non-P.T. separately strapping 1x3 strapping under trusses LFT only when specified

Rigid insulation on CMU is a separate row Insulation at CMU (Exterior Wall Materials). If the client does not want to see metal, Z-furring and RC under the floor framing: verify scope.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• 2x4 furring added at CMU although the detail shows only 1-1/2" insulation.
  • Furring at CMU listed as optional stick framing with no reason.
  • P.T. strip at concrete counted together with regular SPF.
  • Strapping on MA/RI jobs not checked.
  • Basement furring wall (treated) not split out as a separate P.T. assembly.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.text:
walls/base floor walls/
  furr 2x4 9.24        Line, 36.8 LFT    Notes: 8/A500, P.T. plates at concrete
siding/
  1x4 furring          Line, 410.0 LFT   Notes: rainscreen per A4.25

docs.title: Gable Walls
docs.text: Gable truss: a truss with vertical studs. Framing is by others, we count only the sheathing and the layers. Gable stick: the wall carried up with studs. We count plates, studs, blocking, bracing and sheathing.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A gable is the triangle of wall under a gable roof, from the top of the wall's top plate up to the ridge. There are two types, and the whole takeoff depends on the type: gable trusses (a truss, by others, only the sheathing package is ours) and gable stick (the framing is all ours). The attic draft stop lives in the same branch. Do not confuse it with Truss Heel (the strip at the truss heel) and Box Sheathing (the strip at the floor framing level).

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Roof framing plan, truss layout Trusses = gable trusses; 2x8, 2x10, TJI, stick = gable stick Elevations el Triangle outline, dormers, steps, porch gables Sections sec Where the wall ends and the gable starts; wall stud height Draftstops plan (a1-00 and the like) Attic draft stop lines Attic section a4 Span and rise for the draft stop triangle Wall notes 2x4 or 2x6 size, FRT, sheathing material

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Branch gables/gable trusses/... or gables/gable stick/.... A name with gable truss or gable stick goes into gables by itself.

  1. Area along the real face on the elevation: gable (trusses) or gable stick. Include dormers, steps and openings. All gables of one type can be collected as several polygons in one takeoff.
  2. For stick, add two Lines: btm along the top of the wall (bottom of the triangle) and top along both slopes.
  3. Area starts at the top face of the top plate, not at the bottom of the wall. A gable seen on two elevations is drawn once.
  4. Draft stop: location from the Draftstops Plan sheet, attic profile (span x rise) from the section. One Area triangle per line: base = span, apex under the ridge. Place it on the architectural roof plan, not on an S sheet. Takeoff gables/gable trusses/draft stop, its own color, source sheets in Notes. At hips the triangle is smaller: mark it "check".
  5. Porch, garage and storage gables are their own polygons in the same building tree.

A stick gable takeoff looks like this: triangle Area 556 SQ FT, btm line 52.4 FT along the top of the wall, top line 70.3 FT along the slopes.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
The GB button on the XL strip puts gables into the Gable Walls block; the a2_sqft_gable_trussheel macro reads the areas and lengths.

Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor gable stick/gable stick + btm + top Plates Ext (3) btm and dbl top 2x6 LFT (BTM + 2 x TOP) x 1.1, to an even number same Studs for Gables 2x6 pcs SQFT / stud height, to an even number same Blocking 2x6 LFT BTM / 2 same Bracing Ext Walls 2x4 (14') pcs BTM / 8 x 1.1 both types Wall Sheathing 7/16" Zip or 1/2" Ply 4x8 SQFT x 1.1 / 32, round up both types Vapor Barrier (WRB material per spec) SQ FT SQFT x 1.1, to 10 both types Insulation SQ FT SQFT x 1.1, to 10 both types Tape Zip Tape LFT SQFT x 0.4 x 1.1, to 10 gable trusses/draft stop Draft Stop 1/2" OSB SQ FT sum of the triangles, thickness per detail

Gable trusses have no plates and studs rows. Sheathing material and FRT follow the exterior wall notes (Wall Sheathing).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Attic draft stop missed or copied from the shear wall total: the most frequent miss.
  • One gable counted twice from two elevations, or included both in gable and in the regular wall area.
  • Area taken from the bottom of the wall instead of the top of the top plate.
  • Plates and studs listed for gable trusses.
  • Gable confused with truss heel or box sheathing: the geometry is different.
  • Area measured, but the old number stayed in Excel.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.text:

  gable trusses/
    gable          Area, 2 polygons, 812 SQ FT
    draft stop     Area, 3 triangles, 390 SQ FT   Notes: A1-00, A4.1
Grge/gables/
  gable stick/
    gable stick    Area, 556 SQ FT
    btm            Line, 52.4 LFT
    top            Line, 70.3 LFT

docs.title: Metal Tracks / CFMF
docs.text: Light gauge metal framing: bottom track on the slab, C-section studs, an opening with a head track and doubled jamb studs. The whole sheathing package is counted the same as for a wood wall. Photo: Wikimedia Commons, public domain, source.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
CFMF (cold-formed metal framing) is a steel wall frame instead of a wood one. Two elements change: plates become tracks (U-section at the bottom and top), studs become mtl studs (C-section). Everything else (sheathing, WRB, insulation, gypsum, bracing, blocking) stays and is counted as for a wood wall with the same function. Shafts built from CH/H studs are a separate topic: Shaft Walls.

Element Wood Metal Wall bottom btm plate bottom track Wall top dbl top plate top track or deflection track Studs studs mtl studs (6" 18ga) Opening king/jack, header double jamb stud, head track, box header Sheathing, WRB, insulation, gypsum, bracing, blocking as for wood the same

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Wall type schedule, WT sheets Stud size (6", 3 5/8", 2 1/2"), gauge, layers, rating Section details (a402) Deflection head, wall-to-beam or wall-to-floor joint Structural notes, cover sheet CFMF, GA, X-bracing, deflection requirements Plans Wall length by type and floor Scope, client rules Metal is ours or by others: Client rules

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, as for a wood wall, in walls/<floor> floor walls.

  1. Scope first: if metal is by others, the walls are still traced, but the DFL gets 0 and the note Metal Studs by others; verify. The sheathing package can still be ours.
  2. Name with stud size, gauge and height: ext 6" 18ga mtl 11.7; the wall type from the schedule can be added at the end: ext 11.7 E2A (mtl 11.7).
  3. Under a steel beam split the height into pieces: the run under the beam (6" track) and the run next to it (3 1/2") are different takeoffs.
  4. Spacing 16 or 24 per the wall schedule, each takeoff has its own.
  5. Write the wall clear span once as a note before the block (ext wall 14.5 clear span).

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor ext 6" 18ga mtl 11.7 Tracks (1) btm 6" 18ga LFT LFT x 1.1 same Deflection Tracks (1) top LFT LFT x 1.1; only on walls that go up to the floor framing same Mtl Studs 16" o.c. 6" 18ga mtl pcs LFT x 1.1 (16") or x 0.625 (24") same extra studs, double jambs, Head Track at openings pcs, LFT per opening same Wall Sheathing, Air / Water Barrier, Insulation, Gypsum 5/8" Type X, Bracing, Blocking as for wood 2x4 jamb in a metal wall Window Jamb 2x4 LFT wood in a metal wall is normal

For a CFS building the fasteners are metal. Group by stud size, floor and wall type (ext, int, dem, corr). If the gauge is given on the plans, it goes into the takeoff spec; if not, add a note and check against the structural sheets.

Deflection track, gauge and jambs: details

Deflection track (slip, slotted, deep-leg) is the top track where the wall meets the structure above. The stud sits in it but is not fastened rigidly, so the floor can deflect without loading the wall. Required on non-bearing partitions under the structure, rated and shaft walls; walls that stop short of the floor framing do not have it. Check the type and leg depth against the details.

GA (gauge) is the steel thickness, and the rule runs backwards: a smaller number means thicker steel. 25ga light partitions, 20/18ga medium, 16ga and heavier structural.

Jambs: the jamb of an opening in a metal wall is often wood 2x4, doubled on wide openings ((2)2x4 or a doubled stud); a head track on top, extra studs at the sides. A box header bears on the doubled jamb studs.

Deflection head where the wall meets a steel beam: fireproofing, fire sealant, two layers of 5/8" Type X. The deflection track is a separate row from the bottom track.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Only tracks and studs counted for a metal wall, without sheathing, WRB, insulation, gypsum.
  • Metal by others, but no Metal Studs by others note: neither a row nor a note.
  • Deflection track used on a wall that does not reach the floor framing.
  • Gauge made up, or 24" o.c. copied when the spec says 16".
  • Height under a steel beam not split into 6" and 3 1/2" pieces.
  • Wood jamb in a metal wall missed.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
walls/1st floor walls/
  ext 6" 18ga mtl 14.5        Line, 96.0 LFT    Notes: E2A, ext wall 14.5 clear span
  ext 6" 18ga mtl 3.5         Line, 24.0 LFT    Notes: under W14 beam, 2/A402
  int 3 5/8" 20ga mtl 10.0    Line, 140.2 LFT   Notes: by others, sheathing ours

docs.title: Parapet Walls
docs.text: Parapet in section: outside height Hout from the top of the wall, inside height Hin from the roof, top width Wtop. Three sheathing planes (outside, inside, top) plus cap and flashing.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A parapet is the exterior wall carried up above a flat roof. It has two different heights (outside from the wall's top plate, inside from the roof deck) and a top that is sheathed too. The parapet is either built into the truss (parapet integral with truss) or a separate frame on the wall. Parapets built on the roof are counted separately from wall parapets.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Roof plan a105 rf Parapet lines, zones (upper roof, lower roof, porch) Parapet details (1/S402, 2/S405) Hout, Hin, Wtop, blocking between trusses, cap plate, clips Arch details Coping, flashing, inside face material (DensDeck, plywood) Wall notes FRT: if the exterior wall is FRT, the parapet and blocking are FRT too Truss drawings Parapet integral with truss or not Parapet integral with truss: continuous 2x on top, 2x8 blocking between trusses, double top plate, H2.5A at every truss. Sheathing is not in the truss package: we count it ourselves.

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, along the parapet on the roof plan. A name with prpt goes into the parapets branch by itself.

  1. Name prpt <Hout> <Hin> <Wtop> <detail> in feet: prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 par, prpt 3.4 3 2 2/S405. Three numbers first, then the detail number or zone: the A4_Parapet macro reads the numbers from the end, and 2/S405 before the dimensions breaks the parsing.
  2. A separate takeoff for each pair of heights, set of faces, roof zone (parapets/lower roof/...), concrete or wood, parallel or perpendicular.
  3. One line feeds both faces and the top: do not duplicate the length per surface.
  4. The exporter replaces a zero Wtop with 0.66: an export quirk, not a dimension. A height of 0 can be real.
  5. Write the top part (cap, top) together with the parapet: it is one assembly.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
The PP button on the XL strip moves parapets into the Parapet Walls block.

Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor prpt 3.4 3 2 2/S405 Studs (size by height) pcs LFT x 1.1 same Plates btm and top (cap is often 2x6 P.T.) LFT LFT x 1.1 each same Wall Sheathing outside SQ FT or 4x8 LFT x Hout x 1.1 same Inside Sheathing (OSB, plywood, DensDeck per detail) SQ FT LFT x Hin x 1.1 same Top Sheathing SQ FT LFT x Wtop x 1.1 same Vapor Barrier (WRB per spec), Insulation SQ FT on the outside face same Flashing Drip Edge, coping on a separate row or in Drip Edge LFT LFT same Blocking (2) 2x8 FRT between trusses, 2x6/2x8 around the rim LFT per detail

If the trusses bear perpendicular to the wall, the parapet is a separate stud wall; if parallel, the top-floor wall is carried up. Top-floor box sheathing is written into the parapet with a note.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Top sheathing forgotten: there are three sheathing faces, not one.
  • Detail number placed before the numbers: prpt 2/S405 3.4 3 2.
  • x 2 on top and bottom read as two layers, when it means two surfaces.
  • Blocking (2) 2x8 FRT from the detail not listed.
  • Unrealistic cut: two 5.3' boards do not come out of one 10'.
  • Inside face written as OSB although the detail calls for DensDeck.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
parapets/
  upper roof/
    prpt 3.4 3 2 2/S405      Line, 212.0 LFT
    prpt 1.2 1.2 0.6         Line, 48.5 LFT    (low parapet at the porte-cochere)
  lower roof/
    prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 par     Line, 96.0 LFT
    prpt 6.4 5.3 0.5 perp    Line, 60.2 LFT

docs.title: Shaft Walls
docs.text: Type 2 assembly: 1" x 24" shaftliner panels between 2" H-studs, 2" C-runner around the perimeter. Source: PABCO Gypsum, H-Stud ASW.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A shaft wall encloses a vertical shaft: elevator, vent duct, trash chute, mechanical. It is almost always fire-rated and almost always built from metal studs with a gypsum liner, so it is neither a regular partition nor Metal Tracks. Two working types: 2-1/2" CH + J-channel (one liner layer) and 2" H + C-channel (two layers). A CMU elevator gives no wood or liner framing.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Floor plans a101 Where the shafts actually are: elevator, chute, vent, mech Wall type schedule (wt), type 7A and similar CH or H, stud size, liner layers, gypsum outside Shaft details a806 Perimeter channels, joint with the floor framing, transition to wood Sections Shaft height by floor; where the shaft stops above the ceiling S plans Hangers over the shaft (DHU) when joists bear over a fire wall

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, around the shaft perimeter on the plan of each floor. One takeoff per assembly type and height; branch walls/<floor> floor walls, the takeoff is named shaft, then the wall type and height (for example shaft 7A 10.5). The SHF button on the XL strip builds the Shaft walls block above the first framing sheet.

  1. A typical detail is not a quantity by itself: find every shaft on the plan.
  2. Always record the material: CMU elevator, metal shaftliner, wood. Do not throw a shaft out because of a general note walls are panels by others.
  3. Do not multiply a wood-to-shaft transition above the ceiling by the full floor height.
  4. If the wall type gives a shaft assembly but the plan shows only resilient channel, count the resilient channel separately, not a full shaft.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Type 1, 2-1/2" CH + J-channel, one liner layer:

DFL row Material Unit Formula Linear Panels 1" Shaft Panels 2x12 panels LFT x 1.1 / 24, to 2 CH Channels Vertical 2-1/2" CH-channels 12' LFT x 0.5 x 1.1 / 12, to 2 J Channels Horizontal 2-1/2" J-channels 12' horizontal LFT x 1.1 / 12, to 2

Type 2, 2" H + C-channel, two liner layers (x 2 multiplier on the panels):

DFL row Material Unit Formula Linear Panels 1" Shaft Panels 2x12 panels LFT x 2 x 1.1 / 24, to 2 Channels Vertical 2" H-channels 12' LFT x 0.5 x 1.1 / 12, to 2 Channels Horizontal 2" H-channels 12' horizontal LFT x 2 x 1.1 / 12, to 2 Channels Perimeter 2" C-channels 12' perimeter LFT x 1.1 / 12, to 2

Full breakdown of the formulas: Formulas: Shaft Walls. Without a detail, write the assembly with assumed; verify. Resilient channels: CEILING(area x 12 / spacing x 1.1, 10) only where shown in the wall type; metal RC under the floor framing is usually by others.

Type 1: C-T (CH) stud 2-1/2", 4", 6", J-track and J-L corner. Size from the wall type. Type 2: 2" H-stud, the panels slide into the slots on both sides. Type 2: 2" C-runner around the perimeter: top, bottom, end cap. 1" shaftliner: one layer in Type 1, two layers in Type 2. A separate row.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A CMU elevator written as shaftliner, or a type 7A chute wall missed altogether.
  • Shafts thrown out as "panels by others".
  • Two types mixed into one block: they have different channels and different formulas.
  • A wood-to-shaft transition multiplied by the full floor height.
  • Hangers over the shaft taken as ITS instead of DHU per detail.
  • Resilient channel counted as a full shaft.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
walls/2nd floor walls/
  shaft 7A 10.5        Line, 64.0 LFT     Notes: A806 det 3, 2-1/2" CH + 1" liner
  shaft elev 10.5      Line, 48.0 LFT     Notes: CMU per S201, framing by others

docs.text:

docs.title: Sill Plates
docs.text: The stack on concrete from bottom to top: foundation, sill sealer, termite shield, P.T. sill plate with anchor bolt and washer, wall btm plate, stud. Each layer gets its own DFL row.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
The sill plate is the lowest wood member. It sits on the foundation or stem wall concrete, so it is always P.T. A sill plate is not a btm plate: the wall btm plate sits on the floor framing above, the sill plate sits under the floor framing on concrete. Each goes on its own row. It can be single, double or triple, typically 2x6 P.T., but take the size only from the detail.

Wall bottom plate on top, sill plate (red) on concrete, anchor bolt through it, foundation wall.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Foundation plan s101 f Length of walls on the foundation and slab; garage separately Typical sill detail, wall section at foundation Size and number of plies, P.T., sill sealer, termite shield Anchor bolt schedule, SW schedule, general notes Anchor diameter, embed and spacing, washer size 1st floor plans Openings (garage doors, doors) subtracted from the sill line once Specs (COM) Sill plate species (DF, SYP); plate rules are often hidden here

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, along the walls on concrete on the foundation plan or the 1st floor plan. The F dot on s101 f puts the Line into framing/<floor> framing/details; the name follows the detail material: 2x6 P.T. sill, 4x10 P.T. Sill grge.

  1. Separate lines for the house and the garage, for single and double sill, for different sizes.
  2. Line length = the length the detail applies to, not the length of the leader on the detail.
  3. Sill sealer, termite shield, anchor bolts and washers are figured from the same length: these three items are not shown on the plan and are easy to forget.
  4. Subtract openings (garage doors) once, on their own floor.
P.T. sill plate on pink sill sealer, the anchor bolt comes up out of the slab. This is how it looks on site. Termite shield: 1 ft lap at joints, bead of caulk along the edge, anchor through the sheet. Sill sealer (gasket) between the concrete and the sill plate, anchor bolts, joists and subfloor on top.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Material Unit Formula / factor 2x6 P.T. sill PT Sill Plates at ext. found 2x6 P.T. LFT LFT x 1.1; double x 2 same Sill Sealer 6" (less often 4", 8") LFT LFT same Termite Shield Copper LFT LFT x 1.1 (1 ft lap) same Anchor Bolts 48" o.c. per detail / SW schedule pcs LFT / spacing, to an even number same Washers, Nuts size per detail pcs one per bolt 4x10 P.T. Sill grge PT Sill Plates garage 4x10 P.T. LFT on a separate row

Anchor size, embed and washers come from your detail, not from the template: Anchor Bolts. Anchor spacing is split by run (1st floor SW to concrete have their own spacing), not one spacing for the whole building. Sill plate species unclear: a visible note, not a silent choice of SPF.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Sill sealer and termite shield missing from the DFL: they are not visible on the plan, but on concrete they are almost always there.
  • P.T. plate on wood floor framing: P.T. only on concrete and masonry.
  • Double sill or double btm plate everywhere although the detail shows it only on some floors.
  • One anchor spacing for the whole building; wedge anchor swapped for Titen HD with no reason.
  • Garage doors not subtracted from the sill, sill sealer and anchors, or subtracted twice.
  • Washers written as generic 3x3 without checking the table.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
framing/1st floor framing/details/
  2x6 P.T. sill          Line, 318.0 LFT    Notes: 2/S501, dbl sill at stair
  4x10 P.T. Sill grge    Line, 64.5 LFT     Notes: 5/S501

docs.title: Unit Walls
docs.text: Unit type sheet with the U dot: every new takeoff from it goes into units. Lines only on the interior partitions of the unit, one takeoff per size.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Unit walls are the interior partitions of one typical unit. Units repeat, so the walls of one type are measured once on the enlarged unit plan, and the number of repeats is taken separately. Exterior, corridor and demising walls are not part of the unit: they are counted on the floor plan (Exterior, Corridor, Demising).

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Sheet What to take Unit plans a3011 u (scale usually 1/4") Partitions of types A, B1, B1A; size by the thickness on the plan: 3 1/2" = 2x4, 5 1/2" = 2x6 Unit matrix, keyplan, floor plans a101 1st How many times and on which floors each type occurs, mirrored versions Wall type schedule (wt) What the partitions are: wood or metal studs, spacing, rated walls Interior elevations in el, RCP Blocking for kitchen and bath, dropped soffit Door schedule Interior doors and their jambs by the size of the adjacent wall

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Line tool, LFT unit, on the unit sheet.

  1. The sheet name ends in u (a3011 u): the sheet gets the U dot, and any new takeoff from it goes straight into units. Set the floor or type subfolder by moving it.
  2. One takeoff per type and size: A 2x4, A 2x6, B1A 2x4. A mirrored repeat is the same type; a really different version (shaft, accessibility, different ceiling) is its own type.
  3. Run a line along the centerline of each interior partition of the unit. A wall with no mark on the types sheet follows its neighbors.
  4. Fix the boundary with common walls once: a partition must not end up both in units and in walls/<floor> floor walls.
  5. Repeats are a separate count, not a number of lines: Count points on the floor plan, name = unit mark (B1, B1A), one point per unit.
  6. Sort the sheet legend with Organize > Sort Sheet Legend by Key (before space): A1 2x4, A1 2x6, A2 2x4, B1 2x4, B1A 2x4.

If the unit partitions are metal studs or walls are panels by others, the walls are still marked up, but the DFL gets 0 and a scope note (Metal Tracks, Wall Panels).

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text:
Takeoff name DFL row Unit Formula / factor units/A 2x4 Studs Interior 2x4 pcs LFT x repeats x 1.1 (16") units/A 2x6 Studs Interior 2x6 pcs the same, 24" = 0.625 same Plates Interior (1) btm, (2) dbl top LFT LFT x repeats x 1.1; btm P.T. only on concrete same Blocking, Bracing LFT by wall type B1 (Count on the floor plan) repeat multiplier ea number of units of that type on the floor

The UN button on the XL strip puts the unit table into the workbook (AM3) with totals by floor; the C_UnitTable macro multiplies the unit lengths by the number of repeats. Per unit there is also kitchen blocking (2x6, 4 at 14') and bath blocking (2x6, 1 at 14'), jamb blocking for interior doors and dropped soffit from the RCP. Interior drywall, interior insulation and sound batts are not counted in the frame scope.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Repeats multiplied twice: the geometry was copied and a factor was applied too.
  • A demising or corridor wall ended up inside the unit and was counted again on the floor.
  • Types A1 and A10 from the previous building carried over to a new job without the matrix.
  • 24" o.c. spacing copied although the spec calls for 16" o.c..
  • Interior door jamb taken as generic instead of by the size of the adjacent wall.
  • The u tag is not last in the sheet name (a301 u el): no U dot, the lines went into walls.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
units/
  A 2x4      Line, 58.7 LFT
  A 2x6      Line, 3.1 LFT
  B1 2x4     Line, 71.2 LFT
  B1A 2x4    Line, 74.0 LFT
walls/1st floor walls/
  B1         Count, 6 ea      (repeats of type B1 on the 1st floor)

docs.text:

  • Windows and Doors: interior doors and jambs
  • U sheet dot, legend order
  • Formulas: stud factors

docs.title: Wall Panels: what we count
docs.text: Wall panel makeup: plates, studs, opening framing, sometimes sheathing and WRB. SBCA illustration. What exactly is in the supply is decided by the job, not by the picture.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A wall panel is a factory-built wall section (studs, plates, opening framing, often one side of sheathing and WRB). On a panel job we do not duplicate the factory framing; we count the loose scope and the stick exceptions. The word panels in the scope does not mean "do not count the walls": the walls are still measured in full, so that sheathing, headers, holdowns and exceptions are figured from real lengths.

docs.title: Where to find it on the plans
docs.text: Source What to take Job scope tag (Frame. Wall panels), client email Panel job or not; what the client wants to see as loose Sections and plans Which walls are below the slab or podium, which are inside an existing frame Wall type schedule, SW schedule Which sheathing side is in the panel, which is loose Panel drawings, if any Panel numbers, RO, bearing points Details Flush headers, build-ups, short and sloped walls

docs.title: How to measure in OurPlanCore
docs.text:
Walls are measured as usual: Exterior, Corridor, Demising, BW. What is different on a panel job:

  1. Headers inside panels are not drawn: only flush and loose per scope (Headers).
  2. One side of sheathing is already in the panel; only the required second side and loose zones are separate (Shear Wall).
  3. Mark stick runs as separate takeoffs or with a note: under the slab, in an existing frame, short and sloped.

docs.title: E-Wood rules (confirmed by the owner 2026-10-09)
docs.text:
Run What we do Regular wall in the panel package Do not duplicate the factory framing; count the loose scope Wall under a concrete slab / podium Count as stick: studs, plates, headers, sheathing New wall inside an existing frame (reconstruction) Count as stick for the new work Short wall, irregular sloped wall Stick exception Exterior build-up wall Possible exception; check the construction, do not exclude all build-ups automatically Wood wall next to CMU Can be panelized; being next to CMU is no reason for optional stick Furring under insulation/siding Separate strips per detail and scope Shaft, elevator Always record; determine the material and package, do not lose it because of panels by others

"Under concrete" and "on concrete" are different: a wall that sits on a P.T. plate on a concrete base can be panelized; the exception is walls below the slab or podium. On a mixed building find the boundary from the sections, not from the floor name. Full list in Tips.

docs.title: Takeoff name and DFL row
docs.text: Element Check before a separate row Studs, plates, corners, in-panel blocking In the package: not counted; in stick exceptions: counted in full Headers, king/jack/cripple Only flush and loose; the words special header alone do not prove loose Sheathing, shear plywood Which side and layer is in the panel; loose zones per details WRB, insulation, exterior gypsum Can be in the supply or the field scope; do not duplicate and do not exclude without checking Sill plates, gasket, anchors, holdowns, straps Their own connections, the factory framing does not cover them Double top plate, splice Part of it is installed in the field: check the loose material Box sheathing, truss heel, parapet, gable, roof edge Each assembly separately; it is not automatically part of the panel Beams, posts, hangers, ledgers Their own structural schedule and scope

docs.title: Reconstruction: existing does not mean "do not count"
docs.text:
We do not recount the existing structure, but we do count new walls, replacements, reinforcement, connections and specified finishes. If a detail calls for new subfloor over all existing flooring, include the full area of the new layer. An addition and a remodel inside an existing frame can have a different scope; the word reconstruction alone neither turns the panel rule on nor off. Details: Reconstruction.

In the DFL, on panel floors the stick block stays under the local note Note: Optional stick frame, if walls are not panels; verify. The template note Walls are panels by others is deleted if there are no panels in the scope. The reviewer strikes an optional with no reason: every optional block has a note saying why.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Shafts and walls below the podium thrown out together with the panels.
  • All build-ups automatically stick; or furring at CMU added as optional.
  • Second-side sheathing counted although one side is in the panel and the schedule has no second side.
  • Headers inside panels counted again.
  • Optional with no explanation why; shown framing called optional because spacing is missing.
  • New subfloor over the existing floor missed although the detail calls for it.

Walkthrough with examples: all wall mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Note: Walls are panels by others; walls below podium counted as stick framing.
Note: Optional stick frame, if walls are not panels; verify.      (under the floor header)
Note: New walls within existing frame counted as stick framing.

docs.text:

  • Exterior Walls, Furring, Shaft Walls
  • Tips and key rules: Wall panels
  • SBCA: Wall Panels

docs.title: COM Commercial
docs.text:
Large projects: multifamily, hotels, podium buildings, mixed-use. Many floors, corridors, demising walls, shafts, often wall panels and FRT.

A typical COM detail: ladder truss at the exterior wall, rim board around the perimeter, 2x4 brace at 4' o.c. On a panel job the wall is in the panel, while rim, blocking and brace are loose and we count them.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: COM differs from a house not in size but in what it is made of: walls are split into exterior, corridor, demising and unit; floor framing is trusses or I-joists with fire hangers at shafts; the roof is flat with parapets or uses piggyback trusses; walls often come as panels. Scope is most often Frame, Frame. Wall panels or Frame. EWP by others - Client rules.

docs.title: COM order
docs.text:
Go down the "Work" menu, one scope per pass over the sheet:

  1. Exterior walls.
  2. Corridor walls.
  3. Demising walls.
  4. Unit / interior walls (by unit type).
  5. Openings.
  6. Sheathing: walls, gables, truss heel, parapets, shear walls.
  7. SQFT by floor and roof.
  8. Floor framing: posts, beams, headers, joists, details, stairs.
  9. Roof framing and eaves.
  10. Deck / porch / balcony and other items.

docs.title: Two types of COM plan
docs.text:
Panel COM: a wall panel with sheathing and insulation is assembled at the plant and set by crane. On such a project the panel supplier counts the walls, and the DFL gets only the items built on site (see the table below). Photo: phoenixhaus.com, source, found via Pinterest. Type What we count What we do not count Regular walls (Frame) Studs, plates, blocking, sheathing, bracing, headers, openings Whatever is explicitly by others (trusses, metal per client) Panels (Frame. Wall panels) Loose scope: bracing along ext/corridor/demising, floor-height plywood, box sheathing, truss heel, parapets, gables, shear plywood, holdowns, beams, posts; stick exceptions Studs, plates, in-panel blocking and plywood, corners, typical headers in the panels

What the panel package includes, which walls stay stick (under concrete, in an existing frame, short, sloped) and how to record it: the canon is on the Wall Panels page. Exterior build-up walls are checked against the assembly and scope; do not automatically exclude them from panels. On a panel job headers inside the panels are not counted; only flush and loose headers are counted separately - Headers.

docs.title: Studs: spacing, extra studs, dbl extra
docs.text:
Wall framing is not just field studs at spacing. We count three groups:

Field studs 16" o.c., extra (corner, king/jack/cripple), dbl on bearing and demising. Group Where How to count Field studs Across the wall By spacing factor (base16 = 1.1, base24 = 0.625) - Formulas Extra studs Corners, T-intersections, king/jack/cripple at openings The 1.1 factor partly covers them; corners as a separate row on stick Dbl / extra on bearing walls Lower floors, demising per structural A separate Extra row (Extra16 = 0.75, Extra24 = 0.5); plies and spacing from the stud schedule of each floor

Bearing walls sit in their own branch in the tree, BW/<floor> (Line along the wall strip), and go to Excel as Extra after the regular studs.

docs.title: Walls: order and makeup
docs.text:
• First ext, then corr, dem; unit partitions after that, by unit type (A 2x4) - Unit / Interior.
  • Demising walls can be double: two frames only if the plan shows two frames, row dem (2) 2x6 ....
  • Corridor 2x4 staggered = two rows at 16" on 2x6 plates (detail).
  • Shafts always: elevator, stair, trash chute; material per the wall type (Shaft).
  • Bracing for drywall by wall height: table on the Bracing for Drywall page. Blocking flat and diagonal 48" o.c.: formulas in Formulas.
Staggered stud wall: two rows of 2x4 staggered on 2x6 plates, insulation woven between them. This is how corridor walls and some demising walls are built in COM.

docs.title: Corridor and floor framing
docs.text:
• A 6'-7' corridor is often framed with 2x10 on a ledger: its own joist area, with ledger and hangers as separate rows per detail.
  • Floor and roof trusses have different depths, do not mix them up; joist direction per the structural detail.
  • Hardware around the truss perimeter (accessories): bearing parallel or perpendicular per the structural plans.
  • DHU fire hangers only over stair, elevator and shaft walls; demising with gypsum under the floor framing = ITS - Hangers.

docs.title: FRT and construction type
docs.text:
The construction type comes from the Code Compliance Summary on the cover sheet; it is not a conditional note.

Type What is FRT Type III (podium, 4-7 floors of wood) Everything in the plane of the exterior wall: studs, plates, headers, blocking, sheathing; wood walls below the podium. No LVL/PSL/LSL in the plane of the exterior wall, do not write "LVL FRT" Type V-A, V-B No general FRT; only what the details show Any If the exterior wall is FRT, then exterior blocking and parapets are FRT too; FRT subfloor strips 2' or 4' around the perimeter of their own floor

The note all wood materials at exterior to be FRT means all loose plywood is FRT with verify. FRT and FRTW are different designations, write them as in the project. Table: Tips: FRT.

1/2" OSB draft stop over a demising wall in the attic: a separate row in Gable Walls, area from the attic profile in the section. The most common miss in COM.

docs.title: What to look for in the specs
docs.text:
Full checklist before delivery: Pre-delivery check. Here only what you read in a COM specification:

  • Sheathing names: Flame Block, Densglass (often on metal walls), ZIP-R; write them as in the project, do not turn them into "7/16 OSB".
  • Glulam grades (24F-V3), the word camber: note it.
  • Stud and plate specs: SP plates, SPF vs DF, DF#2, HF, MSR, LSL; a different grade goes on a separate row.
  • Gypcrete on the floor usually means double bottom plates.
  • Insulation: only exterior continuous insulation over the sheathing; interior gypsum, interior insulation and sound batt are not counted in a frame scope.
  • Piggyback trusses: 2x6 sleepers - Overframes.
  • Flat roof curb blocking (2) 2x6 P.T. if nothing is specified and there is no detail.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Wall type assigned as a group, stud height = floor-to-floor.
  • Shaft walls dropped as "panels by others".
  • Draft stop missed or copied from the shear total.
  • Headers inside panels counted separately.
  • All wall mistakes: Common mistakes, sheathing mistakes: sheathing.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/
  Main/
    walls/2nd floor walls/ext 2x6 9.09
    walls/2nd floor walls/corr 2x6 9.09
    walls/2nd floor walls/dem 2x6 9.09
    BW/2nd/BW4-4-24
    units/2nd/A 2x4
    shear walls/2nd/shear/SW1-1
    gables/gable trusses/draft stop

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Wall Panels, Exterior Walls
  • Client and job type rules
  • EWP / Capital, Reconstruction, Residential

docs.title: EWP / Capital
docs.text:
EWP (Engineered Wood Products) - factory-made engineered framing materials: I-joists, LVL / PSL / LSL / GL beams and engineered rim. There are two opposite job types: "EWP only" (Capital-type) and "everything except EWP" (Frame. EWP by others).

EWP only: we count I-joists, LVL/PSL/GL, engineered rim and hangers for them. Not 2x, trusses, nails.

EWP on site: I-joists sit on a glued beam, the beam sits on a post with a metal post cap. In an "EWP only" job we count the I-joists, the beam and the hangers for them; not the 2x post or the trusses in the background. Photo: redbuilt.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What these materials are
docs.text:
Material What it is Where I-joist OSB web and LVL/OSB flanges; a light floor joist (TJI, LPI, BCI, RFPI, Nordic) Floors, flat roofs LVL Laminated veneer; strong, stable Beams, headers, rim under load PSL Parallel strand lumber; high bearing capacity Beams, columns LSL Laminated strand; often rim and short beams Rim, headers GL / Glulam Glued laminations; often exposed Long spans

Product details: Joist and Beam.

docs.title: EWP only (Capital-type)
docs.text:
Count: I-joists, LVL / PSL / GL beams, engineered rim and blocking in LF, hangers for them; possibly columns and stair stringers.

Do not count: regular 2x, trusses, ties (CS, MST and similar), nails, stair connectors, unless the scope explicitly asks for them.

Rules:

  • TJI series as shown: 110 does not become 230.
  • Most hangers are top mount; joists deeper than 16" take HIT, not ITS. Over walls with double gypsum (firewall) at stairs and shafts: DHU / DGU as a separate row - Hangers.
  • Rim: if LVL is not specified anywhere, do not assume 1-3/4 LVL Rim; by default use Rim or the product marked assumed. Rim thicknesses: 1-1/8" OSB, 1-1/2" LSL, 1-3/4" LVL - Rim Board.
  • Rim factor 1.05; blocking continuous in LF, factor per Formulas.
  • Identical floor: note 4th floor frame is identical to 3rd floor, but still list the materials.

docs.title: The opposite case: Frame. EWP by others
docs.text:
The Frame. EWP by others tag on the project folder: the client supplies the EWP, we count all the other framing.

Count: walls, openings, sheathing, areas, all posts (including those under EWP beams), 2x headers, roofing, eaves, truss heel, hardware.

Do not count: I-joists, LVL / PSL / LSL beams and headers, engineered rim. Remove the EWP rows, do not leave them at zero.

Rules:

  • Header note All EWP products are by others. The template note Walls are panels by others is deleted if there is no panel scope.
  • Hangers for EWP are not counted; other hardware as usual: Zmax outside and on P.T., ties to trusses under sheathing without Zmax.
  • Furring and rainscreen, if in question, go in as optional with a note giving the reason.
  • Posts under EWP beams are still ours: per schedule, with cap and base.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• EWP counted with EWP by others, or not counted with EWP only.
  • Rim recorded as LVL with no callout.
  • Hangers counted from the purchased boards, not by assembly.
  • All floor framing mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Takeoffs/
  framing/2nd floor framing/joists/11 7/8 TJI 210 16"
  framing/2nd floor framing/beams/(2) 1 3/4 x 11 7/8 LVL 14
  framing/2nd floor framing/details/rim
  framing/2nd floor framing/posts/C4 9.0

docs.text:
• Joist, Beam, Rim Board, Hangers
  • Client and job type rules
  • COM Commercial, Residential

docs.title: Reconstruction
docs.text:
Part of the building already exists, part is demolished, part is added. The main difficulty: do not count the whole building as new, and do not lose the places where new framing connects to existing.

Existing - do not count, Demo - only if in scope, New and connections - count.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A job on an existing building: an addition on top, a re-layout, floor framing replacement, new openings, roof or porch repair. Scope comes with a tag like Frame. Interior trim and Int doors. NO metal or Revision. Panel rules do not apply here to new walls inside an existing frame: Wall Panels.

docs.title: How it differs
docs.text: New construction Reconstruction Floor plan The whole plan is a takeoff plan The existing floor plan is often just context; measure from the new work plan Walls Per the wall schedule Only New, Replace, Patch; do not count Existing to remain Panels Possible New walls inside an existing frame are always stick Main focus Completeness New-to-existing connections: ledgers, straps, anchors, hangers

docs.title: What to count and what not
docs.text:
Count: new walls, openings, floor framing and roofing shown as new; repair and rebuild areas (rotten framing, replaced subfloor, patched roof, rebuilt porch, new beams and posts); new connections (hangers, straps, anchors, bolts, blocking, ledgers); bracing, if in the structural notes; envelope: WRB, sheathing patches, siding backing, insulation, flashing; a new subfloor over the whole existing floor, if the detail requires it (the old floor is covered entirely).

Do not count: existing framing with no changes; demo-only items without demo scope; existing walls and openings shown for context; old joists and rafters with the note existing to remain; trim with a structural scope; steel partitions with NO metal (note Metal Studs by others).

docs.title: How to read the marks
docs.text: Mark on the drawings How to read it What to do Existing / E Already built Do not count unless a repair or replacement is shown Existing to remain Stays Do not add material; check only the connection to new work Demo / dashed line Removed Count only with demo scope New / heavy line / keyed note New work Count as regular material scope Replace in kind Replace with the same Count the replacement area or length, not the whole existing run Patch / Repair Local repair Only the indicated area, plus a note

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
Where on the drawings What to check Cover, code, general notes What the remodel scope includes; construction type Demo plans What is removed and what stays New work plans Where new framing actually appears Structural details Connections to existing: ledgers, straps, anchors, sistering Elevations, sections Height changes, roof tie-ins, wall rebuild areas Keynotes Patch, repair, replace items that are not visible on the plan Photos, field notes Existing condition, if the drawings are incomplete
  • Legend first: line weights, dashed lines, hatch, keynote symbols.
  • An opening is moved or widened: header, king/jack studs, sill, sheathing patch.
  • An existing roof or floor is opened up: temporary support, sistering, scab, reinforcement.
  • Old member sizes are not the same as new ones: do not assume 2x10 if the detail shows the actual existing member.
  • If the drawings show only the repair area, do not multiply it over the whole floor.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A demo plan taken as a material takeoff.
  • A patch area stretched over the whole floor.
  • A new subfloor over the old floor missed ("it is already there").
  • Steel partitions counted with NO metal, or not marked with a note.
  • All wall mistakes: Common mistakes.

docs.title: Notes in the DFL
docs.text:
• Existing framing to remain - not counted.
  • Counted new work only per shaded/keyed repair area.
  • Header counted only at enlarged opening.
  • Ledger and hangers counted at new-to-existing connection per <detail>.
  • Demo shown for context only - no demo material counted.
  • Metal Studs by others.

docs.title: Residential
docs.text:
A single-family house, duplex or townhouse: one or two buildings, a garage, a porch, often wood walls for the full height and regular stick framing.

Walls + openings, floor/roof framing, sheathing, SQFT, roof/deck/porch. Same order as in the "Work" menu.

Residential at the framing stage: 2x walls with sheathing at the corners, rafters on a ridge beam, OSB floor decking, temporary braces. All of this is the regular full scope: walls, openings, floor and roof framing, sheathing. Photo: threediamondsconstruction.com, source, found via Pinterest.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A residential full-framing job. Unlike COM, there are usually no corridors, demising walls, shafts or panels; instead there is almost always a garage, porch, balcony or deck with its own outlines and roof pitches. Scope is most often Frame or Frame. EWP by others.

docs.title: How it differs from COM
docs.text: Residential COM Walls ext and partitions with no prefix, bearing walls as BW ext, corridor, demising, unit, shaft Panels Rarely Often (COM w/panel) Floor framing Joists and beams per the framing plan, EWP per the specification Same, plus fire hangers, firewall Roofing Trusses or rafters, overframes, dormers Flat roof, parapets, piggyback trusses Buildings House, garage, sometimes an ADU Several buildings, a workbook per building

docs.title: What to count and what not
docs.text:
Count: walls per the wall schedule, openings, sheathing and WRB, areas by floor, joists, beams, posts, headers, details, stairs, roofing by pitch, eaves and rakes, truss heel, gables, deck / porch / balcony, hardware if shown.

Do not count: trusses (by others, note in the header), nails, interior gypsum and interior insulation, trim not in scope. With EWP by others, also I-joists, LVL and engineered rim - EWP by others.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Structural and Arch give different wall sizes: structural wins, record the discrepancy with a note.
  • Exact stud heights from the section, if the schedules differ by floor.
  • Shaft walls in a duplex or townhouse (between units): demising with gypsum, attic draft stop.
  • Exterior sheathing against the energy and Zip notes.
  • Overframes, canopy, dormers, truss heel: their own areas and rows.
  • Garage, porch, porte cochere: their own outlines and pitches, they do not inherit from the main house.
  • EWP per the specification (TJI series as shown), not out of habit.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Garage roof pitch taken from the main house.
  • Exterior posts (porch, deck) not P.T.; posts under the roof recorded as P.T.
  • Hangers outside without Zmax.
  • Balcony and porch counted as one block.
  • All mistakes by section: Common mistakes, deck and porch.
